Reports 20801–21033 use the English translation supplied by the user, including its clarifications, variant readings, and noted textual uncertainties. Arabic is reproduced from the uploaded source. This merge checks alignment and completeness of numbered entries; it does not establish philological accuracy.

**Translator's notes**
- Several passages contain scribal corruptions or elliptical phrasing (for example 20813, 20844, 20932, 21005, 21010, 21017, 21031 and 21032). I translated these literally and flagged them rather than guessing at emendations.
- Obscure terms such as *ruwaybiḍa*, *thaghb*, *ʿanātīn* and *ṭaḥraba* are transliterated and explained in brackets or inline, following the glosses given in the text itself where it offers them.

records.text_en: Abu Umar Ahmad ibn Khalid narrated to us: Abu Yaqub Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Abbad narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq ibn Hammam informed us: Mamar informed us, from Qatada, who said: Ibn Abbas used to say, 'There are three definitive verses by which people no longer act; they have abandoned them: O you who believe, those whom your right hands possess and those among you who have not reached puberty must ask your permission on three occasions [Quran 24:58]; and this verse: O people, We created you from a male and a female, and made you peoples and tribes so that you may know one another; the noblest of you before God is the most righteous [Quran 49:13]. Yet you insist on so-and-so son of so-and-so and so-and-so son of so-and-so.' [The transmitted wording says 'three verses' but cites these two passages in this entry.]
records.text_ar: ١٩٤١٩ - حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو عُمَرَ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ خَالِدٍ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو يَعْقُوبَ إِسْحَاقُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ عَبَّادٍ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ بْنُ هَمَّامٍ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، قَالَ: كَانَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ يَقُولُ:   «§ثَلَاثُ آيَاتٍ مُحْكَمَاتٍ لَا يُعْمَلُ بِهِنَّ الْيَوْمَ، تَرَكَهُنَّ النَّاسُ:  {يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لِيَسْتَأْذِنْكُمُ الَّذِينَ مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ وَالَّذِينَ لَمْ يَبْلُغُوا الْحُلُمَ مِنْكُمْ ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ}   [النور: ٥٨]  ، وَهَذِهِ الْآيَةُ  {يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ مِنْ ذَكَرٍ وَأُنْثَى وَجَعَلْنَاكُمْ شُعُوبًا وَقَبَائِلَ لِتَعَارَفُوا إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ أَتْقَاكُمْ}   [الحجرات: ١٣]  فَأَبَيْتُمْ إِلَّا فُلَانَ بْنَ فُلَانٍ، وَفُلَانَ بْنَ فُلَانٍ»

records.text_en: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Mamar informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: 'Those who are enslaved and those who have not reached puberty seek permission at these three times: before the dawn prayer, at midday, and after the night prayer. And when your children attain puberty, let them seek permission just as those before them sought permission [Quran 24:59].'
records.text_ar: ١٩٤٢٠ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، قَالَ:   «الْمَمْلُوكُونَ، وَمَنْ لَمْ يَبْلُغِ الْحُلُمَ يَسْتَأْذِنُونَ فِي هَذِهِ الثَّلَاثِ سَاعَاتٍ: قَبْلَ صَلَاةِ الْفَجْرِ، وَنِصْفِ النَّهَارِ، وَبَعْدَ الْعِشَاءِ،  {§وَإِذَا بَلَغَ الْأَطْفَالُ مِنْكُمُ الْحُلُمَ فَلْيَسْتَأْذِنُوا كَمَا اسْتَأْذَنَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ}   [النور: ٥٩]»

records.text_en: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Muslim ibn Nadhir: Hudhayfa was asked, 'Must a man seek permission before entering upon his mother?' He replied, 'Yes. If you do not, you may see something of her that you dislike.'

records.text_en: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Mamar informed us, from Said al-Jurayri, from Abu Nadra, from Abu Said al-Khudri, who said: Abd Allah ibn Qays, Abu Musa al-Ashari, greeted Umar ibn al-Khattab three times. He was not granted permission to enter, so he went back. Umar pursued him and asked, 'Why did you go back?' He replied, 'I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: If one of you offers greetings three times and receives no answer, let him go back.' Umar said, 'You must bring me evidence for what you say, or I shall do such-and-such to you,' and threatened him. Abu Musa came to us, his face drained of color, while I was sitting in a circle. We asked what had happened. He told us how he had greeted Umar and what had followed, and asked, 'Has any one of you heard this from the Messenger of God ﷺ?' They said, 'All of us have heard it.' They sent one of their number with him to Umar, who confirmed it.
records.text_ar: ١٩٤٢٣ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ سَعِيدٍ الْجُرَيْرِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِي نَضْرَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيِّ، قَالَ: سَلَّمَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ قَيْسٍ أَبُو مُوسَى الْأَشْعَرِيُّ، عَلَى عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ، فَلَمْ يُؤْذَنْ لَهُ، فَرَجَعَ، فَأَقْبَلَ عُمَرُ فِي أَثَرِهِ، فَقَالَ: لِمَ رَجَعْتَ؟ فَقَالَ: إِنِّي سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَقُولُ:   «§إِذَا سَلَّمَ أَحَدُكُمْ ثَلَاثًا فَلَمْ يُجَبْ فَلْيَرْجِعْ»   . فَقَالَ عُمَرُ: لَتَأْتِيَنِّي عَلَى مَا تَقُولُ بِبَيِّنَةٍ، أَوْ لَأَفْعَلَنَّ بِكَ كَذَا، غَيْرَ أَنَّهُ قَدْ أَوْعَدَهُ، فَجَاءَنَا أَبُو مُوسَى مُنْتَقِعًا لَوْنُهُ، وَأَنَا فِي حِلْقَةٍ جَالِسٌ، فَقُلْنَا: مَا شَأْنُكَ؟ فَقَالَ: سَلَّمْتُ عَلَى عُمَرَ، فَأَخْبَرَنَا خَبَرَهُ، فَهَلْ سَمِعَ أَحَدٌ مِنْكُمْ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ؟ قَالُوا: كُلُّنَا قَدْ سَمِعَهُ، فَأَرْسَلُوا مَعَهُ رَجُلًا مِنْهُمْ، حَتَّى أَتَى عُمَرَ فَأَخْبَرَهُ ذَلِكَ

records.text_en: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Asim ibn Sulayman, from Abu al-Aliya, who said: I greeted Abu Said al-Khudri three times, and no one answered me. I moved to one side of the house, whereupon a messenger came out and said, 'Come in.' When I entered, Abu Said said, 'Had you added more greetings, I would not have given you permission.'

records.text_en: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Mamar informed us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas or someone else: The Messenger of God ﷺ asked permission to enter upon Sad ibn Ubada and said, 'Peace be upon you and the mercy of God.' Sad replied, 'And upon you be peace and the mercy of God,' but the Prophet ﷺ did not hear him. The Prophet ﷺ greeted him three times, and Sad responded three times without letting him hear, so the Prophet ﷺ left. Sad followed him and said, 'Messenger of God, may my father be your ransom, each time you greeted me I heard you and returned the greeting, but I did not make you hear me. I wanted to receive more of your greetings and blessing.' He then brought him into the house and offered him raisins, of which the Prophet of God ﷺ ate. When he finished, he said, 'May the righteous eat your food, the angels pray for you, and those who fast break their fast in your home.'

records.raw_text_en: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Mamar informed us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas or someone else: The Messenger of God ﷺ asked permission to enter upon Sad ibn Ubada and said, 'Peace be upon you and the mercy of God.' Sad replied, 'And upon you be peace and the mercy of God,' but the Prophet ﷺ did not hear him. The Prophet ﷺ greeted him three times, and Sad responded three times without letting him hear, so the Prophet ﷺ left. Sad followed him and said, 'Messenger of God, may my father be your ransom, each time you greeted me I heard you and returned the greeting, but I did not make you hear me. I wanted to receive more of your greetings and blessing.' He then brought him into the house and offered him raisins, of which the Prophet of God ﷺ ate. When he finished, he said, 'May the righteous eat your food, the angels pray for you, and those who fast break their fast in your home.'

records.text_en: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Mamar, from Abd Allah ibn Aqil, who said: The Prophet ﷺ greeted Sad ibn Ubada three times but Sad did not grant him permission, because he was occupied with a personal need. The Prophet ﷺ went away. Sad hurried, washed himself, then followed him and said, 'Messenger of God, I was occupied with a personal need and rose to wash.' The Prophet ﷺ said, 'Water is due to water.'

records.text_en: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Mamar, from Ayyub, from Ibn Sirin, who said: A Bedouin asked permission to enter upon the Prophet ﷺ, saying, 'May I enter?' without offering a greeting. The Messenger of God ﷺ said to one of the household, 'Tell him to give the greeting.' The Bedouin heard this, offered the greeting, and was allowed in.

records.text_en: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Mamar, from a man, who said: I was with Ibn Umar when a man asked permission to enter and said, 'May I come in?' Ibn Umar said, 'No.' Someone told the man to offer the greeting; he greeted them, and Ibn Umar allowed him in.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Aʿmash, who said: Ibn ʿUmar passed a house and saw a woman at its door. Wishing to enter, he asked her, “May I come in?” She replied, “Come in with a greeting of peace.” He went on his way, reluctant to enter.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Sahl ibn Saʿd al-Sāʿidī: A man peered at the Prophet ﷺ through the screen of his room while the Prophet ﷺ held a comb-like implement in his hand. The Prophet ﷺ said, “Had I known that someone was looking at me so that I could reach him, I would have thrust this implement into his eye. Was permission to enter instituted for any reason other than to protect people from being looked at?”
records.text_ar: ١٩٤٣١ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ السَّاعِدِيِّ، أَنَّ رَجُلًا اطَّلَعَ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ مِنْ سُتْرَةِ الْحُجْرَةِ، وَفِي يَدِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ مِدْرَى، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§لَوْ أَعْلَمُ أَنَّ أَحَدًا يَنْظُرُنِي حَتَّى آتِيَهُ، لَطَعَنْتُ بِالْمِدْرَى فِي عَيْنِهِ، وَهَلْ جُعِلَ الِاسْتِئْذَانُ إِلَّا مِنْ أَجْلِ النَّظَرِ؟»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilāba: A man peered into the Prophet’s ﷺ chamber. The Prophet ﷺ tried to catch him unawares with a stick, but missed him.
records.text_ar: ١٩٤٣٢ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ أَبِي قِلَابَةَ،   «§أَنَّ رَجُلًا اطَّلَعَ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فِي حُجْرَتِهِ، فَخَتَلَهُ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ بِعُودٍ فَأَخْطَأَهُ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Suhayl ibn Abī Ṣāliḥ, from his father, from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said, “Whoever peers into a people’s home without their permission: they are permitted to put out his eye.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Saʿīd al-Jurayrī, from Abū Tamīma al-Hujaymī, who said: Abū Jurayy greeted the Prophet ﷺ by saying, “Upon you be peace.” The Prophet ﷺ replied, “'Upon you be peace' is the greeting of the dead. Say instead: 'Peace be upon you.'”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Hammām ibn Munabbih, from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said, “God created Adam in his form, sixty cubits tall. When He created him, He said, 'Go and greet that group'—a number of angels who were sitting there—'and listen to what they say in reply. That will be your greeting and the greeting of your descendants.' So he went and said, 'Peace be upon you.' They said, 'Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God,' adding 'and the mercy of God.' Everyone who enters Paradise will be in Adam's form, sixty cubits tall, and created beings have continued to diminish in stature until now.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٤٣٥ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ هَمَّامِ بْنِ مُنَبِّهٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «خَلَقَ اللَّهُ آدَمَ عَلَى صُورَتِهِ، طُولُهُ سِتُّونَ ذِرَاعًا، فَلَمَّا خَلَقَهُ قَالَ: §اذْهَبْ فَسَلِّمْ عَلَى أُولَئِكَ النَّفَرِ - وَهُمْ نَفَرٌ مِنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ جُلُوسٌ - فَاسْتَمِعْ إِلَى مَا يُجِيبُونَكَ، فَإِنَّهَا تَحِيَّتُكَ، وَتَحِيَّةُ ذُرِّيَّتِكَ، قَالَ: فَذَهَبَ، فَقَالَ: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ، فَقَالُوا: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ، فَزَادُوهُ: وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ، قَالَ: فَكُلُّ مَنْ يَدْخُلُ الْجَنَّةَ عَلَى صُورَةِ آدَمَ طُولُهُ سِتُّونَ ذِرَاعًا، فَلَمْ يَزَلِ الْخَلْقُ يَنْقُصُ حَتَّى الْآنَ»

records.isnad_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Hammām ibn Munabbih, from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said, “
records.matn_en: God created Adam in his form, sixty cubits tall. When He created him, He said, 'Go and greet that group'—a number of angels who were sitting there—'and listen to what they say in reply. That will be your greeting and the greeting of your descendants.' So he went and said, 'Peace be upon you.' They said, 'Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God,' adding 'and the mercy of God.' Everyone who enters Paradise will be in Adam's form, sixty cubits tall, and created beings have continued to diminish in stature until now.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, who said: When someone greeted him and he returned the greeting, he would say, “And upon you.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٤٣٦ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، قَالَ: كَانَ §إِذَا سُلِّمَ عَلَيْهِ فَرَدَّ، قَالَ:   «وَعَلَيْكُمْ»
records.section_title_en: How to Greet and Respond to a Greeting

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: وَذُكِرَ، أَنَّ عَمَّارَ بْنَ يَاسِرٍ §سَلَّمَ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، فَرَدَّ عَلَيْهِ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ السَّلَامَ، فَقَالَ:   «وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: It was also related that ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir greeted the Messenger of God ﷺ. The Messenger of God ﷺ returned the greeting, saying, “And upon you be peace.”

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: قَالَ: وَكَانَ الْحَسَنُ §إِذَا رَدَّ السَّلَامَ، قَالَ:   «وَعَلَيْكُمْ»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: He said: Whenever al-Ḥasan returned a greeting, he would say, “And upon you.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, that ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn said: “In the pre-Islamic period we used to say, 'May God delight your eye' and 'Have a pleasant morning.' When Islam came, we were prohibited from doing that.” Maʿmar said: “It is disliked to say, 'May God delight your eye' in that form, but there is no harm in saying, 'May God bring delight to your eye.'” [The Arabic distinguishes the formulas أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ بِكَ عَيْنًا and أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَيْنَكَ.]

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Yaʿīsh ibn al-Walīd, who raised it to the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “The disease of earlier nations has crept among you: envy and mutual hatred. This is the shaver. I do not say that it shaves hair; rather, it shaves away religion. By the One in whose hand is Muhammad's soul, you will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another. Shall I tell you something which, if you do it, will cause you to love one another? Spread the greeting of peace among yourselves.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Abū ʿAmr al-Nadbī, who said: “I went with Ibn ʿUmar to the market. He met neither young nor old without greeting them. He even passed a blind slave and kept greeting him, though the other man did not answer. Someone said to him, 'He is blind.'”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Zayd ibn Aslam, that the Prophet ﷺ said, “The rider should greet the pedestrian; the pedestrian, the seated person; the few, the many; and the younger, the older. When one group passes another and one of them offers the greeting, it suffices for the group; and when one person from the other group responds, it suffices for them.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٤٤٣ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ:   «§يُسَلِّمُ الرَّاكِبُ عَلَى الْمَاشِي، وَالْمَاشِي عَلَى الْقَاعِدِ، وَالْقَلِيلُ عَلَى الْكَثِيرِ، وَالصَّغِيرُ عَلَى الْكَبِيرِ، وَإِذَا مَرَّ الْقَوْمُ بِالْقَوْمِ فَسَلَّمَ مِنْهُمْ وَاحِدٌ أَجْزَأَ عَنْهُمْ، وَإِذَا رَدَّ مِنَ الْآخَرِينَ وَاحِدٌ أَجْزَأَ عَنْهُمْ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Zayd ibn Sallām, from his grandfather, who said: Muʿāwiya wrote to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Shibl, instructing him to teach the people what he had heard from the Messenger of God ﷺ. He gathered them and said, “I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: 'Learn the Qurʾān; when you have learned it, do not go to extremes concerning it, do not neglect it, do not make a livelihood from it, and do not use it to accumulate wealth.'” [The report continues in the following three unnumbered source paragraphs.]
records.text_ar: ١٩٤٤٤ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ أَبِي كَثِيرٍ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ سَلَّامٍ، عَنْ جَدِّهِ، قَالَ: كَتَبَ مُعَاوِيَةُ إِلَى عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ شِبْلٍ: أَنْ عَلِّمِ النَّاسَ مَا سَمِعْتَ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، فَجَمَعَهُمْ، فَقَالَ: إِنِّي سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَقُولُ:   «§تَعَلَّمُوا الْقُرْآنَ، فَإِذَا تَعَلَّمْتُمُوهُ، فَلَا تَغْلُوا فِيهِ، وَلَا تَجْفُوا عَنْهُ، وَلَا تَأْكُلُوا بِهِ، وَلَا تَسْتَكْثِرُوا بِهِ»

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: ثُمَّ قَالَ:   «إِنَّ §التُّجَّارَ هُمُ الْفُجَّارُ»   ، قَالُوا: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، أَلَيْسَ قَدْ أَحَلَّ اللَّهُ الْبَيْعَ وَحَرَّمَ الرِّبَا؟ قَالَ:   «بَلَى، وَلَكِنَّهُمْ يَحْلِفُونَ وَيَأْثَمُونَ»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: Then he said: “Traders are the wicked.” They asked, “Messenger of God, has God not permitted trade and forbidden usury?” He replied, “Yes, but they swear oaths and thereby commit sins.”

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: ثُمَّ قَالَ:   «إِنَّ §الْفُسَّاقَ هُمْ أَهْلُ النَّارِ»   ، قَالُوا: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، وَمَنِ الْفُسَّاقُ؟ قَالَ:   «النِّسَاءُ»   ، قَالُوا: أَوَلَيْسَ بِأُمَّهَاتِنَا وَبَنَاتِنَا وَأَخَوَاتِنَا؟ قَالَ:   «بَلَى، وَلَكِنَّهُنَّ إِذَا أُعْطِينَ لَمْ يَشْكُرْنَ، وَإِذَا ابْتُلِينَ لَمْ يَصْبِرْنَ»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: Then he said: “The transgressors are the people of the Fire.” They asked, “Messenger of God, who are the transgressors?” He replied, “Women.” They asked, “Are they not our mothers, daughters, and sisters?” He replied, “Yes; but when they are given something they do not show gratitude, and when they are tested they do not remain patient.”

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: ثُمَّ   «§- [٣٨٨] - لِيُسَلِّمِ الرَّاكِبُ عَلَى الرَّاجِلِ، وَالرَّاجِلُ عَلَى الْجَالِسِ، وَالْأَقَلُّ عَلَى الْأَكْثَرِ، مَنْ أَجَابَ السَّلَامَ كَانَ لَهُ، وَمَنْ لَمْ يُجِبْ فَلَا شَيْءَ لَهُ»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: Then he said: “Let the rider greet the pedestrian; the pedestrian, the seated person; and the fewer, the more numerous. Whoever responds to the greeting has its reward, and whoever does not respond gains nothing.” [The printed page changes to p. 388 inside this paragraph.]

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Hammām ibn Munabbih, who heard Abū Hurayra say: The Messenger of God ﷺ said, “The younger should greet the older, the one passing should greet the one seated, and the few should greet the many.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, who said: “Two companions of the Prophet ﷺ would be together, then a tree would separate them. When they came together again, one would greet the other.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī and Qatāda, regarding the words, “Greet yourselves with a greeting from God” [Qurʾān 24:61]. They said: “When you enter your own house, say, 'Peace be upon you.'”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, who said: “It has reached me that it is disliked for men to offer greetings of peace to women, or women to men.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٤٤٨ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ أَبِي كَثِيرٍ، قَالَ: بَلَغَنِي   «§أَنَّهُ يُكْرَهُ أَنْ يُسَلِّمَ الرِّجَالُ عَلَى النِّسَاءِ، وَالنِّسَاءُ عَلَى الرِّجَالِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said, “When you enter a home, greet its occupants with peace; when you leave, bid its occupants farewell with a greeting of peace.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٤٥٠ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، قَالَ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§إِذَا دَخَلْتُمْ بَيْتًا فَسَلِّمُوا عَلَى أَهْلِهِ، وَإِذَا خَرَجْتُمْ فَأَوْدِعُوا أَهْلَهُ السَّلَامَ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from an unnamed man, from Mujāhid, and from Qatāda; both said: “When you enter a house in which there is no one, say, 'Peace be upon us and upon God's righteous servants,' for the angels will return the greeting to you.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٤٥١ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ رَجُلٍ، عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ، وَعَنْ قَتَادَةَ، قَالَا: §إِذَا دَخَلْتَ بَيْتًا لَيْسَ فِيهِ أَحَدٌ فَقُلِ:   «السَّلَامُ عَلَيْنَا وَعَلَى عِبَادِ اللَّهِ الصَّالِحِينَ، فَإِنَّ الْمَلَائِكَةَ تَرُدُّ عَلَيْكَ»

records.raw_text_ar: ١٩٤٥١ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ رَجُلٍ، عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ، وَعَنْ قَتَادَةَ، قَالَا: §إِذَا دَخَلْتَ بَيْتًا لَيْسَ فِيهِ أَحَدٌ فَقُلِ:   «السَّلَامُ عَلَيْنَا وَعَلَى عِبَادِ اللَّهِ الصَّالِحِينَ، فَإِنَّ الْمَلَائِكَةَ تَرُدُّ عَلَيْكَ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Abū Hārūn al-ʿAbdī, who said: I heard Ibn ʿUmar say: A man came and said, “Peace be upon you.” The Prophet ﷺ said, “Ten.” Another came and said, “Peace be upon you and the mercy of God.” He said, “Twenty.” Another came and said, “Peace be upon you and the mercy of God and His blessings.” He said, “Thirty,” meaning thirty good deeds.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Ayyūb, from Nāfiʿ or someone else, that a man used to meet Ibn ʿUmar and greet him at length, saying, “Peace be upon you, and God's mercy and blessings, and His forgiveness and protection.” He kept extending the formula. Ibn ʿUmar said to him, “And upon you—a hundred times! If you do that again, I will certainly give you a hard time.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, who said: ʿUthmān ibn Ḥunayf greeted Muʿāwiya, saying, “Peace be upon you, O commander.” Some men from Syria were present and said, “Who is this hypocrite who shortchanged the Commander of the Faithful in his greeting?” ʿUthmān ibn Ḥunayf said to Muʿāwiya, “These people have criticized me over a matter you know better than they do. I used the same greeting for Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿUthmān.” Muʿāwiya replied, “I think some of what he says may well have happened. But when civil strife broke out, the Syrians said, 'By God, our religion will be recognized, and we will not diminish the honor due in greeting our caliph.' I do not suppose that you people of Medina address a collector of alms as 'O commander.'”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, who said: I heard a man of al-Jazīra called Dāwūd recount to Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbbās, whom we had visited at al-Ruṣāfa: “Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ entered upon Muʿāwiya and said, 'Peace be upon you, O king!' Muʿāwiya said, 'Why not call me something else? You are the believers, and I am your commander.' Saʿd replied, 'Yes—if it was we who appointed you commander.' Muʿāwiya said, 'Let me not hear anyone say that Saʿd is not of Quraysh, or I will deal severely with him.'” Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī said, “Indeed Saʿd occupies the central position among Quraysh and has an established lineage.”

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, who said: I heard a man of al-Jazīra called Dāwūd recount to Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbbās, whom we had visited at al-Ruṣāfa: “Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ entered upon Muʿāwiya and said, 'Peace be upon you, O king!' Muʿāwiya said, 'Why not call me something else? You are the believers, and I am your commander.' Saʿd replied, 'Yes—if it was we who appointed you commander.' Muʿāwiya said, 'Let me not hear anyone say that Saʿd is not of Quraysh, or I will deal severely with him.'” Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī said, “Indeed Saʿd occupies the central position among Quraysh and has an established lineage.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, that Ibn Sīrīn entered upon Ibn Hubayra and did not greet him with his official title. He simply said, “Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Suhayl ibn Abī Ṣāliḥ, from his father, from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said, “Do not initiate greetings of peace to the Jews and Christians; when you encounter them on a road, force them to its narrowest part.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, that Ibn ʿUmar greeted a Jewish man whom he had not recognized. When he was informed of the man's identity, he went back and said, “Give me back my greeting!” The man replied, “I have already done so.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatāda, who said: A Jewish man milked a ewe for the Prophet ﷺ, who said, “O God, make him handsome.” His hair became black, darker than one might imagine. Maʿmar added, “I also heard someone besides Qatāda mention that the man lived for around seventy years without going gray.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٤٦٢ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، قَالَ: حَلَبَ يَهُودِيٌّ لِلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ نَعْجَةً، فَقَالَ:   «§اللَّهُمَّ جَمِّلْهُ»   ، فَاسْوَدَّ شَعْرُهُ حَتَّى صَارَ أَشَدَّ سَوَادًا مِنْ كَذَا وَكَذَا قَالَ مَعْمَرٌ:   «وَسَمِعْتُ غَيْرَ قَتَادَةَ يَذْكُرُ أَنَّهُ عَاشَ نَحْوًا مِنْ سَبْعِينَ سَنَةً لَمْ يَشِبْ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilāba: A man came to Salmān al-Fārisī and found him kneading dough. He asked, “Where is your servant?” Salmān replied, “I sent him on an errand; we would not impose two burdens on him by sending him out and making him do the household work as well.” The man said, “Abū al-Dardāʾ sends you greetings of peace.” Salmān asked, “When did you arrive?” He answered, “Three days ago.” Salmān said, “Had you not delivered it, it would have remained a trust in your keeping.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٤٦٤ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ أَبِي قِلَابَةَ، أَنَّ رَجُلًا أَتَى سَلْمَانَ الْفَارِسِيَّ فَوَجَدَهُ يَعْجِنُ، فَقَالَ: أَيْنَ الْخَادِمُ؟ فَقَالَ:   «أَرْسَلْتُهُ فِي حَاجَةٍ، فَلَمْ يَكُنْ لِنَجْمَعَ عَلَيْهِ اثْنَتَيْنِ، أَنْ نُرْسِلَهُ وَلَا نَكْفِيَهُ عَمَلَهُ»   ، قَالَ: فَقَالَ الرَّجُلُ: إِنَّ أَبَا الدَّرْدَاءِ يَقُولُ: عَلَيْكَ السَّلَامُ، قَالَ:   «مَتَى قَدِمْتَ؟»   قَالَ: مُنْذُ ثَلَاثٍ، قَالَ:   «§أَمَا إِنَّكَ لَوْ لَمْ تُؤَدِّهَا كَانَتْ أَمَانَةً عِنْدَكَ»

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: قَالَ:   «§وَأَمَرَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ بِلَالًا فَأَذَّنَ يَوْمَ الْفَتْحِ فَوْقَ الْكَعْبَةِ»   ، فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ مِنْ قُرَيْشٍ لِلْحَارِثِ بْنِ هِشَامٍ: أَلَا تَرَى إِلَى هَذَا الْعَبْدِ كَيْفَ صَعَدَ؟ قَالَ: دَعْهُ فَإِنْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ يَكْرَهُهُ فَسَيُغَيِّرُهُ
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: He said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ commanded Bilāl to give the call to prayer from the top of the Kaʿba on the day of the Conquest.” A man of Quraysh asked al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām, “Do you not see how this slave has climbed up there?” He replied, “Leave him alone. If God dislikes it, He will change it.”

records.raw_text_ar: ١٩٤٦٤ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ أَبِي قِلَابَةَ، أَنَّ رَجُلًا أَتَى سَلْمَانَ الْفَارِسِيَّ فَوَجَدَهُ يَعْجِنُ، فَقَالَ: أَيْنَ الْخَادِمُ؟ فَقَالَ:   «أَرْسَلْتُهُ فِي حَاجَةٍ، فَلَمْ يَكُنْ لِنَجْمَعَ عَلَيْهِ اثْنَتَيْنِ، أَنْ نُرْسِلَهُ وَلَا نَكْفِيَهُ عَمَلَهُ»   ، قَالَ: فَقَالَ الرَّجُلُ: إِنَّ أَبَا الدَّرْدَاءِ يَقُولُ: عَلَيْكَ السَّلَامُ، قَالَ:   «مَتَى قَدِمْتَ؟»   قَالَ: مُنْذُ ثَلَاثٍ، قَالَ:   «§أَمَا إِنَّكَ لَوْ لَمْ تُؤَدِّهَا كَانَتْ أَمَانَةً عِنْدَكَ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Thābit al-Bunānī, from Anas ibn Mālik, that the Prophet ﷺ had a silver signet ring made, on which he engraved “Muḥammad, Messenger of God.” He then said, “Do not engrave anything like this upon your rings.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Abān, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: “I saw the Prophet’s ﷺ ring on his hand on the night he had it made. It is as if I can still see its glitter when he prayed”—I think he said the night prayer. Maʿmar added: “Later I was told that he set it aside.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Ayyūb, from Nāfiʿ, that Ibn ʿUmar had a ring made, then set it aside and did not wear it.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from ʿAbdallāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAqīl, who produced a ring and claimed that the Prophet ﷺ used to wear it. It bore the image of a lion.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: “I saw that Maʿmar owned a ring, but he did not wear it. Whenever he wished to seal something, he called for it.” Abū Bakr did not know what its engraving was.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb saw a man wearing a gold ring and ordered him to throw it away. Ziyād said, “Commander of the Faithful, my ring is made of iron.” He replied, “That is even more repugnant, even more repugnant.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٤٧٣ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنِ ابْنِ سِيرِينَ، أَنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ، §رَأَى عَلَى رَجُلٍ خَاتَمًا مِنْ ذَهَبٍ،   «فَأَمَرَهُ أَنْ يُلْقِيَهُ»   فَقَالَ زِيَادٌ: يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: إِنَّ خَاتَمِي مِنْ حَدِيدٍ، قَالَ:   «ذَلِكَ أَنْتَنُ وَأَنْتَنُ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Ayyūb, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ had a gold ring made and wore its setting facing inward. One day, while delivering a sermon, he said, “I had a ring made, and I used to wear it.” He then threw it away, and the people threw away their rings.
records.text_ar: ١٩٤٧٤ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ، قَالَ: اتَّخَذَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ خَاتَمًا مِنْ ذَهَبٍ وَجَعَلَ فَصَّهُ مِنْ دَاخِلٍ، قَالَ: فَبَيْنَا هُوَ يَخْطُبُ ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ، قَالَ:   «§إِنِّي صَنَعْتُ خَاتَمًا، وَكُنْتُ أَلْبَسُهُ»   ، قَالَ: فَنَبَذَهُ وَنَبَذَ النَّاسُ خَوَاتِمَهُمْ.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbdallāh ibn Ḥunayn, from his father, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ forbade me to wear a gold ring, to wear *qassī* cloth, to recite [Qurʾān] while bowing or prostrating, and to wear garments dyed with safflower.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, who said: “The Prophet ﷺ saw a man wearing a gold ring and struck his finger until he threw it away.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٤٧٧ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، قَالَ:   «§رَأَى النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عَلَى رَجُلٍ خَاتَمًا مِنْ ذَهَبٍ، فَضَرَبَ إِصْبَعَهُ حَتَّى رَمَى بِهِ»

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: قَالَ: §وَرَأَى ابْنُ عُمَرَ عَلَى رَجُلٍ خَاتَمًا مِنْ ذَهَبٍ، فَأَخَذَهُ فَخَذَفَ بِهِ "
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: He said: “Ibn ʿUmar saw a man wearing a gold ring, seized it, and threw it away.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father: Whenever he mounted [an animal], he said, “In the name of God. O God, this is from Your favor and bounty to us. Praise belongs to God, our Lord.” He then recited the verse beginning, “Glory be to the One who has subjected this to us” [Qurʾān 43:13].

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAlī ibn Rabīʿa, who saw ʿAlī mounting [his animal]. When he put his foot in the stirrup, he said, “In the name of God.” Once seated, he said, “Praise belongs to God,” then recited, “Glory be to the One who has subjected this to us” [Qurʾān 43:13], continuing to the words “to our Lord we shall return” [43:14]. He then praised God three times and magnified Him three times, and said, “There is no god but You. I have wronged myself, so forgive me; no one forgives sins except You.” He laughed. We asked, “What makes you laugh, Commander of the Faithful?” He said, “I saw the Messenger of God ﷺ do as I have done, say what I have said, and then laugh. We asked him, 'What makes you laugh, Prophet of God?' He said, '[I am amazed at] the servant who says, 'There is no god but You; I have wronged myself, so forgive me, for none forgives sins except You,' knowing that none but He forgives sins.'” [The source offers an alternative opening: “The servant ...” or “I am amazed at the servant ...”.]
records.text_ar: ١٩٤٨٠ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ رَبِيعَةَ، أَنَّهُ شَهِدَ عَلِيًّا حِينَ رَكِبَ، فَلَمَّا   «وَضَعَ رِجْلَهُ فِي الرِّكَابِ، قَالَ:»   §بِسْمِ اللَّهِ   «، فَلَمَّا اسْتَوَى قَالَ:»   الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ   «ثُمَّ قَالَ:  {سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا}   [الزخرف: ١٣]  الْآيَةَ، حَتَّى  {لَمُنْقَلِبُونَ}   [الزخرف: ١٤]  ثُمَّ حَمِدَ اللَّهَ ثَلَاثًا، وَكَبَّرَ ثَلَاثًا، ثُمَّ قَالَ:»   لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِي فَاغْفِرْ لِي، إِنَّهُ لَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ   «، - [٣٩٧] - ثُمَّ ضَحِكَ، فَقُلْنَا: مَا يُضْحِكُكَ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ؟ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَعَلَ مِثْلَ مَا فَعَلْتُ، وَقَالَ مِثْلَ مَا قُلْتُ، ثُمَّ ضَحِكَ، فَقُلْنَا: مَا يُضْحِكُكَ يَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ؟ قَالَ:»   الْعَبْدُ - أَوْ قَالَ: عَجِبْتُ لِلْعَبْدِ - إِذَا قَالَ: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِي، فَاغْفِرْ لِي إِنَّهُ لَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، يَعْلَمُ أَنَّهُ لَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا هُوَ "

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid, from Abū Maʿmar, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: “When a man mounts an animal without mentioning God's name, Satan rides behind him and tells him, 'Sing!' If he cannot sing well, he tells him, 'Indulge in vain wishes!'”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, who said: ʿUbaydallāh ibn ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUtba told me that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: I heard Abū Ṭalḥa say: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say, “Angels do not enter a house containing a dog or an image of a living figure.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, who said: al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad told me that ʿĀʾisha related to him: The Messenger of God ﷺ entered while she had hung a decorated curtain bearing images of figures. The color of his face changed. He went to the curtain and tore it down with his hand, saying, “Among those most severely punished on the Day of Resurrection are those who imitate God's creation.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٤٨٤ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنِي الْقَاسِمُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، أَنَّ عَائِشَةَ أَخْبَرَتْهُ: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ دَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا وَهِيَ مُسْتَتِرَةٌ بِقِرَامٍ فِيهِ صُورَةُ تَمَاثِيلَ، فَتَلَوَّنَ وَجْهُهُ ثُمَّ أَهْوَى إِلَى الْقِرَامِ فَهَتَكَهُ بِيَدِهِ، ثُمَّ قَالَ:   «إِنَّ §مِنْ أَشَدِّ النَّاسِ عَذَابًا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ الَّذِينَ يُشَبِّهُونَ بِخَلْقِ اللَّهِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Ayyūb, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that when the Prophet ﷺ saw images in the House—that is, the Kaʿba—he refused to enter until he had ordered them erased. He saw [images of] Abraham and Ishmael holding divining arrows and said, “May God fight them! By God, neither of those two ever sought decisions with divining arrows.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Ayyūb, from Nāfiʿ, from Aslam, the client of ʿUmar: When ʿUmar arrived in Syria, a Christian notable prepared a meal and said to him, “I would like you and your companions to honor me by coming to my house.” ʿUmar replied, “We do not enter your churches because of the images in them”—meaning the representations of figures.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbayda ibn ʿAbdallāh ibn Masʿūd, who said: “Among those suffering the most severe punishment on the Day of Resurrection are a misleading leader who leads people astray without knowledge, a man who killed a prophet, a man whom a prophet killed, and a maker of images who fashions these figures.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Mujāhid, from Abū Hurayra: Gabriel came to the Prophet ﷺ, who recognized his voice and said, “Come in.” Gabriel replied, “There is a curtain on the wall of the house bearing images of figures. Cut off their heads, or turn the curtain into a rug or cushions to be trodden on, for we do not enter a house in which there are images of figures.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from ʿIkrima, who said: “There is no harm in an image that has been brought down into the dust [that is, placed on the ground and treated as something underfoot].” Maʿmar added: “Someone who heard Mujāhid told me that he said the same as ʿIkrima.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Those who make images will be punished on the Day of Resurrection, and will be told, 'Give life to what you have created.'”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Ayyūb, from ʿIkrima, who said, “I know it only as being from Ibn ʿAbbās,” that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever makes an image will be charged on the Day of Resurrection with breathing a spirit into it, but will never be able to do so. Whoever listens secretly to the conversation of people who dislike it will have molten lead poured into his ear canals. Whoever lies in his judgment will be charged with tying a knot in a grain of barley—or, he said, between two grains of barley—and punished for it, though he will be unable to do it.” [The source reads *fī ḥukmihi*, 'in his judgment'; parallel versions may differ.]

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, that Kaʿb said: “A neck will rise out of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection and say, 'I have been commanded to seize three: whoever invokes a deity alongside God, and every stubborn tyrant'”—Maʿmar said, “I have forgotten the third”—“and it will seize them. Then another neck will rise and say, 'I have been commanded to seize three: whoever denies God, whoever tells lies about God, and whoever harms God. The one who denies God is the one who says God will not resurrect him. The one who lies about God is the one who ascribes a child to Him. The ones who harm God are those who make images, and they will be told, “Give life to what you have created.”' It will snatch them up as a bird picks up seeds.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, who had images on the door of the outer part of his house. He was asked, “Abū al-Khaṭṭāb, what is this?” He answered, “This is something I neither ordered nor made. Someone else ordered it, and I was reproached for it.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, that the Prophet ﷺ swore not to enter upon his wives for one month. Al-Zuhrī said: ʿUrwa informed me, from ʿĀʾisha, who said: “After twenty-nine nights, which I counted, the Messenger of God ﷺ entered upon me, beginning with me. I said, 'Messenger of God, you swore you would not enter upon us for a month, yet you have come after twenty-nine nights, which I have counted.' He said, 'A month may be twenty-nine days.'”
records.text_ar: ١٩٤٩٧ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَقْسَمَ أَلَّا يَدْخُلَ عَلَى أَزْوَاجِهِ شَهْرًا، قَالَ الزُّهْرِيُّ: فَأَخْبَرَنِي عُرْوَةُ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ قَالَتْ: لَمَّا مَضَتْ تِسْعٌ وَعِشْرُونَ لَيْلَةً أَعُدُّهُنَّ، دَخَلَ عَلَيَّ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، قَالَتْ: بَدَأَ بِي، فَقُلْتُ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، إِنَّكَ أَقْسَمْتَ أَلَّا تَدْخُلَ عَلَيْنَا شَهْرًا، وَإِنَّكَ دَخَلْتَ مِنْ تِسْعٍ وَعِشْرِينَ أَعُدُّهُنَّ، قَالَ:   «إِنَّ §الشَّهْرَ تِسْعٌ وَعِشْرُونَ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Muḥammad ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, from his father, who said: “We were standing with ʿUmar on the mountain at ʿArafa when I heard a man cry out, 'O Caliph!' A Bedouin of [the clan of] Lihb behind me said, 'What is this voice? May God cut off his tongue! By God, the Commander of the Faithful will never stand here again after this year.' I rebuked and insulted him. Later, while we were throwing pebbles at the pillar with ʿUmar, a pebble struck ʿUmar's head, opening a vein. Someone said, 'The Commander of the Faithful has been marked! By God, he will never stand here again after this year.' I turned and saw it was the same man of Lihb.” He said: “By God, ʿUmar never performed the pilgrimage after that.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٤٩٩ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ جُبَيْرِ بْنِ مُطْعِمٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، قَالَ:   «§إِنَّا لَوَاقِفُونَ مَعَ عُمَرَ عَلَى الْجَبَلِ بِعَرَفَةَ، إِذْ سَمِعْتُ رَجُلًا يَقُولُ: يَا خَلِيفَةُ، فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ أَعْرَابِيٌّ خَلْفِي مِنْ لِهْبٍ: مَا لِهَذَا الصَّوْتِ؟ قَطَعَ اللَّهُ لَهْجَتَهُ، وَاللَّهِ لَا يَقِفُ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ هَاهُنَا بَعْدَ هَذَا الْعَامِ أَبَدًا، قَالَ: فَشَتَمْتُهُ وَآذَيْتُهُ، قَالَ: فَلَمَّا رَمَيْنَا الْجَمْرَةَ مَعَ عُمَرَ، أَقْبَلَتْ حَصَاةٌ فَأَصَابَتْ رَأْسَهُ، فَفَتَحَتْ عِرْقًا مِنْ رَأْسِهِ، فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ: أَشْعَرَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ، لَا وَاللَّهِ لَا يَقِفُ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ بَعْدَ هَذَا الْعَامِ هَاهُنَا أَبَدًا، فَالْتَفَتُّ فَإِذَا هُوَ ذَلِكَ اللِّهْبِيُّ»   ، قَالَ: فَوَاللَّهِ مَا حَجَّ عُمَرُ بَعْدَهَا

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: «وَأَنَّ عُمَرَ §خَضَبَ لِحْيَتَهُ بِالْحِنَّاءِ فَرْدًا»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: And ʿUmar dyed his beard with pure henna.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Hilāl ibn Abī Maymūna, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, who said: Muʿāwiya ibn al-Ḥakam told us: “I said, 'Messenger of God, some of us take omens.' He replied, 'That is something you find within yourselves; do not let it stop you.' I said, 'Some of us visit soothsayers.' He replied, 'Do not visit them.' I said, 'Some of us draw lines [for divination].' He answered, 'A prophet used to draw lines; whoever coincides with his knowledge knows.'”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from ʿAwf al-ʿAbdī, from Ḥayyān, from Qaṭan ibn Qabīṣa, from his father, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Augury from birds, divination by drawing lines, and taking bad omens are among the practices of *jibt* [sorcery or false superstition].”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbaydallāh ibn ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUtba, from Abū Hurayra, who said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say, “There is no [valid] evil omen; the best of it is a good portent.” He was asked, “What is a good portent, Messenger of God?” He replied, “A good word one of you hears.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās said, “If you go forward, you are relying upon God; if you turn back, you are acting upon an omen.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Abū Salama, from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said, “There is no contagion [of itself], no Ṣafar, and no hāma [an omen-bird].” A Bedouin asked, “What of camels that are healthy on the sands, like gazelles, until a mangy camel joins them and they develop mange?” The Prophet ﷺ said, “Who infected the first one?” [An unnumbered continuation of this report follows.]
records.text_ar: ١٩٥٠٧ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِي سَلَمَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§لَا عَدْوَى وَلَا صَفَرَ وَلَا هَامَةَ»   قال: فَقَالَ أَعْرَابِيٌّ: فَمَا بَالُ الْإِبِلِ تَكُونُ فِي الرَّمْلِ، كَأَنَّهَا الظِّبَاءُ؟ فَيُخَالِطُهَا الْبَعِيرُ الْأَجْرَبُ فَيُجْرِبُهَا، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «فَمَنْ أَعْدَى الْأَوَّلَ»

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: قَالَ الزُّهْرِيُّ: وَحَدَّثَنِي رَجُلٌ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَقُولُ:   «§لَا يُورِدَنَّ مُمْرِضٌ عَلَى مُصِحٍّ»   قَالَ: فَرَاجَعَهُ الرَّجُلُ فَقَالَ: أَلَيْسَ قَدْ حَدَّثْتَنَا أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ:   «لَا عَدْوَى - [٤٠٥] - وَلَا صَفَرَ وَلَا هَامَةَ»   ؟ فَقَالَ أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ: لَمْ أُحَدِّثْكُمُوهُ، قَالَ الزُّهْرِيُّ: قَالَ لِي أَبُو سَلَمَةَ:   «بَلَى قَدْ حَدَّثَ بِهِ، وَمَا سَمِعْتُ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ نَسِيَ حَدِيثًا قَطُّ غَيْرَهُ»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: Al-Zuhrī said: A man narrated to me from Abū Hurayra, who said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say, “A person with diseased animals must not bring them to water with healthy animals.” The man challenged him: “Did you not narrate to us that the Prophet ﷺ said, ‘There is no contagion, no Ṣafar, and no hāma’?” Abū Hurayra said, “I did not narrate that to you.” Al-Zuhrī said: Abū Salama told me, “Indeed, he did narrate it; I never heard Abū Hurayra forget another report besides this one.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Abū al-Zinād: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said to Muʿayqīb al-Dawsī, “Come closer. If you were someone else, I would not sit within a spear’s length of you.” Muʿayqīb had leprosy.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, who said: “I was told that a man suffering from leprosy came to the Prophet ﷺ, apparently begging. The Prophet ﷺ did not hasten him away; he provided for him and said, 'There is no contagion [of itself].'” [An unnumbered continuation follows.]
records.text_ar: ١٩٥١١ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، قَالَ: بَلَغَنِي أَنَّ رَجُلًا أَجْذَمَ أَتَى النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ كَأَنَّهُ سَائِلٌ، فَلَمْ يُعْجِلْهُ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وجَهَّزَهُ، وَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§لَا عَدْوَى»

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: قَالَ مَعْمَرٌ: وَبَلَغَنِي أَنَّ رَجُلًا أَجْذَمَ جَاءَ إِلَى ابْنِ عُمَرَ، فَسَأَلَهُ   «فَقَامَ ابْنُ عُمَرَ §فَأَعْطَاهُ دِرْهَمًا، فَوَضَعَهُ فِي يَدِهِ»   ، وَكَانَ رَجُلٌ قَدْ قَالَ لِابْنِ عُمَرَ: أَنَا أُعْطِيهِ، فَأَبَى ابْنُ عُمَرَ أَنْ يَنَاوِلَهُ الرَّجُلُ الدِّرْهَمَ "
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: Maʿmar said: It has also reached me that a man suffering from leprosy came to Ibn ʿUmar to ask for charity. Ibn ʿUmar stood and placed a dirham in his hand. Another man had offered to deliver it for him, but Ibn ʿUmar refused to let that man hand the dirham over.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Aʿmash, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said, “The truest form of omen is the good portent, and it should not turn a Muslim back. records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Ṭāwūs or someone else: A man was walking with Ṭāwūs when he heard a raven croak and said, “Good!” Ṭāwūs replied, “What good or evil could this bird bring? Do not accompany me”—or “Do not travel with me.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatāda, who said: ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn was cauterized. records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Abū Umāma ibn Sahl ibn Ḥunayf: The Messenger of God ﷺ visited Asʿad ibn Zurāra when he was afflicted by an illness called *al-shawka*. He cauterized him at Ḥawrān on his neck, but he died. The Prophet ﷺ said, “What a wretched death, in the eyes of the Jews! They will say, 'His companion treated him, but it was of no use.'” [The wording and proper noun Ḥawrān are preserved as supplied.]

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī: “Ibn ʿUmar was cauterized because of facial paralysis, and he cauterized his son Wāqid.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Jābir, from al-Shaʿbī, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said, “Warm compresses are dearer to me than cauterization; medicine administered into the side of the mouth is dearer to me than blowing [on the patient]; medicine placed in the nose is dearer to me than leeches; and a good portent is dearer to me than an evil omen.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, from al-Ḥasan, from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: One night we spent a long time talking with the Messenger of God ﷺ. The next morning, he said, “Last night the prophets were shown to me with their communities. A prophet passed with three followers; another with a band; another with a few people; and another with no one at all. Then Moses passed me with a great crowd of the Children of Israel. They pleased me, so I asked, 'Who are these?' I was told, 'That is your brother Moses, with the Children of Israel.' I asked, 'Where is my community?' I was told, 'Look to your right.' I looked, and the hills were covered with the faces of people. Then I was told, 'Look to your left.' I looked, and the horizon was filled with the faces of people. I was asked, 'Are you satisfied?' I said, 'I am satisfied, my Lord, I am satisfied.' I was told, 'With these are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without reckoning.'” The Prophet ﷺ said, “May my father and mother be your ransom! If you can be among those seventy thousand, then do so. If you fall short, be among the people on the hills, and if you fall short again, be among the people of the horizon, for I saw many others mixed in among them.” ʿUkāsha ibn Miḥṣan al-Asadī stood and said, “Pray to God for me, Messenger of God, that He make me one of the seventy thousand.” He prayed for him. Another man stood and made the same request. The Prophet ﷺ said, “ʿUkāsha has preceded you to it.” We then discussed among ourselves who those seventy thousand might be, and said, “Perhaps they are people born into Islam who never associated anything with God until they died.” This reached the Prophet ﷺ, who said, “They are those who do not cauterize themselves, do not ask others to perform healing incantations for them, do not take omens, and rely on their Lord.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٥١٩ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ، عَنْ عِمْرَانَ بْنِ الْحُصَيْنِ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، قَالَ: أَكْثَرْنَا الْحَدِيثَ عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ذَاتَ لَيْلَةٍ، ثُمَّ غَدَوْنَا، فَقَالَ:   «§عُرِضَتْ عَلَيَّ الْأَنْبِيَاءُ اللَّيْلَةَ بِأُمَمِهَا، فَجَعَلَ النَّبِيُّ يَمُرُّ، وَمَعَهُ الثَّلَاثَةُ، وَالنَّبِيُّ وَمَعَهُ الْعِصَابَةُ، وَالنَّبِيُّ وَمَعَهُ النَّفَرُ، وَالنَّبِيُّ وَلَيْسَ مَعَهُ أَحَدٌ، حَتَّى مَرَّ عَلَيَّ مُوسَى، وَمَعَهُ كَبْكَبَةٌ مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ، فَأَعْجَبُونِي، فَقُلْتُ: مَنْ هَؤُلَاءِ؟ فَقِيلَ: هَذَا أَخُوكَ مُوسَى، وَمَعَهُ بَنُو إِسْرَائِيلَ، قَالَ: قُلْتُ: فَأَيْنَ أُمَّتِي؟ قَالَ: فَقِيلَ: انْظُرْ عَنْ يَمِينِكَ، فَنَظَرْتُ فَإِذَا الظِّرَابُ قَدْ سُدَّ بِوُجُوهِ الرِّجَالِ، ثُمَّ قِيلَ لِي: انْظُرْ عَنْ يَسَارِكَ، فَنَظَرْتُ فَإِذَا الْأُفُقُ قَدْ سُدَّ بِوُجُوهِ الرِّجَالِ، فَقِيلَ لِي: أَرَضِيتَ؟ فَقُلْتُ: رَضِيتُ يَا رَبِّ رَضِيتُ يَا رَبِّ قَالَ: فَقِيلَ لِي: مَعَ هَؤُلَاءِ سَبْعُونَ أَلْفًا يَدْخُلُونَ الْجَنَّةَ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ»   قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «فِدَاكُمْ أَبِي وَأُمِّي إِنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ أَنْ تَكُونُوا مِنَ السَّبْعِينَ أَلْفًا فَافْعَلُوا، فَإِنْ قَصَّرْتُمْ فَكُونُوا مِنْ أَهْلِ الظِّرَابِ، فَإِنْ قَصَّرْتُمْ فَكُونُوا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْأُفْقِ، فَإِنِّي رَأَيْتُ ثَمَّ نَاسًا يَتَهَاوَشُونَ»   قَالَ: فَقَامَ عُكَّاشَةُ بْنُ مِحْصَنٍ الْأَسَدِيُّ فَقَالَ: ادْعُ اللَّهَ لِي يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، أَنْ يَجْعَلَنِي مِنَ السَّبْعِينَ، قال: فَدَعَا لَهُ، قَالَ: فَقَامَ رَجُلٌ آخَرُ، فَقَالَ: ادْعُ اللَّهَ لِي يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَنْ يَجْعَلَنِي مِنْهُمْ، فَقَالَ:   «قَدْ - [٤٠٩] - سَبَقَكَ بِهَا عُكَّاشَةُ»   قَالَ: ثُمَّ تَحَدَّثْنَا، فَقُلْنَا: مَنْ تَرَوْنَ هَؤُلَاءِ السَّبْعِينَ الْأَلْفِ، قَوْمٌ وُلِدُوا فِي الْإِسْلَامِ لَمْ يُشْرِكُوا بِاللَّهِ شَيْئًا حَتَّى مَاتُوا، فَبَلَغَ ذَلِكَ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، فَقَالَ:   «هُمُ الَّذِينَ لَا يَكْتَوُونَ، وَلَا يَسْتَرْقُونَ، وَلَا يَتَطَيَّرُونَ، وَعَلَى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ»

رَضِيتُ يَا رَبِّ قَالَ: فَقِيلَ لِي: مَعَ هَؤُلَاءِ سَبْعُونَ أَلْفًا يَدْخُلُونَ الْجَنَّةَ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ»   قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «فِدَاكُمْ أَبِي وَأُمِّي إِنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ أَنْ تَكُونُوا مِنَ السَّبْعِينَ أَلْفًا فَافْعَلُوا، فَإِنْ قَصَّرْتُمْ فَكُونُوا مِنْ أَهْلِ الظِّرَابِ، فَإِنْ قَصَّرْتُمْ فَكُونُوا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْأُفْقِ، فَإِنِّي رَأَيْتُ ثَمَّ records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, from al-Ḥasan, from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: One night we spent a long time talking with the Messenger of God ﷺ. The next morning, he said, “Last night the prophets were shown to me with their communities. A prophet passed with three followers; another with a band; another with a few people; and another with no one at all. Then Moses passed me with a great crowd of the Children of Israel. They pleased me, so I asked, 'Who are these?' I was told, 'That is your brother Moses, with the Children of Israel.' I asked, 'Where is my community?' I was told, 'Look to your right.' I looked, and the hills were covered with the faces of people. Then I was told, 'Look to your left.' I looked, and the horizon was filled with the faces of people. I was asked, 'Are you satisfied?' I said, 'I am satisfied, my Lord, I am satisfied.' I was told, 'With these are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without reckoning.'” The Prophet ﷺ said, “May my father and mother be your ransom! If you can be among those seventy thousand, then do so. If you fall short, be among the people on the hills, and if you fall short again, be among the people of the horizon, for I saw many others mixed in among them.” ʿUkāsha ibn Miḥṣan al-Asadī stood and said, “Pray to God for me, Messenger of God, that He make me one of the seventy thousand.” He prayed for him. Another man stood and made the same request. records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Zayd ibn Sallām, from ʿAbdallāh ibn Zayd al-Azraq, from ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir al-Juhanī, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “There are two kinds of protective jealousy: one God loves and the other He hates. There are also two kinds of pride or display: one God loves and the other He hates. God loves jealousy when there are grounds for suspicion, but hates jealousy when there are no grounds for it. He loves the pride [or uplifting sense of dignity] a man shows when giving charity, but hates the pride born of arrogance.” [An unnumbered statement follows.]
records.text_ar: ١٩٥٢٢ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ أَبِي كَثِيرٍ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ سَلَّامٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ زَيْدٍ الْأَزْرَقِ، عَنْ عُقْبَةَ بْنِ عَامِرٍ الْجُهَنِيِّ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ:   «§غَيْرَتَانِ: إِحْدَاهُمَا أَحَبُّ إِلَى اللَّهِ، وَالْأُخْرَى يُبْغِضُهَا، وَمَخِيلَتَانِ: إِحْدَاهُمَا يُحِبُّهَا اللَّهُ، وَالْأُخْرَى يُبْغِضُهَا اللَّهُ، - [٤١٠] - الْغَيْرَةُ فِي الرِّيبَةِ يُحِبُّهَا اللَّهُ، وَالْغَيْرَةُ فِي غَيْرِ الرِّيبَةِ يُبْغِضُهَا اللَّهُ، وَالْمَخِيلَةُ إِذَا تَصَدَّقَ الرَّجُلُ يُحِبُّهَا اللَّهُ، وَالْمَخِيلَةُ فِي الْكِبْرِ يُبْغِضُهَا اللَّهُ»

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: وَقَالَ:   «§ثَلَاثٌ تُسْتَجَابُ دَعْوَتُهُمْ: الْوَالِدُ، وَالْمُسَافِرُ، وَالْمَظْلُومُ»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: He also said: “Three people have their prayers answered: a parent, a traveler, and a person who has been wronged.”

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: وَقَالَ:   «إِنَّ §اللَّهَ يُدْخِلُ بِالسَّهْمِ الْوَاحِدِ الْجَنَّةَ ثَلَاثَةً: صَانِعَهُ، وَالْمُمِدَّ بِهِ، وَالرَّامِيَ بِهِ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: And he said: “By means of a single arrow, God brings three people into Paradise: the one who makes it, the one who supplies it, and the one who shoots it in God’s cause.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, that the Prophet ﷺ delivered a sermon and said, “Community of Muḥammad, by God, no one has greater protective jealousy than God when He sees His male servant committing adultery with His female servant. If you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from someone who heard al-Ḥasan say: A man passed another man seated with a group of women who had placed a cushion for him. They were conversing with him, while he spoke to them in a soft, alluring manner. The passerby struck him with a staff until he wounded his head. The injured man brought him before ʿUmar and said, “Commander of the Faithful, this man passed me when I was talking to some women of my household, and struck me with a staff until he gashed my head.” ʿUmar asked the assailant, “Why did you strike him?” He replied, “Commander of the Faithful, I passed him and found him with women I did not recognize; they were talking with him, and he was speaking alluringly to them. I could not restrain myself.” ʿUmar said, “As for you, the man who struck him, may God have mercy upon you; and as for you, the man struck, one of God's eyes has fallen upon you.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Aʿmash, from Shaqīq, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said, “No one loves praise more than God, and for that reason He has praised Himself. No one has greater protective jealousy than God, and for that reason He forbade indecencies.”

records.display_matn_ar: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، مَا سَكَنَّا دَارَنَا، وَنَحْنُ كَثِيرٌ فَهَلَكْنَا، وَحَسُنَ ذَاتُ بَيْنِنَا، فَسَاءَتْ أَخْلَاقُنَا، وَكَثِيرَةٌ أَمْوَالُنَا فَافْتَقَرْنَا، قَالَ:   «§أَفَلَا تَنْتَقِلُونَ عَنْهَا ذَمِيمَةً؟»   ، قَالَتْ: فَكَيْفَ نَصْنَعُ بِهَا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ؟ قَالَ:   «تَبِيعُونَهَا أَوْ تَهَبُونَهَا»
records.display_isnad_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAbdallāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal, from ʿAbdallāh ibn Shaddād ibn al-Hād: A woman of the Ansar said, “
records.display_matn_en: Messenger of God, we moved into our house while we were numerous, then deaths reduced our numbers. Our relations were good, then our dispositions turned sour. We had abundant wealth, then became poor.” He said, “Why do you not leave it behind as an ill-omened place?” She asked, “What should we do with it, Messenger of God?” He replied, “Sell it or give it away.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Aʿmash, that Ibn Masʿūd said, “If ill fortune resides anywhere, it is between the two jaws”—meaning the tongue—“and nothing is more in need of long imprisonment than the tongue.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān used to send for Umm al-Dardāʾ. She would spend the night among his wives, and he would ask her about various matters. One night he rose and called for his female servant, who was slow to come, so he cursed her. Umm al-Dardāʾ said, “Do not curse her! Abū al-Dardāʾ told me that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say, 'Those who habitually curse others will neither intercede nor bear witness on the Day of Resurrection.'”
records.text_ar: ١٩٥٣٠ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، قَالَ: كَانَ عَبْدُ الْمَلِكِ بْنُ مَرْوَانَ يُرْسِلُ إِلَى أُمِّ الدَّرْدَاءِ، فَتَبِيتُ عِنْدَ نِسَائِهِ، وَيُسَائِلُهَا عَنِ الشَّيْءِ، قَالَ: فَقَامَ لَيْلَةً فَدَعَا خَادِمَهُ فَأَبْطَأَتْ عَلَيْهِ، فَلَعَنَهَا فَقَالَتْ: لَا تَلْعَنْ، فَإِنَّ أَبَا الدَّرْدَاءِ حَدَّثَنِي أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَقُولُ:   «إِنَّ §اللَّعَّانِينَ لَا يَكُونُونَ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ شُفَعَاءَ وَلَا شُهَدَاءَ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl, who raised the report [to the Prophet ﷺ]: “Do not curse one another with God's curse, God's wrath, or [consignment to] Hell.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilāba, from Abū al-Muhallab, from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, who said: A woman cursed a she-camel she owned. The Prophet ﷺ said, “She has been cursed, so leave her alone.” I saw the grayish camel afterward moving among the camps, with no one interfering with her.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Ẓabyān, that Ḥudhayfa said, “Whenever people exchange curses among themselves, the [divine] decree against them becomes due.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Masrūq, who said: “Whoever is compelled by necessity to eat carrion, blood, or pork, but refuses to eat or drink until he dies, will enter the Fire.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, who said: “He may eat enough carrion to keep himself alive, but must not gorge himself on it.” Maʿmar said: “There is no dispensation concerning wine.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٥٣٧ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، قَالَ:   «§يَأْكُلُ مِنَ الْمَيْتَةِ مَا يُبَلِّغُهُ، وَلَا يَتَضَلَّعُ مِنْهَا»   . قَالَ مَعْمَرٌ:   «لَيْسَ فِي الْخَمْرِ رُخْصَةٌ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, that the Prophet ﷺ said to ʿĀʾisha, “When God wishes good for a people, He grants them gentleness in their way of life; but when He wishes them harm—or something other than good—He imposes clumsiness and harshness in their living.” [The alternative wording 'or something other than that' occurs in the source.]

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from an unnamed man, from al-Ḥasan, that Luqmān said to his son, “My son, do not eat until you are full and then eat more. It would be better for you to throw that food to a dog. My son, do not be weaker than this rooster, which calls out before dawn while you remain asleep in your bed.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٥٣٩ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ رَجُلٍ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ،   «§أَنَّ لُقْمَانَ، قَالَ لِابْنِهِ: يَا بُنَيَّ، لَا تَأْكُلْ شِبَعًا فَوْقَ شِبَعٍ، فَإِنَّكَ إِنْ تَنْبِذْهُ إِلَى الْكَلْبِ خَيْرٌ لَكَ، وَيَا بُنَيَّ لَا تَكُونَنَّ أَعْجَزَ مِنْ هَذَا الدِّيكِ الَّذِي يُصَوِّتُ بِالْأَسْحَارِ وَأَنْتَ نَائِمٌ عَلَى فِرَاشِكَ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, who said: “A whole month might pass without our lighting a fire. We had nothing but water and dates. May God reward some women of the Ansar with good: they would occasionally send us a little milk.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٥٤٠ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، قَالَتْ:   «§لَقَدْ كَانَ يَأْتِي عَلَيْنَا الشَّهْرُ مَا نُوقِدُ فِيهِ نَارًا، وَمَا هُوَ إِلَّا الْمَاءُ وَالتَّمْرُ، غَيْرَ أَنْ جَزَى اللَّهُ نِسَاءً مِنَ الْأَنْصَارِ خَيْرًا، كُنَّ رُبَّمَا أَهْدَيْنَ لَنَا الشَّيْءَ مِنَ اللَّبَنِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from an unnamed man, from al-Ḥasan, that the Prophet ﷺ said, “When *tharīd* [bread soaked in broth] is set before you, eat from its sides, for blessing descends from its top.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb and others, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “If one of you drops a morsel of food, let him pick it up and remove anything harmful from it; he should not leave it for Satan.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Majesty is God's cloak; whoever contends with God over His cloak, He will crush him.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from ʿIkrima ibn Khālid, who said: A son of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb entered upon him, having combed his hair and put on fine clothing. ʿUmar struck him with his whip until he made him cry. Ḥafṣa said, “He had done nothing indecent. Why did you strike him?” He replied: “I saw that he was pleased with himself, and I wanted to diminish his conceit in his own eyes.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, who said: An angel came to the Prophet ﷺ who had never come to him before and never came again afterward. He said, “Your Lord gives you the choice of being a prophet who is a king or a prophet who is a servant.” The Prophet ﷺ looked toward Gabriel as though seeking his counsel. Gabriel gestured to him to be humble. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Rather, a prophet who is a servant.” After that, the Prophet ﷺ was never seen reclining.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Ḥasan, that the Prophet ﷺ used to say: “When one of you eats, he should not wipe his fingers until he has licked them, for he does not know in which portion of his food the blessing lies.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٥٥٥ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ كَانَ يَقُولُ:   «§إِذَا أَكَلَ أَحَدُكُمْ فَلَا يَمْسَحْ أَصَابِعَهُ حَتَّى يَلْعَقَهَا، فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَدْرِي فِي أَيِّ طَعَامِهِ كَانَتِ الْبَرَكَةُ»

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: قَالَ: وَكَانَ الْحَسَنُ يَقُولُ:   «إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ كَانَ §لَا يُغْلِقُ دُونَهُ الْأَبْوَابَ، وَلَا يَقُومُ دُونَهُ الْحَجَبَةُ، وَلَا يُغْدَى عَلَيْهِ بِالْجِفَانِ، وَلَا يُرَاحُ عَلَيْهِ بِهَا»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: He said: Al-Ḥasan used to say: “The Messenger of God ﷺ did not have doors closed against people, nor did guards stand in front of him, nor were large dishes carried to him morning and evening.”

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: «كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ §بَارِزًا مَنْ أَرَادَ أَنْ يَلْقَى رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ لَقِيَهُ، كَانَ يَجْلِسُ بِالْأَرْضِ، وَيُوضَعُ طَعَامُهُ بِالْأَرْضِ، وَيَلْبَسُ الْغَلِيظَ، وَيَرْكَبُ الْحِمَارَ، وَيُرْدِفُ خَلْفَهُ، وَيَلْعَقُ وَاللَّهِ يَدَهُ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: “The Messenger of God ﷺ was accessible: whoever wished to meet him could do so. He sat on the ground, his food was placed on the ground, he wore coarse clothing, rode a donkey, took a passenger behind him, and—by God—licked his hand after eating.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, that when the Prophet ﷺ ate, he would lick three of his fingers—the thumb and the two next to it—putting them into his mouth one at a time.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Food enough for one suffices for two; food enough for two suffices for four; and food enough for four suffices for eight.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: “The devil accompanying a believer meets the devil accompanying an unbeliever. The believer's devil is pale, dusty, and emaciated. The unbeliever's devil says to him, ‘What is wrong with you? Woe to you! You look ruined.’ He replies, ‘By God, I can get nothing from him. When he eats, he mentions God's name; when he drinks, he mentions God's name; when he goes to sleep, he mentions God's name; and when he enters his house, he mentions God's name.’ The other says, ‘But I eat his food, drink his drink, and sleep in his bed.’ Thus the first is pale and the other is well-nourished.” [The closing adjectives in the source are somewhat awkward.]
records.text_ar: ١٩٥٦٠ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنْ أَبِي الْأَحْوَصِ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، قَالَ:   «إِنَّ §شَيْطَانَ الْمُؤْمِنِ يَلْقَى شَيْطَانَ الْكَافِرِ، فَيَرَى شَيْطَانَ الْمُؤْمِنِ شَاحِبًا، أَغْبَرَ مَهْزُولًا، فَيَقُولُ لَهُ شَيْطَانُ الْكَافِرِ: مَا لَكَ، وَيْحَكَ، قَدْ هَلَكْتَ، فَيَقُولُ شَيْطَانُ الْمُؤْمِنِ: لَا وَاللَّهِ مَا أَصِلُ مَعَهُ إِلَى شَيْءٍ، إِذَا طَعِمَ ذَكَرَ اسْمَ اللَّهِ، وَإِذَا شَرِبَ ذَكَرَ اسْمَ اللَّهِ، وَإِذَا نَامَ ذَكَرَ اسْمَ اللَّهِ، وَإِذَا دَخَلَ بَيْتَهُ ذَكَرَ اسْمَ اللَّهِ، فَيَقُولُ الْآخَرُ: لَكِنِّي آكُلُ مِنْ طَعَامِهِ، وَأَشْرَبُ مِنْ شَرَابِهِ، وَأَنَامُ عَلَى فِرَاشِهِ، فَهَذَا شَاحٍبٌ، وَهَذَا مَهْزُولٌ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ḥarām ibn ʿUthmān, from Ibn Jābir, from Jābir, who said that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “When you reach the door of your dwelling, mention God and your attendant [devil] will turn back. When you enter your house, mention God and its occupant [devil] will leave. When your food is set before you, mention God so that they will not share your food.” He added: “I think he also said, ‘When one of you lies down, let him mention God, so that they will not sleep in your beds.’”
records.text_ar: ١٩٥٦١ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ حَرَامِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ، عَنِ ابْنِ جَابِرٍ، عَنْ جَابِرٍ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§إِذَا جِئْتَ بَابَ حُجْرَتِكَ فَاذْكُرِ اللَّهَ، يَرْجِعْ قَرِينُكَ، وَإِذَا دَخَلْتَ بَيْتَكَ فَاذْكُرِ اللَّهَ، يَخْرُجْ سَاكِنُهُ، وَإِذَا قُرِّبَ طَعَامُكَ فَاذْكُرِ اللَّهَ، لَا يُشَارِكُوكُمْ فِي طَعَامِكُمْ»   ، قَالَ: وَحَسِبْتُهُ قَالَ:   «وَإِذَا اضْطَجَعَ أَحَدُكُمْ فَلْيَذْكُرِ اللَّهَ لَا يَنَامُوا عَلَى فُرُشِكُمْ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, who said: “When a person goes out in the morning, Satan follows him. If he enters his home and offers the greeting of peace, Satan sleeps at the door. When food is brought and the person mentions God, Satan says, ‘No midday rest and no supper.’ But if he does not mention God upon entering or over his food, Satan says, ‘A midday rest and lunch!’ The same applies to supper.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Aʿmash, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from Ḥudhayfa, who said: “When we were invited to a meal with the Prophet ﷺ, we did not put our hands into the food until he had done so. Once a large dish was brought and he withheld his hand, so we withheld ours. Then a Bedouin came rushing in as though driven, and put his hand into the dish. The Prophet ﷺ seized his hand and made him sit. Then a young girl came rushing toward it, and the Prophet ﷺ seized her as well. He then said: ‘Satan makes a people's food lawful for himself if they do not mention God's name over it. When Satan saw us withholding our hands, he brought this man and this girl to make our food lawful for himself through them. By Him besides whom there is no god, his hand was in my hand along with both of their hands.’”

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Aʿmash, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from Ḥudhayfa, who said: “When we were invited to a meal with the Prophet ﷺ, we did not put our hands into the food until he had done so. Once a large dish was brought and he withheld his hand, so we withheld ours. Then a Bedouin came rushing in as though driven, and put his hand into the dish. The Prophet ﷺ seized his hand and made him sit. Then a young girl came rushing toward it, and the Prophet ﷺ seized her as well. He then said: ‘Satan makes a people's food lawful for himself if they do not mention God's name over it. When Satan saw us withholding our hands, he brought this man and this girl to make our food lawful for himself through them. By Him besides whom there is no god, his hand was in my hand along with both of their hands.’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī and Muḥammad ibn Ziyād, from Abū Hurayra, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “When your servant brings you your food, having endured its heat, trouble, smoke, and preparation, let him sit and eat with you. If he refuses, then hand him a mouthful of it.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٥٦٥ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، وَمُحَمَّدِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ:   «§إِذَا أَتَى أَحَدَكُمُ الْخَادِمُ بِطَعَامِهِ، قَدْ وَلِيَ حَرَّهُ وَمَشَقَّتَهُ، وَدُخَانَهُ وَمَؤُونَتَهُ، فَلْيُجْلِسْهُ مَعَهُ، فَإِنْ أَبَى فَلْيُنَاوِلْهُ أُكْلَةً فِي يَدِهِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, who said: “He—that is, the Messenger of God ﷺ—forbade two ways of eating: taking two fruits together [when sharing food], and eating while standing.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٥٦٦ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، قَالَ:   «§نَهَى - يَعْنِي - رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عَنْ أَكْلَتَيْنِ: أَنْ يَقْرِنَ بَيْنَ ثَمْرَتَيْنِ، وَالْأُخْرَى أَنْ يَأْكُلَ وَهُوَ قَائِمٌ»
records.section_title_en: Eating Two Fruits Together, Standing, or Walking
records.section_title_ar: بَابُ: الرَّجُلُ يَقْرِنُ، أَوْ يَأْكُلُ وَهُوَ قَائِمٌ، أَوْ مَاشٍ

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: قَالَ: أَبُو بَكْرٍ: وَسَأَلْتُ مَعْمَرًا عَنِ §الرَّجُلِ يَأْكُلُ وَهُوَ مَاشٍ، فَقَالَ: قَدْ   «كَانَ الْحَسَنُ يُرَخِّصُ فِيهِ لِلْمُسَافِرِ»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: Abū Bakr said: “I asked Maʿmar about a man eating while walking. He replied: ‘Al-Ḥasan used to allow it for a traveler.’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, who said: “Three kinds of blowing are disliked: blowing into food, blowing into drink, and blowing while prostrating.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ibn al-Munkadir, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “A household with vinegar is not destitute of condiments.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٥٧٠ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ الْمُنْكَدِرِ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ:   «§لَيْسَ بَيْتٌ مُفْقَرٌ مِنْ أُدْمٍ فِيهِ خَلٌّ»

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Abū Hurayra, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ prayed for blessing in the pre-dawn meal and in *tharīd* [bread soaked in broth].”
records.text_ar: ١٩٥٧١ - أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَر، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي لَيْلَى، عَنْ عَطَاءٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ:   «§دَعَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ بِالْبَرَكَةِ فِي السَّحُورِ وَالثَّرِيدِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from a man of Ghifār who heard Saʿīd al-Maqburī narrating from Abū Hurayra, who said that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “One who eats and gives thanks is like one who fasts and is patient.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Praise is the foundation of gratitude. A servant who does not praise God has not thanked Him.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda and al-Ḥasan, who both said: “Adam was shown his descendants and saw that some were favored over others. He said, ‘My Lord, why did You not make them equal?’ God replied, ‘I love to be thanked.’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, who said: When Salmān finished eating, he would say, “Praise belongs to God, who has spared us the labor [of providing it] and given us abundant sustenance.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar—this attribution is repeated in the Arabic text—from Ibn ʿAjlān, that after eating the Prophet ﷺ would say: “Praise belongs to God, who has provided for us and made us Muslims. records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ was in our house. Milk was drawn from a domestic animal for him and mixed with water from the house, and it was passed to the Prophet ﷺ. He drank. records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ was asked, “Which drink is most pleasant?” He replied: “One that is sweet and cold.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, from ʿIkrima, who said: “Do not drink in a single breath; that is Satan's way of drinking.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Abū Hurayra, who said that the Prophet ﷺ said: “If the person who drinks while standing knew what was in his stomach, he would make himself vomit.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, who said: I asked Anas about drinking while standing, and he disliked it. I asked, “What about eating?” He replied: “That is even worse.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٥٩٠ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَنَسًا §عَنِ الشُّرْبِ، قَائِمًا فَكَرِهَهُ، قُلْتُ: فَالْأَكْلُ؟ قَالَ:   «هُوَ أَشَدُّ مِنْهُ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, that Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ and ʿĀʾisha saw no objection to drinking while standing.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Jaʿfar al-Jazarī, from Yazīd ibn al-Aṣamm, from Abū Hurayra, who disliked a man drinking from the chipped edge of a cup or using such a cup for ablution.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Abī Ḥusayn, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “When one of you drinks, let him sip slowly, not gulp it down, for liver trouble comes from gulping.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Layth, from an unnamed man, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ passed a pool and said: “Drink, but do not put your mouths straight into the water. Let each of you wash his hands and then drink. What vessel is purer and cleaner than one's own washed hands?”
records.text_ar: ١٩٥٩٦ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ لَيْثٍ، عَنْ رَجُلٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ، قَالَ: مَرَّ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ بِغَدِيرٍ، فَقَالَ:   «§اشْرَبُوا وَلَا تَكْرَعُوا، لِيَغْسِلْ أَحَدُكُمْ يَدَيْهِ، ثُمَّ لِيَشْرَبْ، وَأَيُّ إِنَاءٍ أَنْقَى وأنْظَفُ مِنْ يَدَيْهِ إِذَا غَسَلَهَما»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from ʿIkrima, from Abū Hurayra, who was asked about drinking from the mouth of a waterskin and said it was forbidden. A man asked ʿIkrima, “What about drinking through a spout attached to the skin?” He replied: “There is no harm in that; one sucks from it as from a breast.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٥٩٧ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ عِكْرِمَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، سُئِلَ §عَنِ الشُّرْبِ، مِنْ فِي السِّقَاءِ، قَالَ: يُنْهَى عَنْهُ، قَالَ: فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ لِعِكْرِمَةَ: فَمِنَ الرَّصَاصَةِ يُجْعَلُ فِي السِّقَاءِ، قَالَ:   «لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ، إِنَّمَا يُمَصُّ مِثْلَ الثَّدْيِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ forbade drinking directly from the mouth of a waterskin.” Hishām added: “That makes it smell foul.”
