records.display_matn_en: “The Messenger of God ﷺ forbade drinking directly from the mouth of a waterskin.” Hishām added: “That makes it smell foul.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, who said: Maḥmūd ibn Labīd told me that he remembered the Messenger of God ﷺ, including an occasion when the Messenger of God ﷺ took a mouthful of water and spat it into a bucket in their home.
records.text_ar: ١٩٦٠٠ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنِي مَحْمُودُ بْنُ لَبِيدٍ، أَنَّهُ عَقَلَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ،   «§وَعَقَلَ مَجَّةً مَجَّهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ مِنْ دَلْوٍ كَانَ فِي دَارِهِمْ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn, who said: Whenever ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb dispatched governors, he wrote to their people: “I have sent you so-and-so and instructed him to do such-and-such; listen to him and obey.” But when he sent Ḥudhayfa to al-Madāʾin, he wrote: “I have sent so-and-so to you; obey him.” The people said, “This must be an important man,” and rode out to meet him. They encountered a man riding a mule fitted with a pack-saddle, sitting sideways with both legs on one side. Not recognizing him, they passed him and asked others, “Where is the governor?” They replied, “He is the man you passed.” They galloped after him and caught up with him as he was eating, holding a loaf in one hand and a meat-covered bone in the other. They greeted him. He looked at one of their leading men and offered him the loaf and bone. When Ḥudhayfa was distracted, the man threw it away or gave it to his servant.
records.text_ar: ١٩٦٠١ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنِ ابْنِ سِيرِينَ، قَالَ: كَانَ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ إِذَا بَعَثَ أُمَرَاءَ كَتَبَ إِلَيْهِمْ:   «§إِنِّي بَعَثْتُ - [٤٣٠] - إِلَيْكُمْ فُلَانًا فَأَمَرْتُهُ بِكَذَا وَكَذَا، فَاسْمَعُوا لَهُ وَأَطِيعُوا»   فَلَمَّا بَعَثَ حُذَيْفَةَ إِلَى الْمَدَائِنِ كَتَبَ إِلَيْهِمْ:   «إِنِّي بَعَثْتُ إِلَيْكُمْ فُلَانًا فَأَطِيعُوهُ»   . فَقَالُوا: هَذَا رَجُلٌ لَهُ شَأْنٌ، فَرَكِبُوا إِلَيْهِ لِيَتَلَقَّوْهُ، فَلَقَوْهُ عَلَى بَغْلٍ تَحْتَهُ إِكَافٌ، وَهُوَ مُعْتَرِضٌ عَلَيْهِ، رِجْلَاهُ مِنْ جَانِبٍ وَاحِدٍ، فَلَمْ يَعْرِفُوهُ، وَأَجَازُوهُ فَلَقِيَهُمُ النَّاسُ فَقَالُوا: أَيْنَ الْأَمِيرُ؟ قَالُوا: هُوَ الَّذِي لَقِيتُمْ. قَالُوا: فَجَعَلُوا يَرْكُضُونَ فِي أَثَرِهِ، وأدْرَكُوهُ وَفِي يَدِهِ رَغِيفٌ، وَفِي يَدِهِ الْأُخْرَى عِرْقٌ، وَهُوَ يَأْكُلُ فَسَلَّمُوا عَلَيْهِ، قَالَ: فَنَظَرَ إِلَى عَظِيمٍ مِنْهُمْ، فَنَاوَلَهُ الْعِرْقَ وَالرَّغِيفَ، قَالَ: فَلَمَّا غَفَلَ حُذَيْفَةُ أَلْقَاهُ، أَوْ أَعْطَاهُ خَادِمَهُ

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn, who said: Whenever ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb dispatched governors, he wrote to their people: “I have sent you so-and-so and instructed him to do such-and-such; listen to him and obey.” But when he sent Ḥudhayfa to al-Madāʾin, he wrote: “I have sent so-and-so to you; obey him.” The people said, “This must be an important man,” and rode out to meet him. They encountered a man riding a mule fitted with a pack-saddle, sitting sideways with both legs on one side. Not recognizing him, they passed him and asked others, “Where is the governor?” They replied, “He is the man you passed.” They galloped after him and caught up with him as he was eating, holding a loaf in one hand and a meat-covered bone in the other. They greeted him. He looked at one of their leading men and offered him the loaf and bone. When Ḥudhayfa was distracted, the man threw it away or gave it to his servant.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from an unnamed man, from al-Ḥasan, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “I was commanded to use the tooth-stick so insistently that I feared it would wear away my teeth [or gums].” The Messenger of God ﷺ would clean his teeth when he awoke at night, before performing ablution.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ was cleaning his teeth with a tooth-stick while two men were with him. He received the instruction, ‘Give preference to the elder,’ meaning that he should hand it to the older of them.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from an unnamed man, from Abū Hurayra, who said: “Had the Messenger of God ﷺ not wished to impose hardship on his community, he would have commanded them to use the tooth-stick at every prayer.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb disliked a man traveling alone and said: “What if he dies? Whom could I ask about him?”
records.text_ar: ١٩٦٠٦ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، قَالَ: §كَرِهَ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ أَنْ يُسَافِرَ الرَّجُلُ، وَحْدَهُ، وَقَالَ:   «أَرَأَيْتَ إِنْ مَاتَ مَنْ أَسْأَلُ عَنْهُ؟»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, who said: Someone who heard al-Ḥasan told me that the Messenger of God ﷺ saw a man on a journey and said, “A devil.” Then he saw two men and said, “Two devils.” Then he saw three men, was silent, and said, “A traveling party.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٦٠٨ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنِي مَنْ، سَمِعَ الْحَسَنَ، يَقُولُ: §رَأَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ رَجُلًا فِي سَفَرٍ، فَقَالَ:   «شَيْطَانٌ»   ثُمَّ رَأَى رَجُلَيْنِ، فَقَالَ:   «شَيْطَانَانِ»   ، ثُمَّ رَأَى ثَلَاثَةً، فَصَمَتَ، وَقَالَ:   «سَفَرٌ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, that the Prophet ﷺ ordered dogs to be killed in Medina. He was told about a woman who had a dog on the outskirts of Medina; he sent for the dog, and it was killed.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Abū Salama, from Abū Hurayra, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever keeps a dog, except one for livestock, hunting, or crops, has one qīrāṭ deducted from his reward every day.” Al-Zuhrī said: When Ibn ʿUmar was told of Abū Hurayra's wording, he said: “May God have mercy on Abū Hurayra; he owned cultivated land.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Abū Isḥāq, who said: I heard Ibn Hubayra say: A group of Muḥammad's companions ﷺ went to visit a sick man of Khuzāʿa. When his door was opened, dogs sprang toward their faces. Some said to others, “How much of so-and-so's good deeds will these dogs leave him? Each dog deducts a qīrāṭ every day.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, who said: One morning the Messenger of God ﷺ was gloomy in Maymūna's house. She said, “Messenger of God, we notice something unusual in your appearance today.” He said: “Gabriel promised to come to me, and by God he has never broken a promise to me.” Then he remembered that they had a puppy beneath one of their pieces of furniture. He ordered it taken out and its place sprinkled with water. Gabriel came, and the Prophet ﷺ asked him, “Did you not promise to come to me?” Gabriel replied: “There was a puppy in the house, and we do not enter a house containing a dog.” Maʿmar added: “I think he also said that the Prophet ﷺ then ordered the killing of dogs.”

records.display_matn_en: One morning the Messenger of God ﷺ was gloomy in Maymūna's house. She said, “Messenger of God, we notice something unusual in your appearance today.” He said: “Gabriel promised to come to me, and by God he has never broken a promise to me.” Then he remembered that they had a puppy beneath one of their pieces of furniture. He ordered it taken out and its place sprinkled with water. Gabriel came, and the Prophet ﷺ asked him, “Did you not promise to come to me?” Gabriel replied: “There was a puppy in the house, and we do not enter a house containing a dog.” Maʿmar added: “I think he also said that the Prophet ﷺ then ordered the killing of dogs.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Sālim, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “Kill snakes, and kill the snake with two stripes and the short-tailed snake, for these two cause miscarriages and destroy eyesight.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٦١٦ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ سَالِمٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَقُولُ:   «§اقْتُلُوا الْحَيَّاتِ، وَاقْتُلُوا ذَا الطُّفْيَتَيْنِ، وَالْأَبْتَرَ، فَإِنَّهُمَا يُسْقِطَانِ الْحَبَلَ، وَيَطْمِسَانِ الْبَصَرَ»

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: قَالَ ابْنُ عُمَرَ: فَرَآنِي أَبُو لُبَابَةَ، أَوْ زَيْدُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ، وَأَنَا أُطَارِدُ حَيَّةً لِأَقْتُلَهَا فَنَهَانِي، فَقُلْتُ: إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَدْ أَمَرَ بِقَتْلِهِنَّ، قَالَ: إِنَّهُ قَدْ   «§نَهَى بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ عَنْ قَتْلِ ذَوَاتِ الْبُيُوتِ»   ، قَالَ الزُّهْرِيُّ:   «وَهُنَّ الْعَوَامِرُ»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: Ibn ʿUmar said: Abū Lubāba—or Zayd ibn al-Khaṭṭāb—saw me pursuing a snake to kill it and forbade me. I said, “The Messenger of God ﷺ ordered us to kill snakes.” He replied: “After that, he forbade killing those that dwell in houses.” Al-Zuhrī said: “These are the house-dwelling snakes (*ʿawāmir*).”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said—I think he raised the report to the Prophet ﷺ—that he used to order the killing of snakes and said: “Whoever leaves them alone for fear of retaliation [by their kind] is not one of us.”

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: قَالَ: وَقَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ:   «إِنَّ §الْحَيَّاتِ مَسِيخُ الْجِنِّ، كَمَا مُسِخَتِ الْقِرَدَةُ مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: He said: Ibn ʿAbbās also said: “Snakes are transformed jinn, just as some of the Children of Israel were transformed into apes.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd, from Abū al-ʿAdabbas, who said that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: “Disperse your possessions against the risk of death; make one head into two; do not remain in a place of helplessness; put your dwellings in order; and frighten snakes before they frighten you.” Maʿmar explained: “‘Make one head into two’ means [instead of one slave] two half-shares in slaves.” ʿAbd al-Razzāq explained: “*Mathāwī* means dwellings, and ‘disperse against death’ means to distribute one's estates.” [The wording of the maxim is difficult and the two explanations are preserved as given.]
records.text_ar: ١٩٦١٨ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ عَاصِمِ بْنِ أَبِي النَّجُودِ، عَنْ أَبِي الْعَدَبَّسِ، قَالَ: قَالَ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ:   «§فَرِّقُوا عَنِ الْمَنِيَّةِ وَاجْعَلُوا الرَّأْسَ رَأْسَيْنِ، وَلَا تُلِثُّوا بِدَارٍ معُجِزَةٍ، وَأَصْلِحُوا مثَاوِيَكُمْ، وَأَخِيفُوا الْحَيَّاتِ قَبْلَ أَنْ تُخِيفَكُمْ»   قَالَ مَعْمَرٌ:   «اجْعَلُوا الرَّأْسَ رَأْسَيْنِ أَنْصَافَ عَبْدَيْنِ»   قَالَ عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ:   «وَالْمَثَاوِي الْبُيُوتُ، وَفَرِّقُوا عَنِ الْمَنِيَّةِ: فَرِّقُوا الضِّيَاعَ»

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd, from Abū al-ʿAdabbas, who said that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: “Disperse your possessions against the risk of death; make one head into two; do not remain in a place of helplessness; put your dwellings in order; and frighten snakes before they frighten you.” Maʿmar explained: “‘Make one head into two’ means [instead of one slave] two half-shares in slaves.” ʿAbd al-Razzāq explained: “*Mathāwī* means dwellings, and ‘disperse against death’ means to distribute one's estates.” [The wording of the maxim is difficult and the two explanations are preserved as given.]

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ forbade killing the *jānn* [a type of small or house-dwelling snake].”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, who said: A scorpion stung the Prophet ﷺ. He shook his hand and said: “May God curse you! You care nothing whether you sting a prophet or anyone else.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from certain Kufans, that Ibn Masʿūd said: “Whoever kills a snake is as though he has killed an unbeliever, and whoever kills a scorpion is as though he has killed an unbeliever.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٦٢١ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ بَعْضِ الْكُوفِيِّينَ، أَنَّ ابْنَ مَسْعُودٍ، قَالَ:   «§مَنْ قَتَلَ حَيَّةً فَكَأَنَّمَا قَتَلَ كَافِرًا، وَمَنْ قَتَلَ عَقْرَبًا، فَكَأَنَّمَا قَتَلَ كَافِرًا»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from Mujāhid or someone else, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, who said that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Give to anyone who asks you in God's name; respond to anyone who invites you to something good; and repay anyone who does you a kindness. If you cannot find anything with which to repay him, pray for him until he sees that you have repaid him.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “If the son of Adam had two valleys of wealth, he would wish for a third. Nothing fills the belly of the son of Adam except dust. Then God accepts the repentance of whoever repents.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٦٢٣ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ طَاوُسٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ:   «§لَوْ كَانَ لِابْنِ آدَمَ وَادِيَانِ مِنْ مَالٍ، تَمَنَّى إِلَيْهِمَا وَادِيًا ثَالِثًا، وَلَا يَمْلَأُ جَوْفَ ابْنِ آدَمَ إِلَّا التُّرَابُ، ثُمَّ يَتُوبُ اللَّهُ عَلَى مَنْ تَابَ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, who said: Maymūna freed a female slave of hers who was Black and mentioned it to the Messenger of God ﷺ. He said: “Why did you not give her to your Bedouin sister?” The narrator added: “I think he also said, ‘So she could tend her flock.’”
records.text_ar: ١٩٦٢٦ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ طَاوُسٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، قَالَ: أَعْتَقَتْ مَيْمُونَةُ أَمَةً لَهَا سَوْدَاءَ، فَذَكَرَتْهَا لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَقَالَ:   «§أَلَا كُنْتِ أَعْطَيْتِهَا أُخْتَكِ الْأَعَرَابِيَّةَ»   - قَالَ: حَسِبْتُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: -   «فَتَرْعَى عَلَيْهَا»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, from Zaynab daughter of Abū Salama, who said: “Messenger of God, the children of Abū Salama are in my care, and they have nothing except what I spend on them. I will not abandon them. Will I receive a reward for what I spend on them?” The Prophet ﷺ said: “Spend on them; you will receive the reward of what you spend on them.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٦٢٨ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ زَيْنَبَ بِنْتِ أَبِي سَلَمَةَ، أَنَّهَا قَالَتْ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، إِنَّ بَنِي أَبِي سَلَمَةَ فِي حِجْرِي، وَلَيْسَ لَهُمْ إِلَّا مَا أَنْفَقْتُ عَلَيْهِمْ، وَلَسْتُ بِتَارِكَتِهِمْ كَذَا وَلَا كَذَا، أَفَلِي أَجْرُ مَا أَنْفَقْتُ عَلَيْهِمْ؟ فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§أَنْفِقِي عَلَيْهِمْ فَإِنَّ لَكِ أَجْرَ مَا أَنْفَقَتِ عَلَيْهِمْ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from someone who heard ʿIkrima narrating from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: “Maintaining kinship is not merely treating kindly someone who treats you kindly—that is only reciprocity. Maintaining kinship is treating kindly someone who has cut you off.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwa, from ʿĀʾisha, that the Prophet ﷺ would seek refuge from sin and indebtedness. ʿĀʾisha asked, “Messenger of God, how often you seek refuge from debt!” He replied: “A person who falls into debt makes promises and breaks them, and speaks and lies.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, that the Prophet ﷺ would say: “O God, I seek refuge in You from the trial of the Fire, the trial of the grave and the punishment of the grave. I seek refuge in You from the evil of the trial of poverty and the evil of the trial of wealth, and from the trial of the false messiah, the Dajjāl. O God, purify my heart of my sins as You have cleansed a white garment of dirt. Separate me from my sins as You have separated east from west. O God, I seek refuge in You from laziness, decrepitude, sin, and debt.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, that the Prophet ﷺ would say: “O God, help me to thank You, remember You, and worship You well. records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from ʿAmr ibn Muslim, from Ṭāwūs, who used to say: “O God, I seek refuge in You from wealth that leads to arrogance, and from poverty that clings relentlessly [or: ruins a person].” [The Arabic source gives alternative final wording.]

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Abān, from Anas, that the Prophet ﷺ would say: “O God, I seek refuge in You from a heart that does not humble itself, an appetite that is never satisfied, knowledge that does not benefit, and words that are not heeded. O God, I seek refuge in You from the evil of these four things.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Layth, from an unnamed man, from Abū Hurayra, that the Prophet ﷺ would say: “O God, I seek refuge in You from hunger, for it is a miserable bedfellow. And I seek refuge in You from betrayal, for it is a miserable intimate companion.” He also disliked a person calling himself lazy or saying to a companion, “You are lazy.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from Warrād, the secretary of al-Mughīra ibn Shuʿba, who said: Muʿāwiya wrote to al-Mughīra asking him to send something he had heard from the Messenger of God ﷺ. Al-Mughīra wrote: “I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ seek refuge from three things: undutifulness toward mothers, burying daughters alive, and withholding [what is due] while demanding [what belongs to others]. I heard him forbid three things: gossip and hearsay, wasting wealth, and asking too many questions. And I heard him say: ‘O God, none can withhold what You give, none can reverse what You decree, and the fortune of the fortunate does not avail against You.’”
records.text_ar: ١٩٦٣٨ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ بْنِ عُمَيْرٍ، عَنْ وَرَّادٍ كَاتِبِ الْمُغِيرَةِ بْنِ شُعْبَةَ، قَالَ: كَتَبَ مُعَاوِيَةُ إِلَى الْمُغِيرَةِ أَنِ اكْتُبْ إِلَيَّ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ حَدِيثِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، فَكَتَبَ إِلَيْهِ: إِنِّي سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ   «§يَتَعَوَّذُ مِنْ ثَلَاثٍ: مِنْ عُقُوقِ الْأُمَّهَاتِ، وَمِنْ وَأْدِ الْبَنَاتِ، وَمِنْ مَنْعٍ وَهَاتِ. وَسَمِعْتُهُ يَنْهَى عَنْ ثَلَاثٍ: عَنْ قِيلَ وَقَالَ، وَإِضَاعَةِ الْمَالِ، وَكَثْرَةِ السُّؤَالِ. وَسَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ: اللَّهُمَّ لَا مَانِعَ لِمَا أَعْطَيْتَ، وَلَا رَادَّ لِمَا قَضَيْتَ، وَلَا يَنْفَعُ ذَا الْجَدِّ مِنْكَ الْجَدُّ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, that the Prophet ﷺ would say: “O God, let me benefit from my hearing and my sight, and let them remain with me to the end. O God, do not give my enemy power over me, and let me see my vindication against him.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Hammām ibn Munabbih, who heard Abū Hurayra say that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “None of you should say, ‘O God, forgive me if You wish; O God, have mercy on me if You wish; O God, provide for me if You wish.’ Rather, he should make his request with resolve, for God does whatever He wishes and no one can compel Him.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbayda ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: “When one of you wishes to ask [God for something], let him begin by praising and extolling God as He deserves, then invoke blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ, and afterward make his supplication; that is more likely to succeed.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from an unnamed man, from Abū Hurayra, who said that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Your supplication is answered so long as you are not hasty and say, ‘I have prayed but have not been answered.’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, that the Prophet ﷺ would say: “O One who makes hearts steadfast, make our hearts steadfast in Your religion.” Umm Salama asked him, “How often you say, ‘O Turner of hearts’!” The Prophet ﷺ replied: “Hearts are between two fingers of God's fingers; He turns them.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, who said: I heard a man narrate that the Prophet ﷺ used to say: “O God, adorn us with the adornment of faith and make us guides who are themselves rightly guided. O God, guide us and guide others through us; grant us victory and grant victory through us. O God, Turner of hearts, make our hearts steadfast in Your religion. O God, I ask You for bliss that never ceases, and delight of the eyes that never ends. I ask You for the pleasure of looking upon Your face and longing to meet You, without harmful hardship or misleading trial. O God, I ask You for contentment after the decree has come to pass, and the cool comfort of life after death.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Abān, from Anas, who said that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Your Lord is modest and generous. When a servant raises his hands to Him, He is too generous to send them back empty without placing some good in them.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Abān, from al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtayba, who used to say: “There are three phrases that God will cause a person for whom He intends good to memorize and never forget: ‘O God, I am weak, so strengthen my weakness in what pleases You; take me by the forelock toward what is good; and make Islam the utmost object of my contentment.’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Hārūn ibn Riʾāb, from Mujāhid, who said: “When birds begin beating their wings”—that is, at the pre-dawn time—“a caller cries out: ‘You who seek good, come! You who do evil, stop! Is there anyone seeking forgiveness who might be forgiven? Is there anyone repenting whose repentance might be accepted?’ Then he calls out: ‘O God, grant replacement to the one who spends, and destruction to the one who withholds,’ until morning.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٦٥٢ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ هَارُونَ بْنِ رِئَابٍ، عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ، قَالَ:   «§إِذَا أخْفَقَتِ الطَّيْرُ بِأَجْنِحَتِهَا - يَعْنِي السَّحَرَ -، نَادَى مُنَادٍ: يَا بَاغِيَ الْخَيْرِ هَلُمَّ، وَيَا فَاعِلَ الشَّرِّ انْتَهِ، هَلْ مِنْ مُسْتَغْفِرٍ يُغْفَرُ لَهُ، هَلْ مِنْ تَائِبٍ يُتَابُ عَلَيْهِ، قَالَ: ثُمَّ يُنَادِي: اللَّهُمَّ أَعْطِ مُنْفِقًا خَلَفًا، وَأَعْطِ مُمْسِكًا تَلَفًا، حَتَّى الصُّبْحِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, who said: Abū Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and al-Agharr Abū ʿAbd Allāh, both companions of Abū Hurayra, told me that Abū Hurayra informed them that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Our Lord, blessed and exalted, descends each night to the lowest heaven when the final third of the night remains and says: ‘Who calls upon Me, that I may answer him? Who asks My forgiveness, that I may forgive him? Who asks Me, that I may give him?’”
records.text_ar: ١٩٦٥٣ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنِي أَبُو سَلَمَةَ بْنُ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، وَالْأَغَرُّ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، صَاحِبَا أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، أَنَّ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ أَخْبَرَهُمَا، عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ:   «يَنْزِلُ رَبُّنَا تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى كُلَّ لَيْلَةٍ حَتَّى يَبْقَى ثُلُثُ اللَّيْلِ الْآخِرُ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ الدُّنْيَا فَيَقُولُ: §مَنْ يَدْعُونِي؟ فَأَسْتَجِيبَ لَهُ، مَنْ يَسْتَغْفِرُنِي؟ فَأَغْفِرَ لَهُ، مَنْ يَسْأَلُنِي؟ فَأُعْطِيَهُ»

records.display_matn_en: “Our Lord, blessed and exalted, descends each night to the lowest heaven when the final third of the night remains and says: ‘Who calls upon Me, that I may answer him? Who asks My forgiveness, that I may forgive him? Who asks Me, that I may give him?’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Agharr Abū Muslim, from Abū Hurayra and Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “God grants respite until the final third of the night; then He descends to this heaven and calls out: ‘Is there anyone repenting, that his repentance may be accepted? records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: It used to be said: “When a man encounters someone afflicted by one of these calamities and says, ‘Praise belongs to God, who has spared me the affliction with which He has tested you, and has favored me greatly over many of those He has created,’ that calamity will never befall him, whatever it might be.” Maʿmar said: “I also heard someone other than Ayyūb add to this report: ‘That affliction will not befall him, God willing.’”
records.text_ar: ١٩٦٥٥ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ سَالِمِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، قَالَ: كَانَ يُقَالُ:   «§إِذَا اسْتَقْبَلَ الرَّجُلُ شَيْئًا مِنْ هَذَا الْبَلَاءِ فَقَالَ: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي عَافَانِي مِمَّا ابْتَلَاكَ بِهِ، وَفَضَّلَنِي عَلَى كَثِيرٍ مِمَّنْ خَلَقَ تَفْضِيلًا، لَمْ يُصِبْهُ ذَلِكَ الْبَلَاءُ أَبَدًا، كَائِنًا مَا كَانَ»   ، قَالَ مَعْمَرٌ:   «وَسَمِعْتُ غَيْرَ أَيُّوبَ يَذْكُرُ فِي هَذَا الْحَدِيثِ، قَالَ: لَمْ يُصِبْهُ ذَلِكَ الْبَلَاءُ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn, from Abū Hurayra; and from Hammām ibn Munabbih, from Abū Hurayra, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “God has ninety-nine names, one hundred less one. Whoever enumerates them will enter Paradise.” Hammām ibn Munabbih added, transmitting from Abū Hurayra from the Prophet ﷺ: “He is One [literally, odd] and loves what is odd.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Muḥammad ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, from his father, who said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “I have several names. I am Aḥmad and I am Muḥammad; I am al-Māḥī, through whom God effaces unbelief; I am al-Ḥāshir, at whose feet people will be gathered; and I am al-ʿĀqib.” Maʿmar said: I asked al-Zuhrī, “What does al-ʿĀqib mean?” He answered: “The one after whom there is no prophet.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik, who said: Mulāʿib al-Asinna brought a gift to the Messenger of God ﷺ. records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Ibn al-Musayyib and al-Aʿraj, from Abū Hurayra, who said: “The worst food is the food of a wedding feast to which the wealthy are invited while the poor are left out. Yet attendance is a duty: whoever neglects it has disobeyed.” Maʿmar would sometimes say: “Whoever does not respond to the invitation has disobeyed God and His Messenger.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٦٦٢ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنِ ابْنِ الْمُسَيِّبِ، وَالْأَعْرَجِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ:   «§شَرُّ الطَّعَامِ طَعَامُ الْوَلِيمَةِ، يُدْعَى إِلَيْهِ الْغَنِيُّ وَيُتْرَكُ الْمِسْكِينُ، وَهِيَ حَقٌّ، مَنْ تَرَكَهَا فَقَدْ عَصَى»   . وَكَانَ مَعْمَرٌ رُبَّمَا قَالَ:   «وَمَنْ لَمْ يُجِبْ فَقَدْ عَصَى اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Mujāhid, that Ibn ʿUmar was invited to a meal one day. A man among the people said, “As for me, excuse me from this.” Ibn ʿUmar said to him: “There is no excuse for you in this.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās was invited to a meal while he was occupied with matters connected with the provision of drinking water. He said to the people: “Go to your brother, accept your brother's invitation, give him my greeting of peace, and tell him that I am busy.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٦٦٤ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ دِينَارٍ، عَنْ عَطَاءِ بْنِ أَبِي رَبَاحٍ، قَالَ: دُعِيَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ إِلَى طَعَامٍ، وَهُوَ يُعَالِجُ مِنْ أَمْرِ السِّقَايَةِ شَيْئًا، فَقَالَ لِلْقَوْمِ:   «§قُومُوا إِلَى أَخِيكُمْ، وَأَجِيبُوا أَخَاكُمْ، فَاقْرَءُوا عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامَ، وَأَخْبِرُوهُ أَنِّي مَشْغُولٌ»

records.display_matn_ar: دُعِيَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ إِلَى طَعَامٍ، وَهُوَ يُعَالِجُ مِنْ أَمْرِ السِّقَايَةِ شَيْئًا، فَقَالَ لِلْقَوْمِ:   «§قُومُوا إِلَى أَخِيكُمْ، وَأَجِيبُوا أَخَاكُمْ، فَاقْرَءُوا عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامَ، وَأَخْبِرُوهُ أَنِّي مَشْغُولٌ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn, who said: My father married and invited people for eight days. He invited Ubayy ibn Kaʿb among them; Ubayy came that day while fasting, prayed, offered a supplication for blessing, and then left.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “When one of you is invited by his brother, let him accept, whether to a wedding or something similar.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Thābit al-Bunānī, from ʿĀṣim, from Anas ibn Mālik, that a tailor invited the Messenger of God ﷺ and served him *tharīd*, with meat and gourd poured over it. The Messenger of God ﷺ picked out the gourd pieces and ate them, for he loved gourd. Thābit said: I heard Anas say: “After that, whenever food was prepared for me in which gourd could be included, I had it included.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٦٦٧ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ ثَابِتٍ الْبُنَانِيِّ، عَنْ عَاصِمٍ، عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، أَنَّ رَجُلًا خَيَّاطًا دَعَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، فَقَرَّبَ لَهُ ثَرِيدًا قَدْ صُبَّ عَلَيْهِ لَحْمٌ فِيهِ دُبَّاءٌ،   «فَكَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَأْخُذُ الدُّبَّاءَ فَيَأْكُلُهُ»   ، قَالَ:   «§وَكَانَ يُحِبُّ الدُّبَّاءَ»   ، قَالَ ثَابِتٌ: فَسَمِعْتُ أَنَسًا يَقُولُ:   «فَمَا صُنِعَ لِي طَعَامٌ بَعْدُ، أَقْدِرُ عَلَى أَنْ يُصْنَعَ فِيهِ دُبَّاءٌ إِلَّا صُنِعَ»

records.display_matn_en: that a tailor invited the Messenger of God ﷺ and served him *tharīd*, with meat and gourd poured over it. records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Zayd ibn Aslam, that the Prophet ﷺ met a woman leaving ʿĀʾisha's home carrying something. He asked, “What is this?” She replied: “I offered it to ʿĀʾisha, but she refused it.” When the Prophet ﷺ entered upon ʿĀʾisha he asked: “Why did you not accept it?” She said, “Messenger of God, she is in need of it and had greater need of it than I did.” He replied: “Why did you not accept it from her and then give her something better in return?”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, who said: The Prophet ﷺ wanted some meat and sent to a woman. She replied, “We have nothing left except necks, and I was embarrassed to offer those to you.” The Prophet ﷺ said: “Why? Are they not the parts closest to what is good and furthest from harm?”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Thābit, from Anas, who said: A funeral procession passed before the Prophet ﷺ, and he said, “Speak of him.” The people said he had loved God and His Messenger, as far as they knew, and spoke well of him. The Prophet ﷺ said, “It has become due.” Another funeral passed, and he asked them to speak of the deceased. They said, “He was a wretched man in the religion of God.” The Prophet ﷺ said, “It has become due. You are God's witnesses on earth.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Ḥasan, who said: It used to be said: “Beware of the discernment of a believer, for he sees by God's light.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Budayl al-ʿUqaylī, from Abū al-ʿAlāʾ ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr, who said: A man sneezed in the presence of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and said, “Peace be upon you.” ʿUmar replied: “And upon you and upon your mother! When one of you sneezes, let him say, ‘Praise belongs to God.’ The people should respond, ‘May God have mercy on you,’ and he should reply, ‘May God forgive you.’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Sulaymān al-Taymī, that Anas said: Two men sneezed in the presence of the Messenger of God ﷺ. He invoked mercy for one but not the other. The other man asked, “Messenger of God, you invoked mercy for him but not for me.” He replied: “He praised God, but you did not.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, who said that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Five things are due to a Muslim from his brother: returning the greeting of peace, invoking mercy for someone who sneezes, accepting an invitation, visiting the sick, and following funeral processions.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, who related it from some of them: “When a man sneezes, it is his duty to praise God, raising his voice so that those near him hear. When he praises God, it is their duty to invoke mercy for him.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٦٨٠ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ أَبِي كَثِيرٍ، ذَكَرَهُ عَنْ بَعْضِهِمْ، قَالَ:   «§حَقٌّ عَلَى الرَّجُلِ إِذَا عَطَسَ أَنْ يَحْمَدَ اللَّهَ، وَيَرْفَعَ بِذَلِكَ صَوْتَهُ فَيُسْمِعَ مَنْ عِنْدَهُ، وَحَقٌّ عَلَيْهِمْ إِذَا حَمِدَ اللَّهَ أَنْ يُشَمِّتُوهُ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, who said: “One responds to a person who repeatedly sneezes up to three times.” A man asked Maʿmar, “Should a man invoke mercy for a woman when she sneezes?” He replied: “Yes, there is no harm in that.”

records.text_en: We recited to ʿAbd al-Razzāq, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, who said that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Might one of you deny what I said while reclining?” The narrator added, “I think he also said: ‘A report from me is recounted to him, and he says, “The Messenger of God ﷺ never said that.”’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Ḥasan, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Might one of you deny what I said while reclining upon his cushions? A report of mine is recounted to him and he says, ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ did not say that. How are we to know?’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwa, from Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām, who said: I asked, “Messenger of God, what do you say about things I did in the pre-Islamic period as acts of piety, such as freeing slaves and maintaining ties of kinship? Will I have any reward for them?” The Prophet ﷺ replied: “You became Muslim while retaining the good you had done before.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٦٨٥ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ عُرْوَةَ، عَنْ حَكِيمِ بْنِ حِزَامٍ، قَالَ: قُلْتُ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، أَرَأَيْتَ أُمُورًا كُنْتُ أَتَحَنَّثُ بِهَا فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ، مِنْ عَتَاقَةٍ، وَصِلَةِ رَحِمٍ، هَلْ لِي فِيهَا مِنْ أَجْرٍ؟ فَقَالَ لَهُ: النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§أَسْلَمْتَ عَلَى مَا سَلَفَ لَكَ مِنْ خَيْرٍ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Manṣūr, from Abū Wāʾil, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: A man asked the Prophet ﷺ, “What of a man who behaves well after becoming Muslim? Will he be held accountable for what he did during the pre-Islamic period?” The Prophet ﷺ replied: “Whoever does well in Islam will not be held accountable for what he did in the pre-Islamic period. Whoever behaves badly in Islam will be held accountable for both his earlier and later deeds.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٦٨٦ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ مَنْصُورٍ، عَنْ أَبِي وَائِلٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَجُلٌ لِلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ  أَرَأَيْتَ الرَّجُلَ يُحْسِنُ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ، أَيُؤَاخَذُ بِمَا عَمِلَ فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ؟ فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§مَنْ أَحْسَنَ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ لَمْ يُؤَاخَذْ بِمَا عَمِلَ فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ، وَمَنْ أَسَاءَ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ أُخِذَ بِالْأَوَّلِ وَالْآخِرِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, who said: A Bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, “Prophet of God, my father used to care for orphans, maintain family ties, and do such-and-such. Where will he go?” The Prophet ﷺ asked, “Did your father die in the pre-Islamic period?” He replied, “Yes.” The Prophet ﷺ said, “He will enter the Fire.” The Bedouin became angry and asked, “Then where will your father go?” The Prophet ﷺ told him: “Whenever you pass the grave of an unbeliever, give him the news of the Fire.” The Bedouin said, “The Messenger of God ﷺ has given me hard work to do: I never passed the grave of an unbeliever without giving him the news of the Fire.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٦٨٧ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، قَالَ: جَاءَ أَعْرَابِيٌّ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَقَالَ: يَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ ‍، إِنَّ أَبِي كَانَ يَكْفُلُ الْأَيْتَامَ، وَيَصِلُ الْأَرْحَامَ، وَيَفْعَلُ كَذَا، فَأَيْنَ مَدخَلُهُ؟ قَالَ:   «هَلَكَ أَبُوكَ فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ؟»   قَالَ: نَعَمْ، قَالَ:   «فَمَدْخَلُهُ النَّارُ»   ، قَالَ: فَغَضِبَ الْأَعْرَابِيُّ، وَقَالَ: فَأَيْنَ مَدْخَلُ أَبِيكَ؟ فَقَالَ لَهُ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «حَيْثُ §مَا مَرَرْتَ بِقَبْرِ كَافِرٍ فَبَشِّرْهُ بِالنَّارِ»   فَقَالَ الْأَعْرَابِيُّ: لَقَدْ كَلَّفَنِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ تَعَبًا، مَا مَرَرْتُ بِقَبْرِ كَافِرٍ إِلَّا بَشَّرْتُهُ بِالنَّارِ

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Thābit, from Anas, that a Bedouin named Zāhir ibn Ḥarām—or Ḥizām—used to bring gifts from the desert to the Prophet ﷺ, and the Messenger of God ﷺ would equip him with provisions when he was about to leave. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Zāhir is our man of the desert, and we are his people of the town.” The Prophet ﷺ loved him, although he was an unattractive man. One day the Prophet ﷺ came upon him selling his goods and embraced him from behind without being seen. Zāhir said, “Let me go! Who is this?” He turned, recognized the Prophet ﷺ, and then pressed his back against the Prophet's chest as closely as he could. The Prophet ﷺ called out, “Who will buy this slave?” Zāhir said, “Messenger of God, by God, you will find me unsaleable.” The Prophet ﷺ replied: “But in God's sight you are not unsaleable,” or he said, “In God's sight you are valuable.”

The Prophet ﷺ said: “Zāhir is our man of the desert, and we are his people of the town.” The Prophet ﷺ loved him, although he was an unattractive man. One day the Prophet ﷺ came upon him selling his goods and embraced him from behind without being seen. Zāhir said, “Let me go! Who is this?” He turned, recognized the Prophet ﷺ, and then pressed his back against the Prophet's chest as closely as he could. The Prophet ﷺ called out, “Who will buy this slave?” Zāhir said, “Messenger of God, by God, you will find me unsaleable.” The Prophet ﷺ replied: “But in God's sight you are not unsaleable,” or he said, “In God's sight you are valuable.”
records.display_isnad_ar: أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ ثَابِتٍ، عَنْ أَنَسٍ،
records.display_matn_ar: أَنَّ رَجُلًا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْبَادِيَةِ كَانَ اسْمَهُ زَاهِرُ بْنُ حَرَامٍ أَوْ حِزَامٍ، وَكَانَ يُهْدِي لِلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ الْهَدِيَّةَ مِنَ الْبَادِيَةِ، فَيُجَهِّزُهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ إِذَا أَرَادَ أَنْ يَخْرُجَ، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «إِنَّ زَاهِرًا بَادِينَا وَنَحْنُ حَاضِرُوهُ»   ، قَالَ: وَكَانَ يُحِبُّهُ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَكَانَ رَجُلًا دَمِيمًا، فَأَتَاهُ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَوْمًا وَهُوَ يَبِيعُ مَتَاعَهُ، فَاحْتَضَنَهُ مِنْ خَلْفِهِ، وَهُوَ لَا يُبْصِرُهُ فَقَالَ:   «أَرْسِلْنِي، مَنْ هَذَا؟»   فَالْتَفَتَ فَعَرَفَ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، فَجَعَلَ لَا يَأْلُو مَا أَلْصَقَ ظَهْرَهُ بِصَدْرِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ حِينَ عَرَفَهُ، وَجَعَلَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَقُولُ:   «مَنْ يَشْتَرِي الْعَبْدَ؟»   فَقَالَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، إِذًا وَاللَّهِ تَجِدُنِي كَاسِدًا، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «لَكِنْ §عِنْدَ اللَّهِ لسَتَ بِكَاسِدٍ، - أَوْ قَالَ: - لَكِنْ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ أَنْتَ غَالٍ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever brings a plot of land into cultivation will be rewarded for whatever a human, animal, or bird eats from it, as long as it remains rooted there.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Sufyān, from Jābir, that the Prophet ﷺ visited Umm Mubashshir in a date-palm grove and asked, “Who planted these palms—a Muslim or an unbeliever?” She replied, “A Muslim.” He said: “Whenever a Muslim plants palms or sows a crop and a bird, animal, or person eats from it, that is charity for him.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Abū Isḥāq, who said: Kudayr al-Ḍabbī told me that a Bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked, “Tell me of a deed that will bring me nearer to Paradise and further from the Fire.” The Prophet ﷺ replied, “Are those the two things that concern you?” He said, “Yes.” The Prophet ﷺ said: “Speak justly and give from your surplus.” The man replied, “By God, I cannot speak justly every moment, nor can I give away my surplus wealth.” He said: “Then feed people and spread the greeting of peace.” The man replied, “That too is difficult.” The Prophet ﷺ asked: “Do you have camels?” He said, “Yes.” He said: “Take one of your camels and a waterskin, and find a household who can obtain drinking water only every other day. Provide them with water. Perhaps neither your camel will perish nor your waterskin wear out before Paradise becomes due to you.” The Bedouin departed proclaiming God's greatness. Neither his waterskin wore out nor his camel perished before he was killed as a martyr.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿĀʾisha, who said: A woman with two daughters came asking me for something. I had nothing but one date, which I gave her. She split it between her daughters and ate none of it herself. Then she and her daughters rose and left. The Messenger of God ﷺ entered soon afterward, and I told him about her. He said: “Whoever is tested through having such daughters and treats them well, they will be a screen for him against the Fire.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٦٩٣ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ عُرْوَةَ بْنِ الزُّبَيْرِ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، قَالَتْ: جَاءَتِ امْرَأَةٌ وَمَعَهَا ابْنَتَانِ لَهَا تَسْأَلُنِي، فَلَمْ تَجِدْ عِنْدِي شَيْئًا غَيْرَ تَمْرَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ، فَأَعْطَيْتُهَا إِيَّاهَا، فَأَخَذَتْهَا فَشَقَّتْهَا بَيْنَ بِنْتَيْهَا، وَلَمْ تَأْكُلْ مِنْهَا شَيْئًا، ثُمَّ قَامَتْ فَخَرَجَتْ هِيَ وابْنَتَيْهَا، فَدَخَلَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عَلَى هَيْئَتِهِ ذَلِكَ، فَحَدَّثَتْهُ حَدِيثَهَا، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§مَنِ ابْتُلِيَ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْبَنَاتِ بِشَيْءٍ فَأَحْسَنَ إِلَيْهِنَّ، كُنَّ لَهُ سِتْرًا مِنَ النَّارِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilāba, from Thawbān, who said that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “No dinar is better than one a man spends on his dependents, his riding animal, or his companions in God's cause.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, who said: “What you spend on yourself or your household without extravagance or waste is to your credit. But whatever you give in charity for ostentation and reputation is Satan's share.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٦٩٥ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنِ الْحَارِثِ، عَنْ عَلِيٍّ، قَالَ:   «§مَا أَنْفَقْتَ عَلَى نَفْسِكَ، أَوْ عَلَى أَهْلِ بَيْتِكَ فِي غَيْرِ سَرَفٍ، وَلَا تَبْذِيرٍ فَلَكَ، وَمَا تَصَدَّقْتَ رِيَاءً وَسُمْعَةً، فَذَلِكَ حَظُّ الشَّيْطَانِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, who said: A woman used to make things and give them in charity. She told Ibn Masʿūd, “You and your children have stood between me and giving charity.” Ibn Masʿūd replied, “If there is no reward for you in spending on us, I would not want you to do it. Go and ask the Messenger of God ﷺ.” She asked the Prophet ﷺ about it, and he replied: “Spend on them; you will receive a reward for what you spend on them.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٦٩٦ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، أَنَّ امْرَأَةً كَانَتْ تَصْنَعُ الشَّيْءَ تَصَّدَّقُ بِهِ، فَقَالَتْ لِابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ: لَقَدْ حُلْتَ أَنْتَ وَوَلَدُكَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ الصَّدَقَةِ، فَقَالَ لَهَا ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ: مَا أُحِبُّ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَكِ فِي ذَلِكَ أَجْرٌ أَنْ تَفْعَلِي، فَاذْهَبِي فَسَلِي رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، قَالَتْ: فَسَأَلْتُ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عَنْ ذَلِكَ، فَقَالَ:   «§أَنْفِقِي عَلَيْهِمْ فَإِنَّ لَكِ أَجْرَ مَا أَنْفَقْتِ عَلَيْهِمْ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ibn al-Munkadir, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever has three daughters or three sisters, provides for them, shelters them, and shows mercy to them will enter Paradise.” They asked, “What about two?” He said, “Two as well.” The narrator said: “We thought they might even ask, ‘What about one?’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Abū al-Jarrāḥ, a freedman of Umm Ḥabība, from Umm Ḥabība, who said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “The angels do not accompany a caravan containing a bell.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, who said: I heard a man tell Hishām ibn ʿUrwa: A young girl entered upon ʿĀʾisha with tinkling bells attached to her anklet. ʿĀʾisha said: “Take this one who drives away the angels out of my presence.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٦٩٩ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ رَجُلًا يُحَدِّثُ هِشَامَ بْنَ عُرْوَةَ، قَالَ: دَخَلَتْ جَارِيَةٌ عَلَى عَائِشَةَ وَفِي رِجْلِهَا جَلَاجِلُ فِي الْخَلْخَالِ، فَقَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ:   «§أَخْرِجُوا عَنِّي مُفَرِّقَةَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Wabara, from ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: “The greatest of the major sins are associating partners with God, feeling secure from God's plan, despairing of God's mercy, and losing hope in relief from God.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās was asked, “Are the major sins seven?” He replied: “They are closer to seventy.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn, from ʿAmra, who said: “Anything by which God is disobeyed is a major sin.” She referred to the glance of the eye and recited: “Tell the believing men to lower their gaze” [Qurʾān 24:30].

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Saʿīd al-Jurayrī, that a man came to Ibn ʿUmar and said, “I used to be with the Najadāt, and I committed sins. I want you to list the major sins for me.” Ibn ʿUmar listed seven or eight: associating partners with God, disobeying one's parents, killing a person, consuming usury, consuming an orphan's property, falsely accusing a chaste woman, and making a wicked oath. He then asked the man: “Do you have a mother?” He said, “Yes.” Ibn ʿUmar said: “Feed her and speak gently to her. By God, you will surely enter Paradise.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī, that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām said: “Usury comprises seventy-two sins; the least is like having intercourse with one's mother while in Islam. One dirham of usury is more serious than over thirty acts of fornication. On the Day of Resurrection God will permit both righteous and wicked to rise, except the one who consumes usury: he will not stand ‘except as one whom Satan has deranged through his touch’ [Qurʾān 2:275].”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Ḥasan, who said that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Shall I not tell you the gravest of the major sins? Associating partners with God and disobeying one's parents.” Then he said: “And beware of false testimony! Beware of false testimony!”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: The Prophet ﷺ was asked about the two things that make an outcome inevitable. He said: “Whoever meets God without associating anything with Him will enter Paradise, and whoever meets God while associating something with Him will enter the Fire.” Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh was asked, “Is there any polytheist among those who perform prayer?” He replied, “No.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٧٠٨ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، عَنْ جَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، قَالَ: سُئِلَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عَنِ الْمُوجِبَتَيْنِ، فَقَالَ:   «§مَنْ لَقِيَ اللَّهَ لَا يُشْرِكُ بِهِ دَخَلَ الْجَنَّةَ، وَمَنْ لَقِيَ اللَّهَ يُشْرِكُ بِهِ دَخَلَ النَّارَ»   وَسُئِلَ جَابِرُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: هَلْ فِي الْمُصَلِّينَ مُشْرِكٌ؟ قَالَ:   «لَا»   ،

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilāba, from Thābit ibn al-Ḍaḥḥāk, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever kills himself with something will be punished by that thing. Whoever testifies that a Muslim—or he said, a believer—is an unbeliever, it is like killing him. Whoever curses him, it is like killing him. And whoever falsely swears by a religion other than Islam becomes as he has sworn.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٧١٠ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ أَبِي قِلَابَةَ، عَنْ ثَابِتِ بْنِ الضَّحَّاكِ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ:   «§مَنْ قَتَلَ نَفْسَهُ بِشَيْءٍ عُذِّبَ بِهِ، وَمَنْ شَهِدَ عَلَى مُسْلِمٍ - أَوْ قَالَ: عَلَى مُؤْمِنٍ - بِكُفْرٍ، فَهُوَ كَقَتْلِهِ، وَمَنْ لَعَنَهُ فَهُوَ كَقَتْلِهِ، وَمَنْ حَلَفَ عَلَى مِلَّةٍ غَيْرِ الْإِسْلَامِ كَاذِبًا فَهُوَ كَمَا حَلَفَ»
records.section_title_ar: بَابُ مَنْ قَتَلَ نَفْسَهُ، وَمَنْ قَتَلَ نَفْسًا

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilāba, from Thābit ibn al-Ḍaḥḥāk, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever kills himself with something will be punished by that thing. Whoever testifies that a Muslim—or he said, a believer—is an unbeliever, it is like killing him. Whoever curses him, it is like killing him. And whoever falsely swears by a religion other than Islam becomes as he has sworn.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, who said: “Hope for someone who dies among the people of Islam without having shed anyone's blood.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda or another man, from al-Ḥasan, from Abū Bakra, who said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “The scent of Paradise can be perceived from a hundred years' journey, yet any servant who kills a person under a treaty without right will be forbidden by God to enter Paradise or even smell its fragrance.” Abū Bakra said: “May God deafen my ears if I did not hear the Messenger of God ﷺ say this.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Ḥasan, who said: It used to be said: “One who has killed a life and saved a life—perhaps [there is hope for him].” [The Arabic sentence is fragmentary and ends with “perhaps.”]

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muslim, al-Zuhrī's brother, who said: I was sitting with Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh among a group of Medinans when a man said, “The governor has just flogged a man, and the man died.” Sālim said: “God reproached Moses for killing an unbelieving person.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٧١٤ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ، أَخِي الزُّهْرِيِّ، قَالَ: كُنْتُ جَالِسًا عِنْدَ سَالِمِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ فِي نَفَرٍ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْمَدِينَةِ، فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ: ضَرَبَ الْأَمِيرُ آنِفًا رَجُلًا أَسْوَاطًا فَمَاتَ. فَقَالَ سَالِمٌ:   «§عَاتَبَ اللَّهُ عَلَى مُوسَى فِي نَفْسٍ كَافِرَةٍ قَتَلَهَا»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Abū Qilāba, from Thābit ibn al-Ḍaḥḥāk, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “There is no valid vow concerning something one does not own.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٧١٥ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ أَبِي كَثِيرٍ، عَنْ أَبِي قِلَابَةَ، عَنْ ثَابِتِ بْنِ الضَّحَّاكِ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ:   «§لَا نَذْرَ فِيمَا لَا تَمْلِكُ»
records.section_title_ar: بَابُ مَنْ قَتَلَ نَفْسَهُ، وَمَنْ قَتَلَ نَفْسًا

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: «§وَلَعْنُ الْمُؤْمِنِ كَقَتْلِهِ»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: “And cursing a believer is like killing him.” [Unnumbered continuation of the report.]

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: «§وَمَنْ قَتَلَ نَفْسَهُ بِشَيْءٍ فِي الدُّنْيَا، عُذِّبَ بِهِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: “And whoever kills himself with something in this world will be punished by it on the Day of Resurrection.” [Unnumbered continuation.]

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: «§وَمَنْ حَلَفَ بِمِلَّةٍ غَيْرِ الْإِسْلَامِ كَاذِبًا، فَهُوَ كَمَا قَالَ»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: “And whoever falsely swears by a religion other than Islam is as he has said.” [Unnumbered continuation.]

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: «§وَمَنْ قَالَ لِمُؤْمِنٍ: يَا كَافِرُ، فَهُوَ كَقَتْلِهِ»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: “And whoever says to a believer, ‘You unbeliever,’ it is like killing him.” [Unnumbered continuation.]

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Abū Hurayra, who said that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Whoever kills himself with an iron instrument will be thrusting that instrument into his stomach in the Fire of Hell, abiding there forever. Whoever kills himself by falling will keep falling in the Fire of Hell, abiding there forever. Whoever kills himself with poison will hold his poison in his hand and drink it in the Fire of Hell, abiding there forever.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٧١٦ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الْأَعْمَشِ، عَنْ أَبِي صَالِحٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§مَنْ قَتَلَ نَفْسَهُ بِحَدِيدَةٍ، فَحَدِيدَتُهُ يَجَأُ بِهَا فِي بَطْنِهِ فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ خَالِدًا مُخَلَّدًا فِيهَا أَبَدًا، وَمَنْ قَتَلَ نَفْسَهُ بِتَرَدٍّ فَهُوَ يَتَرَدَّى فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ خَالِدًا مُخَلَّدًا فِيهَا أَبَدًا، وَمَنْ قَتَلَ نَفْسَهُ بِسُمٍّ، فَسُمُّهُ فِي يَدِهِ يَتَحَسَّاهُ فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ خَالِدًا مُخَلَّدًا فِيهَا أَبَدًا»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Manṣūr, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAmr ibn Shuraḥbīl, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, who said: I asked, “Messenger of God”—or perhaps someone else asked—“Which sin is greatest in God's sight?” He said: “To set up an equal to Him when He created you.” I asked, “Then which?” He replied: “To kill your child for fear that he will share your food.” I asked, “Then which?” He replied: “To commit adultery with your neighbor's wife.” Then God sent down confirmation of this in His Book: “And those who do not call upon another god along with God ...” [Qurʾān 25:68].
records.text_ar: ١٩٧١٩ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ مَنْصُورٍ، عَنْ أَبِي وَائِلٍ، عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ شُرَحْبِيلَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، قَالَ: قُلْتُ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ - أَوْ قَالَهُ غَيْرِي - §أَيُّ الذُّنُوبِ أَعْظَمُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ؟ قَالَ:   «أَنْ تَجْعَلَ لَهُ نِدًّا وَهُوَ خَلَقَكَ»   ، قَالَ: ثُمَّ أَيُّ؟ قَالَ:   «ثُمَّ أَنْ تَقْتُلَ وَلَدَكَ خَشْيَةَ أَنْ يَطْعَمَ مَعَكَ»   ، قَالَ: ثُمَّ أَيُّ؟ قَالَ:   «ثُمَّ أَنْ تُزَانِيَ حَلِيلَةَ جَارِكَ»   ، قَالَ: فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ تَصْدِيقَ ذَلِكَ فِي كِتَابِهِ:  {وَالَّذِينَ لَا يَدْعُونَ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَهًا آخَرَ}   [الفرقان: ٦٨]  الْآيَةَ - [٤٦٥] -.

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Manṣūr, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAmr ibn Shuraḥbīl, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, who said: I asked, “Messenger of God”—or perhaps someone else asked—“Which sin is greatest in God's sight?” He said: “To set up an equal to Him when He created you.” I asked, “Then which?” He replied: “To kill your child for fear that he will share your food.” I asked, “Then which?” He replied: “To commit adultery with your neighbor's wife.” Then God sent down confirmation of this in His Book: “And those who do not call upon another god along with God ...” [Qurʾān 25:68].

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwa, from ʿĀʾisha, who said: “By God, I saw the Messenger of God ﷺ standing at the door of my room while the Abyssinians were playing with spears in the mosque. The Messenger of God ﷺ shielded me with his cloak so that I could watch their display between his ear and shoulder. He kept standing for my sake until I was the one to leave.” She added: “Consider how a young girl, eager for amusement, would behave.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ghālib, a man from Basra, passed people playing chess and said to al-Ḥasan: “I passed people devoted to their idols.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٧٢٦ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، قَالَ: مَرَّ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ غَالِبٍ - رَجُلٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْبَصْرَةِ - بِقَوْمٍ يَلْعَبُونَ بِالشِّطْرَنْجِ، فَقَالَ لِلْحَسَنِ:   «§مَرَرْتُ بِقَوْمٍ قَدْ عَكَفُوا عَلَى أَصْنَامٍ لَهُمْ»

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: قَالَ مَعْمَرٌ: وَبَلَغَنِي أَنَّ الشَّعْبِيَّ   «كَانَ §يَلْعَبُ بِالشِّطْرَنْجِ وَيَلْبَسُ مِلْحَفَةً حَمْرَاءَ، وَيَرْمِي بِالْجُلَاهِقِ، وَذَلِكَ أَنَّهُ كَانَ مُتَوَارِيًا مِنَ الْحَجَّاجِ»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: Maʿmar said: It reached me that al-Shaʿbī used to play chess, wear a red outer garment, and shoot with a pellet bow, while he was hiding from al-Ḥajjāj.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, who said: I heard Ibn Masʿūd say: “Beware of rolling the two dice, for that is a form of gambling (*maysir*).”
records.text_ar: ١٩٧٢٧ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ يَزِيدَ بْنِ أَبِي زِيَادٍ، عَنْ أَبِي الْأَحْوَصِ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ ابْنَ مَسْعُودٍ، يَقُولُ:   «§إِيَّاكُمْ وَدَحْوًا بِالْكَعْبَيْنِ، فَإِنَّهُمَا مِنَ الْمَيْسِرِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said: “Whoever plays with dice for gambling is as though he has eaten pork; whoever plays with them without gambling is as though he has rubbed himself with pig fat.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Abī Dhiʾb, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Thawbān, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ saw a man release pigeons and follow them with his eyes. The Prophet ﷺ said: “A devil following a devil.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, that Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī said: “People of Basra, spare me the chickens and dogs; do not be like the people of the villages”—that is, the Bedouins.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī and Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from ʿUrwa, who said: Abū Bakr entered upon the Prophet ﷺ while two singing girls were performing for ʿĀʾisha during the days of Minā. The Prophet ﷺ was lying down with his cloth covering his face. Abū Bakr said, “Is this being done in the Messenger of God's presence?” The Prophet ﷺ uncovered his face and said: “Leave them alone, Abū Bakr. These are days of celebration and remembrance of God.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٧٣٥ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، وَهِشَامِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ، عَنْ عُرْوَةَ، قَالَ: دَخَلَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، وَعِنْدَ عَائِشَةَ قَيْنَتَانِ تُغَنِّيَانِ فِي أَيَّامِ مِنًى، وَالنَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ مُضْطَجِعٌ، مُسَجًّى ثَوْبُهُ عَلَى وَجْهِهِ، فَقَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ: أَعِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يُصْنَعُ هَذَا؟ فَكَشَفَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عَنْ وَجْهِهِ، ثُمَّ قَالَ:   «§دَعْهُنَّ يَا أَبَا بَكْرٍ فَإِنَّهَا أَيَّامُ عِيدٍ وَذِكْرِ اللَّهِ»   ،

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn, that when ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb heard singing or a frame drum, he would ask, “What is it?” If told that it was for a wedding or circumcision, he would remain silent.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith, from Nawfal, who said: I saw Usāma ibn Zayd sitting in the mosque with one leg raised over the other, singing in a loud voice. The narrator said: “I think he said he was chanting *naṣb*,” a form of song.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Maṭar al-Warrāq, from Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr, who said: I accompanied ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn from Basra to Mecca. records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn, from Anas, who said: al-Barāʾ ibn Mālik lay on his back and began chanting melodiously. Anas said to him, “Remember God, my brother.” He sat upright and said: “Anas, do you think I will die in bed, when I have killed a hundred polytheists in single combat, besides those I helped to kill?”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from an unnamed man, from al-Ḥasan, who said: “Two sounds are sinful and obscene”—the narrator thought he also said “accursed”—“a sound at a blessing and a sound at a calamity. The sound at a calamity is scratching faces, tearing garments, pulling out hair, and Satan's wailing. The sound at a blessing is frivolity, false amusement, and Satan's flute.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٧٤٤ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ رَجُلٍ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ، قَالَ:   «§صَوْتَانِ فَاجِرَانِ فَاحِشَانِ - قَالَ: حَسِبْتُهُ قَالَ: مَلْعُونَانِ - صَوْتٌ عِنْدَ نِعْمَةٍ، وَصَوْتٌ عِنْدَ مُصِيبَةٍ، فَأَمَّا الصَّوْتُ عِنْدَ الْمُصِيبَةِ فَخَمْشُ الْوُجُوهِ، وَشَقُّ الْجُيُوبِ، وَنَتْفُ الْأَشْعَارِ، وَرَنُّ شَيْطَانٍ، وَأَمَّا الصَّوْتُ عِنْدَ النِّعْمَةِ فَلَهْوٌ وبَاطِلٌ، وَمِزْمَارُ شَيْطَانٍ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Kathīr ibn Ziyād, from al-Ḥasan, who said that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Gabriel continued recommending good treatment of neighbors to me until I thought he would make the neighbor an heir.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Abū Salama, from Abū Hurayra, who said that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Whoever believes in God and the Last Day should honor his guest. Whoever believes in God and the Last Day should not harm his neighbor. Whoever believes in God and the Last Day should speak good or remain silent.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٧٤٦ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِي سَلَمَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلْيُكْرِمْ ضَيْفَهُ، مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلَا يُؤْذِيَنَّ جَارَهُ، مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Kathīr ibn Ziyād, from al-Ḥasan, who said that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “A man is not a believer until his neighbor is safe from his harmful acts.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٧٤٧ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ كَثِيرِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§لَا يَكُونُ الرَّجُلُ مُؤْمِنًا حَتَّى يَأْمَنَ جَارُهُ بَوَائِقَهُ»

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: قَالَ: ثُمَّ يَقُولُ الْحَسَنُ:   «§وَكَيْفَ تَكُونُ مُؤْمِنًا وَلَا يَأْمَنُكَ جَارُكَ؟ وَكَيْفَ تَكُونُ مُؤْمِنًا وَلَا يَأْمَنُكَ النَّاسُ؟»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: Al-Ḥasan would then say: “How can you be a believer if your neighbor is not safe from you? How can you be a believer if people are not safe from you?”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, who said: One of the Anṣār whom I do not suspect told me that when the Messenger of God ﷺ performed ablution or spat, the companions hastened to take his spittle and the water from his ablution, wiping their faces and bodies with it. The Messenger of God ﷺ asked, “Why do you do this?” They said, “We seek blessing through it.” He replied: “Whoever wishes God and His Messenger to love him should speak truthfully, fulfill his trust, and not harm his neighbor.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Manṣūr, from Abū Wāʾil, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: A man asked the Prophet ﷺ, “Messenger of God, how can I know when I have done good or done wrong?” He replied: “When you hear your neighbors say, ‘You have done well,’ you have done well; when you hear them say, ‘You have done wrong,’ you have done wrong.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd God, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from al-Ṣaʿb ibn Jaththāma, who said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “There is no protected grazing land except for God and His Messenger.” Al-Zuhrī added: “ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb did have a protected pasture, and I was told that he reserved it for the camels of the charity tax.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, that ʿUmar said to Hāniʾ ibn Hunayy, a freedman whom he appointed over the protected pasture: “Admit the owner of a few sheep or a small herd, and keep me away from the livestock of Ibn ʿAwf and Ibn ʿAffān. If their livestock perishes, they can return to families and wealth. But if these people's livestock perishes, they will say, ‘Commander of the Faithful!’ Water and grazing are easier for me to provide than gold and silver coins.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, that a woman disputed with Saʿīd ibn Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl before Marwān over the boundaries of Saʿīd's land. Saʿīd said, “Would I alter its boundaries when I have heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say, ‘Whoever steals a handspan of land will have it placed around his neck from seven earths’?” Marwān said, “Then I leave the matter to you.” Saʿīd said, “O God, if she is lying, blind her eyes and cause her to die on her own land.” She became blind, and while walking on her land she fell into one of her wells and died. Later a flood swept over the land and exposed the boundary markers as Saʿīd had described them.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from ʿUthmān ibn Abī Sulaymān, from a man of Thaqīf, from ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr, raising the report to the Messenger of God ﷺ concerning a person who cuts down a lote tree: “Punishment will be poured upon him,” or he said, “His head will be thrust into the Fire.” The narrator said: I asked ʿUrwa's sons about this. records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: I heard al-Muthannā narrate from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī Abū Jaʿfar, who said: During the illness from which he died, the Prophet ﷺ said to ʿAlī: “Go out, ʿAlī, and proclaim, ‘From God, not from the Messenger of God: May God curse whoever cuts down a lote tree.’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Ibrāhīm ibn Yazīd, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from ʿAmr ibn Aws, who said: I met an old man of Thaqīf whose crops were being harmed by a lote tree. I asked, “Why do you not cut it down? The Messenger of God ﷺ made an exception for trees in cultivated fields.” He replied: “I myself heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘Whoever cuts down a lote tree other than one growing amid crops will have punishment poured upon him.’ I therefore dislike uprooting it whether it is in a field or elsewhere.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from Abū Bakr ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥazm, that the Messenger of God ﷺ undertook responsibility for a man's financial liability. When payment fell due, the man brought a lump of silver. The Messenger of God ﷺ asked, “Where did you get it?” He answered, “From a mine exploited by my people.” The Prophet ﷺ said: “You have neither paid the debt nor left matters as they were. Go back to them and forbid them [from doing that].” [The reason given is not supplied by this recension.]

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ismāʿīl ibn Umayya, from an unnamed man, from Abū Hurayra, who said: “Mines will appear at the end of time, and the worst of people will go out to them.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: Maʿmar informed us: ʿAqīl ibn Maʿqil informed us, from Hammām ibn Munabbih, who said: Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh was asked about *nushra* [a ritual to undo sorcery]. He said: “It is the work of Satan.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: Al-Shaʿbī said: “There is no objection to the Arabian kind of *nushra* that causes no harm if stepped upon.” The Arabian *nushra* consists of a person going to a place where thorny trees grow, taking fruits from the right and left, pounding them, reciting over them, and then bathing with the preparation.
records.text_ar: ١٩٧٦٣ - قَالَ عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ: وَقَالَ الشَّعْبِيُّ:   «§لَا بَأْسَ بِالنُّشْرَةِ الْعَرَبِيَّةِ الَّتِي لَا تَضُرُّ إِذَا وُطِئَتْ»   ، وَالنُّشْرَةُ الْعَرَبِيَّةُ: أَنْ يَخْرُجَ الْإِنْسَانُ فِي مَوْضِعِ عِضَاهٍ، فَيَأْخُذَ عَنْ يَمِينِهِ وَشِمَالِهِ مِنْ كُلِّ ثَمَرٍ يَدُقُّهُ وَيَقْرَأُ فِيهِ، ثُمَّ يَغْتَسِلُ بِهِ

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: وَفِي كُتُبِ وَهْبٍ:   «أَنْ §تُؤْخَذَ سَبْعُ وَرَقَاتٍ مِنْ سِدْرٍ أَخْضَرَ فَيَدُقَّهُ بَيْنَ حَجَرَيْنِ، ثُمَّ يَضْرِبَهُ فِي الْمَاءِ، وَيَقْرَأَ فِيهِ آيَةَ الْكُرْسِيِّ، وَذَوَاتَ قُلْ، ثُمَّ يَحْسُو مِنْهُ ثَلَاثَ حَسَوَاتٍ، وَيَغْتَسِلَ بِهِ، فَإِنَّهُ يُذْهِبُ عَنْهُ كُلَّ مَا بِهِ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ، وَهُوَ جَيِّدٌ لِلرَّجُلِ، إِذَا حُبِسَ مِنْ أَهْلِهِ»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: In the writings of Wahb it says: “Take seven leaves from a green lote tree and pound them between two stones. Mix them in water and recite over the water the Throne Verse and the surahs beginning with ‘Say.’ Drink three mouthfuls and wash with it. God willing, this will remove every affliction. It is also good for a man prevented from having relations with his family.”

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: قَالَ عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ:   «§وَحُبِسَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ مِنْ عَائِشَةَ خَاصَّةً حَتَّى أَنْكَرَ بَصَرَهُ»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ was prevented from [having relations with] ʿĀʾisha in particular, until his eyesight was affected.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Ibn al-Musayyib and ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr, that Jews of Banū Zurayq worked sorcery against the Messenger of God ﷺ and placed it in a well. The Prophet ﷺ was affected to the point that his vision almost failed him. God then showed him what they had done. He sent people to the well and the knots containing the sorcery were taken out.
records.text_ar: ١٩٧٦٤ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنِ ابْنِ الْمُسَيِّبِ، وَعُرْوَةَ بْنِ الزُّبَيْرِ،   «أَنَّ §يَهُودَ بَنِي زُرَيْقٍ، سَحَرُوا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، فَجَعَلُوهُ فِي بِئْرٍ، حَتَّى كَادَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يُنْكِرُ بَصَرَهُ، ثُمَّ دَلَّهُ اللَّهُ عَلَى مَا صَنَعُوا، فَأَرْسَلَ إِلَى الْبِئْرِ فَانْتُزِعَتِ الْعُقَدُ الَّتِي فِيهَا السِّحْرُ»

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: قَالَ الزُّهْرِيُّ: فَكَانَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَقُولُ فِيمَا بَلَغَنَا:   «§سَحَرنِي يَهُودُ بَنِي زُرَيْقٍ»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: Al-Zuhrī said: According to what reached us, the Prophet ﷺ would say: “The Jews of Banū Zurayq put me under a spell.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī, from Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmur, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ was prevented from [having relations with] ʿĀʾisha for a year. While he was asleep, two angels came. One sat by his head and the other at his feet. One said to the other, ‘Has Muḥammad been bewitched?’ The other replied, ‘Yes. The spell is in the well of so-and-so.’ In the morning, the Prophet ﷺ ordered the spell to be brought out of that well.” ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: Maʿmar said: “There is no objection to a man collecting the substance used for magic, reciting the Qurʾān over it, and bathing with it.”

records.text_en: Aḥmad ibn Khālid narrated to us: Abū Yaʿqūb narrated to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from Abū Umāma ibn Sahl ibn Ḥunayf, who said: ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿa saw Sahl ibn Ḥunayf bathing and was struck by admiration. He said, “By God, I have never seen anything like this—not even a maiden secluded in her chamber.” Sahl was immediately struck down and could not raise his head. They mentioned this to the Messenger of God ﷺ, who asked, “Do you suspect anyone?” They answered, “No one, Messenger of God, except that ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿa said such-and-such to him.” He summoned Sahl and ʿĀmir and said: “Glory be to God! Why does one of you kill his brother? When one of you sees something he admires in another, let him pray for a blessing upon him.” He then told ʿĀmir to wash for him. ʿĀmir washed his face, the backs of his hands, his elbows, his chest, the inside of his lower garment, his knees, and the outer surfaces of his feet into a vessel. He then ordered the water to be poured over Sahl's head, tipping the vessel from behind him. The narrator thought he also instructed him to take a few mouthfuls. Sahl stood up and departed with the rider. Jaʿfar ibn Burqān remarked, “We used to consider this mere roughness.” Al-Zuhrī replied: “Rather, this is the Sunnah.”

records.raw_text_en: Aḥmad ibn Khālid narrated to us: Abū Yaʿqūb narrated to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from Abū Umāma ibn Sahl ibn Ḥunayf, who said: ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿa saw Sahl ibn Ḥunayf bathing and was struck by admiration. He said, “By God, I have never seen anything like this—not even a maiden secluded in her chamber.” Sahl was immediately struck down and could not raise his head. They mentioned this to the Messenger of God ﷺ, who asked, “Do you suspect anyone?” They answered, “No one, Messenger of God, except that ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿa said such-and-such to him.” He summoned Sahl and ʿĀmir and said: “Glory be to God! Why does one of you kill his brother? When one of you sees something he admires in another, let him pray for a blessing upon him.” He then told ʿĀmir to wash for him. ʿĀmir washed his face, the backs of his hands, his elbows, his chest, the inside of his lower garment, his knees, and the outer surfaces of his feet into a vessel. He then ordered the water to be poured over Sahl's head, tipping the vessel from behind him. The narrator thought he also instructed him to take a few mouthfuls. Sahl stood up and departed with the rider. Jaʿfar ibn Burqān remarked, “We used to consider this mere roughness.” Al-Zuhrī replied: “Rather, this is the Sunnah.”

records.display_matn_ar: رَأَى عَامِرُ بْنُ رَبِيعَةَ سَهْلَ بْنَ حُنَيْفٍ وَهُوَ يَغْتَسِلُ، فَعَجِبَ مِنْهُ، فَقَالَ: تَالَلَّهِ إِنْ رَأَيْتُ كَالْيَوْمِ مُخَبَّأَةً فِي خِدْرِهَا، قَالَ: فَكُسِحَ بِهِ حَتَّى مَا يَرْفَعُ رَأْسَهُ، قَالَ: فَذُكِرَ ذَلِكَ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَقَالَ:   «هَلْ تَتَّهِمُونَ أَحَدًا؟»   فَقَالُوا: لَا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، إِلَّا أَنَّ عَامِرَ بْنَ رُبَيِّعَةَ قَالَ لَهُ كَذَا وَكَذَا، قَالَ: فَدَعَاهُ وَدَعَا عَامِرًا، فَقَالَ:   «§سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، عَلَامَ يَقْتُلُ أَحَدُكُمْ أَخَاهُ؟ إِذَا رَأَى مِنْهُ شَيْئًا يُعْجِبُهُ فَلْيَدْعُ لَهُ بِالْبَرَكَةِ»   ، قَالَ: ثُمَّ أَمَرَهُ يَغْسِلُ لَهُ، فَغَسَلَ وَجْهَهُ وَظَاهِرَ كَفَّيْهِ، وَمِرْفَقَيْهِ، وَغَسَلَ صَدْرَهُ، وَدَاخِلَةَ إِزَارِهِ، وَرُكْبَتَيْهِ، وَأَطْرَافَ قَدَمَيْهِ، ظَاهِرُهُمَا فِي الْإِنَاءِ، ثُمَّ أَمَرَ بِهِ فَصُبَّ عَلَى رَأْسِهِ، وَكَفَأَ الْإِنَاءَ مِنْ خَلْفِهِ - حَسِبْتُهُ قَالَ: وَأَمَرَهُ فَحَسَى مِنْهُ حَسَوَاتٍ - فَقَامَ فَرَاحَ مَعَ الرَّاكِبِ. فَقَالَ لَهُ جَعْفَرُ بْنُ بُرْقَانَ:   «مَا كُنَّا نَعُدُّ هَذَا إِلَّا جَفَاءً»   . فَقَالَ الزُّهْرِيُّ:   «بَلْ هِيَ السُّنَّةُ»
records.display_isnad_en: Aḥmad ibn Khālid narrated to us: Abū Yaʿqūb narrated to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from Abū Umāma ibn Sahl ibn Ḥunayf, who said:
records.display_matn_en: ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿa saw Sahl ibn Ḥunayf bathing and was struck by admiration. He said, “By God, I have never seen anything like this—not even a maiden secluded in her chamber.” Sahl was immediately struck down and could not raise his head. They mentioned this to the Messenger of God ﷺ, who asked, “Do you suspect anyone?” They answered, “No one, Messenger of God, except that ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿa said such-and-such to him.” He summoned Sahl and ʿĀmir and said: “Glory be to God! Why does one of you kill his brother? When one of you sees something he admires in another, let him pray for a blessing upon him.” He then told ʿĀmir to wash for him. ʿĀmir washed his face, the backs of his hands, his elbows, his chest, the inside of his lower garment, his knees, and the outer surfaces of his feet into a vessel. He then ordered the water to be poured over Sahl's head, tipping the vessel from behind him. The narrator thought he also instructed him to take a few mouthfuls. Sahl stood up and departed with the rider. Jaʿfar ibn Burqān remarked, “We used to consider this mere roughness.” Al-Zuhrī replied: “Rather, this is the Sunnah.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, who said: When the Messenger of God ﷺ came to Medina, its people used protective incantations mixed with polytheistic expressions, so he forbade incantations. records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, who said: It reached me that the Prophet ﷺ said to a woman: “Will you not teach her the incantation for *namla* [a skin complaint]?” He meant his wife Ḥafṣa, and added, “Just as you taught her writing.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, who said that the Prophet ﷺ said: “The evil eye is real. If anything could precede destiny, the evil eye would precede it. When any of you is asked to wash [for another afflicted by the evil eye], let him wash.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Abū ʿUmar, from Ibrāhīm ibn Ismāʿīl, from Dāwūd ibn al-Ḥuṣayn, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ used to teach us this supplication for every pain and for fever: “In the name of God the Great, I seek refuge in God the Mighty from the evil of every throbbing vein and from the evil of the heat of the Fire.”
