records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Abān, from al-Ḥasan, who attributed the report to the Prophet ﷺ: “Whoever ties a knot and recites an incantation over it has practiced sorcery; whoever practices sorcery has disbelieved; and whoever hangs an amulet upon himself will be left to rely upon it.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, who said: The companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ asked him, “Messenger of God, what about precautions we take, medicines we use, and incantations we seek? Do they avail against destiny?” The Prophet ﷺ said: “They themselves are part of destiny.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Hammām ibn Munabbih, from Abū Hurayra, who said that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The evil eye is real,” and forbade tattooing.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: The Prophet ﷺ used to perform incantations, saying: “I seek refuge in God's might and His power over all that He wills, from the evil of what I find in you.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar: Abū ʿUmar informed us and supplied a chain for us, saying that the Messenger of God ﷺ would perform an incantation with the words: “In the name of God the Mighty, I seek refuge in God the Great from the evil of every throbbing vein and from the evil of the heat of the Fire.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, that the Prophet ﷺ would blow lightly into his palms after reciting from the Qurʾān and then wipe his face with them.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Aʿmash, from Masrūq, from ʿĀʾisha, who said: When a member of his household fell ill, the Messenger of God ﷺ would say: “Remove the harm, Lord of humankind. Heal, for You are the Healer. Grant a healing that leaves no illness behind.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٧٨٣ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الْأَعْمَشِ، عَنْ مَسْرُوقٍ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، قَالَتْ: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ إِذَا مَرِضَ أَحَدٌ مِنْ أَهْلِهِ قَالَ:   «§أَذْهِبِ الْبَأْسَ رَبَّ النَّاسِ، وَاشْفِ أَنْتَ الشَّافِي، اشْفِ شِفَاءً لَا يُغَادِرُ سَقَمًا»
records.section_title_en: Healing Incantations, the Evil Eye, and Light Blowing

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: قَالَتْ: فَلَمَّا اشْتَكَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَثَقُلَ، أسْنَدْتُهُ إِلَى صَدْرِي، ثُمَّ مَسَحْتُ بِيَدِي عَلَى وَجْهِهِ وَقُلْتُ: أَذْهِبِ الْبَأْسَ كَمَا كَانَ يَقُولُ، قَالَتْ: وَأَخَّرَ يَدِي عَنْهُ، وَقَالَ:   «§رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي، وَاجْعَلْنِي فِي الرَّفِيقِ الْأَعْلَى»   ، قَالَتْ: ثُمَّ ثَقُلَ عَلَيَّ وَقُبِضَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: She said: When the Messenger of God ﷺ became ill and his condition worsened, I supported him against my chest and passed my hand over his face, saying, “Remove the harm,” as he had said. He pushed my hand away and said: “My Lord, forgive me, and place me among the highest company.” Then he grew heavy against me and the Messenger of God ﷺ died.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Abān, that the Prophet ﷺ was riding a mule when it shied. He told a man: “Recite over it, ‘Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak’” [Qurʾān 113:1].

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwa, from ʿĀʾisha, who said: “During the illness in which he died, the Messenger of God ﷺ would blow lightly upon himself while reciting the protective surahs (*al-muʿawwidhāt*).” Maʿmar said: I asked al-Zuhrī how he did this, and he said: “He blew into his hands and wiped his face with them.” ʿĀʾisha continued: “When his condition became grave, I recited them and blew upon him, wiping him with his own hand.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٧٨٥ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ عُرْوَةَ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، قَالَتْ:   «كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ §يَنْفُثُ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ فِي الْمَرَضِ الَّذِي قُبِضَ فِيهِ بِالْمُعَوِّذَاتِ»   - قَالَ مَعْمَرٌ: فَسَأَلْتُ الزُّهْرِيَّ: كَيْفَ كَانَ يَنْفُثُ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ؟ فَقَالَ: كَانْ يَنْفُثُ عَلَى يَدَيْهِ، وَيَمْسَحُ بِهِمَا وَجْهَهُ - قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ: فَلَمَّا ثَقُلَ جَعَلْتُ أَتْفُلُ عَلَيْهِ بِهِنَّ، وَأَمْسَحُهُ بِيَدِ نَفْسِهِ

records.text_en: We recited to ʿAbd al-Razzāq, from Maʿmar, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from an unnamed man, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Beware of sitting on the road”—or, as he sometimes said, “in the thoroughfares.” They replied, “Messenger of God, we must have places to gather.” He said: “Then give the road its due rights.” They asked, “What are its rights?” He replied: “Returning the greeting of peace, lowering the gaze, directing one who asks for directions, commanding what is right, and forbidding what is wrong.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٧٨٦ - قرأنا علي عبد الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، عَنْ رَجُلٍ، عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيِّ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ:   «§إِيَّاكُمْ وَالْجُلُوسَ عَلَى الطَّرِيقِ»   - وَرُبَّمَا قَالَ:   «الصُّعُدَاتِ»   - قَالُوا: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، لَا بُدَّ مِنْ مَجَالِسِنَا، قَالَ:   «فَأَدُّوا حَقَّهَا»   قَالُوا: وَمَا حَقُّهَا؟ قَالَ:   «رَدُّ السَّلَامِ، وَغَضُّ الْبَصَرِ، وَإِرْشَادُ السَّائِلِ، وَالْأَمْرُ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ، وَالنَّهْيُ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, who said: It used to be said: “You rarely find a Muslim except in one of three places: a mosque that he attends and maintains, a home in which he lives, or out seeking sustenance from his Lord's bounty.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, raising the report to the Prophet ﷺ: “No group ever gathers and then disperses without remembering God but that they have parted as though from a carcass.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatāda, who said: “When you converse at night, lower your voice. When you converse by day, look at who is around you.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Bishr ibn Rāfiʿ informed us: An elderly man of Ṣanʿāʾ called Abū ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, saying: I heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say to my father: “I found in the wisdom of the family of David: A rational person should not neglect four periods of time: a time to commune with his Lord; a time to take account of himself; a time to confide in brothers who tell him truthfully of his faults and give sincere advice for his welfare; and a time when he allows himself lawful and seemly pleasures. This last period helps sustain the others, refreshes the heart, and provides strength and provision. A rational person should travel only for one of three reasons: to prepare for the life to come, to repair his livelihood, or to enjoy a pleasure that is not forbidden. A rational person should understand his own time, restrain his tongue, and attend to his own affairs.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٧٩٠ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا بِشْرُ بْنُ رَافِعٍ، قَالَ: - [٢٢] - حَدَّثَنَا شَيْخٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ صَنْعَاءَ يُقَالُ لَهُ: أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ وَهْبَ بْنَ مُنَبِّهٍ يَقُولُ لِأَبِي: وَجَدْتُ فِي حِكْمَةِ آلِ دَاوُدَ: §عَلَى الْعَاقِلِ أَنْ لَا يُشْتَغَلَ عَنْ أَرْبَعِ سَاعَاتٍ: سَاعَةٍ يُنَاجِي فِيهَا رَبَّهُ، وَسَاعَةٍ يُحَاسِبُ فِيهَا نَفْسَهُ، وَسَاعَةٍ يُفْضِي فِيهَا إِلَى إِخْوَانِهِ الَّذِينَ يَصْدُقُونَهُ عُيُوبَهُ، وينْصَحُونَهُ فِي نَفْسِهِ، وَسَاعَةٍ يُخَلِّي فِيهَا بَيْنَ نَفْسِهِ وَبَيْنَ لذَّتِهَا مِمَّا يَحِلُّ وَيَجْمُلُ، فَإِنَّ هَذِهِ السَّاعَةَ عَوْنٌ لِهَذِهِ السَّاعَاتِ، واسْتِجْمَامٌ لِلْقُلُوبِ، وَفَضْلٌ وَبُلْغَةٌ، وَعَلَى الْعَاقِلِ أَنْ لَا يَكُونَ ظَاعِنًا إِلَّا فِي إِحْدَى ثَلَاثٍ: تَزوُّدٍ لِمَعَادٍ، أَوْ مَرَمَّةٍ لِمَعَاشٍ، أَوْ لَذَّةٍ فِي غَيْرِ مُحَرَّمٍ، وَعَلَى الْعَاقِلِ أَنْ يَكُونَ عَالِمًا بزَمَانِهِ، مُمْسِكًا لِلِسَانِهِ، مُقْبِلًا عَلَى شَانِهِ "

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Bishr ibn Rāfiʿ informed us: An elderly man of Ṣanʿāʾ called Abū ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, saying: I heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say to my father: “I found in the wisdom of the family of David: A rational person should not neglect four periods of time: a time to commune with his Lord; a time to take account of himself; a time to confide in brothers who tell him truthfully of his faults and give sincere advice for his welfare; and a time when he allows himself lawful and seemly pleasures. This last period helps sustain the others, refreshes the heart, and provides strength and provision. A rational person should travel only for one of three reasons: to prepare for the life to come, to repair his livelihood, or to enjoy a pleasure that is not forbidden. A rational person should understand his own time, restrain his tongue, and attend to his own affairs.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Jaḥshī, from Abū Bakr ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥazm, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “People who sit together do so under God's trust. It is not lawful for anyone to disclose about his companion something that the companion would dislike.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Sālim, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “None of you should make his brother get up from his seat and then sit in it himself.” He said: A man would voluntarily get up for Ibn ʿUmar, but Ibn ʿUmar would not sit in his place.
records.text_ar: ١٩٧٩٣ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ سَالِمٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ، قَالَ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§لَا يُقِمْ أَحَدُكُمْ أَخَاهُ مِنْ مَجْلِسِهِ ثُمَّ يَجْلِسُ فِيهِ»   ، قَالَ:   «وَكَانَ الرَّجُلُ يَقُومُ لِابْنِ عُمَرَ مِنْ نَفْسِهِ، فَمَا يَجْلِسُ فِي مَجْلِسِهِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Wuhayb ibn al-Ward, from Abān, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Whoever separates two people in a gathering out of arrogance toward them, let him take his seat in the Fire.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Jazarī, from Abū ʿUthmān al-Faqīr, that Gabriel, ﷺ, taught the Prophet ﷺ to say when rising from his gathering: “Glory and praise be to You, O God. I testify that there is no god except You, alone, without partner. I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance.” Maʿmar said: “I also heard someone else say that this declaration is an expiation for what takes place in a gathering.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٧٩٦ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الْكَرِيمِ الْجَزَرِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِي عُثْمَانَ الْفَقِيرِ، أَنَّ جِبْرِيلَ، عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ عَلَّمَ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ §إِذَا قَامَ مِنْ مَجْلِسِهِ أَنْ يَقُولَ:   «سُبْحَانَكَ اللَّهُمَّ وَبِحَمْدِكَ، أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، وَحْدَكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ، أَسْتَغْفِرُكَ وَأَتُوبُ إِلَيْكَ»   قَالَ مَعْمَرٌ:   «وَسَمِعْتُ غَيْرَهُ يَقُولُ: هَذَا الْقَوْلُ كَفَّارَةُ الْمَجْلِسِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Ayyūb, from Nāfiʿ or someone else, who said: Ibn ʿUmar was sitting with a group who wished to rise. A man said, “Rise upon the name of God [ʿalā ism God].” Ibn ʿUmar objected and said: “Say, ‘Rise in the name of God [bi-ism God].’”
records.text_ar: ١٩٧٩٨ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ نَافِعٍ، أَوْ غَيْرِهِ، قَالَ: كَانَ ابْنُ عُمَرَ جَالِسًا فِي نَفَرٍ، فَأَرَادُوا الْقِيَامَ، فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ: قُومُوا عَلَى اسْمِ اللَّهِ، فَأَنْكَرَ ذَلِكَ ابْنُ عُمَرَ وَقَالَ:   «§قُومُوا بِسْمِ اللَّهِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Abū Hurayra, who said: “When one of you is sitting in the shade and the shade withdraws from him, let him get up, for that is a seat of Satan.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٧٩٩ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْمُنْكَدِرِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ:   «§إِذَا كَانَ أَحَدُكُمْ فِي الْفَيْءِ فَقَلَصَ عَنْهُ، فَلْيَقُمْ فَإِنَّهُ مَجْلِسُ الشَّيْطَانِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, whom I heard say: “It is disliked for a person to sit with part of himself in the shade and part in the sun.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Abān, who said: I heard Ibn al-Munkadir transmit this hadith from Abū Hurayra while I myself was sitting partly in the shade and partly in the sun. When I heard it I got up, but Ibn al-Munkadir said to me: “Sit down; there is no harm for you, since that is how you were sitting already.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Abū Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, that a man among the People of the Bench said: The Prophet ﷺ invited me and a group of the People of the Bench to his home. When we entered, he said: “Give us something to eat, ʿĀʾisha.” She brought something, which they ate. Then he said: “Bring us some more, ʿĀʾisha.” She brought them a little more, less than the first portion. Then he said: “Give us something to drink, ʿĀʾisha.” She brought a cup of milk, and they drank. Then he said: “Bring us some more, ʿĀʾisha,” and she brought a bowl of milk. The Messenger of God ﷺ then said: “If you wish, you can sleep here; or, if you wish, in the mosque.” They said: “Rather, in the mosque.” We went out and slept in the mosque. Toward dawn my stomach became uncomfortable, so I lay on my stomach. Suddenly someone was nudging me with his foot and saying: “Not like this, for this is a way of lying down that God dislikes.” I lifted my head, and it was the Messenger of God ﷺ.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn, who said: “It is disliked for a man to lie on his stomach and for a woman to lie on her back.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Hārūn ibn Riʾāb, from Ibn al-Musayyib, concerning a man who comes with a litigant, giving the impression that he possesses testimony when he has none. He said: “He is a false witness.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: “Some people calculate with the letters of the alphabet [abjad] and study the stars. I do not think anyone who does that has any share [of good].”
records.text_ar: ١٩٨٠٥ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ طَاوُسٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ، قَالَ:   «§إِنَّ قَوْمًا يَحْسِبُونَ أَبَا جَادٍ، وَيَنْظُرُونَ فِي النُّجُومِ، وَلَا أَرَى لِمَنْ فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ مِنْ خَلَاقٍ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Ayyūb, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “When there are three of you, two must not converse privately to the exclusion of the third without his permission, for that would grieve him.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Abū al-Zinād, who said: Ibn Jarhad informed me, from his father, that the Messenger of God ﷺ passed a man whose thigh was uncovered. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Cover your thigh, for it is part of the nakedness [ʿawra].”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Ayyūb, from Ghaylān ibn Jarīr, from Abū al-Ḥalāl al-ʿAtakī, who said: I went to ʿUthmān and spoke to him about a need. When I spoke, he said to me: “Whatever you wish.” Then he said: “Rather, God has greater power to dispose of matters; rather, God has greater power.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Mughīra, from Ibrāhīm, who said: The Prophet ﷺ heard a man say: “Whoever obeys God and His Messenger has been rightly guided; and whoever disobeys the two of them has gone astray.” The Messenger of God's ﷺ face changed [in displeasure]. He said, explaining: “He should have said ‘God and His Messenger’ [separately],” rather than referring to both with a dual pronoun.
records.text_ar: ١٩٨١٠ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ مُغِيرَةَ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، قَالَ: سَمِعَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ رَجُلًا، يَقُولُ: §مَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَقَدْ رَشَدَ، وَمَنْ يَعْصِهِمَا فَقَدْ غَوَى، قَالَ: فَتَلَوَّنَ وَجْهُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ:   «يَعْنِي حَتَّى يَقُولَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, that during the Prophet's ﷺ lifetime a man dreamed that he passed a group of Jews and was impressed by their appearance. He said: “You would be a fine people, were it not that you say Ezra is God's son.” They replied: “And you would be a fine people, were it not that you say: ‘What God wills and what Muḥammad wills.’” He passed a group of Christians and was impressed by their appearance, and said: “You would be a fine people, were it not that you say the Messiah is God's son.” They replied: “And you would be a fine people, were it not that you say: ‘What God wills and what Muḥammad wills.’” The next morning he went to the Prophet ﷺ and told him. The Prophet ﷺ said: “I had been hearing you say that, and it troubled me. Do not say ‘What God wills and what Muḥammad wills’; say instead, ‘What God alone wills.’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik, that a Jewish woman presented the Prophet ﷺ with a roasted sheep at Khaybar. He asked: “What is this?” She said: “A gift,” taking care not to describe it as charity, which he would not eat. The Prophet ﷺ and his Companions ate. He then said: “Stop.” He asked the woman: “Did you poison this sheep?” She asked: “Who told you?” He replied: “This bone from its leg,” which was in his hand. She said: “Yes.” He asked: “Why?” She answered: “I wanted, if you were lying, for people to be relieved of you; but if you were a prophet, it would not harm you.” The Prophet ﷺ had cupping performed at the upper back, and instructed his Companions to undergo cupping. Some of them died. Al-Zuhrī said: “She accepted Islam, and the Prophet ﷺ let her go.” Maʿmar said: “As for other people, they say that the Prophet ﷺ killed her.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٨١٤ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ كَعْبِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، أَنَّ امْرَأَةً يَهُودِيَّةً أَهْدَتْ لِلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ شَاةً مَصْلِيَّةً بِخَيْبَرَ، فَقَالَ:   «مَا هَذِهِ؟»   قَالَتْ: هَدِيَّةٌ، وحَذِرَتْ أَنْ تَقُولَ: هِيَ مِنَ الصَّدَقَةِ، فَلَا يَأْكُلَ، قَالَ: فَأَكَلَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، وَأَكَلَ أَصْحَابُهُ، ثُمَّ قَالَ:   «أَمْسِكُوا»   ، فَقَالَ لِلْمَرْأَةِ:   «§هَلْ سَمَّمْتِ هَذِهِ الشَّاةَ؟»   قَالَتْ: مَنْ أَخْبَرَكَ؟ قَالَ:   «هَذَا الْعَظْمُ»   لِسَاقِهَا وَهُوَ فِي يَدِهِ، قَالَتْ: نَعَمْ، - [٢٩] - قَالَ:   «لِمَ؟»   قَالَتْ: أَرَدْتُ إِنْ كُنْتَ كَاذِبًا أَنْ يَسْتَرِيحَ مِنْكَ النَّاسُ، وَإِنْ كُنْتَ نَبِيًّا لَمْ يَضُرَّكَ. قَالَ: فَاحْتَجَمَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عَلَى الْكَاهِلِ، وَأَمَرَ أَصْحَابَهُ فَاحْتَجَمُوا، فَمَاتَ بَعْضُهُمْ، قَالَ الزُّهْرِيُّ:   «فَأَسْلَمَتْ فَتَرَكَهَا النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ»   . قَالَ مَعْمَرٌ:   «وَأَمَّا النَّاسُ فَيَقُولُونَ: قَتَلَهَا النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ»

records.display_matn_ar: أَنَّ امْرَأَةً يَهُودِيَّةً أَهْدَتْ لِلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ شَاةً مَصْلِيَّةً بِخَيْبَرَ، فَقَالَ:   «مَا هَذِهِ؟»   قَالَتْ: هَدِيَّةٌ، وحَذِرَتْ أَنْ تَقُولَ: هِيَ مِنَ الصَّدَقَةِ، فَلَا يَأْكُلَ، قَالَ: فَأَكَلَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، وَأَكَلَ أَصْحَابُهُ، ثُمَّ قَالَ:   «أَمْسِكُوا»   ، فَقَالَ لِلْمَرْأَةِ:   «§هَلْ سَمَّمْتِ هَذِهِ الشَّاةَ؟»   قَالَتْ: مَنْ أَخْبَرَكَ؟ قَالَ:   «هَذَا الْعَظْمُ»   لِسَاقِهَا وَهُوَ فِي يَدِهِ، قَالَتْ: نَعَمْ، قَالَ:   «لِمَ؟»   قَالَتْ: أَرَدْتُ إِنْ كُنْتَ كَاذِبًا أَنْ يَسْتَرِيحَ مِنْكَ النَّاسُ، وَإِنْ كُنْتَ نَبِيًّا لَمْ يَضُرَّكَ. قَالَ: فَاحْتَجَمَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عَلَى الْكَاهِلِ، وَأَمَرَ أَصْحَابَهُ فَاحْتَجَمُوا، فَمَاتَ بَعْضُهُمْ، قَالَ الزُّهْرِيُّ:   «فَأَسْلَمَتْ فَتَرَكَهَا النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ»   . قَالَ مَعْمَرٌ:   «وَأَمَّا النَّاسُ فَيَقُولُونَ: قَتَلَهَا النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik, that Umm Mubashshir said to the Prophet ﷺ during his final illness: “What do you suspect is causing your illness, Messenger of God? I suspect nothing concerning my son except the roasted sheep he ate with you at Khaybar.” The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “I, too, suspect nothing else concerning myself. Now is the time when my aorta is being severed,” meaning the large blood vessel.
records.text_ar: ١٩٨١٥ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنِ ابْنِ كَعْبِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، أَنَّ أُمَّ مُبَشِّرٍ، قَالَتْ لِلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فِي الْمَرَضِ الَّذِي مَاتَ فِيهِ: مَا تَتَّهِمُ بِنَفْسِكَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، فَإِنِّي لَا أَتَّهِمُ بِابْنِي إِلَّا الشَّاةَ الْمَشْوِيَّةَ الَّتِي أَكَلَ مَعَكَ بِخَيْبَرَ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «وَأَنَا لَا أَتَّهِمُ إِلَّا ذَلِكَ بِنَفْسِي، §هَذَا أَوَانُ قَطْعِ أَبْهَرِي»   يَعْنِي عِرْقَ الْوَرِيدِ

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us: A man from Basra named al-Mughīra ibn Ḥabīb told me: I came to Medina and found an old man undergoing cupping on his head. He said: “This is a blessed site for cupping, where the Messenger of God ﷺ underwent it.” He also said: “It is beneficial for leprosy, vitiligo, toothache, eye pain, headache and drowsiness. The cupper should make only three draws; if much blood comes out, put your hand upon it” — meaning the affected place [the last expression is textually uncertain]. Maʿmar said: “I had cupping done there and was cut badly. I got up unable to recall even a letter of the Qurʾān, so that when I was praying I had to ask somebody to prompt me. Then God took that affliction away, and I never had cupping done there again.”

Then God took that affliction away, and I never had cupping done there again.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ underwent cupping and paid the cupper his fee.” If it had been unlawful earnings, the Messenger of God ﷺ would not have paid him.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from a man — I think he attributed it to the Prophet ﷺ — who said: “The Arabs have not treated themselves with anything better than a cupper's draw or a drink of honey.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Ayyūb, from ʿIkrima and Khālid ibn Ṣafwān ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: Ṣafwān ibn Umayya married and invited ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb to his house, which had been hung with patterned leather coverings. ʿUmar said: “If you had put coarse cloths in place of these, they would have caught the dust better than these.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from someone who heard al-Ḥasan say: ʿUmar learned that a woman of Basra named Khaḍrāʾ had adorned her house with hangings. He wrote to Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī: “To proceed: I have learned that al-Khuḍayrāʾ has decorated her home. When my letter reaches you, tear down its hangings — may God tear them down.” Al-Ashʿarī went with several men and entered the house. They stood in different parts of it and he said: “Let each of you tear down what is nearest to him, God have mercy on you.” They did so and then departed.

records.matn_en: ʿUmar learned that a woman of Basra named Khaḍrāʾ had adorned her house with hangings. He wrote to Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī: “To proceed: I have learned that al-Khuḍayrāʾ has decorated her home. When my letter reaches you, tear down its hangings — may God tear them down.” Al-Ashʿarī went with several men and entered the house. They stood in different parts of it and he said: “Let each of you tear down what is nearest to him, God have mercy on you.” They did so and then departed.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Nāfiʿ, who said: News reached ʿUmar that Ṣafiyya, the wife of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, had hung her rooms with a patterned curtain or something similar that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar had given her. ʿUmar went intending to tear it down; but they heard he was coming and removed it. When he arrived, he found nothing and said: “What is wrong with people who bring us false reports?”
records.text_ar: ١٩٨٢٢ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ نَافِعٍ، قَالَ: بَلَغَ عُمَرَ، أَنَّ صَفِيَّةَ، امْرَأَةَ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ سَتَرَتْ بُيُوتَهَا بِقِرَامٍ، أَوْ غَيْرِهِ أَهْدَاهُ لَهَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عُمَرَ، فَذَهَبَ عُمَرُ وَهُوَ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَهتِكَهُ، فَبَلَغَهُمْ فَنَزَعُوهُ، فَلَمَّا جَاءَ عُمَرُ لَمْ يَجِدْ شَيْئًا فَقَالَ:   «§مَا بَالُ أَقْوَامٍ يَأْتُونَنَا بِالْكَذِبِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, who said: When Ibn al-Zubayr entered upon his wife, al-Ḥusayn's daughter, he found three mattresses in the room. He said: “This one is for me, this one for her, and the third is for Satan. Take it out of here.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from a man whom he named, that Muḥammad ibn ʿAbbād ibn Jaʿfar told him: The Messenger of God ﷺ was invited to a meal. When he arrived, the house was dark and lavishly decorated. He stood at the door and said: “Green and red,” enumerating its colors; then he said: “If only it had been one color!” He turned away without entering.

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from a man whom he named, that Muḥammad ibn ʿAbbād ibn Jaʿfar told him: The Messenger of God ﷺ was invited to a meal. When he arrived, the house was dark and lavishly decorated. He stood at the door and said: “Green and red,” enumerating its colors; then he said: “If only it had been one color!” He turned away without entering.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ḥarām ibn ʿUthmān, from Ibn Jābir, from Jābir, that the Prophet ﷺ forbade leaving rubbish in a room, saying that it is a sitting place for Satan; leaving in the house a cloth used to wipe food from the hands; and sitting or lying on saddle pads [walāyā].

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid, from Kaʿb, who said: When a man leaves his house and says, “In the name of God,” an angel tells him: “You have been guided.” When he says, “I place my trust in God,” the angel tells him: “You have been provided for.” When he says, “There is no power and no strength except through God,” the angel tells him: “You have been protected.” The devils then disperse, saying: “You have no way to reach him; he has been guided, provided for, and protected.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٨٢٧ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ مَنْصُورٍ، عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ، عَنْ كَعْبٍ، قَالَ: إِذَا خَرَجَ الرَّجُلُ مِنْ بَيْتِهِ فَقَالَ:   «§بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، قَالَ لَهُ الْمَلَكُ: هُدِيتَ. وَإِذَا قَالَ: تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اللَّهِ، قَالَ لَهُ الْمَلَكُ: كُفِيتَ، وَإِذَا قَالَ: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ. قَالَ الْمَلَكُ: وُقِيتَ. قَالَ: فتَتَفَرَّقُ الشَّيَاطِينُ فَتَقُولُ: لَا سَبِيلَ لَكُمْ إِلَيْهِ، إِنَّهُ قَدْ هُدِيَ وَكُفِيَ وَوُقِيَ»

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid, from Kaʿb, who said: When a man leaves his house and says, “In the name of God,” an angel tells him: “You have been guided.” When he says, “I place my trust in God,” the angel tells him: “You have been provided for.” When he says, “There is no power and no strength except through God,” the angel tells him: “You have been protected.” The devils then disperse, saying: “You have no way to reach him; he has been guided, provided for, and protected.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, who said: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn informed me that Fāṭima, the daughter of the Messenger of God ﷺ, came to him asking for a servant from captives who had been brought, and there were marks on her hand from the handle of the millstone because of all her grinding. He said to her: “I will tell you something better than that. When you go to bed, glorify God thirty-three times, praise God thirty-three times, and magnify God thirty-three times; then say ‘There is no god but God’ to complete one hundred.” She returned with that instruction, and he gave her no servant. Maʿmar said: I also heard Makḥūl transmit something similar, adding that ʿAlī said: “I never neglected these words from the time the Messenger of God ﷺ instructed Fāṭima to say them, not even on the Night of the Clamor at Ṣiffīn.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Abū Isḥāq, who said: I heard al-Barāʾ say: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ instruct a man, when retiring to bed at night, to say: “O God, I submit myself to You, direct my face toward You, entrust my affair to You, and lean my back upon You, in fear of You and hope in You. records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from ʿUbayd God ibn ʿUmar, from Saʿīd al-Maqburī, from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “When one of you rises during the night and returns to his bed, let him dust off his bed with the inside of his waist-wrapper, for he does not know what has occupied it in his absence. Then let him say: ‘In Your name, my Lord, I lay down my side, and in Your name I raise it. O God, if You take my soul, forgive it; and if You release it, protect it as You protect the righteous.’”
records.text_ar: ١٩٨٣٠ - أخبرنا عبد الرزاق عن معمر عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ، عَنْ سَعِيدٍ الْمَقْبُرِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§إِذَا قَامَ أَحَدُكُمْ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ ثُمَّ رَجَعَ إِلَى فِرَاشِهِ فَلْيَنْفُضْ فِرَاشَهُ بِدَاخِلَةِ إِزَارِهِ، فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَدْرِي مَا خَلَفَهُ بَعْدَهُ، ثُمَّ لْيَقُلْ: بِاسْمِكَ رَبِّ وَضَعْتُ جَنْبِي، وَبِاسْمِكَ أَرْفَعُهُ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنْ أَمْسَكْتَ نَفْسِي فَاغْفِرْ لَهَا، وَإِنْ أَرْسَلْتَهَا فَاحْفَظْهَا بِمَا تَحْفَظُ بِهِ الصَّالِحِينَ»

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from ʿUbayd God ibn ʿUmar, from Saʿīd al-Maqburī, from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “When one of you rises during the night and returns to his bed, let him dust off his bed with the inside of his waist-wrapper, for he does not know what has occupied it in his absence. Then let him say: ‘In Your name, my Lord, I lay down my side, and in Your name I raise it. O God, if You take my soul, forgive it; and if You release it, protect it as You protect the righteous.’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, from Abū Rāfiʿ, that Khālid ibn al-Walīd came to the Prophet ﷺ complaining of a feeling of dread that he experienced. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: “Shall I teach you what the Trustworthy Spirit, Gabriel, taught me? He said to me: ‘A powerful jinn is plotting against you. When you go to bed, say: I seek refuge in the perfect words of God, which neither the righteous nor the wicked can transgress, from the evil of whatever descends from heaven and whatever ascends into it, from the evil of what He has spread throughout the earth and of what emerges from it, and from the evil of the visitations of night and day, and from the evil of every visitor who comes by night, except a visitor who comes with good, O Most Merciful.’”
records.text_ar: ١٩٨٣١ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي رَافِعٍ، أَنَّ خَالِدَ بْنَ الْوَلِيدِ، جَاءَ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَشَكَا إِلَيْهِ وَحْشَةً يجِدُهَا، فَقَالَ لَهُ:   «أَلَا أُعَلِّمُكَ مَا عَلَّمَنِي الرُّوحُ الْأَمِينُ جِبْرِيلُ قَالَ لِي: إِنَّ عِفْرِيتًا مِنَ الْجِنِّ يَكِيدُكَ، §فَإِذَا أَوَيْتَ إِلَى فِرَاشِكَ فَقُلْ: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ الَّتِي لَا يُجَاوِزُهُنَّ بَرٌّ وَلَا فَاجِرٌ، مِنْ شَرِّ مَا يَنْزِلُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ، وَمِنْ شَرِّ مَا يَعْرُجُ فِيهَا، وَمِنْ شَرِّ مَا ذَرَأَ فِي الْأَرْضِ، وَمِنْ شَرِّ مَا يَخْرُجُ مِنْهَا، وَمِنْ شَرِّ طَوَارِقِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ، وَمِنْ شَرِّ كُلِّ طَارِقٍ يَطْرُقُ إِلَّا طَارِقًا يَطْرُقُ بِخَيْرٍ يَا رَحْمَانُ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Suhayl ibn Abī Ṣāliḥ, from his father, from a man of Aslam, who said: A scorpion stung a man, and word reached the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “If he had said in the evening, ‘I seek refuge in the perfect words of God from the evil of what He has created,’ it would not have harmed him.” The narrator said: A woman of my family recited those words and was bitten by a snake, but it did not harm her.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, who said: It has reached me that if someone says morning and evening, “O God, I seek refuge in You from the evil of poisonous things and dangerous creatures and from the evil of what You have created,” no creature will harm him.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Jaʿfar ibn Burqān, that Jesus son of Mary used to say: “O God, I have begun this morning unable to avert what I dislike and unable to secure the benefit I hope for. My affair is in another's hand, and I am held in pledge by my own deeds. No poor person is poorer than I. O God, do not allow my enemy to rejoice over my misfortune, do not cause my friend distress through me, do not make my calamity befall my religion, and do not give power over me to someone who will show me no mercy.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Saʿīd al-Jurayrī, from Abū al-Salīl, from Abū Marthad al-ʿIjlī, who said: “Whoever goes to bed in a state of ritual purity and falls asleep remembering God, his bed becomes a place of worship and he remains in prayer and remembrance until he wakes. Whoever goes to bed without ritual purity and falls asleep without remembering God, his bed becomes a grave and he remains like a corpse until he wakes.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, who mentioned it from a man, from ʿĀʾisha, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “The human being has three hundred and sixty joints. Whoever magnifies God, praises God, and declares His oneness that number of times in a day will reach evening having been removed from the Fire.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from a man, from al-Ḥasan, that Saʿīd ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ married a former wife of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. He said: “I did not marry you out of desire for women, but so that you would tell me about ʿUmar's habits.” She replied: “When he went to bed at night, he would place a vessel of water beside him. If he stirred during the night, he would take some of the water, wipe his hands and face, and then remember God.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd God ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtba, attributing it to the Prophet ﷺ: “Whoever sleeps with traces of greasy food on his hand and then suffers a misfortune should blame no one but himself.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Jazarī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ noticed the smell of food grease on a man and said: “Why did you not wash this grease off yourself?”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from a man who asked al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtayba: “May a man sleep without ablution?” He said: “It is disliked, though we ourselves do it.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Aʿmash, who urinated and then performed dry ablution against the walls. When questioned about it, he said: “I fear that death might overtake me before I perform ablution.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh, who said: Abū Yaḥyā informed me that he heard Mujāhid say: Ibn ʿAbbās said to me: “Never sleep except in a state of ablution, for souls are raised in the condition in which they were taken.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “When a person sleeps, three knots are tied near his head by Satan's work. When he wakes and remembers God, one knot is untied; when he performs ablution, another is untied; when he prays, the third is untied. He reaches morning cheerful, wishing he had done still more.” He said: “A person is awakened three times in the night. At the first awakening Satan comes and says, ‘You still have the night ahead of you; sleep.’ If he obeys Satan, he sleeps. Then he is awakened a second time, and Satan again says, ‘You still have the night ahead of you; sleep.’ If he obeys, he sleeps. His knots remain as they were, and he reaches morning ill-tempered — or he said sluggish — regretting his neglect. That is the one in whose ears Satan urinates.”

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “When a person sleeps, three knots are tied near his head by Satan's work. When he wakes and remembers God, one knot is untied; when he performs ablution, another is untied; when he prays, the third is untied. He reaches morning cheerful, wishing he had done still more.” He said: “A person is awakened three times in the night. At the first awakening Satan comes and says, ‘You still have the night ahead of you; sleep.’ If he obeys Satan, he sleeps. Then he is awakened a second time, and Satan again says, ‘You still have the night ahead of you; sleep.’ If he obeys, he sleeps. His knots remain as they were, and he reaches morning ill-tempered — or he said sluggish — regretting his neglect. That is the one in whose ears Satan urinates.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Is there not a man who will rise at night and recite ten verses, so that by morning a hundred good deeds will have been recorded for him? Is there not a righteous man who will wake his wife at night, and if she does not get up will sprinkle her face with water, so that the two of them stand before God for a time during the night?”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Dāwūd ibn Ibrāhīm, that a lion blocked the pilgrims' route one night, separating the travelers from one another. Toward dawn it went away. People lay down to the right and left and fell asleep, but Ṭāwūs stood in prayer. A man said to him: “Will you not sleep? You have exhausted yourself tonight.” Ṭāwūs replied: “Is the time just before dawn a time for sleeping?”
records.text_ar: ١٩٨٤٨ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ دَاوُدَ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّ الْأَسَدَ حَبَسَ النَّاسَ لَيْلَةً فِي طَرِيقِ الْحَجِّ، فَرَّقَ النَّاسُ بَعْضُهُمْ بَعْضًا، فَلَمَّا كَانَ فِي السَّحَرِ ذَهَبَ عَنْهُمْ، فَنَزَلَ النَّاسُ يَمِينًا وَشِمَالًا، فَأَلْقَوْا أَنْفُسَهُمْ فَنَامُوا، وَقَامَ طَاوُسٌ يُصَلِّي، فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ لِطَاوُسٍ: أَلَا تَنَامُ، فَإِنَّكَ قَدْ نَصِبْتَ اللَّيْلَةَ، قَالَ: فَقَالَ طَاوُسٌ:   «§وَهَلْ يُنَامُ السَّحَرُ؟»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, that a man named al-Ḥubāb was renamed ʿAbd Allāh by the Messenger of God ﷺ, who said: “Al-Ḥubāb is a name of Satan.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, who said: I asked Ḥammād ibn Abī Sulaymān, “What do you say about a man being named Jibrīl or Mīkāʾīl?” He replied: “There is no harm in it.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Ibn al-Musayyib, from his father, that the Prophet ﷺ asked him: “What is your name?” He replied: “Ḥazn [Roughness].” The Prophet ﷺ said: “Rather, you are Sahl [Ease].” He answered: “I will not change a name my father gave me.” Ibn al-Musayyib said: “Roughness remained among us thereafter.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٨٥١ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنِ ابْنِ الْمُسَيِّبِ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ:   «§مَا اسْمُكَ؟»   قَالَ: حَزْنٌ، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «بَلْ أَنْتَ سَهْلٌ»   ، قَالَ: لَا أُغَيِّرُ اسْمًا سَمَّانِيهِ أَبِي، قَالَ ابْنُ الْمُسَيِّبِ: فَمَا زَالَتْ فِينَا حُزُونَةٌ بَعْدُ

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, that ʿUthmān addressed al-Furāfiṣa al-Ḥanafī by his kunya although he was a Christian, saying: “We have a greater duty to be mindful of this, Abū Ḥassān.” [The referent of “this” is not specified in the transmitted extract.]

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Simāk ibn al-Faḍl, from ʿIkrima, that a man said in the Prophet's ﷺ presence: “Get up and milk this she-camel, Murra [Bitterness].” The Prophet ﷺ said: “Sit down, Murra.” The other man again said: “Get up and milk her, Murra.” The Prophet ﷺ again said: “Sit down, Murra.” It was as though he disliked the name.
records.text_ar: ١٩٨٥٤ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ سِمَاكِ بْنِ الْفَضْلِ، عَنْ عِكْرِمَةَ، أَنَّ رَجُلًا، قَالَ عِنْدَ النَّبِيِّ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ  قُمْ فَاحْلُبْ هَذِهِ النَّاقَةَ يَا مُرَّةُ، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «اجْلِسْ يَا مُرَّةُ»   فَقَالَ الْآخَرُ: قُمْ فَاحْلُبْهَا يَا مُرَّةُ، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§اجْلِسْ يَا مُرَّةُ»   ، كَأَنَّهُ كَرِهَ الِاسْمَ

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn, who said: A letter came to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb from a Persian landed official called Jawānānbeh. ʿUmar wished to reply and asked: “Translate his name for me.” They said: “In Arabic it means ‘The Best of Young Men.’” ʿUmar said: “There are names by which people should not be named. Write: ‘From the servant of God, ʿUmar, Commander of the Believers, to the Worst of Young Men.’”
records.text_ar: ١٩٨٥٥ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنِ ابْنِ سِيرِينَ، قَالَ: أَتَى عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ كِتَابٌ مِنْ دِهْقَانٍ يُقَالُ لَهُ جوانانبه فَأَرَادَ عُمَرُ أَنْ يَكْتُبَ إِلَيْهِ، فَقَالَ:   «تَرْجِمُوا لِي اسْمَهُ؟»   ، فَقَالُوا: هَذَا بِالْعَرَبِيَّةِ خَيْرُ الْفِتْيَانِ، فَقَالَ عُمَرُ:   «إِنَّ §مِنَ الْأَسْمَاءِ أَسْمَاءً لَا يَنْبَغِي أَنْ يُسَمَّى بِهَا، اكْتُبْ مِنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عُمَرَ أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِلَى شَرِّ الْفِتْيَانِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, that a son of ʿUmar took the kunya Abū ʿĪsā, but ʿUmar forbade him from doing so.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, that ʿĀʾisha said to the Prophet ﷺ: “Messenger of God, all your wives except me have a kunya.” The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Take the kunya Umm ʿAbd Allāh.” She was called Umm ʿAbd Allāh until her death, although she never bore a child.
records.text_ar: ١٩٨٥٨ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، أَنَّ عَائِشَةَ، قَالَتْ لِلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ  يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، كُلُّ نِسَائِكَ لَهَا كُنْيَةٌ غَيْرِي، فَقَالَ لَهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§اكْتَنِي أَنْتِ أُمَّ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ»   ، فَكَانَ يُقَالُ لَهَا: أُمُّ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ حَتَّى مَاتَتْ وَلَمْ تَلِدْ قَطُّ

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Layth ibn Abī Sulaym, that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: “Do not give people the name al-Ḥakam or the kunya Abū al-Ḥakam, for God is the Judge [al-Ḥakam]. And do not call a road a sikka.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from a man of Kufa, who said: “The names most hateful to God are Mālik and Abū Mālik.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, who said: A man intended to name a son al-Walīd. The Prophet ﷺ forbade him and said: “There will be a man called al-Walīd who will do among my community what Pharaoh did among his people.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٨٦١ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، قَالَ: أَرَادَ رَجُلٌ أَنْ يُسَمِّيَ ابْنًا لَهُ الْوَلِيدَ، فَنَهَاهُ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَقَالَ:   «إِنَّهُ §سَيَكُونُ رَجُلٌ يُقَالُ لَهُ: الْوَلِيدُ يَعْمَلُ فِي أُمَّتِي كَمَا فَعَلَ فِرْعَوْنُ فِي قَوْمِهِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, that a place had been called “Remnant of Misguidance,” but the Prophet ﷺ renamed it “Remnant of Guidance.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٨٦٢ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، أَنَّ مَكَانًا، كَانَ اسْمُهُ بَقِيَّةَ الضَّلَالَةِ،   «§فَسَمَّاهُ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ بَقِيَّةَ الْهُدَى»

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: قَالَ: وَمَرَّ بِقَوْمٍ، فَقَالَ لَهُمْ:   «مَنْ أَنْتُمْ؟»   قَالُوا: بَنُو مُغْوِيَةَ،   «§فَسَمَّاهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ بَنُو رِشْدَةَ»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: He said: The Prophet ﷺ also passed a group and asked, “Who are you?” They replied: “The Sons of Mughwiya [Misguidance].” The Messenger of God ﷺ renamed them “The Sons of Rishda [Right Guidance].”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Sīrīn, that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf had been called ʿAbd al-Kaʿba before Islam, but the Messenger of God ﷺ renamed him ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. Ibn Sīrīn said: “Abū Bakr's name was ʿAtīq ibn ʿUthmān.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from a man, from Ibn al-Musayyib, that a man came to ʿUmar, who asked: “What is your name?” He said: “Jamra [Ember].” “Whose son?” “Ibn Shihāb [Flame].” “Where are you from?” “Al-Ḥarqa [the Burning Place].” “Where do you live?” “Ḥarrat al-Nār [the Lava Field of Fire].” “In which part?” “Dhāt al-Laẓā [the Blazing One].” ʿUmar said: “Hurry to your people, lest they burn!”
records.text_ar: ١٩٨٦٤ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ رَجُلٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ الْمُسَيِّبِ، أَنَّ رَجُلًا أَتَى عُمَرَ، فَقَالَ لَهُ عُمَرُ:   «§مَا اسْمُكَ؟»   قَالَ: جَمْرَةُ، فَقَالَ:   «ابْنُ مَنْ؟»   قَالَ: ابْنُ شِهَابٍ، قَالَ:   «مِنْ أَيْنَ أَنْتَ؟»   قَالَ مِنَ الْحَرْقَةِ،. قَالَ:   «أَيْنَ تَسْكُنُ؟»   قَالَ: حَرَّةَ النَّارِ، قَالَ:   «بِأَيِّهَا؟»   قَالَ: بِذَاتِ اللَّظَى، فَقَالَ عُمَرُ:   «أَدْرِكْ بِالْحَيِّ لَا يَحْتَرِقُوا»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Isḥāq ibn Rāshid, a man of al-Jazīra, that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: “What purifies a man's brotherly affection for another is to address him by the names he likes best, make room for him in a gathering, and greet him when he meets him.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٨٦٥ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ رَاشِدٍ - رَجُلٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْجَزِيرَةِ - أَنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ، قَالَ:   «§يُصَفِّي لِلْمَرْءِ وُدَّ أَخِيهِ، أَنْ يَدْعُوَهُ بِأَحَبِّ الْأَسْمَاءِ إِلَيْهِ، وَأَنْ يُوَسِّعَ لَهُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ، وَيُسَلِّمَ عَلَيْهِ إِذَا لَقِيَهُ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Manṣūr, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: A boy was born to a man of the Anṣār, and he named him al-Qāsim. The Anṣār said: “By God, we will never address you by that kunya.” This reached the Messenger of God ﷺ, who spoke well of the Anṣār and then said: “Name yourselves after my name, but do not take my kunya.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn, from Abū Hurayra, who said: “None of you should say ‘my male slave’ or ‘my female slave’; rather, let him say ‘my boy’ and ‘my girl.’ Nor should the enslaved person say ‘my lord’ or ‘my lady’; rather, let him say ‘my master’ and ‘my mistress.’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Sufyān, from Jābir, who said: Abū Ḥumayd al-Anṣārī came to the Messenger of God ﷺ carrying a cup of milk uncovered. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: “Why did you not cover it, even by laying a stick across it?”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, who said — I think he attributed it to the Prophet ﷺ: “Beware of going out after the night has grown still, for God has creatures that He scatters throughout the earth and that do as they are commanded. When one of you hears a donkey bray or a dog bark, let him seek refuge with God from Satan, for they see what you do not see.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٨٧٢ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ طَاوُسٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، قَالَ: لَا أُرَاهُ إِلَّا رَفَعَهُ، قَالَ:   «§إِيَّاكُمْ وَالْخُرُوجَ بَعْدَ هَدْأَةِ اللَّيْلِ، فَإِنَّ لِلَّهِ دَوَابَّ يَبُثُّهَا فِي الْأَرْضِ تَفْعَلُ مَا تُؤْمَرُ بِهِ، فَإِذَا سَمِعَ أَحَدُكُمْ نَهِيقَ حِمَارٍ، أَوْ نُبَاحَ كَلْبٍ فَلْيَسْتَعِذْ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ فَإِنَّهُمْ يَرَوْنَ مَا لَا تَرَوْنَ»

records.display_matn_ar: إِيَّاكُمْ وَالْخُرُوجَ بَعْدَ هَدْأَةِ اللَّيْلِ، فَإِنَّ لِلَّهِ دَوَابَّ يَبُثُّهَا فِي الْأَرْضِ تَفْعَلُ مَا تُؤْمَرُ بِهِ، فَإِذَا سَمِعَ أَحَدُكُمْ نَهِيقَ حِمَارٍ، أَوْ نُبَاحَ كَلْبٍ فَلْيَسْتَعِذْ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ فَإِنَّهُمْ يَرَوْنَ مَا لَا تَرَوْنَ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ instructed that doors be closed, lamps put out, vessels covered, and waterskins tied, “for Satan does not open a closed door, untie a cord, or uncover a vessel; and a little mischief-making creature [a mouse] can approach a lamp, take hold of its wick, and set the household on fire.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٨٧٣ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، عَنْ جَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، قَالَ:   «أَمَرَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ بِأَنْ §تُجَافَ الْأَبْوَابُ، وتُطْفَى الْمَصَابِيحُ، وَتُخَمَّرَ الْآنِيَةُ، وَتُوكَى الْأَوْعِيَةُ، فَإِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ لَا يَفْتَحُ غَلَقًا، وَلَا يَحِلُّ وِكَاءً، وَلَا يَكْشِفُ غِطَاءً، وَإِنَّ الْفُوَيْسِقَةَ تَأْتِي الْمِصْبَاحَ فَتَأْخُذُ الْفَتِيلَةَ فَتُحَرِّقُ عَلَى أَهْلِ الْبَيْتِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Jaḥshī, from Abū Bakr ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥazm, from al-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb would pass by us at midday, or shortly before it, and say: “Get up and take your midday rest; the rest [of this time] belongs to Satan.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Nāfiʿ, who said: Ibn ʿUmar used to travel from Mecca to Medina in four nights, with his riding animal at the pass of Harshā; but when he grew old he took six nights.
records.text_ar: ١٩٨٧٥ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ نَافِعٍ، قَالَ:   «كَانَ ابْنُ عُمَرَ §يَسِيرُ مِنْ مَكَّةَ إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ أَرْبَعَ لَيَالٍ، وَرَاحِلَتُهُ فِي عَقَبَةِ هَرْشَى، فَلَمَّا كَبُرَ سَارَ سِتًّا»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Layth, from a man, from ʿAlqama ibn Qays, who said: “It has reached us that the earth cries out to God because of a scholar sleeping after the dawn prayer.”

records.text_en: Abū Yaʿqūb Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn, from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Aslam, Ghifār, and some of Juhayna and Muzayna will be better in God's sight on the Day of Resurrection than Tamīm, Asad ibn Khuzayma, Hawāzin, and Ghaṭafān.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٨٧٧ - قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو يَعْقُوبَ إِسْحَاقُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنِ ابْنِ سِيرِينَ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§أَسْلَمُ، وَغِفَارٌ، وَشَيْءٌ مِنْ جُهَيْنَةَ، وَمُزَيْنَةَ خَيْرٌ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ مِنْ تَمِيمٍ، وَأَسَدِ بْنِ خُزَيْمَةَ، وَهَوَازِنَ، وَغَطَفَانَ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Abū Hammām al-Shaʿbānī, from a man of Khathʿam who was among the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ, who said: We accompanied the Prophet ﷺ on the expedition to Tabūk. One night he halted, and his Companions gathered around him. He said: “God has given me the two treasuries, that of Persia and that of Rome, and has supported me by kings, the kings of Ḥimyar. Sovereignty belongs to God alone. They will come and take God's wealth and fight in God's cause.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٨٧٨ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ أَبِي كَثِيرٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هَمَّامٍ الشَّعْبَانِيِّ، عَنْ رَجُلٍ مِنْ خَثْعَمٍ، مِنْ أَصْحَابِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، قَالَ: كُنَّا مَعَ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فِي غَزْوَةِ تَبُوكَ، فَوَقَفَ ذَاتَ لَيْلَةٍ وَاجْتَمَعَ إِلَيْهِ أَصْحَابُهُ، فَقَالَ:   «إِنَّ §اللَّهَ أَعْطَانِي الْكَنْزَيْنِ، كَنْزَ فَارِسَ وَالرُّومِ، وَأَيَّدَنِي بِالْمُلُوكِ، مُلُوكِ حِمْيَرَ، وَلَا مُلْكَ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ، يَأْتُونَ فَيَأْخُذُونَ مَالَ اللَّهِ، وَيُقَاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ»

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Abū Hammām al-Shaʿbānī, from a man of Khathʿam who was among the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ, who said: We accompanied the Prophet ﷺ on the expedition to Tabūk. One night he halted, and his Companions gathered around him. He said: “God has given me the two treasuries, that of Persia and that of Rome, and has supported me by kings, the kings of Ḥimyar. Sovereignty belongs to God alone. They will come and take God's wealth and fight in God's cause.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatāda, who said: “Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī came to the Prophet ﷺ accompanied by eighty men of his people, whereas not even ten men from Banū Tamīm came to the Prophet ﷺ.” Qatāda added: “And no one from Bakr ibn Wāʾil traveled to the Messenger of God ﷺ.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from a man, who said: Al-Shaʿbī passed a man of Banū Asad and a man of Qays. The man of Asad was trying to free himself from the other's grip, but the other would not let him go, saying: “No, by God, not until I tell you about your people and you learn who you are.” Al-Shaʿbī told him to let the man go, but he refused. Al-Shaʿbī said: “Leave him; by my life, he has things to boast about if only he knew them.” When the man continued to refuse, al-Shaʿbī made both of them sit down and sat with them. He asked the man of Qays: “Was the first banner raised in Islam among your people?” “No,” the man replied. “It was among Banū Asad. Was the first booty taken in Islam among you?” “No.” “It was among Banū Asad. Was one-seventh of the emigrants at Badr from among you?” “No.” “That too was from Banū Asad. Was there among you a man whom the Messenger of God ﷺ gave glad tidings of Paradise?” “No.” “That man was among Banū Asad. Was there among you a woman whose marriage was concluded by God from heaven, with the Messenger of God ﷺ as the suitor and Gabriel as the envoy?” “No.” “That was among Banū Asad. Leave the man alone; by my life, he has reason to take pride if only he knew it.” The other man then left him alone.

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from a man, who said: Al-Shaʿbī passed a man of Banū Asad and a man of Qays. The man of Asad was trying to free himself from the other's grip, but the other would not let him go, saying: “No, by God, not until I tell you about your people and you learn who you are.” Al-Shaʿbī told him to let the man go, but he refused. Al-Shaʿbī said: “Leave him; by my life, he has things to boast about if only he knew them.” When the man continued to refuse, al-Shaʿbī made both of them sit down and sat with them. He asked the man of Qays: “Was the first banner raised in Islam among your people?” “No,” the man replied. “It was among Banū Asad. Was the first booty taken in Islam among you?” “No.” “It was among Banū Asad. Was one-seventh of the emigrants at Badr from among you?” “No.” “That too was from Banū Asad. Was there among you a man whom the Messenger of God ﷺ gave glad tidings of Paradise?” “No.” “That man was among Banū Asad. Was there among you a woman whose marriage was concluded by God from heaven, with the Messenger of God ﷺ as the suitor and Gabriel as the envoy?” “No.” “That was among Banū Asad. Leave the man alone; by my life, he has reason to take pride if only he knew it.” The other man then left him alone.

records.display_matn_ar: مَرَّ الشَّعْبِيُّ بِرَجُلٍ مِنْ بَنِي أَسَدٍ، وَرَجُلٍ مِنْ قَيْسٍ، فَجَعَلَ الْأَسَدِيُّ يَتَقَلَّبُ مِنْهُ وَلَا يَدَعُهُ الْآخَرُ، قَالَ:   «لَا وَاللَّهِ حَتَّى أُعَرِّفَكَ قَوْمَكَ، وَتَعْرِفَ مِمَّنْ أَنْتَ»   ، قَالَ: فَقَالَ لَهُ الشَّعْبِيُّ: دَعِ الرَّجُلَ، قَالَ:   «لَا، حَتَّى أُعَرِّفَهُ قَوْمَهُ وَنَفْسَهُ»   ، قَالَ: دَعْهُ فَلَعَمْرِي إِنَّهُ لَيَجِدُ مَفْخَرًا لَوْ كَانَ يَعْلَمُ، قَالَ: فَأَبَى، قَالَ الشَّعْبِيُّ: فَاجْلِسَا، وَجَلَسَ مَعَهُمَا الشَّعْبِيُّ فَقَالَ: يَا أَخَا قَيْسٍ، أَكَانَ فِيكُمْ أَوَّلُ رَايَةٍ عُقِدَتْ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ؟ قَالَ: لَا، قَالَ: فَإِنَّ ذَلِكَ قَدْ كَانَ فِي بَنِي أَسَدٍ، قَالَ: فَهَلْ كَانَتْ فِيكُمْ أَوَّلُ غَنِيمَةٍ كَانَتْ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ؟ قَالَ: لَا، قَالَ: فَإِنَّ ذَلِكَ قَدْ كَانَ فِي بَنِي أَسَدٍ، قَالَ: فَهَلْ كَانَ فِيكُمْ سُبُعُ الْمُهَاجِرِينَ يَوْمَ بَدْرٍ؟ قَالَ: لَا، قَالَ: فَإِنَّ ذَلِكَ قَدْ كَانَ فِي بَنِي أَسَدٍ، قَالَ:   «§فَهَلْ كَانَ فِيكُمْ رَجُلٌ بَشَّرَهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ بِالْجَنَّةِ؟»   قَالَ: لَا، قَالَ:   «فَإِنَّ ذَلِكَ قَدْ كَانَ فِي بَنِي أَسَدٍ»   ، قَالَ:   «فَهَلْ كَانَتْ مِنْكُمُ امْرَأَةٌ زَوَّجَهَا اللَّهُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ، كَانَ الْخَاطِبُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، وَالسَّفِيرُ جِبْرِيلَ؟»   ، قَالَ: لَا، قَالَ:   «فَقَدْ كَانَ ذَلِكَ فِي بَنِي أَسَدٍ»   ، خَلِّ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ، فَلَعَمْرِي إِنَّهُ لَيَجِدُ مَفْخَرًا، لَوْ كَانَ يَعْلَمُ، قَالَ: فَانْطَلَقَ الرَّجُلُ وَتَرَكَهُ
records.display_isnad_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from a man, who said:
records.display_matn_en: Al-Shaʿbī passed a man of Banū Asad and a man of Qays. The man of Asad was trying to free himself from the other's grip, but the other would not let him go, saying: “No, by God, not until I tell you about your people and you learn who you are.” Al-Shaʿbī told him to let the man go, but he refused. Al-Shaʿbī said: “Leave him; by my life, he has things to boast about if only he knew them.” When the man continued to refuse, al-Shaʿbī made both of them sit down and sat with them. He asked the man of Qays: “Was the first banner raised in Islam among your people?” “No,” the man replied. “It was among Banū Asad. Was the first booty taken in Islam among you?” “No.” “It was among Banū Asad. Was one-seventh of the emigrants at Badr from among you?” “No.” “That too was from Banū Asad. Was there among you a man whom the Messenger of God ﷺ gave glad tidings of Paradise?” “No.” “That man was among Banū Asad. Was there among you a woman whose marriage was concluded by God from heaven, with the Messenger of God ﷺ as the suitor and Gabriel as the envoy?” “No.” “That was among Banū Asad. Leave the man alone; by my life, he has reason to take pride if only he knew it.” The other man then left him alone.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: “ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh was the man whom the Messenger of God ﷺ sent with the first banner; and ʿUkāsha ibn Miḥṣan was the man to whom the Prophet ﷺ gave the good news of Paradise.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, who said: A nephew of Abū Ruhm told me that he heard Abū Ruhm al-Ghifārī, one of the Companions who pledged allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ beneath the tree, say: I went with the Messenger of God ﷺ on the expedition to Tabūk. One night as we traveled, I rode close to him and grew drowsy. I would wake to find my mount close to his, which startled me, because I feared striking his foot where it rested in the stirrup. I would draw my mount back, until at some point in the night sleep overcame me and my animal pressed against his foot in the stirrup and struck it. I woke only when I heard him cry out, “Ouch!” I said: “Ask forgiveness for me, Messenger of God.” He said: “Keep going.” He then questioned me about those of Banū Ghifār who had stayed behind, and I told him. He asked: “What became of the tall, reddish men with little facial hair?” I told him they had stayed behind. He asked: “And what of the dark-skinned men — or he said, the short men with tightly curled hair — who own livestock at Shabakat Sharkh?” I searched my memory among Banū Ghifār but could not identify them, until I recalled a group of Aslam. I said: “Messenger of God, they are a group of Aslam, and they too stayed behind.” The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “What prevented any of them, when staying behind, from placing an eager man on one of his camels to take part in God's cause? Of my people, those whose staying behind grieves me most are the emigrants of Quraysh, the Anṣār, Ghifār, and Aslam.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٨٨٢ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ أَخِي أَبِي رُهْمٍ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ أَبَا رُهْمٍ الْغِفَارِيَّ، وَكَانَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، الَّذِينَ بَايَعُوهُ تَحْتَ الشَّجَرَةِ، يَقُولُ: غَزَوْتُ مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ غَزْوَةَ تَبُوكَ، فَلَمَّا سَرَى لَيْلَةً سِرْتُ قَرِيبًا مِنْهُ إِلَيْهِ، وَأُلْقِيَ عَلَيَّ النُّعَاسُ، فَطَفِقْتُ أَسْتَيْقِظُ، وَقَدْ دَنَتْ رَاحِلَتِي مِنْ رَاحِلَتِهِ، فَيُفْزِعُنِيَ دُنُوُّهَا، خَشْيَةَ أَنْ أُصِيبَ رِجْلَهُ فِي الْغَرْزِ، فَأُؤَخِّرُ رَاحِلَتِي، حَتَّى غَلَبَتْنِي عَيْنِي بَعْضَ - [٥٠] - اللَّيْلِ، فَزَحَمَتْ رَاحِلَتِي رِجْلَهُ فِي الْغَرْزِ، فَأَصَابَتْ رِجْلَهُ، فَلَمْ أَسْتَيْقِظْ إِلَّا لِقَوْلِهِ:   «حَسِّ»   ، فَقُلْتُ: اسْتَغْفِرْ لِي يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، قَالَ:   «سِرْ»   فَطَفِقَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَستخْبِرُنِي عَمَّنْ تَخَلَّفَ مِنْ بَنِي غِفَارٍ فَأَخْبَرْتُهُ، فَقَالَ إِذْ هُوَ يَسْأَلُنِي:   «مَا فَعَلَ الْحُمْرُ الطُّوَالُ الثِّطَاطُ؟»   ، فَحَدَّثْتُهُ بِتَخَلُّفِهِمْ، قَالَ:   «فَمَا فَعَلَ النَّفَرُ السُّودُ - أَوْ قَالَ: الْقِصَارُ الْجِعَادُ الْقِطَاطُ - الَّذِينَ لَهُمْ نَعَمٌ بِشَبَكَةِ شَرْخٍ؟»   ، فتذَكَّرْتُ فِي بَنِي غِفَارٍ، فَلَمْ أَذْكُرْهُمْ حَتَّى ذَكَرْتُ رَهْطًا مِنْ أَسْلَمَ، قَالَ: فَقُلْتُ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، أُولَئِكَ رَهْطٌ مِنْ أَسْلَمَ، وَقَدْ تَخَلَّفُوا، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «فَمَا يَمْنَعُ أَحَدٌ أُولَئِكَ حِينَ يَتَخَلَّفُ، أَنْ يَحْمِلَ عَلَى بَعِيرٍ مِنْ إِبِلِهِ امْرَأً نَشِيطًا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ، فَإِنَّ §أَعَزَّ أَهْلِي عَلَيَّ أَنْ يَتَخَلَّفَ عَنِّي الْمُهَاجِرُونَ مِنْ قُرَيْشٍ، وَالْأَنْصَارُ، وَغِفَارٌ، وَأَسْلَمُ»

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, who said: A nephew of Abū Ruhm told me that he heard Abū Ruhm al-Ghifārī, one of the Companions who pledged allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ beneath the tree, say: I went with the Messenger of God ﷺ on the expedition to Tabūk. One night as we traveled, I rode close to him and grew drowsy. I would wake to find my mount close to his, which startled me, because I feared striking his foot where it rested in the stirrup. I would draw my mount back, until at some point in the night sleep overcame me and my animal pressed against his foot in the stirrup and struck it. I woke only when I heard him cry out, “Ouch!” I said: “Ask forgiveness for me, Messenger of God.” He said: “Keep going.” He then questioned me about those of Banū Ghifār who had stayed behind, and I told him. He asked: “What became of the tall, reddish men with little facial hair?” I told him they had stayed behind. He asked: “And what of the dark-skinned men — or he said, the short men with tightly curled hair — who own livestock at Shabakat Sharkh?” I searched my memory among Banū Ghifār but could not identify them, until I recalled a group of Aslam. I said: “Messenger of God, they are a group of Aslam, and they too stayed behind.” The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “What prevented any of them, when staying behind, from placing an eager man on one of his camels to take part in God's cause? Of my people, those whose staying behind grieves me most are the emigrants of Quraysh, the Anṣār, Ghifār, and Aslam.”

records.isnad_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, who said: A nephew of Abū Ruhm told me that he heard Abū Ruhm al-Ghifārī, one of the Companions who pledged allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ beneath the tree, say:
records.matn_en: I went with the Messenger of God ﷺ on the expedition to Tabūk. One night as we traveled, I rode close to him and grew drowsy. I would wake to find my mount close to his, which startled me, because I feared striking his foot where it rested in the stirrup. I would draw my mount back, until at some point in the night sleep overcame me and my animal pressed against his foot in the stirrup and struck it. I woke only when I heard him cry out, “Ouch!” I said: “Ask forgiveness for me, Messenger of God.” He said: “Keep going.” He then questioned me about those of Banū Ghifār who had stayed behind, and I told him. He asked: “What became of the tall, reddish men with little facial hair?” I told him they had stayed behind. He asked: “And what of the dark-skinned men — or he said, the short men with tightly curled hair — who own livestock at Shabakat Sharkh?” I searched my memory among Banū Ghifār but could not identify them, until I recalled a group of Aslam. I said: “Messenger of God, they are a group of Aslam, and they too stayed behind.” The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “What prevented any of them, when staying behind, from placing an eager man on one of his camels to take part in God's cause? Of my people, those whose staying behind grieves me most are the emigrants of Quraysh, the Anṣār, Ghifār, and Aslam.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilāba, who said: One thousand households of Hamdān set out during ʿUmar's reign. When they reached Medina, ʿUmar asked: “Where are you headed?” They answered: “Syria.” He said: “Rather, Iraq.” They insisted: “Rather, Syria, for our predecessors migrated there.” ʿUmar replied: “Rather, Iraq, for there is good fighting there and prosperity and abundant land.” He repeatedly turned their mounts toward Iraq while they turned them toward Syria, until a piece of wood from their saddles struck him and bloodied his head. When they saw that, they said: “Wherever you wish, Commander of the Believers.” He said: “Iraq.” They settled in Kufa. Abū Qilāba said: “To this day they are its most numerous and powerful people.”

records.text_ar: ١٩٨٨٤ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ عِكْرِمَةَ، قَالَ: جَاءَ عَامِرُ بْنُ الطُّفَيْلِ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَقَالَ: أُسْلِمُ يَا مُحَمَّدُ وَأَكُونُ الْخَلِيفَةَ مِنْ بَعْدِكَ؟ قَالَ:   «لَا»   ، قَالَ: فَيَكُونُ لِي الْوَبَرُ وَلَكَ الْمَدَرُ؟ قَالَ:   «لَا»   ، قَالَ:   «فَمَا تُعْطِينِي؟»   ، قَالَ: أُعْطِيكَ أَعِنَّةَ الْخَيْلِ تُقَاتِلُ عَلَيْهَا، فَإِنَّكَ امْرُؤٌ فَارِسٌ، قَالَ: أَوَلَيْسَتْ أَعِنَّةُ الْخَيْلِ بِيَدِي؟ وَاللَّهِ لَأَمْلَأَنَّ عَلَيْكَ بَنِي عَامِرٍ خَيْلًا، وَرِجَالًا، ثُمَّ وَلَّى، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§اللَّهُمَّ أَهْلِكْ عَامِرًا»   ، قَالَ عِكْرِمَةُ: وَيَزْعُمُ قَوْمُهُ أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ:   «وَأَهْلِكْ بَنِي عَامِرٍ»   ، قَالَ: فَقَالَ لَهُ أُسَيْدُ بْنُ حُضَيْرٍ حِينَ قَالَ لِلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ  وَأَكُونُ الْخَلِيفَةَ مِنْ بَعْدِكَ: زَحْزِحْ قَدَمَيْكَ لَا أُنْفِذَ الرُّمْحَ حُضْنَيْكَ، فَوَاللَّهِ لَوْ سَأَلْتَنَا سَيَابَةً مَا أُعْطِيتَهَا،   «يَعْنِي بِالسَّيَابَةِ: بُسْرَةً خَضْرَاءَ لَا يُنْتَفَعُ بِهَا»

records.matn_en: ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: “If I accept Islam, Muḥammad, will I be your successor after you?” He said: “No.” ʿĀmir said: “Will the people of tents [the desert] be mine and the people of buildings [the towns] yours?” “No.” “Then what will you give me?” He said: “I will give you command of horses with which to fight, for you are a skilled horseman.” ʿĀmir said: “Do I not already hold the reins of horses? By God, I will fill your country with the horsemen and foot soldiers of Banū ʿĀmir.” He turned away, and the Prophet ﷺ said: “O God, destroy ʿĀmir.” ʿIkrima said: His people claim that the Prophet ﷺ said: “And destroy Banū ʿĀmir.” When he had demanded to be the Prophet's successor, Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr told him: “Move your feet away, or I will run this spear through your sides. By God, were you to ask us for a siyāba, you would not be given even that.” By siyāba he meant a green, unripe date of no use.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from Ibn al-Musayyib, from Abū Hurayra, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Pride and arrogance are among the loud-voiced owners of camels and dwellers in tents; calmness is among those who keep sheep. Faith is Yemeni, and wisdom is Yemeni.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, who said: “When the Messenger of God ﷺ died, the Arabs apostatized except for three mosques: the Sacred Mosque, the mosque of Medina, and the mosque of Bahrain.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Faith is Yemeni as far as here,” pointing with his hand toward Judhām. May God's blessings be upon Judhām.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn, from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The people of Yemen have come to you. They are more tenderhearted. Faith is Yemeni, religious understanding is Yemeni, and wisdom is Yemeni.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Wahb ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Abū al-Ṭufayl, who said: ʿAmr ibn Ṣulayʿ al-Muḥāribī and I went to see Ḥudhayfa. We found him sitting on his bed with his knees drawn up, speaking to people. Out of youthful shyness I sat at the edge of the gathering; ʿAmr advanced, leaning on his stick, and sat near him. He said: “Tell us something, Ḥudhayfa.” Ḥudhayfa said: “What should I tell you? If I told you everything I know, you would kill me — or,” he said, “you would not believe me.” They asked: “Even though it was true?” He replied: “Yes.” They said: “We have no need for a truth that would lead us to kill you. Tell us something of benefit to us that will not harm you.” He said: “Suppose I told you that your mother would march against you. Would you believe me?” They asked: “Even if this is true?” He continued: “Accompanying her will be Muḍar — may God cast them into the Fire — and Asad of ʿAmmān — may God make their feet slip.” He said: “Qays will continue to seek evil in God's religion until God sends angels against them, and they will be unable to defend even the tail end of a valley.” ʿAmr said: “You have terrified the tribes, except Qays.” Ḥudhayfa replied: “Are you from Muḥārib of Qays, or is Qays from Muḥārib? When you see Qays turning away from Syria, be on your guard.” [The dialogue and tribal invocations are translated according to this recension; its phrasing is difficult in places.]
records.text_ar: ١٩٨٨٩ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ وَهْبِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، عَنْ أَبِي الطُّفَيْلِ، قَالَ: خَرَجْتُ أَنَا وَعَمْرُو بْنُ صُلَيْعٍ الْمُحَارِبِيُّ، حَتَّى دَخَلْنَا - [٥٣] - عَلَى حُذَيْفَةَ، فَإِذَا هُوَ مُحْتَبٍ عَلَى فِرَاشِهِ يُحَدِّثُ النَّاسَ قَالَ: فَغَلَبَنِي حَيَاءُ الشَّبَابِ، فَقَعَدْتُ فِي أَدْنَاهُمْ، وَتَقَدَّمَ عَمْرٌو مُجتَنِئًا عَلَى عُودِهِ حَتَّى قَعَدَ إِلَيْهِ، فَقَالَ: حَدِّثْنَا يَا حُذَيْفَةُ، فَقَالَ:   «عَمَّ أُحَدِّثُكُمْ؟»   ، فَقَالَ:   «لَوْ أَنِّي أُحَدِّثُكُمْ بِكُلِّ مَا أَعْلَمُ قَتَلْتُمُونِي - أَوْ قَالَ: لَمْ تُصَدِّقُونِي -»   ، قَالُوا: وَحَقٌّ ذَلِكَ؟ قَالَ:   «نَعَمْ»   ، قَالُوا: فَلَا حَاجَةَ لَنَا فِي حَقٍّ تُحَدِّثُنَاهُ فنقْتُلُكَ عَلَيْهِ، وَلَكِنْ حَدِّثْنَا بِمَا يَنْفَعُنَا وَلَا يَضُرُّكَ، فَقَالَ:   «أَرَأَيْتُمْ لَوْ حَدَّثْتُكُمْ أَنَّ §أُمَّكُمْ تَغْزُوكُمْ، إِذًا صَدَّقْتُمُونِي؟»   ، قَالُوا: وَحَقٌّ ذَلِكَ؟   «وَمَعَهَا مُضَرُ مَضَّرَهَا اللَّهُ فِي النَّارِ، وَأَسَدُ عَمَّانَ، سَلَتَ اللَّهُ أَقْدَامَهُمْ»   ، ثُمَّ قَالَ:   «إِنَّ قَيْسًا لَا تَزَالُ تَبْغِي فِي دِينِ اللَّهِ شَرًّا، حَتَّى يَرْكَبَهَا اللَّهُ بِمَلَائِكَةٍ، فَلَا يَمْنَعُوا ذَنَبَ تَلْعَةٍ»   ، قَالَ عَمْرٌو: أَذْهَلْتَ الْقَبَائِلَ إِلَّا قَيْسًا، فَقَالَ:   «أَمِنْ مُحَارِبِ قَيْسٍ؟ أَمْ مِنْ قَيْسِ مُحَارِبٍ، إِذَا رَأَيْتَ قَيْسًا تَوَالَتْ عَنِ الشَّامِ فَخُذْ حِذْرَكَ»

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Wahb ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Abū al-Ṭufayl, who said: ʿAmr ibn Ṣulayʿ al-Muḥāribī and I went to see Ḥudhayfa. We found him sitting on his bed with his knees drawn up, speaking to people. Out of youthful shyness I sat at the edge of the gathering; ʿAmr advanced, leaning on his stick, and sat near him. He said: “Tell us something, Ḥudhayfa.” Ḥudhayfa said: “What should I tell you? If I told you everything I know, you would kill me — or,” he said, “you would not believe me.” They asked: “Even though it was true?” He replied: “Yes.” They said: “We have no need for a truth that would lead us to kill you. Tell us something of benefit to us that will not harm you.” He said: “Suppose I told you that your mother would march against you. Would you believe me?” They asked: “Even if this is true?” He continued: “Accompanying her will be Muḍar — may God cast them into the Fire — and Asad of ʿAmmān — may God make their feet slip.” He said: “Qays will continue to seek evil in God's religion until God sends angels against them, and they will be unable to defend even the tail end of a valley.” ʿAmr said: “You have terrified the tribes, except Qays.” Ḥudhayfa replied: “Are you from Muḥārib of Qays, or is Qays from Muḥārib? When you see Qays turning away from Syria, be on your guard.” [The dialogue and tribal invocations are translated according to this recension; its phrasing is difficult in places.]

records.display_matn_ar: خَرَجْتُ أَنَا وَعَمْرُو بْنُ صُلَيْعٍ الْمُحَارِبِيُّ، حَتَّى دَخَلْنَا عَلَى حُذَيْفَةَ، فَإِذَا هُوَ مُحْتَبٍ عَلَى فِرَاشِهِ يُحَدِّثُ النَّاسَ قَالَ: فَغَلَبَنِي حَيَاءُ الشَّبَابِ، فَقَعَدْتُ فِي أَدْنَاهُمْ، وَتَقَدَّمَ عَمْرٌو مُجتَنِئًا عَلَى عُودِهِ حَتَّى قَعَدَ إِلَيْهِ، فَقَالَ: حَدِّثْنَا يَا حُذَيْفَةُ، فَقَالَ:   «عَمَّ أُحَدِّثُكُمْ؟»   ، فَقَالَ:   «لَوْ أَنِّي أُحَدِّثُكُمْ بِكُلِّ مَا أَعْلَمُ قَتَلْتُمُونِي - أَوْ قَالَ: لَمْ تُصَدِّقُونِي -»   ، قَالُوا: وَحَقٌّ ذَلِكَ؟ قَالَ:   «نَعَمْ»   ، قَالُوا: فَلَا حَاجَةَ لَنَا فِي حَقٍّ تُحَدِّثُنَاهُ فنقْتُلُكَ عَلَيْهِ، وَلَكِنْ حَدِّثْنَا بِمَا يَنْفَعُنَا وَلَا يَضُرُّكَ، فَقَالَ:   «أَرَأَيْتُمْ لَوْ حَدَّثْتُكُمْ أَنَّ §أُمَّكُمْ تَغْزُوكُمْ، إِذًا صَدَّقْتُمُونِي؟»   ، قَالُوا: وَحَقٌّ ذَلِكَ؟   «وَمَعَهَا مُضَرُ مَضَّرَهَا اللَّهُ فِي النَّارِ، وَأَسَدُ عَمَّانَ، سَلَتَ اللَّهُ أَقْدَامَهُمْ»   ، ثُمَّ قَالَ:   «إِنَّ قَيْسًا لَا تَزَالُ تَبْغِي فِي دِينِ اللَّهِ شَرًّا، حَتَّى يَرْكَبَهَا اللَّهُ بِمَلَائِكَةٍ، فَلَا يَمْنَعُوا ذَنَبَ تَلْعَةٍ»   ، قَالَ عَمْرٌو: أَذْهَلْتَ الْقَبَائِلَ إِلَّا قَيْسًا، فَقَالَ:   «أَمِنْ مُحَارِبِ قَيْسٍ؟ أَمْ مِنْ قَيْسِ مُحَارِبٍ، إِذَا رَأَيْتَ قَيْسًا تَوَالَتْ عَنِ الشَّامِ فَخُذْ حِذْرَكَ»
records.display_isnad_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Wahb ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Abū al-Ṭufayl, who said:
records.display_matn_en: ʿAmr ibn Ṣulayʿ al-Muḥāribī and I went to see Ḥudhayfa. We found him sitting on his bed with his knees drawn up, speaking to people. Out of youthful shyness I sat at the edge of the gathering; ʿAmr advanced, leaning on his stick, and sat near him. He said: “Tell us something, Ḥudhayfa.” Ḥudhayfa said: “What should I tell you? If I told you everything I know, you would kill me — or,” he said, “you would not believe me.” They asked: “Even though it was true?” He replied: “Yes.” They said: “We have no need for a truth that would lead us to kill you. Tell us something of benefit to us that will not harm you.” He said: “Suppose I told you that your mother would march against you. Would you believe me?” They asked: “Even if this is true?” He continued: “Accompanying her will be Muḍar — may God cast them into the Fire — and Asad of ʿAmmān — may God make their feet slip.” He said: “Qays will continue to seek evil in God's religion until God sends angels against them, and they will be unable to defend even the tail end of a valley.” ʿAmr said: “You have terrified the tribes, except Qays.” Ḥudhayfa replied: “Are you from Muḥārib of Qays, or is Qays from Muḥārib? When you see Qays turning away from Syria, be on your guard.” [The dialogue and tribal invocations are translated according to this recension; its phrasing is difficult in places.]

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from more than one person, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Aslam — may God grant her peace; Ghifār — may God forgive her; and ʿUṣayya disobeyed God and His Messenger.” ʿUṣayya was a branch of Banū Sulaym.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, saying: It reached me that the Prophet ﷺ was once sitting among his Companions and said: “O God, save the people of the ship.” After a time he said: “They have continued on their way.” When they approached Medina, he said: “They have arrived, led by a righteous man.” Those who had come in the ship were the Ashʿarīs, and their leader was ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥamiq al-Khuzāʿī. records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from ʿAmr ibn Abī Bakr, from Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī, from ʿĀʾisha, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, who asked during the Battle of the Confederates: “What would become of us, Messenger of God, if the Yemenis joined Hawāzin and Ghaṭafān against us?” The Prophet ﷺ replied: “No. Those people pose no danger to the followers of this religion.”
records.text_ar: ١٩٨٩٢ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ أَبِي بَكْرٍ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ كَعْبٍ الْقُرَظِيِّ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ زَوْجِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، يَوْمَ الْأَحْزَابِ، كَيْفَ بِنَا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ لَوِ اجْتَمَعَتْ عَلَيْنَا الْيَمَنُ مَعَ هَوَازِنَ، وَغَطَفَانَ؟ فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «كَلَّا §أُولَئِكَ قَوْمٌ لَيْسَ عَلَى أَهْلِ هَذَا الدِّينِ مِنْهُمْ بَأْسٌ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from Sulaymān ibn Abī Ḥathma, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Do not instruct Quraysh; learn from them instead. records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Hammām ibn Munabbih, who heard Abū Hurayra say: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “People follow Quraysh in this affair” — he said, “I think he meant rulership” — “their Muslims follow the Muslims of Quraysh, and their unbelievers follow its unbelievers.”
