records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported: Maʿmar informed us from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Hilāl ibn Abī Maymūna, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, who said: While the Messenger of God ﷺ was delivering a sermon, he said: “Among the things I fear for you is that, when the world's blossoms and adornments are opened to you, you will compete for them as those before you competed for them, and they will destroy you as they destroyed them.” A man resembling a Bedouin stood up and asked: “Messenger of God, can good bring about evil?” The Messenger of God ﷺ remained silent for a time, until we thought revelation had come to him. Then, wiping sweat from his forehead, he said: “Where is the questioner? Good brings only good. Some of what the spring produces kills or nearly kills—except the animal that eats fresh greenery: it eats until its flanks swell, then faces the sun, urinates and defecates. Wealth is a fine companion to one who gives from it to the needy, the poor, and relatives.” Or he said words to that effect.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from a companion of his, that Abū al-Dardāʾ wrote to Salmān: “My brother, make use of your health and free time before an affliction descends upon you that people cannot avert. Make use of the supplication of one afflicted. My brother, let the mosque be your home, for I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘The mosque is the home of every God-fearing person. God has guaranteed those who make mosques their homes relief, mercy, and passage over the Bridge to God's pleasure.’ My brother, show compassion to the orphan; bring him near, stroke his head, and feed him from your food. For I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ when a man came complaining of the hardness of his heart. He asked him: ‘Would you like your heart to become soft?’ He said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘Bring the orphan close to you, stroke his head, and feed him from your food. That will soften your heart and enable you to obtain what you need.’”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٠٢٩ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ صَاحِبٍ لَهُ أَنَّ أَبَا - [٩٧] - الدَّرْدَاءِ، كَتَبَ إِلَى سَلْمَانَ: أَنْ يَا أَخِي اغْتَنِمْ صِحَّتَكَ وَفَرَاغَكَ، قَبْلَ أَنْ يَنْزِلَ بِكَ مِنَ الْبَلَاءِ مَا لَا يَسْتَطِيعُ الْعِبَادُ رَدَّهُ، وَاغْتَنِمْ دَعْوَةَ الْمُبْتَلَى، وَيَا أَخِي لِيَكُنِ الْمَسْجِدُ بَيْتَكَ، فَإِنِّي سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَقُولُ:   «إِنَّ §الْمَسْجِدَ بَيْتُ كُلِّ تَقِيٍّ، وَقَدْ ضَمِنَ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ كَانَتِ الْمَسَاجِدُ بُيُوتَهُمْ بِالرَّوْحِ وَالرَّحْمَةِ وَالْجَوَازِ عَلَى الصِّرَاطِ إِلَى رِضْوَانِ اللَّهِ»   وَيَا أَخِي ارْحَمِ الْيَتِيمَ، وَأَدنِهِ مِنْكَ، وَامْسَحْ بِرَأْسِهِ، وَأَطْعِمْهُ مِنْ طَعَامِكَ، فَإِنِّي سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَأَتَاهُ رَجُلٌ يَشْكُو قَسْوَةَ قَلْبِهِ، فَقَالَ لَهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ:   «أَتُحِبُّ أَنْ يَلِينَ قَلْبُكَ؟»   ، قَالَ: نَعَمْ، قَالَ:   «فَأَدْنِ الْيَتِيمَ إِلَيْكَ، وَامْسَحْ بِرَأْسِهِ، وَأَطْعِمْهُ مِنْ طَعَامِكَ، فَإِنَّ ذَلِكَ يُلَيِّنُ قَلْبَكَ، وَتَقْدِرُ عَلَى حَاجَتِكَ»

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: وَيَا أَخِي لَا تَجْمَعْ مَا لَا تَسْتَطِيعُ شُكْرَهُ، فَإِنِّي سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَقُولُ:   «§يُجَاءُ بِصَاحِبِ الدُّنْيَا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ، الَّذِي أَطَاعَ اللَّهَ فِيهَا هُوَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْ مَالِهِ، وَمَالُهُ خَلْفَهُ، فَكُلَّمَا تَكَفَّأَ بِهِ الصِّرَاطُ قَالَ لَهُ: امْضِ، فَقَدْ أَدَّيْتَ الْحَقَّ الَّذِي عَلَيْكَ، قَالَ: وَيُجَاءُ بِالْآخَرِ الَّذِي لَمْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ فِيهِ، وَمَالُهُ بَيْنَ كَتِفَيْهِ، فُيُعْثِرُهُ مَالُهُ، وَيَقُولُ: وَيْلَكَ، هَلَّا عَمِلْتَ بِطَاعَةِ اللَّهِ فِي مَالِكَ؟ فَلَا يَزَالُ كَذَلِكَ يَدْعُو بِالْوَيْلِ وَالثُّبُورِ»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: “My brother, do not accumulate more wealth than you can properly show gratitude for. For I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘On the Day of Resurrection, a person who possessed worldly wealth and obeyed God concerning it will be brought forth, with his wealth following behind him. Whenever the Bridge [over Hell] tilts beneath him, his wealth will tell him: “Go on, for you have discharged the duty you owed.” Another person who did not obey God concerning his wealth will be brought, with his wealth upon his shoulders; it will make him stumble, saying: “Woe to you! Why did you not obey God in disposing of your wealth?” He will keep crying out in woe and ruin.’”

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: وَيَا أَخِي إِنِّي حُدِّثْتُ أَنَّكَ اشْتَرَيْتَ خَادِمًا، وَإِنِّي سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَقُولُ:   «§لَا يَزَالُ الْعَبْدُ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَهُوَ مِنْهُ مَا لَمْ يُخْدَمْ، فَإِذَا خُدِمَ، وَجَبَ عَلَيْهِ الْحِسَابُ»   ، وَإِنَّ أُمَّ الدَّرْدَاءِ سَأَلَتْنِي خَادِمًا، وَأَنَا يَوْمَئِذٍ مُوسِرٌ، فَكَرِهْتُ ذَلِكَ لَهَا، خَشِيتُ مِنَ الْحِسَابِ، وَيَا أَخِي مَنْ لِي وَلَكَ بِأَنْ نُوَافِيَ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ، وَلَا نَخَافَ حِسَابًا، وَيَا أَخِي لَا تَغْتَرَّنَّ - [٩٨] - بِصَحَابَةِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، فَإِنَّا قَدْ عِشْنَا بَعْدَهُ دَهْرًا طَوِيلًا، وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِالَّذِي أَصَبْنَا بَعْدَهُ
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: “My brother, I have been told that you bought a servant. I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘A servant continues to have a close relationship with God so long as he is not served by others; when others serve him, he becomes liable to an accounting.’ Umm al-Dardāʾ once asked me for a servant while I was well off, but I disliked acquiring one for her, because I feared the reckoning. My brother, who will guarantee that you and I reach the Day of Resurrection with no fear of accounting? My brother, do not be deceived by having accompanied the Messenger of God ﷺ. We have lived for a long time after him, and God knows best what we have fallen into since then.”

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from a companion of his, that Abū al-Dardāʾ wrote to Salmān: “My brother, make use of your health and free time before an affliction descends upon you that people cannot avert. Make use of the supplication of one afflicted. My brother, let the mosque be your home, for I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘The mosque is the home of every God-fearing person. God has guaranteed those who make mosques their homes relief, mercy, and passage over the Bridge to God's pleasure.’ My brother, show compassion to the orphan; bring him near, stroke his head, and feed him from your food. For I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ when a man came complaining of the hardness of his heart. He asked him: ‘Would you like your heart to become soft?’ He said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘Bring the orphan close to you, stroke his head, and feed him from your food. That will soften your heart and enable you to obtain what you need.’”

records.display_matn_ar: أَنَّ أَبَا الدَّرْدَاءِ، كَتَبَ إِلَى سَلْمَانَ: أَنْ يَا أَخِي اغْتَنِمْ صِحَّتَكَ وَفَرَاغَكَ، قَبْلَ أَنْ يَنْزِلَ بِكَ مِنَ الْبَلَاءِ مَا لَا يَسْتَطِيعُ الْعِبَادُ رَدَّهُ، وَاغْتَنِمْ دَعْوَةَ الْمُبْتَلَى، وَيَا أَخِي لِيَكُنِ الْمَسْجِدُ بَيْتَكَ، فَإِنِّي سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَقُولُ:   «إِنَّ §الْمَسْجِدَ بَيْتُ كُلِّ تَقِيٍّ، وَقَدْ ضَمِنَ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ كَانَتِ الْمَسَاجِدُ بُيُوتَهُمْ بِالرَّوْحِ وَالرَّحْمَةِ وَالْجَوَازِ عَلَى الصِّرَاطِ إِلَى رِضْوَانِ اللَّهِ»   وَيَا أَخِي ارْحَمِ الْيَتِيمَ، وَأَدنِهِ مِنْكَ، وَامْسَحْ بِرَأْسِهِ، وَأَطْعِمْهُ مِنْ طَعَامِكَ، فَإِنِّي سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَأَتَاهُ رَجُلٌ يَشْكُو قَسْوَةَ قَلْبِهِ، فَقَالَ لَهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ:   «أَتُحِبُّ أَنْ يَلِينَ قَلْبُكَ؟»   ، قَالَ: نَعَمْ، قَالَ:   «فَأَدْنِ الْيَتِيمَ إِلَيْكَ، وَامْسَحْ بِرَأْسِهِ، وَأَطْعِمْهُ مِنْ طَعَامِكَ، فَإِنَّ ذَلِكَ يُلَيِّنُ قَلْبَكَ، وَتَقْدِرُ عَلَى حَاجَتِكَ»
records.display_isnad_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from a companion of his,
records.display_matn_en: that Abū al-Dardāʾ wrote to Salmān: “My brother, make use of your health and free time before an affliction descends upon you that people cannot avert. Make use of the supplication of one afflicted. My brother, let the mosque be your home, for I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘The mosque is the home of every God-fearing person. God has guaranteed those who make mosques their homes relief, mercy, and passage over the Bridge to God's pleasure.’ My brother, show compassion to the orphan; bring him near, stroke his head, and feed him from your food. For I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ when a man came complaining of the hardness of his heart. He asked him: ‘Would you like your heart to become soft?’ He said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘Bring the orphan close to you, stroke his head, and feed him from your food. That will soften your heart and enable you to obtain what you need.’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father: The Messenger of God ﷺ passed people discussing something and asked: “What were you discussing?” They said: “We were discussing worldly life and its worries, and fearing poverty.” He said: “I fear wealth for you more than I fear poverty.” They asked: “Messenger of God, can good bring evil?” The Prophet ﷺ replied: “Is it [necessarily] good?”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilāba, who traced the report to the Prophet ﷺ: “Whoever gives away what exceeds his needs in wealth, it is better for him; whoever withholds it, it is worse for him. God does not blame anyone for retaining enough to meet his needs.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Ibn al-Musayyib and Abū Salama, from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “I was aided by fear [cast into the enemy], and I was given concise, comprehensive speech. While I was sleeping, the keys to the treasures of the earth were brought and placed in my hands.” Abū Hurayra added: “The Messenger of God ﷺ has departed, and you are now drawing those treasures out.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “If I had gold equal to Mount Uḥud, I would not wish three days to pass while any of it remained with me, except something I had set aside to repay a debt.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, who said: When the treasures of Khusraw were brought to ʿUmar, ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Arqam al-Zuhrī asked him: “Why not place them in the treasury until you distribute them?” He replied: “No roof will shelter them until I have distributed them.” He ordered them placed in the mosque courtyard, and guards watched them overnight. In the morning the coverings were removed, and he saw gold and silver gleaming so brightly as almost to dazzle the eyes. ʿUmar wept. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf said: “Why do you weep, Commander of the Believers? By God, this is a day for gratitude, joy, and happiness.” ʿUmar replied: “No. Whenever a people were given this, enmity and hatred were cast among them.” Then he asked: “Shall we measure their shares by the *ṣāʿ*, or heap it into their hands?” ʿAlī said: “Heap it out to them.” He called Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī first and he took his handfuls; then he called Ḥusayn and afterward gave to the people. He established the registers of stipends and assigned each of the Emigrants five thousand dirhams per year, each of the Anṣār four thousand, and each wife of the Prophet ﷺ twelve thousand, except Ṣafiyya and Juwayriya, for each of whom he assigned six thousand dirhams.
records.text_ar: ٢٠٠٣٦ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ - [١٠٠] - بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ عَوْفٍ، قَالَ: لَمَّا أُتِيَ عُمَرُ بِكُنُوزِ كِسْرَى، قَالَ لَهُ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ الْأَرْقَمِ الزُّهْرِيُّ: أَلَا تَجْعَلُهَا فِي بَيْتِ الْمَالِ حَتَّى تَقْسِمَهَا؟ قَالَ:   «لَا يُظِلُّهَا سَقْفٌ حَتَّى أُمْضِيَهَا»   ، فَأَمَرَ بِهَا، فَوُضِعَتْ فِي صَرْحِ الْمَسْجِدِ، فَبَاتُوا يَحْرُسُونَهَا، فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ أَمَرَ بِهَا فَكُشِفَ عَنْهَا، فَرَأَى فِيهَا مِنَ الْحَمْرَاءِ وَالْبَيْضَاءِ مَا يَكَادُ يَتَلَأْلَأُ مِنْهُ الْبَصَرُ، قَالَ: فَبَكَى عُمَرُ، فَقَالَ لَهُ عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ عَوْفٍ: مَا يُبْكِيكَ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ؟ فَوَاللَّهِ إِنْ كَانَ هَذَا لَيَوْمَ شُكْرٍ، وَيَوْمَ سُرُورٍ، وَيَوْمَ فَرَحٍ، فَقَالَ عُمَرُ:   «كَلَّا، إِنَّ §هَذَا لَمْ يُعْطَهُ قَوْمٌ إِلَّا أُلْقِيَ بَيْنَهُمُ الْعَدَاوَةُ وَالْبَغْضَاءُ، ثُمَّ قَالَ: أَنَكِيلُ لَهُمْ بِالصَّاعِ أَمْ نَحْثُوَ؟»   ، فَقَالَ عَلِيٌّ: بَلِ احْثُوا لَهُمْ، ثُمَّ دَعَا حَسَنَ بْنَ عَلِيٍّ أَوَّلَ النَّاسِ فَحَثَا لَهُ، ثُمَّ دَعَا حُسَيْنًا ثُمَّ أَعْطَى النَّاسَ، وَدَوَّنَ الدَّوَاوِينَ، وَفَرَضَ لِلْمُهَاجِرِينَ لِكُلِّ رَجُلٍ مِنْهُمْ خَمْسَةَ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ فِي كُلِّ سَنَةٍ، وَلِلْأَنْصَارِ لِكُلِّ رَجُلٍ مِنْهُمْ أَرْبَعَةَ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ، وَفَرَضَ لِأَزْوَاجِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ لِكُلِّ امْرَأَةٍ مِنْهُنَّ اثْنَيْ عَشَرَ أَلْفَ دِرْهَمٍ، إِلَّا صَفِيَّةَ وَجُوَيْرِيَةَ، فَرَضَ لِكُلِّ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنْهُمَا سِتَّةَ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, who said: When the treasures of Khusraw were brought to ʿUmar, ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Arqam al-Zuhrī asked him: “Why not place them in the treasury until you distribute them?” He replied: “No roof will shelter them until I have distributed them.” He ordered them placed in the mosque courtyard, and guards watched them overnight. In the morning the coverings were removed, and he saw gold and silver gleaming so brightly as almost to dazzle the eyes. ʿUmar wept. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf said: “Why do you weep, Commander of the Believers? By God, this is a day for gratitude, joy, and happiness.” ʿUmar replied: “No. Whenever a people were given this, enmity and hatred were cast among them.” Then he asked: “Shall we measure their shares by the *ṣāʿ*, or heap it into their hands?” ʿAlī said: “Heap it out to them.” He called Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī first and he took his handfuls; then he called Ḥusayn and afterward gave to the people. He established the registers of stipends and assigned each of the Emigrants five thousand dirhams per year, each of the Anṣār four thousand, and each wife of the Prophet ﷺ twelve thousand, except Ṣafiyya and Juwayriya, for each of whom he assigned six thousand dirhams.

records.display_matn_ar: لَمَّا أُتِيَ عُمَرُ بِكُنُوزِ كِسْرَى، قَالَ لَهُ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ الْأَرْقَمِ الزُّهْرِيُّ: أَلَا تَجْعَلُهَا فِي بَيْتِ الْمَالِ حَتَّى تَقْسِمَهَا؟ قَالَ:   «لَا يُظِلُّهَا سَقْفٌ حَتَّى أُمْضِيَهَا»   ، فَأَمَرَ بِهَا، فَوُضِعَتْ فِي صَرْحِ الْمَسْجِدِ، فَبَاتُوا يَحْرُسُونَهَا، فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ أَمَرَ بِهَا فَكُشِفَ عَنْهَا، فَرَأَى فِيهَا مِنَ الْحَمْرَاءِ وَالْبَيْضَاءِ مَا يَكَادُ يَتَلَأْلَأُ مِنْهُ الْبَصَرُ، قَالَ: فَبَكَى عُمَرُ، فَقَالَ لَهُ عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ عَوْفٍ: مَا يُبْكِيكَ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ؟ فَوَاللَّهِ إِنْ كَانَ هَذَا لَيَوْمَ شُكْرٍ، وَيَوْمَ سُرُورٍ، وَيَوْمَ فَرَحٍ، فَقَالَ عُمَرُ:   «كَلَّا، إِنَّ §هَذَا لَمْ يُعْطَهُ قَوْمٌ إِلَّا أُلْقِيَ بَيْنَهُمُ الْعَدَاوَةُ وَالْبَغْضَاءُ، ثُمَّ قَالَ: أَنَكِيلُ لَهُمْ بِالصَّاعِ أَمْ نَحْثُوَ؟»   ، فَقَالَ عَلِيٌّ: بَلِ احْثُوا لَهُمْ، ثُمَّ دَعَا حَسَنَ بْنَ عَلِيٍّ أَوَّلَ النَّاسِ فَحَثَا لَهُ، ثُمَّ دَعَا حُسَيْنًا ثُمَّ أَعْطَى النَّاسَ، وَدَوَّنَ الدَّوَاوِينَ، وَفَرَضَ لِلْمُهَاجِرِينَ لِكُلِّ رَجُلٍ مِنْهُمْ خَمْسَةَ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ فِي كُلِّ سَنَةٍ، وَلِلْأَنْصَارِ لِكُلِّ رَجُلٍ مِنْهُمْ أَرْبَعَةَ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ، وَفَرَضَ لِأَزْوَاجِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ لِكُلِّ امْرَأَةٍ مِنْهُنَّ اثْنَيْ عَشَرَ أَلْفَ دِرْهَمٍ، إِلَّا صَفِيَّةَ وَجُوَيْرِيَةَ، فَرَضَ لِكُلِّ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنْهُمَا سِتَّةَ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ
records.display_isnad_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, who said:
records.display_matn_en: When the treasures of Khusraw were brought to ʿUmar, ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Arqam al-Zuhrī asked him: “Why not place them in the treasury until you distribute them?” He replied: “No roof will shelter them until I have distributed them.” He ordered them placed in the mosque courtyard, and guards watched them overnight. In the morning the coverings were removed, and he saw gold and silver gleaming so brightly as almost to dazzle the eyes. ʿUmar wept. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf said: “Why do you weep, Commander of the Believers? By God, this is a day for gratitude, joy, and happiness.” ʿUmar replied: “No. Whenever a people were given this, enmity and hatred were cast among them.” Then he asked: “Shall we measure their shares by the *ṣāʿ*, or heap it into their hands?” ʿAlī said: “Heap it out to them.” He called Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī first and he took his handfuls; then he called Ḥusayn and afterward gave to the people. He established the registers of stipends and assigned each of the Emigrants five thousand dirhams per year, each of the Anṣār four thousand, and each wife of the Prophet ﷺ twelve thousand, except Ṣafiyya and Juwayriya, for each of whom he assigned six thousand dirhams.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, who said: A young she-camel from the charity livestock broke a limb, so ʿUmar had it prepared in serving dishes and invited people to eat. records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from ʿIkrima ibn Khālid, from Mālik ibn Aws ibn al-Ḥadathān, who said: ʿUmar recited, “Alms are only for the poor...” (9:60), to the end of the verse, “Knowing, Wise.” He said: “These belong to those [named in the verse].” Then he recited, “Know that whatever you acquire as spoils, a fifth belongs to God...” (8:41), until the mention of the traveler, and said: “These belong to those [named there].” Then he recited the passage beginning “Whatever God has restored to His messenger from the people of the towns...” (59:7), continuing to “those who came after them” (59:10). He said: “This encompasses all Muslims. If I live, even a herdsman in the heights of Ḥimyar will receive his share of it, though he has not sweated a drop to acquire it.” [The Arabic source associates one quoted phrase with 2:177; its context here is the spoils verse, 8:41.]
records.text_ar: ٢٠٠٤٠ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ عِكْرِمَةَ بْنِ خَالِدٍ، عَنْ مَالِكِ بْنِ أَوْسِ بْنِ الْحَدَثَانِ، قَالَ: قَرَأَ عُمَرُ:   «{§إِنَّمَا الصَّدَقَاتُ لِلْفُقُرَاءِ}   [التوبة: ٦٠]  حَتَّى بَلَغَ  {عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ}   [التوبة: ٦٠]  ثُمَّ قَالَ: هَذِهِ لِهَؤُلَاءِ ثُمَّ قَرَأَ:  {وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّمَا غَنِمْتُمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَأَنَّ لِلَّهِ خُمُسَهُ}   [الأنفال: ٤١]  حَتَّى بَلَغَ  {وَابْنِ السَّبِيلِ}   [البقرة: ١٧٧]  ، ثُمَّ قَالَ: هَذِهِ لِهَؤُلَاءِ، ثُمَّ قَرَأَ:  {مَا أَفَاءَ}   [الحشر: ٧]  اللَّهُ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْقُرَى حَتَّى بَلَغَ  {وَالَّذِينَ جَاءُوا مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ}  ثُمَّ قَالَ: هَذِهِ اسْتَوْعَبَتِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ عَامَّةً، فَلَئِنْ عِشْتُ لَيَأْتِيَنَّ الرَّاعِي وَهُوَ بِسَرْوِ حِمْيَرَ نَصِيبُهُ مِنْهَا، لَمْ يَعْرَقْ فِيهَا جَبِينُهُ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr and Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, and from Hishām, from his father: The Prophet ﷺ gave Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām less than he had given others. Ḥakīm said: “Messenger of God, I never thought you would put me below anyone.” The Prophet ﷺ increased his gift. He asked for more, and he increased it again until Ḥakīm was satisfied. He asked: “Messenger of God, which of your gifts was best?” He replied: “The first.” Then the Prophet ﷺ said: “Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām, this wealth is green and sweet. Whoever takes it with an open, contented soul and uses it well will be blessed in it. Whoever takes it with craving and uses it badly will not be blessed in it and will be like one who eats yet is never satisfied. The upper hand is better than the lower hand.” He asked: “Even if it is taken from you, Messenger of God?” He answered: “Even from me.” Ḥakīm said: “By the One who sent you with the truth, after you I shall take nothing from anyone.” He accepted neither a stipend nor a place on the public payroll until he died. Later, ʿUmar summoned him to receive his entitlement, but he refused. ʿUmar said: “God, I call You to witness regarding Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām that I invite him to take his right from this wealth, but he refuses; I absolve myself of responsibility before God.” Ḥakīm said: “By God, I will never take anything from you or anyone else.” He died as one of the wealthiest men of Quraysh.

records.display_matn_ar: أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَعْطَى حَكِيمَ بْنَ حِزَامٍ دُونَ مَا أَعْطَى أَصْحَابَهُ، فَقَالَ حَكِيمٌ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، مَا كُنْتُ أَظُنُّ أَنْ تَقْصُرَ بِي دُونَ أَحَدٍ، فَزَادَهُ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، ثُمَّ اسْتَزَادَهُ فَزَادَهُ، حَتَّى رَضِيَ، فَقَالَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، أَيُّ عَطِيَّتِكَ خَيْرٌ؟ قَالَ:   «الْأُولَى»   ، ثُمَّ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «يَا حَكِيمُ بْنَ حِزَامٍ، إِنَّ §هَذَا الْمَالَ خَضِرَةٌ حُلْوَةٌ، فَمَنْ أَخَذَهُ بِسَخَاوَةِ نَفْسٍ، وَحُسْنِ أُكْلَةٍ بُورِكَ لَهُ فِيهِ، وَمَنْ أَخَذَهُ بِإِشْرَافِ نَفْسٍ، وَسُوءِ أُكْلَةٍ لَمْ يُبَارَكْ لَهُ فِيهِ، وَكَانَ كَالَّذِي يَأْكُلُ وَلَا يَشْبَعُ، وَالْيَدُ الْعُلْيَا خَيْرٌ مِنَ الْيَدِ السُّفْلَى»   ، قَالَ: وَمِنْكَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ؟ قَالَ:   «وَمِنِّي»   ، قَالَ: وَالَّذِي بَعَثَكَ بِالْحَقِّ لَا أَرْزَأُ بَعْدَكَ أَحَدًا شَيْئًا، فَلَمْ يَقْبَلْ عَطَاءً، وَلَا دِيَوَانًا حَتَّى مَاتَ فَكَانَ عُمَرُ يَدْعُوهُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ لِيَأْخُذَ مِنْهُ فَيَأْبَى، فَيَقُولُ عُمَرُ: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أُشْهِدُكَ عَلَى حَكِيمِ بْنِ حِزَامٍ أَنِّي أَدْعُوهُ إِلَى حَقِّهِ مِنْ هَذَا الْمَالِ فَيَأْبَى، وَإِنِّي أَبْرَأُ إِلَى اللَّهِ مِنْهُ، فَقَالَ حَكِيمٌ:   «وَاللَّهِ وَلَا أَرْزَأُكَ وَلَا غَيْرَكَ شَيْئًا أَبَدًا، قَالَ: فَمَاتَ حِينَ مَاتَ، وَإِنَّهُ لَمِنْ أَكْثَرِ قُرَيْشٍ مَالًا»
records.display_isnad_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr and Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, and from Hishām, from his father:
records.display_matn_en: The Prophet ﷺ gave Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām less than he had given others. Ḥakīm said: “Messenger of God, I never thought you would put me below anyone.” The Prophet ﷺ increased his gift. He asked for more, and he increased it again until Ḥakīm was satisfied. He asked: “Messenger of God, which of your gifts was best?” He replied: “The first.” Then the Prophet ﷺ said: “Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām, this wealth is green and sweet. Whoever takes it with an open, contented soul and uses it well will be blessed in it. Whoever takes it with craving and uses it badly will not be blessed in it and will be like one who eats yet is never satisfied. The upper hand is better than the lower hand.” He asked: “Even if it is taken from you, Messenger of God?” He answered: “Even from me.” Ḥakīm said: “By the One who sent you with the truth, after you I shall take nothing from anyone.” He accepted neither a stipend nor a place on the public payroll until he died. Later, ʿUmar summoned him to receive his entitlement, but he refused. ʿUmar said: “God, I call You to witness regarding Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām that I invite him to take his right from this wealth, but he refuses; I absolve myself of responsibility before God.” Ḥakīm said: “By God, I will never take anything from you or anyone else.” He died as one of the wealthiest men of Quraysh.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, who said: Jaʿfar ibn Burqān told me, from Maymūn ibn Mihrān, who said: Muḥammad ibn Marwān invited me to have my name entered on the stipend register, but I refused. He said: “Do you not dislike having no share among the Muslims?” I replied: “I have a share among the Muslims even without being on the register.” He asked: “Do you know anyone among the early generations who was not on the register?” I said: “Yes.” He asked: “Who?” I replied: “Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٠٤٢ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، حَدَّثَنِي جَعْفَرُ بْنُ بُرْقَانَ، عَنْ مَيْمُونِ بْنِ مِهْرَانَ، قَالَ: دَعَانِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مَرْوَانَ إِلَى أَنْ يَكْتُبَنِي فِي الدِّيوَانِ، فَأَبَيْتُ، فَقَالَ لِي: أَمَا تَكْرَهُ أَنْ لَا يَكُونَ لَكَ فِي الْمُسْلِمِينَ سَهْمٌ؟ قَالَ: قُلْتُ:   «إِنَّ §لِي فِي الْمُسْلِمِينَ سَهْمًا، وَإِنْ لَمْ أَكُنْ فِي الدِّيوَانِ»   ، قَالَ: فَهَلْ تَعْلَمُ أَحَدًا مِنَ السَّلَفِ لَمْ يَكُنْ فِي الدِّيوَانِ؟ قَالَ: قُلْتُ:   «نَعَمْ»   ، قَالَ: مَنْ هُوَ؟ قُلْتُ:   «حَكِيمُ بْنُ حِزَامٍ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār: The Prophet ﷺ sent something to ʿUmar, who returned it, saying: “Messenger of God, did you not tell us that it is better for one of us not to take anything from another?” The Prophet ﷺ said: “That concerns asking. records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn, from al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays, who said: We were sitting by ʿUmar's door when a young woman came out. We said: “She is a concubine of the Commander of the Believers.” She replied: “By God, I am not his concubine, nor am I lawful to him. I belong to God's wealth [the public treasury].” She went inside, then ʿUmar came out and asked: “What do you think it is lawful for me to take from God's wealth—or from this wealth?” We said: “The Commander of the Believers knows better than we do.” I think he questioned us again and we answered in the same way. records.text_ar: ٢٠٠٤٦ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنِ ابْنِ سِيرِينَ، عَنِ الْأَحْنَفِ بْنِ قَيْسٍ، قَالَ: كُنَّا جُلُوسًا عِنْدَ بَابِ عُمَرَ فَخَرَجَتْ عَلَيْنَا جَارِيَةٌ، فَقُلْنَا: هَذِهِ سُرِّيَّةُ أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ، فَقَالَتْ: وَاللَّهِ مَا أَنَا بِسُرِّيَّةٍ، وَمَا أَحِلُّ لَهُ، وَإِنِّي لَمِنْ مَالِ اللَّهِ، قَالَ: ثُمَّ دَخَلَتْ فَخَرَجَ عَلَيْنَا عُمَرُ فَقَالَ:   «مَا تَرَوْنَهُ يَحِلُّ لِي مِنْ مَالِ اللَّهِ؟ - أَوْ قَالَ: مِنْ هَذَا الْمَالِ؟ -»   ، قَالَ: قُلْنَا: أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَعْلَمُ بِذَلِكَ مِنَّا، - قَالَ: حَسِبْتُهُ قَالَ: ثُمَّ سَأَلَنَا فَقُلْنَا لَهُ مِثْلَ قَوْلِنَا الْأَوَّلِ - فَقَالَ:   «إِنْ شِئْتُمْ أَخْبَرْتُكُمْ §مَا - [١٠٥] - أَسْتَحِلُّ مِنْهُ: مَا أَحُجُّ وَأَعْتَمِرُ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الظَّهْرِ، وَحُلَّتِي فِي الشِّتَاءِ، وَحُلَّتِي فِي الصَّيْفِ، وَقُوتُ عِيَالِي شِبَعُهُمْ، وَسَهْمِي فِي الْمُسْلِمِينَ، فَإِنَّمَا أَنَا رَجُلٌ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ»   ، قَالَ مَعْمَرٌ:   «وَإِنَّمَا كَانَ الَّذِي يَحُجُّ عَلَيْهِ وَيَعْتَمِرُ بَعِيرًا وَاحِدًا»

I belong to God's wealth [the public treasury].” She went inside, then ʿUmar came out and asked: “What do you think it is lawful for me to take from God's wealth—or from this wealth?” We said: “The Commander of the Believers knows better than we do.” I think he questioned us again and we answered in the same way. He said: “If you wish, I shall tell you what I deem lawful to take from it: a riding animal for my pilgrimage and ʿumra; a set of clothes for winter and another for summer; enough food to feed my household; and my share along with the other Muslims, for I am merely one of the Muslims.” Maʿmar said: “The animal on which he performed pilgrimage and ʿumra was only a single camel.”

records.display_matn_ar: كُنَّا جُلُوسًا عِنْدَ بَابِ عُمَرَ فَخَرَجَتْ عَلَيْنَا جَارِيَةٌ، فَقُلْنَا: هَذِهِ سُرِّيَّةُ أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ، فَقَالَتْ: وَاللَّهِ مَا أَنَا بِسُرِّيَّةٍ، وَمَا أَحِلُّ لَهُ، وَإِنِّي لَمِنْ مَالِ اللَّهِ، قَالَ: ثُمَّ دَخَلَتْ فَخَرَجَ عَلَيْنَا عُمَرُ فَقَالَ:   «مَا تَرَوْنَهُ يَحِلُّ لِي مِنْ مَالِ اللَّهِ؟ - أَوْ قَالَ: مِنْ هَذَا الْمَالِ؟ -»   ، قَالَ: قُلْنَا: أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَعْلَمُ بِذَلِكَ مِنَّا، - قَالَ: حَسِبْتُهُ قَالَ: ثُمَّ سَأَلَنَا فَقُلْنَا لَهُ مِثْلَ قَوْلِنَا الْأَوَّلِ - فَقَالَ:   «إِنْ شِئْتُمْ أَخْبَرْتُكُمْ §مَا أَسْتَحِلُّ مِنْهُ: مَا أَحُجُّ وَأَعْتَمِرُ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الظَّهْرِ، وَحُلَّتِي فِي الشِّتَاءِ، وَحُلَّتِي فِي الصَّيْفِ، وَقُوتُ عِيَالِي شِبَعُهُمْ، وَسَهْمِي فِي الْمُسْلِمِينَ، فَإِنَّمَا أَنَا رَجُلٌ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ»   ، قَالَ مَعْمَرٌ:   «وَإِنَّمَا كَانَ الَّذِي يَحُجُّ عَلَيْهِ وَيَعْتَمِرُ بَعِيرًا وَاحِدًا»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb met a relative who approached him hoping to receive money. ʿUmar rebuked and scolded him, and the man departed. Later ʿUmar met him and said: “Did you come to me so that I might give you God's money? What would I say to God if I met Him as a treacherous ruler? Why did you not ask me from my own money?” He then gave him a considerable amount of his personal wealth. The narrator said: “I think he said ten thousand dirhams.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٠٤٧ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنِ ابْنِ سِيرِينَ، قَالَ: لَقِيَ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ ذَا قَرَابَةٍ لَهُ، فَعَرَضَ لِعُمَرَ أَنْ يُعْطِيَهُ مِنَ الْمَالِ، فَانْتَهَرَهُ عُمَرُ وَزَبَرَهُ، فَانْطَلَقَ الرَّجُلُ، ثُمَّ لَقِيَهُ عُمَرُ بَعْدُ، فَقَالَ لَهُ:   «§أَجِئْتَنِي لِأُعْطِيَكَ مَالَ اللَّهِ؟ مَاذَا أَقُولُ لِلَّهِ إِذَا لَقِيتُهُ مَلِكًا خَائِنًا؟ أَفَلَا كُنْتَ سَأَلْتَنِي مِنْ مَالِي»   ، فَأَعْطَاهُ مِنْ مَالِهِ مَالًا كَثِيرًا، قَالَ: حَسِبْتُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: عَشَرَةَ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, who said: When Abū Bakr became caliph, he said: “My people know that my trade was adequate to support my family. But I have become occupied with the Muslims' affairs, so I shall devote my work to their affairs, and Abū Bakr's household shall eat from this wealth.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, who said: Three men came to the Messenger of God ﷺ. One said: “I owned a hundred *ūqiyas* and spent ten in charity.” The next said: “I owned a hundred dinars and gave ten dinars in charity.” The third said: “I owned ten dinars and gave one dinar in charity.” The Prophet ﷺ said: “You are equal in reward. Each of you gave one-tenth of his wealth.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Whoever spends a pair of things from his wealth will be called from the gates of Paradise—and Paradise has gates. Whoever belongs to the people of prayer will be called from the gate of prayer; whoever belongs to the people of striving will be called from the gate of striving; whoever belongs to the people of fasting will be called from the gate of al-Rayyān.” Abū Bakr said: “By God, Messenger of God, no one is at any loss entering by whichever gate calls him. But is there anyone who will be called from all of them?” He said: “Yes, and I hope you will be one of them.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī, from Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī, who said: A man came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and said: “My mount has failed me; provide me with a mount.” The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “I have nothing, but go to so-and-so and ask him; perhaps he will give you a mount.” He went to him and received one. He then passed the Prophet ﷺ and told him that the man had provided a mount. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Whoever directs another to something good receives a reward like that of the person who does it.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported: Maʿmar reported from Ayyūb, from Ibn Abī Mulayka, that Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr said: “Messenger of God, I possess nothing except what al-Zubayr brings into the household. May I spend from it?” He said: “Spend, and do not tie up [your provision], lest it be tied up against you.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: A man came and asked the Prophet ﷺ for something. He replied: “We have nothing, but purchase something on our account.” ʿUmar said: “Give what you possess, but do not burden yourself with what you do not possess.” An Anṣārī man said: “Spend, Messenger of God, and do not fear poverty from the Lord of the Throne.” The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “That is what my Lord has commanded me.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Qatāda: When ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was stabbed, he said: “I commend the caliph after me to goodness. I commend to him the Emigrants: let him recognize their rights and accord them their proper standing. I commend to him the Anṣār, who had made their home and faith secure before [the others]: let him accept what their virtuous members do and overlook the wrongs of those who err. I commend to him the people of the garrison cities, for they are the support of Islam, a source of vexation to the enemy, and the treasury; let him not take any surplus from their alms except with their willing consent. I commend to him the Bedouin Arabs, for they are the origin of the Arabs and a source of strength for Islam: let their alms be collected from the outlying portions of their wealth and returned to their poor. I commend to him the protected non-Muslim communities: let him not burden them beyond their capacity; let him defend them and fulfill their covenants.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported: Maʿmar reported from al-Zuhrī, who said: Ibn Abī Namla al-Anṣārī informed me from his father, Abū Namla, that while he sat with the Prophet ﷺ a Jewish man approached as a funeral procession passed. He asked: “Muḥammad, does this dead person speak?” The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “God knows best.” The Jewish man said: “It does speak.” The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “When the People of the Book tell you something, neither believe them nor declare them liars. Say, ‘We believe...’ through ‘His books and His messengers’ [2:285]. If it is false you will not have believed it, and if it is true you will not have called it false.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٠٥٩ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ أَبِي نَمْلَةَ الْأَنْصَارِيُّ، أَنَّ أَبَاهُ أَبَا نَمَلَةَ، أَخْبَرَهُ أَنَّهُ بَيْنَا هُوَ جَالِسٌ عِنْدَ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ جَاءَهُ رَجُلٌ مِنَ الْيَهُودِ، وَمُرَّ بِجِنَازَةٍ، فَقَالَ: يَا مُحَمَّدُ، هَلْ تَكَلَّمُ هَذِهِ الْجِنَازَةُ؟ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ»   ، فَقَالَ الْيَهُودِيُّ: إِنَّهَا تَكَلَّمُ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§مَا حَدَّثَكُمْ أَهْلُ الْكِتَابِ فَلَا تُصَدِّقُوهُمْ، وَلَا تُكَذِّبُوهُمْ، وَقُولُوا: آمَنَّا. إِلَى  {وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ}   [البقرة: ٢٨٥]  ، فَإِنْ كَانَ بَاطِلًا لَمْ تُصَدِّقُوهُ، وَإِنْ كَانَ حَقًّا لَمْ تُكَذِّبُوهُ»

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported: Maʿmar reported from al-Zuhrī, who said: Ibn Abī Namla al-Anṣārī informed me from his father, Abū Namla, that while he sat with the Prophet ﷺ a Jewish man approached as a funeral procession passed. He asked: “Muḥammad, does this dead person speak?” The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “God knows best.” The Jewish man said: “It does speak.” The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “When the People of the Book tell you something, neither believe them nor declare them liars. Say, ‘We believe...’ through ‘His books and His messengers’ [2:285]. If it is false you will not have believed it, and if it is true you will not have called it false.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUtba, who said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: “How can you ask the People of the Book about anything when God's Book is among you, pure and unmixed, the most recent account from God? God has informed you that the People of the Book wrote a book with their own hands, said ‘This is from God,’ altered it, changed its words from their places, and sold it for a small price. Does what has come to you from God not restrain you from asking them? By God, we have never seen one of them asking you about the religion revealed to you.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported: Maʿmar reported from al-Zuhrī that Ḥafṣa came to the Prophet ﷺ with a text containing stories of Joseph written on a shoulder blade. She began reading it aloud to him, and the Prophet's ﷺ face changed color. He said: “By the One in whose hand is my soul, if Joseph came to you while I was among you, and you followed him and abandoned me, you would go astray.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilāba: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb passed a man reading a book and listened for a while. He liked what he heard and asked the man: “Will you copy something of this book for me?” He said: “Yes.” ʿUmar bought a piece of leather and prepared it, and the man copied the text on both its sides. ʿUmar brought it to the Messenger of God ﷺ and began to read it aloud, while the Messenger's ﷺ face changed color. An Anṣārī struck the document with his hand and said: “May your mother lose you, son of al-Khaṭṭāb! Have you not seen the expression on the Messenger of God's ﷺ face as you have been reading this book all day?” At that the Prophet ﷺ said: “I was sent as an opener and a seal, and I was given the beginnings and the concise comprehensive forms of speech. Do not let the polytheists destroy you.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٠٦٢ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ أَبِي قِلَابَةَ، أَنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ مَرَّ بِرَجُلٍ وَهُوَ يَقْرَأُ كِتَابًا، فَاسْتَمَعَهُ سَاعَةً، فَاسْتَحْسَنَهُ، فَقَالَ لِلرَّجُلِ: أَتَكْتُبُ لِي مِنْ هَذَا الْكِتَابِ؟ قَالَ: نَعَمْ، فَاشْتَرَى أَدِيمًا فَهَنَّاهُ، ثُمَّ جَاءَ بِهِ إِلَيْهِ فَنَسَخَهُ لَهُ فِي ظَهْرِهِ وَبَطْنِهِ، ثُمَّ أَتَى بِهِ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، فَجَعَلَ يَقْرَؤُهُ عَلَيْهِ، وَجَعَلَ وَجْهُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَتَلَوَّنُ، فَضَرَبَ رَجُلٌ مِنَ الْأَنْصَارِ بِيَدِهِ الْكِتَابَ، وَقَالَ: ثَكِلَتْكَ أُمُّكَ يَا ابْنَ الْخَطَّابِ، أَلَا تَرَى وَجْهَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ مُنْذُ الْيَوْمِ وَأَنْتَ تَقْرَأُ عَلَيْهِ هَذَا الْكِتَابَ، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عِنْدَ ذَلِكَ:   «إِنَّمَا §بُعِثْتُ فَاتِحًا وَخَاتَمًا، وَأُعْطِيتُ جَوَامِعَ الْكَلَامِ وَفَوَاتِحَهُ، فَلَا يُهْلِكَنَّكُمُ الْمُشْرِكُونَ»

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilāba: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb passed a man reading a book and listened for a while. He liked what he heard and asked the man: “Will you copy something of this book for me?” He said: “Yes.” ʿUmar bought a piece of leather and prepared it, and the man copied the text on both its sides. ʿUmar brought it to the Messenger of God ﷺ and began to read it aloud, while the Messenger's ﷺ face changed color. An Anṣārī struck the document with his hand and said: “May your mother lose you, son of al-Khaṭṭāb! Have you not seen the expression on the Messenger of God's ﷺ face as you have been reading this book all day?” At that the Prophet ﷺ said: “I was sent as an opener and a seal, and I was given the beginnings and the concise comprehensive forms of speech. Do not let the polytheists destroy you.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father: The Messenger of God ﷺ was asked: “Why do we act, Messenger of God? records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from his mother Umm Kulthūm bint ʿUqba—one of the earliest female Emigrants—that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf fell unconscious, and they thought his life was ending. She went out to the mosque to seek help through what she had been commanded: patience and prayer. When he recovered, he asked: “Was I unconscious?” They said: “Yes.” He replied: “You are right. Two angels came to me during this unconsciousness and said: ‘Come, let us bring you to judgment before the Mighty, the Trustworthy.’ Another angel said: ‘Send him back. He is among those for whom happiness was written while they were in their mothers’ wombs, and God will allow his children to benefit from him for as long as He wills.’” He lived a month afterward and then died.
records.text_ar: ٢٠٠٦٥ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ حُمَيْدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، عَنِ أُمِّهِ أُمِّ كُلْثُومٍ ابْنَةِ عُقْبَةَ - وَكَانَتْ مِنَ الْمُهَاجِرَاتِ الْأُوَلِ - أَنَّ عَبْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنَ عَوْفٍ غُشِيَ عَلَيْهِ غَشْيَةً، ظَنُّوا أَنَّ نَفْسَهُ فِيهَا، فَخَرَجَتْ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ تَسْتَعِينُ بِمَا أُمِرَتْ أَنْ تَسْتَعِينَ بِهِ مِنَ الصَّبْرِ وَالصَّلَاةِ، فَلَمَّا أَفَاقَ، قَالَ:   «أَغُشِيَ عَلَيَّ؟»   ، قَالُوا: نَعَمْ، قَالَ:   «صَدَقْتُمْ، إِنَّهُ §أَتَانِي مَلَكَانِ فِي غَشْيَتِي هَذِهِ، فَقَالَا: أَلَا تَنْطَلِقُ فَنُحَاكِمَكَ إِلَى الْعَزِيزِ الْأَمِينِ؟ فَقَالَ مَلَكٌ آخَرُ: أَرْجِعَاهُ فَإِنَّ هَذَا مِمَّنْ كُتِبَتْ لَهُ السَّعَادَةُ، وَهُمْ فِي بُطُونِ أُمَّهَاتِهِمْ، وَسَيُمَتِّعُ اللَّهُ بِهِ بَنِيهِ مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ»   ، قَالَ: فَعَاشَ شَهْرًا ثُمَّ مَاتَ

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, and from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, both of whom said: “Jesus son of Mary met Iblīs and said: ‘Do you not know that nothing will happen to you except what is decreed for you?’ Iblīs replied: ‘Then climb to the summit of this mountain and throw yourself down, and see whether you live or die.’ According to Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, Jesus answered: ‘Do you not know that God has said: “Let not My servant test Me, for I do whatever I will”?’ According to al-Zuhrī, he said: ‘A servant does not test his Lord; it is God who tests His servant.’ Thus he defeated Iblīs in the argument.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٠٧٠ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، وَعَنِ ابْنِ طَاوُسٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، قَالَا:   «§لَقِيَ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ إِبْلِيسَ فَقَالَ: أَمَا عَلِمْتَ أَنَّهُ لَا يُصِيبُكَ إِلَّا مَا قُدِّرَ لَكَ؟ فَقَالَ إِبْلِيسُ: فَأَوْفِ بِذِرْوَةِ هَذَا الْجَبَلِ، فتَرَدَّ مِنْهُ، فَانْظُرْ أَتَعِيشُ أَمْ لَا؟ - قَالَ ابْنُ طَاوُسٍ: عَنْ أَبِيهِ - فَقَالَ: أَمَا عَلِمْتَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ قَالَ: لَا يُجَرِّبُنِي عَبْدِي، فَإِنِّي أَفْعَلُ مَا شِئْتُ، قَالَ: - وَقَالَ الزُّهْرِيُّ: قَالَ: - إِنَّ الْعَبْدَ لَا يَبْتَلِي رَبَّهُ، وَلَكُنَّ اللَّهَ يَبْتَلِي عَبْدَهُ، قَالَ: فَخَصَمَهُ»

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, and from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, both of whom said: “Jesus son of Mary met Iblīs and said: ‘Do you not know that nothing will happen to you except what is decreed for you?’ Iblīs replied: ‘Then climb to the summit of this mountain and throw yourself down, and see whether you live or die.’ According to Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, Jesus answered: ‘Do you not know that God has said: “Let not My servant test Me, for I do whatever I will”?’ According to al-Zuhrī, he said: ‘A servant does not test his Lord; it is God who tests His servant.’ Thus he defeated Iblīs in the argument.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported: Maʿmar reported from al-Zuhrī, who said: “It reached me that three tablets, each bearing an inscription, were found at the Station of Abraham. On the first was written: ‘I am God, Lord of Bakka. I fashioned it on the day I fashioned the sun, surrounded it with seven angels, and blessed its people with meat and milk.’ On the second: ‘I am God, Lord of Bakka. I created the ties of kinship, deriving a name for them from My name. Whoever maintains them, I maintain connection with him; whoever severs them, I sever him.’ On the third: ‘I am God, Lord of Bakka. I created good and evil. Blessed is one through whose hands good comes; woe to one through whose hands evil comes.’”

records.display_matn_en: It reached me that three tablets, each bearing an inscription, were found at the Station of Abraham. On the first was written: ‘I am God, Lord of Bakka. I fashioned it on the day I fashioned the sun, surrounded it with seven angels, and blessed its people with meat and milk.’ On the second: ‘I am God, Lord of Bakka. I created the ties of kinship, deriving a name for them from My name. Whoever maintains them, I maintain connection with him; whoever severs them, I sever him.’ On the third: ‘I am God, Lord of Bakka. I created good and evil. Blessed is one through whose hands good comes; woe to one through whose hands evil comes.’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported: Maʿmar reported from Manṣūr, from Saʿd ibn ʿUbayda, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, who said: We went out for a funeral. As we were in al-Baqīʿ, the Messenger of God ﷺ came to us holding a small staff. He sat down and scratched the earth with it for a time, then said: “There is no living soul whose place in Paradise or the Fire has not been written, and who has not been written as wretched or blessed.” A man asked: “Shall we not rely on what has been written for us, Messenger of God, and give up deeds?” He said: “No; rather, act. Everyone is made ready [for his course]. Those destined for wretchedness are made ready for the deeds of the wretched, and those destined for blessedness for the deeds of the blessed.” He then recited: “As for him who gives and is mindful [of God], and affirms the best, We shall ease him toward ease; but whoever is miserly, deems himself self-sufficient, and denies the best, We shall ease him toward hardship” (92:5–10). records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, who said: “Avoid disputing about the decree, for those who argue about it speak without knowledge.”

records.display_matn_ar: إِنَّمَا هُمَا اثْنَتَانِ: الْهَدْي وَالْكَلَامُ، فَأَحْسَنُ الْكَلَامِ كَلَامُ اللَّهِ، وَأَحْسَنُ الْهَدْيِ هَدْي مُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، أَلَا إِيَّاكُمْ وَالْمُحَرَّمَاتِ وَالْبِدَعَ، فَإِنَّ شَرَّ الْأُمُورِ مُحْدَثَاتُهَا، وَكُلَّ مُحْدَثَةٍ ضَلَالَةٌ، أَلَا لَا يَطُولُ عَلَيْكُمُ الْأَمَدُ فَتَقْسُوَ قُلُوبُكُمْ، أَلَا كُلُّ مَا هُوَ آتٍ قَرِيبٌ، أَلَا إِنَّ الْبَعِيدَ مَا لَيْسَ بِآتٍ، أَلَا إِنَّ الشَّقِيَّ مَنْ شَقِيَ فِي بَطْنِ أُمِّهِ، وَإِنَّ السَّعِيدَ مَنْ وُعِظَ بِغَيْرِهِ، أَلَا وَإِنَّ شَرَّ الرَّوَايَا رَوَايَا الْكَذِبِ، أَلَا وَإِنَّ الْكَذِبَ لَا يَصْلُحُ فِي جِدٍّ وَلَا هَزْلٍ، وَلَا أَنْ يَعِدَ الرَّجُلُ صَبِيَّهُ ثُمَّ لَا يُنْجِزُ لَهُ، أَلَا وَإِنَّ الْكَذِبَ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْفُجُورِ، وَإِنَّ الْفُجُورَ يَهْدِي إِلَى النَّارِ، وَإِنَّ الصِّدْقَ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْبِرِّ، وَإِنَّ الْبِرَّ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ، وَإِنَّهُ يُقَالُ لِلصَّادِقِ: صَدَقَ وَبَرَّ، وَيُقَالُ لِلْكَاذِبِ: كَذَبَ وَفَجَرَ، وَإِنِّي سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَقُولُ:   «إِنَّ §الْعَبْدَ لَيَكْذِبُ حَتَّى يُكْتَبَ كَذَّابًا، وَيَصْدُقُ حَتَّى يُكْتَبَ صِدِّيقًا»   ثُمَّ قَالَ:   « إِيَّاكُمْ وَالْعِضَةَ، أَتَدْرُونَ مَا الْعِضَةُ؟ النَّمِيمَةُ، وَنَقْلُ الْأَحَادِيثِ»
records.display_isnad_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported: Maʿmar reported from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: “
records.display_matn_en: There are only two things: guidance and speech. The best speech is God's speech, and the best guidance is the guidance of Muḥammad ﷺ. Beware of forbidden matters and innovations, for the worst matters are those newly introduced, and every innovation is error. Do not let time stretch on for you so that your hearts grow hard. Everything that is coming is near, and the truly distant thing is that which will never come. The wretched one is the one made wretched in his mother's womb, and the blessed one takes warning from what happens to others. The worst accounts are false accounts. Lying is not permissible either in earnest or in jest, nor for a man to promise his child something and fail to deliver it. Lying leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire. Truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. The truthful person is said to have spoken truth and acted rightly, and the liar to have lied and acted wickedly. I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘A servant continues to lie until he is written down as a liar, and continues to speak truth until he is written down as a most truthful person.’” He then said: “Beware of *ʿiḍa*. Do you know what *ʿiḍa* is? Tale-bearing and passing stories between people.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said, placing his hand over his mouth: “A man will never taste faith until he believes in the decree and knows that he will die and be resurrected.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, that Ibn Masʿūd said: “Three things, when present in a person, enable him to taste the sweetness of faith: abandoning disputation even when in the right; abandoning lying in jest; and knowing that what befell him could never have missed him and what missed him could never have befallen him.” [The Arabic text literally has “lying in jest” without an explicit second “abandoning”; supplied for the intended parallel construction.]

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥajjāj, a man of Asad, who said: I asked Salmān: “Abū ʿAbdullāh, what is belief in the decree?” He replied: “That a man should know within himself that what befell him could never have missed him, and what missed him could never have befallen him. That is belief in the decree.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from more than one person, from al-Ḥasan, who used to say: “Appointed lifespans, provisions, afflictions, misfortunes, and good deeds are by God's decree; evil deeds arise from ourselves and from Satan.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Ibn al-Musayyib, from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Every child is born upon the natural disposition (*fiṭra*). His parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Magian, just as a beast gives birth [to a sound animal]: do you notice one born mutilated?” Abū Hurayra would then say: “Recite, if you wish: ‘God's natural disposition upon which He fashioned humanity’” (30:30). Maʿmar said: I asked al-Zuhrī: “How do you narrate this when you hold a different position?” He replied: “We narrate what we have heard.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٠٨٧ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنِ ابْنِ الْمُسَيِّبِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§كُلُّ مَوْلُودٍ يُولَدُ عَلَى الْفِطْرَةِ، فَأَبَوَاهُ يُهَوِّدَانِهِ أَوْ يُنَصِّرَانِهِ أَوْ يُمَجِّسَانِهِ كَمَا تُنْتَجُ الْبَهِيمَةُ، هَلْ تُحِسُّونَ فِيهَا مِنْ جَدْعَاءَ»   ، قَالَ: ثُمَّ يَقُولُ أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ:   «وَاقْرَءُوا إِنْ شِئْتُمْ:  {فِطْرَةَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي فَطَرَ النَّاسَ عَلَيْهَا}   [الروم: ٣٠]»   ، قَالَ مَعْمَرٌ: فَقُلْتُ لِلزُّهْرِيِّ: كَيْفَ تُحَدِّثُ بِهَذَا وَأَنْتَ عَلَى غَيْرِهِ؟ قَالَ:   «نُحَدِّثُ بِمَا سَمِعْنَا»

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Ibn al-Musayyib, from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Every child is born upon the natural disposition (*fiṭra*). His parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Magian, just as a beast gives birth [to a sound animal]: do you notice one born mutilated?” Abū Hurayra would then say: “Recite, if you wish: ‘God's natural disposition upon which He fashioned humanity’” (30:30). Maʿmar said: I asked al-Zuhrī: “How do you narrate this when you hold a different position?” He replied: “We narrate what we have heard.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported: Maʿmar reported from Qatāda, from Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr, from ʿIyāḍ ibn Ḥimār al-Mujāshiʿī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “God commanded me to teach you today what you do not know of what He taught me. He said: ‘All wealth I have granted My dependents is lawful for them. I created all My servants inclined to true faith, but the devils came and turned them away from their religion, forbade them what I had made lawful, and ordered them to associate with Me what I had given no authority for.’ God looked upon the inhabitants of the earth and detested them, Arabs and non-Arabs alike, except for remnants of the People of the Book. God commanded me to burn [fight] Quraysh. I said: ‘My Lord, then they will crush my head until it resembles a flattened loaf.’ He said: ‘I sent you to test you and to test others through you. I have revealed to you a Book that water cannot wash away; you recite it asleep and awake. Campaign against them, and We shall campaign with you. Spend, and We shall provide for you. Dispatch an army, and We shall reinforce you with five times its number. Fight those who disobey you with those who obey you.’ Then he said: ‘The people of Paradise are three: a just ruler; a merciful man, tenderhearted toward every relative and Muslim; and a wealthy man who is chaste and charitable. The people of the Fire are five: a weak person lacking restraint, among you as followers who seek neither family nor property; a man who begins the day plotting deceit against you concerning your family and wealth; a man whose greed, however slight the opportunity, drives him to seize it; and a foul-mouthed, brutal person.’” He said that miserliness and lying were also mentioned.
records.text_ar: ٢٠٠٨٨ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، عَنْ مُطَرِّفِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ الشِّخِّيرِ، عَنْ عِيَاضِ بْنِ حِمَارٍ الْمُجَاشِعِيِّ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «إِنَّ اللَّهَ أَمَرَنِي أَنْ أُعَلِّمَكُمْ مَا جَهِلْتُمْ مِمَّا عَلَّمَنِي يَوْمِي هَذَا، وَأَنَّهُ قَالَ: §إِنَّ كُلَّ مَالٍ نَحَلْتُ عِيَالِي فَهُوَ لَهُمْ حَلَالٌ، وَإِنِّي خَلَقْتُ عِبَادِي كُلَّهُمْ حُنَفَاءَ، فأَتَتْهُمُ الشَّيَاطِينُ فَاجْتَالَتْهُمْ عَنْ دِينِهِمْ، وَحَرَّمَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ مَا أَحْلَلْتُ، وَأَمَرَتْهُمْ أَنْ يُشْرِكُوا بِي مَا لَمْ أُنَزِّلْ بِهِ سُلْطَانًا، وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ نَظَرَ إِلَى أَهْلِ الْأَرْضِ فَمَقَتَهُمْ عَرَبَهُمْ وَعَجَمَهُمْ إِلَّا بَقَايَا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ، وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ أَمَرَنِي أَنْ أُحَرِّقَ قُرَيْشًا، فَقُلْتُ: - [١٢١] - يَا رَبِّ، إِذًا يَثْلَغُوا رَأْسِي حَتَّى يَدْعُوهُ خُبْزَةً، فَقَالَ: إِنَّمَا بَعَثْتُكَ لِأَبْتَلِيَكَ وَأَبْتَلِيَ بِكَ، وَقَدْ أَنْزَلْتُ عَلَيْكَ كِتَابًا لَا يَغْسِلُهُ الْمَاءُ، تَقْرَؤُهُ فِي الْمَنَامِ وَالْيَقَظَةِ، وَاغْزُهُمْ نُغْزِكَ، وَأَنْفِقْ يُنْفَقْ عَلَيْكَ، وَابْعَثْ جَيْشًا نُمْدِدْكَ بِخَمْسَةِ أَمْثَالِهِمْ، وَقَاتِلْ بِمَنْ أَطَاعَكَ مَنْ عَصَاكَ، ثُمَّ قَالَ: أَهْلُ الْجَنَّةِ ثَلَاثَةٌ: إِمَّام مُقْسِطٌ وَرَجُلٌ رَحِيمٌ رَقِيقُ الْقَلْبِ لِكُلِّ ذِي قُرْبَى وَمُسْلِمٍ، وَرَجُلٌ غَنِيُّ عَفِيفٌ مُتَصَدِّقٌ، وَأَهْلُ النَّارِ خَمْسَةٌ: الضَّعِيفُ الَّذِي لَا زَبْرَ لَهُ، الَّذِينَ هُمْ فِيكُمْ تَبَعٌ لَا يَبْتَغُونَ بِذَلِكَ أَهْلًا وَلَا مَالًا، وَرَجُلٌ إِنْ أَصْبَحَ أَصْبَحَ يُخَادِعُكَ عَنْ أَهْلِكَ وَمَالِكَ، وَرَجُلٌ لَا يَخْفَى لَهُ طَمَعٌ وَإِنْ دَقَّ إِلَّا ذَهَبَ بِهِ، وَالشِّنْظِيرُ الْفَاحِشُ، قَالَ: وَذَكَرَ الْبُخْلَ وَالْكَذِبَ»

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported: Maʿmar reported from Qatāda, from Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr, from ʿIyāḍ ibn Ḥimār al-Mujāshiʿī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “God commanded me to teach you today what you do not know of what He taught me. He said: ‘All wealth I have granted My dependents is lawful for them. I created all My servants inclined to true faith, but the devils came and turned them away from their religion, forbade them what I had made lawful, and ordered them to associate with Me what I had given no authority for.’ God looked upon the inhabitants of the earth and detested them, Arabs and non-Arabs alike, except for remnants of the People of the Book. God commanded me to burn [fight] Quraysh. I said: ‘My Lord, then they will crush my head until it resembles a flattened loaf.’ He said: ‘I sent you to test you and to test others through you. I have revealed to you a Book that water cannot wash away; you recite it asleep and awake. Campaign against them, and We shall campaign with you. Spend, and We shall provide for you. Dispatch an army, and We shall reinforce you with five times its number. Fight those who disobey you with those who obey you.’ Then he said: ‘The people of Paradise are three: a just ruler; a merciful man, tenderhearted toward every relative and Muslim; and a wealthy man who is chaste and charitable. The people of the Fire are five: a weak person lacking restraint, among you as followers who seek neither family nor property; a man who begins the day plotting deceit against you concerning your family and wealth; a man whose greed, however slight the opportunity, drives him to seize it; and a foul-mouthed, brutal person.’” He said that miserliness and lying were also mentioned.

records.isnad_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported: Maʿmar reported from Qatāda, from Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr, from ʿIyāḍ ibn Ḥimār al-Mujāshiʿī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “
records.matn_en: God commanded me to teach you today what you do not know of what He taught me. He said: ‘All wealth I have granted My dependents is lawful for them. I created all My servants inclined to true faith, but the devils came and turned them away from their religion, forbade them what I had made lawful, and ordered them to associate with Me what I had given no authority for.’ God looked upon the inhabitants of the earth and detested them, Arabs and non-Arabs alike, except for remnants of the People of the Book. God commanded me to burn [fight] Quraysh. I said: ‘My Lord, then they will crush my head until it resembles a flattened loaf.’ He said: ‘I sent you to test you and to test others through you. I have revealed to you a Book that water cannot wash away; you recite it asleep and awake. Campaign against them, and We shall campaign with you. Spend, and We shall provide for you. Dispatch an army, and We shall reinforce you with five times its number. Fight those who disobey you with those who obey you.’ Then he said: ‘The people of Paradise are three: a just ruler; a merciful man, tenderhearted toward every relative and Muslim; and a wealthy man who is chaste and charitable. The people of the Fire are five: a weak person lacking restraint, among you as followers who seek neither family nor property; a man who begins the day plotting deceit against you concerning your family and wealth; a man whose greed, however slight the opportunity, drives him to seize it; and a foul-mouthed, brutal person.’” He said that miserliness and lying were also mentioned.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from someone who heard al-Ḥasan relate from al-Aswad ibn Sarīʿ, who said: The Prophet ﷺ sent a detachment that went so far in killing that it killed children. The Prophet ﷺ asked them: “What induced you to kill children?” They said: “Messenger of God, are they not the children of polytheists?” Then the Prophet ﷺ stood to preach and said: “Every newborn is born upon the natural disposition until his tongue begins to articulate [his choice].”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, who said: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz wrote to ʿAdī ibn Arṭāʾa: “To proceed: Your appointment of Saʿd ibn Masʿūd over Oman was among the mistakes God decreed for you and decreed that you would be tested by.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported: Maʿmar informed us, saying: My father informed us that Abū al-Miqdām said to Wahb: “Abū Muḥammad, I have sat with you, and earlier you said: ‘I sat with ʿAṭāʾ and Mujāhid, and they disagreed with you.’” He answered: “Each side arrived at something right: these declared God above imperfection, and those were zealous on God's behalf, but they erred in interpretation.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from al-Thawrī, from al-Aʿmash, from Zayd ibn Wahb, who said: Ibn Masʿūd informed us: The Messenger of God ﷺ—who is truthful and affirmed as truthful—told us: “The creation of each of you is gathered in his mother's womb for forty nights. Then he is a clot for a similar period, and then a lump of flesh for a similar period. God then sends the angel with four instructions, saying: ‘Write his lifespan, his deeds, and whether he is wretched or blessed.’ A man may perform the deeds of the people of Paradise until only an arm's length separates him from it, but what was written previously overtakes him, so his life ends with the deeds of the people of the Fire. A man may perform the deeds of the people of the Fire until only an arm's length separates him from it, but what was written previously overtakes him, and he performs the deeds of the people of Paradise and enters it.” [The Arabic says “four” but lists lifespan, deeds, and the alternative of wretchedness or blessedness.]
records.text_ar: ٢٠٠٩٣ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنِ الثَّوْرِيِّ، عَنِ الْأَعْمَشِ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ وَهْبٍ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَهُوَ الصَّادِقُ الْمَصْدُوقُ:   «إِنَّ خَلْقَ أَحَدِكُمْ يُجْمَعُ فِي بَطْنِ أُمِّهِ أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً، ثُمَّ يَكُونُ عَلَقَةً مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ يَكُونُ مُضْغَةً مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ يَبْعَثُ اللَّهُ الْمَلَكَ بِأَرْبَعِ كَلِمَاتٍ فَيَقُولُ: §اكْتُبْ أَجَلَهُ وَعَمَلَهُ، وَشَقِيُّ أَوْ سَعِيدٌ، وَإِنَّ الرَّجُلَ لَيَعْمَلُ بِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ حَتَّى يَكُونَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ الْجَنَّةِ إِلَّا ذِرَاعٌ، فَيَغْلِبُ عَلَيْهِ الْكِتَابُ الَّذِي سَبَقَ، فَيُخْتَمُ لَهُ بِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ النَّارِ، وَإِنَّ الرَّجُلَ لَيَعْمَلُ بِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ النَّارِ حَتَّى يَكُونَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَهَا إِلَّا ذِرَاعٌ، فَيَغْلِبُ عَلَيْهِ الْكِتَابُ الَّذِي سَبَقَ، فَيَعْمَلُ بِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ فَيَدْخُلُ الْجَنَّةَ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from al-Thawrī, from Fiṭr, from Ibn Sābiṭ, from Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, who said: “God created creation, and they were two handfuls. records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Ḥafṣ, from Yaʿlā ibn Murra, who said: A number of us, companions of ʿAlī, gathered, and I said: “We should guard the Commander of the Believers, since he is at war and we cannot be sure someone will not assassinate him.” We guarded the door of his chamber until he came out for dawn prayer. He asked: “What is the matter with you?” We replied: “We have been guarding you, Commander of the Believers, because you are at war and we feared you might be assassinated.” He asked: “Are you guarding me against the inhabitants of heaven or the inhabitants of earth?” We said: “Against the inhabitants of earth. How could we guard you from the inhabitants of heaven?” He answered: “Nothing occurs on earth until it has been decreed in heaven. Every person has two angels entrusted to repel harm from him and protect him until his appointed decree arrives. When it comes, they leave him to what has been decreed for him.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar: It reached me that ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said to Abū Mūsā: “I wish I could find someone before whom I might bring a complaint against my Lord.” Abū Mūsā said: “I [will hear you].” ʿAmr asked: “Does He decree something for me and then punish me for it?” Abū Mūsā replied: “Yes.” ʿAmr asked: “Why?” He answered: “Because He does not wrong him.” ʿAmr said: “You have spoken truly.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, who said: I was with Ibn Ṭāwūs, and a son of his was there, when a man called Ṣāliḥ, who discussed the decree, came and began saying something on the subject. Ibn Ṭāwūs became alert, put his fingers in his ears, and told his son: “Put your fingers in your ears and press them firmly. Do not listen to any of what he says, for the heart is weak.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from ʿImrān, an associate of his, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “I have left nothing that brings you nearer Paradise and farther from the Fire without making it clear to you. The Holy Spirit has breathed into my consciousness and informed me that no soul dies before receiving its complete provision, even if it is slow in coming. People, be mindful of God and seek your livelihood properly. Let no one, because his provision is slow in coming, turn to something God has forbidden him. What is with God is attained only through obedience to Him.”

The Holy Spirit has breathed into my consciousness and informed me that no soul dies before receiving its complete provision, even if it is slow in coming. People, be mindful of God and seek your livelihood properly. Let no one, because his provision is slow in coming, turn to something God has forbidden him. What is with God is attained only through obedience to Him.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, who said: A man said to Ibn ʿAbbās: “Praise be to God, who has placed our inclinations in accordance with yours.” Ibn ʿAbbās replied: “All inclination [of this kind] is error.” [The expression *hawā* can mean personal inclination or caprice.]

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported: Maʿmar reported from Ibn Abī Kathīr, from Zayd ibn Sallām, from Abū Sallām, from Abū Umāma, who said: A man asked: “What is sin, Messenger of God?” He replied: “Whatever troubles your breast—leave it.” He asked: “What is faith?” He said: “Whoever is distressed by his bad deeds and gladdened by his good deeds is a believer.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Suhayl ibn Abī Ṣāliḥ, from his father, from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Faith has seventy-odd—or he said sixty-odd—branches. The highest is testimony that there is no god but God, and the least is removing harmful things from the road. Modesty is a branch of faith.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported: Maʿmar reported from al-Aʿmash, from Shaqīq, who said: We were traveling with Ibn Masʿūd when we met a group of riders. We asked: “Who are you?” They replied: “We are the believers.” Ibn Masʿūd said: “Why did they not say: ‘We are the people of Paradise’?” [His reply is rhetorical, questioning their self-certification.]
records.text_ar: ٢٠١٠٦ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنِ الْأَعْمَشِ، عَنْ شَقِيقٍ، قَالَ: كُنَّا مَعَ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ فِي سَفَرٍ، فَلَقِيَ رَكْبًا فَقُلْنَا: مَنِ الْقَوْمُ؟ قَالُوا: نَحْنُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ، قَالَ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ:   «§فَهَلَّا قَالُوا: نَحْنُ أَهْلُ الْجَنَّةِ»

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported: Maʿmar reported from al-Aʿmash, from Shaqīq, who said: We were traveling with Ibn Masʿūd when we met a group of riders. We asked: “Who are you?” They replied: “We are the believers.” Ibn Masʿūd said: “Why did they not say: ‘We are the people of Paradise’?” [His reply is rhetorical, questioning their self-certification.]

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilāba, from ʿAmr ibn ʿAbasa, who said: A man asked: “Messenger of God, what is Islam?” He replied: “That your heart submit to God, and that Muslims be safe from your tongue and your hand.” He asked: “Which Islam is best?” He said: “Faith.” He asked: “What is faith?” He said: “To believe in God, His angels, His books, His messengers, and resurrection after death.” He asked: “Which aspect of faith is best?” He said: “Emigration.” He asked: “What is emigration?” He replied: “To abandon evil.” He asked: “Which emigration is best?” He said: “Striving.” He asked: “What is striving?” He replied: “To fight the unbelievers when you encounter them.” He asked: “Which kind of striving is best?” He replied: “That of one whose horse is hamstrung and whose blood is shed.” The Prophet ﷺ then said: “There are two further deeds among the finest of all deeds, unless someone does their equal: a pilgrimage accepted [by God], or an ʿumra.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠١٠٧ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ أَبِي قِلَابَةَ، عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ عَبْسَةَ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَجُلٌ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، مَا الْإِسْلَامُ؟ قَالَ:   «أَنْ §يُسْلِمَ قَلْبُكَ لِلَّهِ، وَأَنْ يَسْلَمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِكَ وَيَدِكَ»   ، قَالَ: فَأَيُّ الْإِسْلَامِ أَفْضَلُ؟ قَالَ:   «الْإِيمَانُ»   ، قَالَ: وَمَا الْإِيمَانُ؟ قَالَ:   «أَنْ تُؤْمِنَ بِاللَّهِ، وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ، وَكُتُبِهِ، وَرُسُلِهِ، وَالْبَعْثِ بَعْدَ الْمَوْتِ»   ، قَالَ: فَأَيُّ الْإِيمَانِ أَفْضَلُ؟ قَالَ:   «الْهِجْرَةُ»   ، قَالَ: وَمَا الْهِجْرَةُ؟ قَالَ:   «أَنْ تَهْجُرَ السُّوءَ»   ، قَالَ: فَأَيُّ الْهِجْرَةِ أَفْضَلُ؟ قَالَ:   «الْجِهَادُ»   ، قَالَ: وَمَا الْجِهَادُ؟ قَالَ:   «أَنْ تُقَاتِلَ الْكُفَّارَ إِذَا لَقِيتَهُمْ»   ، قَالَ: فَأَيُّ الْجِهَادِ أَفْضَلُ؟ قَالَ:   «مَنْ عُقِرَ جَوَادُهُ وَأُهْرِيقَ دَمُهُ»   ، قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «ثُمَّ عَمَلَانِ هُمَا مِنْ أَفْضَلِ الْأَعْمَالِ إِلَّا مَنْ عَمِلَ بِمِثْلِهِمَا: حَجَّةٌ مَبْرُورَةٌ، أَوْ عُمْرَةٌ»

records.display_matn_ar: قَالَ رَجُلٌ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، مَا الْإِسْلَامُ؟ قَالَ:   «أَنْ §يُسْلِمَ قَلْبُكَ لِلَّهِ، وَأَنْ يَسْلَمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِكَ وَيَدِكَ»   ، قَالَ: فَأَيُّ الْإِسْلَامِ أَفْضَلُ؟ قَالَ:   «الْإِيمَانُ»   ، قَالَ: وَمَا الْإِيمَانُ؟ قَالَ:   «أَنْ تُؤْمِنَ بِاللَّهِ، وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ، وَكُتُبِهِ، وَرُسُلِهِ، وَالْبَعْثِ بَعْدَ الْمَوْتِ»   ، قَالَ: فَأَيُّ الْإِيمَانِ أَفْضَلُ؟ قَالَ:   «الْهِجْرَةُ»   ، قَالَ: وَمَا الْهِجْرَةُ؟ قَالَ:   «أَنْ تَهْجُرَ السُّوءَ»   ، قَالَ: فَأَيُّ الْهِجْرَةِ أَفْضَلُ؟ قَالَ:   «الْجِهَادُ»   ، قَالَ: وَمَا الْجِهَادُ؟ قَالَ:   «أَنْ تُقَاتِلَ الْكُفَّارَ إِذَا لَقِيتَهُمْ»   ، قَالَ: فَأَيُّ الْجِهَادِ أَفْضَلُ؟ قَالَ:   «مَنْ عُقِرَ جَوَادُهُ وَأُهْرِيقَ دَمُهُ»   ، قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «ثُمَّ عَمَلَانِ هُمَا مِنْ أَفْضَلِ الْأَعْمَالِ إِلَّا مَنْ عَمِلَ بِمِثْلِهِمَا: حَجَّةٌ مَبْرُورَةٌ، أَوْ عُمْرَةٌ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, who said: A man came to my father and said: “Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, you are my brother.” He replied: “Among God's Muslim servants?” [The Arabic phrase is compressed and its precise rhetorical sense is uncertain.]

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, that Sufyān ibn ʿAbdullāh al-Thaqafī said: “Tell me something from which I can benefit.” He replied: “Say, ‘I believe in God,’ and then remain upright.” I asked: “What do you fear most for me?” He took hold of his tongue and said: “This.” [The source leaves the speaker of the answer implicit; the parallel prophetic wording is reflected by the context.]

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, that a man from Banū Sulaymān came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and said: “Messenger of God, I have heard that whoever does not emigrate is ruined.” The Prophet ﷺ said: “Perform the prayer, pay alms, make pilgrimage to the House, fast the month of Ramadan, and live wherever you wish among your own people.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠١١٢ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، أَنَّ رَجُلًا مِنْ بَنِي سُلَيْمَانَ جَاءَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَقَالَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، بَلَغَنِي أَنَّهُ مَنْ لَمْ يُهَاجِرْ فَقَدْ هَلَكَ؟ فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§اقْضِ الصَّلَاةَ، وَآتِ الزَّكَاةَ، وَحِجَّ الْبَيْتَ، وَصُمْ شَهْرَ رَمَضَانَ، وانْزِلْ مِنْ قَوْمِكَ حَيْثُ أَحْبَبْتَ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Mismār and Jaʿfar ibn Burqān, that the Prophet ﷺ asked al-Ḥārith ibn Mālik: “What are you, Ḥārith ibn Mālik?” He said: “A believer, Messenger of God.” He asked: “A true believer?” He answered: “A true believer.” He said: “Every truth has a reality. What is the reality of that?” He replied: “My soul has turned away from the world. I stay awake at night and thirst by day. records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Bahz ibn Ḥakīm ibn Muʿāwiya, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: “By God, before coming to you I had sworn as many oaths as I have fingers that I would not follow you or your religion. I have now come as a man who knows only what God and His messenger have taught me. By God, I ask you: With what has your Lord sent you to us?” He said: “Sit down,” and then: “With Islam; yes, with Islam.” I asked: “What is the sign of Islam?” He said: “That you testify there is no god but God and Muḥammad is His messenger, establish prayer, give alms, and leave idolatry. Each Muslim is inviolable to another Muslim: two brothers supporting one another. God accepts no deed from an idolater who returns to idolatry after his Islam. My Lord will summon me and ask: ‘Did you convey [the message] to My servants?’ Let those of you present convey it to those absent. You will be summoned with your mouths sealed by a muzzle; the first thing to speak about each of you will be his thigh and his palm.” I said: “Messenger of God, is this our religion?” He said: “Yes. Wherever you do good, it will suffice you. You will be gathered on your faces, on your feet, and riding.”

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Bahz ibn Ḥakīm ibn Muʿāwiya, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: “By God, before coming to you I had sworn as many oaths as I have fingers that I would not follow you or your religion. I have now come as a man who knows only what God and His messenger have taught me. By God, I ask you: With what has your Lord sent you to us?” He said: “Sit down,” and then: “With Islam; yes, with Islam.” I asked: “What is the sign of Islam?” He said: “That you testify there is no god but God and Muḥammad is His messenger, establish prayer, give alms, and leave idolatry. Each Muslim is inviolable to another Muslim: two brothers supporting one another. God accepts no deed from an idolater who returns to idolatry after his Islam. My Lord will summon me and ask: ‘Did you convey [the message] to My servants?’ Let those of you present convey it to those absent. You will be summoned with your mouths sealed by a muzzle; the first thing to speak about each of you will be his thigh and his palm.” I said: “Messenger of God, is this our religion?” He said: “Yes. Wherever you do good, it will suffice you. You will be gathered on your faces, on your feet, and riding.”

I have now come as a man who knows only what God and His messenger have taught me. By God, I ask you: With what has your Lord sent you to us?” He said: “Sit down,” and then: “With Islam; yes, with Islam.” I asked: “What is the sign of Islam?” He said: “That you testify there is no god but God and Muḥammad is His messenger, establish prayer, give alms, and leave idolatry. Each Muslim is inviolable to another Muslim: two brothers supporting one another. God accepts no deed from an idolater who returns to idolatry after his Islam. My Lord will summon me and ask: ‘Did you convey [the message] to My servants?’ Let those of you present convey it to those absent. You will be summoned with your mouths sealed by a muzzle; the first thing to speak about each of you will be his thigh and his palm.” I said: “Messenger of God, is this our religion?” He said: “Yes. Wherever you do good, it will suffice you. You will be gathered on your faces, on your feet, and riding.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported: Maʿmar reported from ʿUthmān ibn Zufar, from a member of the descendants of Rāfiʿ ibn Makīth, from Rāfiʿ ibn Makīth—who had attended al-Ḥudaybiyya—that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Good treatment of those in one's charge brings increase; bad character brings ill fortune; righteousness lengthens one's life; and charity prevents an evil death.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwa, from ʿĀʾisha, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “I slept and saw myself in Paradise. I heard the voice of someone reciting and asked: ‘Who is this?’ They answered: ‘Ḥāritha ibn al-Nuʿmān.’ The Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘Such is the reward of dutifulness.’” He was among the most dutiful of people toward his mother.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Ismāʿīl ibn Umayya: A man said: “Advise me, Messenger of God.” He replied: “Do not associate anything with God, even if you are burned or cut in half.” He asked for more, and he said: “Be dutiful to your parents and do not raise your voice in their presence. If they command you to part with your worldly possessions, do so for them.” He asked for more, and he replied: “Do not drink wine, for it is the key to every evil.” He asked for more, and he said: “Discipline your household, spend on them from your means, and do not withdraw your staff from them; instill in them awe concerning God.” Maʿmar said: “Some interpret ‘the staff’ here to mean the tongue.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, who said: When Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī and Abū ʿĀmir came to the Messenger of God ﷺ, pledged allegiance, and accepted Islam, he asked: “What happened to a woman among you called so-and-so?” They answered: “We left her among her family.” He said: “She has been forgiven.” They asked: “For what, Messenger of God?” He replied: “For her dutifulness to her mother. She had an elderly mother. Word came warning them that enemies intended to raid them that night, and they set out to join their larger tribe. The woman had no mount to carry her mother, so she carried her on her back. Whenever she grew tired, she put her mother down, pressed her belly against her mother's belly, and placed her own feet beneath her mother's feet to protect them from the burning ground, until she brought her to safety.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb turned back a man who had set off to campaign without his parents' permission. His father had recited verses when he departed, and these reached ʿUmar: “You left your father with trembling hands, and your mother unable even to swallow her drink. Two emigrants came and pressed upon him, so that he would leave an old man behind—he erred and failed. When the doves weep in the valley of Wajj over their eggs, they call to mind Kilāb.” [The verse is transmitted in difficult and compressed wording; “Kilāb” is treated here as a personal name.]

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from someone who heard Ibn Sīrīn relate: “A young man called Jurayj was practicing ascetic worship in a cell. His mother came to greet him, and he said to himself, ‘Prayer has a greater claim and takes precedence,’ so he did not answer her. She came a second time, and the same happened. She came a third time and became angry, saying, ‘May God not cause me to die before I see you among prostitutes’—meaning adulteresses. He remained there as long as God willed. One day a shepherd sheltered beside his cell. An Indian slave girl passed, and the shepherd had intercourse with her. She conceived, and when asked who was responsible she said, ‘The monk.’ The people came to Jurayj and spoke to him, but he did not answer. They intended to demolish his cell, so he spoke to them and asked God to relieve him. They said, ‘Hypocrite! This girl has conceived by you!’ He recognized this as the result of his mother's supplication and said, ‘Let me pray two units.’ He prayed and implored God for relief, then went to the girl, placed his hand upon her belly in their presence, and asked, ‘Who is your father?’ [The child] replied: ‘The shepherd of such-and-such a family.’ Thus Jurayj was saved.”
