records.matn_ar: أَنَّ §فَتًى يُقَالُ لَهُ: جُرَيْجٌ كَانَ فِي صَوْمَعَةٍ يَتَرَهَّبُ فِيهَا، فَجَاءَتْهُ أُمُّهُ تُسَلِّمُ عَلَيْهِ، فَقَالَ: الصَّلَاةُ أَحَقُّ وَالصَّلَاةُ آثَرُ، فَلَمْ يُجِبْهَا، ثُمَّ جَاءَتْهُ الثَّانِيَةَ فَكَذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ الثَّالِثَةَ فَغَضِبَتْ، فَقَالَتْ: لَا أَمَاتَنِي اللَّهُ حَتَّى أَرَاكَ مَعَ الْمُومِسَاتِ - تَعْنِي مَعَ الزُّنَاةِ - فَمَكَثَ مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ، فَجَاءَ رَاعِي غَنَمٍ يَوْمًا فَاسْتَظَلَّ فِي صَوْمَعَتِهِ، ثُمَّ مَرَّتْ جَارِيَةٌ هِنْدِيَّةٌ فَقَامَ إِلَيْهَا الرَّاعِي فَوَطِئَهَا، فَحَمَلَتْ، فَسَأَلُوهَا فَقَالَتْ: مِنَ الرَّاهِبِ، فَذَهُبُوا إِلَيْهِ فَكَلَّمُوهُ فَلَمْ يُكَلِّمْهُمْ، فَأَرَادُوا أَنْ يَهْدِمُوا صَوْمَعَتَهُ فَكَلَّمَهُمْ، وَسَأَلَ اللَّهَ أَنْ يُفَرِّجَ عَنْهُ، فَقَالُوا: يَا مُرَائِي، هَذِهِ الْجَارِيَةُ قَدْ حَمَلَتْ مِنْكَ، فَعَرَفَ أَنَّهَا دَعْوَةُ أُمِّهِ، فَقَالَ: دَعُونِي أُصَلِّي سَجْدَتَيْنِ، قَالَ: فَصَلَّى سَجْدَتَيْنِ، فَسَأَلَ اللَّهَ أَنْ يُفَرِّجَ عَنْهُ، فَقَامَ إِلَيْهَا، فَمَسَحَ بِيَدِهِ عَلَى بَطْنِهَا وَإِنَّهُمْ لَوَاقِفُونَ، فَقَالَ: مَنْ أَبُوكَ؟ قَالَ: رَاعِي آلِ فُلَانٍ، قَالَ: فَنَجَا»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Abān, from Saʿd ibn Masʿūd—or someone else—from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Whoever has two parents, or one, who pass the night angry with him will have two gates of the Fire opened against him—or one gate if it is one parent.” I believe he was asked: “Even if they wrong him?” and replied: “Even if they wrong him.” The same applies if their anger continues into the morning.
records.text_ar: ٢٠١٢٨ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَبَانَ، عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، أَوْ غَيْرِهِ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§مَا مِنْ أَحَدٍ يَكُونُ لَهُ وَالِدَانِ أَوْ وَاحِدٌ فَيَبِيتَانِ عَلَيْهِ سَاخِطَيْنِ إِلَّا فُتِحَ لَهُ بَابَانِ مِنَ النَّارِ، وَإِنْ كَانَ وَاحِدٌ فَوَاحِدٌ»   ، لَا أَعْلَمُهُ إِلَّا قَالَ: وَإِنْ ظَلَمَاهُ؟ قَالَ:   «وَإِنْ ظَلَمَاهُ»   قَالَ: وَإِنْ كَانَ صَبَاحًا فَكَذَلِكَ

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Jazarī, from Mujāhid, who attributed this saying [to the Prophet ﷺ]: “One disobedient to his parents shall not enter Paradise, nor one who reminds people of his generosity, nor an habitual wine drinker, nor one who has intercourse with someone forbidden to him by kinship, nor someone who returns to Bedouin life after emigrating.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, who said: “It is written in the Torah: Cursed is one who reviles his father; cursed is one who reviles his mother; cursed is one who moves land boundaries; cursed is one who turns someone away from God's path or misleads a person asking for directions.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠١٣٠ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، قَالَ:   «§مَكْتُوبٌ فِي التَّوْرَاةِ: مَلْعُونٌ مَنْ سَبَّ أَبَاهُ، مَلْعُونٌ مَنْ سَبَّ أُمَّهُ، مَلْعُونٌ مَنْ نَزَعَ تُخُومَ الْأَرْضِ، مَلْعُونٌ مَنْ صَدَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أَوْ ضَالَّ سَائِلًا»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Ibn Abī Dhiʾb, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Saʿīd, who said: A man asked Kaʿb: “What do you find in God's Book about disobedience to one's father?” He replied: “When his father asks him to fulfill an oath, he does not do so; when he asks him for something, he does not give it; when he entrusts something to him, he betrays the trust. That is disobedience.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Abū Hāshim al-Wāsiṭī, who raised the report to the Messenger of God ﷺ, who said: “May God curse whoever slaughters an animal for other than God, and may God curse whoever changes the boundary markers of land.” The transmitter explained that the markers are the signs delimiting land.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, who said: “It belongs to the customary practice to honor four: the scholar, the elderly person, the ruler, and one's parent.” He added: “It is considered discourteous for a man to address his father by his personal name.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠١٣٣ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ طَاوُسٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، قَالَ:   «مِنَ السُّنَّةِ أَنْ §يُوَقَّرَ أَرْبَعَةٌ: الْعَالِمُ، وَذُو الشَّيْبَةِ، وَالسُّلْطَانُ، وَالْوَالِدُ»   ، قَالَ: وَيُقَالُ:   «إِنَّ مِنَ الْجَفَاءِ أَنْ يَدْعُوَ الرَّجُلُ وَالِدَهُ بِاسْمِهِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from a man: Abū Hurayra saw a man walking in front of another man and asked: “What is he to you?” He said: “My father.” Abū Hurayra said: “Then do not walk ahead of him, do not sit until he sits, do not call him by his name, and do not expose him to being insulted.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Abū ʿUthmān, from an elderly man of Basra, that Luqmān said to his son: “My son, do not seek the friendship of the ignorant person, lest he think you approve of his conduct; and do not make light of a wise man's displeasure, lest he lose interest in you.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠١٣٥ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَبِي عُثْمَانَ، عَنْ شَيْخٍ، مِنْ أَهْلِ الْبَصْرَةِ،   «أَنَّ لُقْمَانَ قَالَ لِابْنِهِ: يَا بُنَيَّ، §لَا تَرْغَبْ فِي وُدِّ الْجَاهِلِ، فَيَرَى أَنَّكَ تَرْضَى عَمَلَهُ، وَلَا تَتَهَاوَنْ بِمَقْتِ الْحَكِيمِ فَيَزْهَدُ فِيكَ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported: Maʿmar related from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilāba, that a woman came to the Prophet ﷺ with her ailing son and said: “Messenger of God, pray to God for him. He is the last of three children I have buried.” The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “A fortified shield.” [He means the deceased children afford her protection.]
records.text_ar: ٢٠١٣٧ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ أَبِي قِلَابَةَ، أَنَّ امْرَأَةً جَاءَتِ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ بِابْنٍ لَهَا شَاكٍ، فَقَالَتْ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، ادْعُ اللَّهَ لَهُ، فَإِنَّهُ آخِرُ ثَلَاثَةٍ دَفَنْتُهُمْ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§جُنَّةٌ حَصِينَةٌ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported: Maʿmar reported from al-Zuhrī, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Whoever loses three children before they reach the age of accountability shall not be touched by the Fire except to fulfill the oath.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Thābit, from Anas, who said: Umm Sulaym had a son by Abū Ṭalḥa who fell ill and died. His mother covered him with a cloth. When Abū Ṭalḥa returned, he asked: “How is my son this evening?” She answered: “He is at rest.” He ate his evening meal. Later in the night she asked: “If someone lends you something and then takes it back, would you be distressed?” He said: “No.” She said: “God lent you something and has taken it back.” In the morning he told the Prophet ﷺ what she had said, and he had been intimate with her that night. The Prophet ﷺ said: “May God bless you both in your night.” She bore a boy named ʿAbdullāh, who was said to be among the finest people of his time.
records.text_ar: ٢٠١٤٠ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ ثَابِتٍ، عَنِ أَنَسٍ، قَالَ: كَانَ لِأُمِّ سُلَيْمٍ مِنْ أَبِي طَلْحَةَ ابْنٌ، فَمَرِضَ مَرَضَهُ الَّذِي مَاتَ مِنْهُ، فَلَمَّا مَاتَ غَطَّتْهُ أُمُّهُ بِثَوْبٍ، فَدَخَلَ أَبُو طَلْحَةَ فَقَالَ: كَيْفَ أَمْسَى ابْنِي الْيَوْمَ؟ قَالَتْ: أَمْسَى هَادِئًا، فَتَعَشَّى، ثُمَّ قَالَتْ لَهُ فِي بَعْضِ اللَّيْلِ: أَرَأَيْتَ لَوْ أَنَّ رَجُلًا أَعَارَكَ عَارِيَةً ثُمَّ أَخَذَهَا مِنْكَ، إِذًا جَزِعْتَ، قَالَ: - [١٤٠] - لَا، قَالَتْ: فَإنَّ اللَّهَ أَعَارَكَ عَارِيَةً فَأَخَذَهَا مِنْكَ، قَالَ: فَغَدَا إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، فَأَخْبَرَهُ بِقَوْلِهَا وَقَدْ كَانَ أَصَابَهَا تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§بَارَكَ اللَّهُ لَكُمَا فِي لَيْلَتِكُمَا»   قَالَ: فَوَلَدَتْ غُلَامًا كَانَ اسْمُهُ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ، فَذُكِرَ أَنَّهُ كَانَ خَيْرَ أَهْلِ زَمَانِهِ

records.display_matn_ar: كَانَ لِأُمِّ سُلَيْمٍ مِنْ أَبِي طَلْحَةَ ابْنٌ، فَمَرِضَ مَرَضَهُ الَّذِي مَاتَ مِنْهُ، فَلَمَّا مَاتَ غَطَّتْهُ أُمُّهُ بِثَوْبٍ، فَدَخَلَ أَبُو طَلْحَةَ فَقَالَ: كَيْفَ أَمْسَى ابْنِي الْيَوْمَ؟ قَالَتْ: أَمْسَى هَادِئًا، فَتَعَشَّى، ثُمَّ قَالَتْ لَهُ فِي بَعْضِ اللَّيْلِ: أَرَأَيْتَ لَوْ أَنَّ رَجُلًا أَعَارَكَ عَارِيَةً ثُمَّ أَخَذَهَا مِنْكَ، إِذًا جَزِعْتَ، قَالَ: لَا، قَالَتْ: فَإنَّ اللَّهَ أَعَارَكَ عَارِيَةً فَأَخَذَهَا مِنْكَ، قَالَ: فَغَدَا إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، فَأَخْبَرَهُ بِقَوْلِهَا وَقَدْ كَانَ أَصَابَهَا تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§بَارَكَ اللَّهُ لَكُمَا فِي لَيْلَتِكُمَا»   قَالَ: فَوَلَدَتْ غُلَامًا كَانَ اسْمُهُ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ، فَذُكِرَ أَنَّهُ كَانَ خَيْرَ أَهْلِ زَمَانِهِ

records.display_matn_en: Umm Sulaym had a son by Abū Ṭalḥa who fell ill and died. His mother covered him with a cloth. When Abū Ṭalḥa returned, he asked: “How is my son this evening?” She answered: “He is at rest.” He ate his evening meal. Later in the night she asked: “If someone lends you something and then takes it back, would you be distressed?” He said: “No.” She said: “God lent you something and has taken it back.” In the morning he told the Prophet ﷺ what she had said, and he had been intimate with her that night. The Prophet ﷺ said: “May God bless you both in your night.” She bore a boy named ʿAbdullāh, who was said to be among the finest people of his time.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: “A son of David the prophet ﷺ died, and he grieved intensely. records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from someone who heard Muʿāwiya ibn Qurra say: The Prophet ﷺ asked some of the Anṣār: “Whom do you regard as childless (*raqūb*) among you?” They said: “The one who has no children.” He said: “No, rather the one who has sent no child ahead [through death].” He asked: “And whom do you regard as impoverished?” They answered: “Someone with no wealth.” He said: “No, rather one who has sent no good ahead for himself.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported: Maʿmar related from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym, who attributed it to the Prophet ﷺ: One day the Messenger of God ﷺ took Ḥasan and Ḥusayn, seated one on each thigh, kissed Ḥasan and then Ḥusayn, and said: “God, I love them both, so love them both.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠١٤٣ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ خُثَيْمٍ، يَرْوِيهِ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ  أَخَذَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَوْمًا حَسَنًا، وَحُسَيْنًا، فَجَعَلَ هَذَا عَلَى هَذَا الْفَخِذِ، وَهَذَا عَلَى هَذَا الْفَخِذِ، ثُمَّ أَقْبَلَ عَلَى الْحَسَنِ فَقَبَّلَهُ، ثُمَّ أَقْبَلَ عَلَى الْحُسَيْنِ فَقَبَّلَهُ، ثُمَّ قَالَ:   «§اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أُحِبُّهُمَا فَأَحِبَّهُمَا»

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: ثُمَّ قَالَ:   «إِنَّ §الْوَلَدَ مَجْبَنَةٌ مَبْخَلَةٌ مَجْهَلَةٌ»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: He then said: “A child can make a person cowardly, miserly, and ignorant.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported: Maʿmar related from Ibn al-Munkadir, from ʿUrwa, from ʿĀʾisha, who said: A man came and asked leave to enter upon the Prophet ﷺ. The Prophet ﷺ said: “What a bad brother of his people, and son of his clan, this man is!” When he entered, however, the Prophet ﷺ turned toward him and spoke with him. After he departed, she said: “Messenger of God, you said what you said, yet turned your face to him and conversed with him.” The Messenger of God ﷺ replied: “Among the people of the worst standing before God on the Day of Resurrection is a man whom people avoid for fear of his evil—or he said, his vulgarity.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported: Maʿmar related from Thābit, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Vulgarity never enters a thing without disfiguring it, and modesty never enters a thing without adorning it.” Maʿmar added: “It reached me that God loves the modest, forbearing, and self-restrained person, and hates the vulgar, foul-mouthed, importunate beggar.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠١٤٥ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ ثَابِتٍ، عَنِ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§مَا كَانَ الْفُحْشُ فِي شَيْءٍ قَطُّ إِلَّا شَانَهُ، وَلَا كَانَ الْحَيَاءُ فِي شَيْءٍ قَطُّ إِلَّا زَانَهُ»   قَالَ مَعْمَرٌ:   «وَبَلَغَنِي أَنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْحَيِيَّ الْحَلِيمَ الْمُتَعَفِّفَ، وَيَبْغَضُ الْفَاحِشَ الْبَذِيءَ السَّائِلَ الْمُلْحِفَ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Sālim, from Ibn ʿUmar: The Messenger of God ﷺ passed an Anṣārī admonishing his brother about excessive modesty. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Leave him, for modesty is part of faith.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Qurra, from ʿAwn ibn ʿAbdullāh, who said: “Three qualities belong to faith: modesty, chastity, and hesitancy in speech—not deficiency of heart or incapacity in action. They increase one's share in the hereafter and diminish one's share in this world, but what they increase in the hereafter exceeds what they diminish here. Three qualities diminish one's share in the hereafter and increase one's share here: vulgarity, greed, and coarse speech. Yet what they diminish in the hereafter is greater than what they increase in this world.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from someone who heard al-Ḥasan say: “The Messenger of God ﷺ was modest. No young woman secluded behind her curtain was more bashful than the Messenger of God ﷺ in certain matters.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported: Maʿmar related from Abū Ḥāzim, from Ṭalḥa ibn Kurayz al-Khuzāʿī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “God is generous and loves generosity and lofty character; He dislikes base character.” Maʿmar added: “It reached me from Abū al-Dardāʾ that he said: ‘Through fine character, God grants the rank of one who prays through the night and fasts [through the day].’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported: Maʿmar related from Abū Isḥāq, from a man of Muzayna, who said: The Prophet ﷺ was asked: “What is the best quality a Muslim man can be given?” He replied: “Good character.” He was then asked: “What is the worst thing he can be given?” He replied: “When you would dislike something to be seen in your conduct among the people, do not do it when you are alone.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠١٥١ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنْ رَجُلٍ، مِنْ مُزَيْنَةَ قَالَ: قِيلَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، مَا §أَفْضَلُ مَا أُوتِيَ الرَّجُلُ الْمُسْلِمُ؟ قَالَ:   «الْخُلُقُ الْحَسَنُ»   ، قَالَ: فَمَا شَرُّ مَا أُوتِيَ الرَّجُلُ الْمُسْلِمُ؟ قَالَ:   «إِذَا كَرِهْتَ أَنْ يُرَى عَلَيْكَ شَيْءٌ فِي نَادِي الْقَوْمِ فَلَا تَفْعَلْهُ إِذَا خَلَوْتَ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: “Associate with people in ways they appreciate, but distinguish yourselves from them through your deeds, and be earnest with the common people.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Hārūn ibn Riʾāb, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Shall I tell you who are dearest to me and nearest to me?” They said: “Yes, Messenger of God.” He said: “Those of you with the best character, easy to approach, who form bonds of friendship and are befriended.” He then asked: “Shall I tell you who are most disliked by me and farthest from me?” They said: “Yes, Messenger of God.” He said: “The incessant talkers, those who affect grandiloquence, and the *mutafayhiqūn*.” They said: “We understand the talkers and those who affect grandiloquence; who are the *mutafayhiqūn*?” He replied: “The arrogant.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠١٥٣ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ هَارُونَ بْنِ رِئَابٍ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§أَلَا أُخْبِرُكُمْ بِأَحَبِّكُمْ إِلَيَّ وَأَقْرَبِكُمْ مِنِّي؟»   ، قَالُوا: بَلَى يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، قَالَ:   «أَحَاسِنُكُمْ أَخْلَاقًا الْمُوَطَّئُونَ أكْنَافُهُمْ، الَّذِينَ يَأْلَفُونَ وَيُؤْلَفُونَ»   ثُمَّ قَالَ:   «أَلَا أُخْبِرُكُمْ بأبْغَضِكُمْ إِلَيَّ وَأبعدِكُمْ مِنِّي؟»   ، قَالُوا: بَلَى يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، قَالَ:   «الثَّرْثَارُونَ الْمُتَشَدِّقُونَ الْمُتَفَيْهِقُونَ»   قَالُوا: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، قَدْ عَرَفْنَا الثَّرْثَارُونَ الْمُتَشَدِّقُونَ، فَمَا الْمُتَفَيْهِقُونَ؟ قَالَ:   «الْمُتَكَبِّرُونَ»

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Hārūn ibn Riʾāb, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Shall I tell you who are dearest to me and nearest to me?” They said: “Yes, Messenger of God.” He said: “Those of you with the best character, easy to approach, who form bonds of friendship and are befriended.” He then asked: “Shall I tell you who are most disliked by me and farthest from me?” They said: “Yes, Messenger of God.” He said: “The incessant talkers, those who affect grandiloquence, and the *mutafayhiqūn*.” They said: “We understand the talkers and those who affect grandiloquence; who are the *mutafayhiqūn*?” He replied: “The arrogant.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, who said: The Prophet ﷺ stopped at the dwelling of a man who owned a large herd—sixty, seventy, or ninety to a hundred camels and other cattle and sheep—but the man would neither lodge nor entertain him. He later passed a woman who had only a few sheep. She welcomed him and slaughtered an animal for him. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Look at that man who owns herds of camels, cattle, and sheep: we passed by and he would not lodge or entertain us. Look at this woman, who has only a few sheep: she lodged and fed us. Character is in God's hand. Whoever He wishes to grant a good quality of character, He grants it to him.”

records.text_en: The same ʿAmr [ibn Dīnār] said: I heard Ṭāwūs say: The Messenger of God ﷺ said while standing on the pulpit: “It is God alone who guides to the finest character, and it is He alone who turns away its worst qualities.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠١٥٦ - قَالَ: وَقَالَ عَمْرٌو: سَمِعْتُ طَاوُسًا يَقُولُ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَهُوَ عَلَى الْمِنْبَرِ، يَقُولُ:   «إِنَّمَا §يَهْدِي إِلَى أَحْسَنِ الْأَخْلَاقِ اللَّهُ، وَإِنَّمَا يَصْرِفُ مِنْ أَسْوئِهَا هُوَ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb set out for Syria. Along the way, Abū ʿUbayda ibn al-Jarrāḥ and his companions met him and reported that an epidemic had broken out there. ʿUmar consulted the people. The Emigrants and Anṣār advised him to proceed, saying: “We have set out on a mission and should not turn back.” Those who had entered Islam on the day of the conquest said: “God forbid that we should prefer a land of affliction to a land of well-being.” ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf was absent but then arrived and said: “I have knowledge concerning this: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say, ‘When you hear of an epidemic in a land, do not go there; if it breaks out in a land where you already are, do not leave it fleeing from it.’” ʿUmar called out to the people that he would depart the next morning and told them to prepare. Abū ʿUbayda asked: “Commander of the Believers, are you fleeing God's decree?” ʿUmar replied: “If only someone other than you had said that, Abū ʿUbayda! Yes, we flee from God's decree to God's decree. If you had camels that reached a valley with two sides, one fertile and the other barren, would you not graze them on the fertile side by God's decree, and if you grazed them on the barren side, by God's decree?” He answered: “Yes.” The report also describes a question about whether choosing the barren side and abandoning the fertile one would constitute neglect, and an affirmative response. ʿUmar said: “Then let us go.” He returned to Medina, saying: “This is the place to stop and settle, if God wills.” Al-Zuhrī said: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib informed me that ʿUmar turned the people back from Sargh that day.

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb set out for Syria. Along the way, Abū ʿUbayda ibn al-Jarrāḥ and his companions met him and reported that an epidemic had broken out there. ʿUmar consulted the people. The Emigrants and Anṣār advised him to proceed, saying: “We have set out on a mission and should not turn back.” Those who had entered Islam on the day of the conquest said: “God forbid that we should prefer a land of affliction to a land of well-being.” ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf was absent but then arrived and said: “I have knowledge concerning this: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say, ‘When you hear of an epidemic in a land, do not go there; if it breaks out in a land where you already are, do not leave it fleeing from it.’” ʿUmar called out to the people that he would depart the next morning and told them to prepare. Abū ʿUbayda asked: “Commander of the Believers, are you fleeing God's decree?” ʿUmar replied: “If only someone other than you had said that, Abū ʿUbayda! Yes, we flee from God's decree to God's decree. If you had camels that reached a valley with two sides, one fertile and the other barren, would you not graze them on the fertile side by God's decree, and if you grazed them on the barren side, by God's decree?” He answered: “Yes.” The report also describes a question about whether choosing the barren side and abandoning the fertile one would constitute neglect, and an affirmative response. ʿUmar said: “Then let us go.” He returned to Medina, saying: “This is the place to stop and settle, if God wills.” Al-Zuhrī said: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib informed me that ʿUmar turned the people back from Sargh that day.

records.isnad_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said:
records.matn_en: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb set out for Syria. Along the way, Abū ʿUbayda ibn al-Jarrāḥ and his companions met him and reported that an epidemic had broken out there. ʿUmar consulted the people. The Emigrants and Anṣār advised him to proceed, saying: “We have set out on a mission and should not turn back.” Those who had entered Islam on the day of the conquest said: “God forbid that we should prefer a land of affliction to a land of well-being.” ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf was absent but then arrived and said: “I have knowledge concerning this: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say, ‘When you hear of an epidemic in a land, do not go there; if it breaks out in a land where you already are, do not leave it fleeing from it.’” ʿUmar called out to the people that he would depart the next morning and told them to prepare. Abū ʿUbayda asked: “Commander of the Believers, are you fleeing God's decree?” ʿUmar replied: “If only someone other than you had said that, Abū ʿUbayda! Yes, we flee from God's decree to God's decree. If you had camels that reached a valley with two sides, one fertile and the other barren, would you not graze them on the fertile side by God's decree, and if you grazed them on the barren side, by God's decree?” He answered: “Yes.” The report also describes a question about whether choosing the barren side and abandoning the fertile one would constitute neglect, and an affirmative response. ʿUmar said: “Then let us go.” He returned to Medina, saying: “This is the place to stop and settle, if God wills.” Al-Zuhrī said: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib informed me that ʿUmar turned the people back from Sargh that day.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī: A man died of plague in a rural district, and people were alarmed. When this reached the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “I hope its remnants will not come upon us.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported: Maʿmar reported from Qatāda that whenever Abū Bakr dispatched armies toward Syria, he would say: “God, grant them martyrdom by the spear and by the plague.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn Raysān, from someone who heard Farwa ibn Musayk say: I said: “Messenger of God, we have a region called Abyan, which supplies our produce and provisions, but it is unhealthy”—or he said: “Its epidemic is severe.” The Prophet ﷺ said: “Leave it alone, for contact with disease can lead to ruin.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠١٦٢ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ رَيْسَانَ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنِي مَنْ، سَمِعَ فَرْوَةَ بْنَ مُسَيْكٍ، قَالَ: قُلْتُ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، إِنَّ أَرْضًا عِنْدَنَا يُقَالُ لَهَا: أَبْيَنُ، هِيَ أَرْضُ رِيفِنَا وَمِيرَتِنَا، وَهِيَ وَبِئَةٌ - أَوْ قَالَ: وَبَاؤُهَا شَدِيدٌ - فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «دَعْهَا عَنْكَ، §فَإِنَّ مِنَ الْقَرَفِ التَّلَفَ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from a man, from al-Ḥasan, that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: “I marvel at the merchant who travels to Hajar and at the one who voyages by sea.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, who said: A plague broke out in Syria during ʿUmar's caliphate; a man might not even return to reclaim his she-camel. ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, who then governed Syria, said: “Scatter away from this affliction into the mountains and valleys.” Shuraḥbīl ibn Ḥasana replied: “Rather, it is the mercy of your Lord, the supplication of your Prophet ﷺ, and the death through which righteous people before you passed.” He added: “I accepted Islam with the Messenger of God ﷺ, and this fellow is more misguided than his family's donkey.” When Muʿādh ibn Jabal heard this he said: “God, grant the household of Muʿādh their share of this affliction.” Two of his wives contracted the plague and died. His son was then afflicted. Muʿādh entered and said: “The truth comes from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters” (2:147). The son replied: “You will find me, God willing, among the patient” (37:102), and then died. Muʿādh buried him and was himself struck by the plague. He would faint and, on recovering, say: “My Lord, overwhelm me with Your affliction; by Your might, You know that I love You.” He repeated this as he lost and regained consciousness. Once he awoke to find a man weeping beside him. He asked: “Why do you weep?” The man said: “By God, I do not weep for any worldly gain I hoped to receive from you, but for the knowledge I used to obtain from you.” Muʿādh said: “Do not weep. Knowledge does not disappear: seek it where God's intimate friend Abraham sought it. When I die, seek knowledge from four men: ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām, ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, Salmān, and ʿUwaymir Abū al-Dardāʾ. If they cannot help you, everyone else will be even less able.” Then he died.
records.text_ar: ٢٠١٦٤ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، قَالَ: وَقَعَ طَاعُونٌ بِالشَّامِ فِي عَهْدِ عُمَرَ، فَكَانَ الرَّجُلُ لَا يَرْجِعُ إِلَيْهِ بِنَاقَتِهِ، فَقَالَ عَمْرُو بْنُ الْعَاصِ - وَهُوَ أَمِيرُ الشَّامِ يَوْمَئِذٍ: تَفَرَّقُوا مِنْ هَذَا الرِّجْزِ فِي هَذِهِ الْجِبَالِ وَهَذِهِ الْأَوْدِيَةِ، وَقَالَ شُرَحْبِيلُ ابْنُ حَسَنَةَ:   «§بَلْ رَحْمَةُ رَبِّكُمْ، وَدَعْوَةُ نَبِيِّكُمْ، وَمَوْتُ الصَّالِحِينَ قَبْلَكُمْ»   ، لَقَدْ أَسْلَمْتُ مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، وَإِنَّ هَذَا لَأَضَلُّ مِنْ حِمَارِ أَهْلِهِ، فَقَالَ مُعَاذُ بْنُ جَبَلٍ وَسَمِعَهُ يَقُولُ ذَلِكَ: اللَّهُمَّ أَدْخِلْ عَلَى آلِ مُعَاذٍ نَصِيبَهُمْ مِنْ هَذَا الْبَلَاءِ، قَالَ: فَطُعِنَتْ لَهُ امْرَأَتَانِ فَمَاتَتَا، ثُمَّ طُعِنَ ابْنٌ لَهُ فَدَخَلَ عَلَيْهِ، فَقَالَ:  {الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكَ فَلَا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْمُمْتَرِينَ}   [البقرة: ١٤٧]  ، فَقَالَ:  {سَتَجِدُنِي إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ مِنَ الصَّابِرِينَ}   [الصافات: ١٠٢]  ، قَالَ: ثُمَّ مَاتَ ابْنُهُ ذَلِكَ، - [١٥٠] - فَدَفَنَهُ ثُمَّ طُعِنَ مُعَاذٌ فَجَعَلَ يُغْشَى عَلَيْهِ فَإِذَا أَفَاقَ قَالَ: رَبِّ غُمَّنِي غَمَّكَ، فَوَعِزَّتِكَ إِنَّكَ لَتَعْلَمُ أَنِّي أُحِبُّكَ، قَالَ: ثُمَّ يُغْشَى عَلَيْهِ، فَإِذَا أَفَاقَ قَالَ مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ، قَالَ: فَأَفَاقَ فَإِذَا هُوَ بِرَجُلٍ يَبْكِي عِنْدَهُ، قَالَ: مَا يُبْكِيكَ؟ فَقَالَ: أَمَا وَاللَّهِ مَا أَبْكِي عَلَى دُنْيَا أطْمَعُ أَنْ أُصِيبَهَا مِنْكَ، وَلَكِنِّي أَبْكِي عَلَى الْعِلْمِ الَّذِي أُصِيبُ مِنْكَ، قَالَ: فَلَا تَبْكِ، فَإِنَّ الْعِلْمَ لَا يَذْهَبُ وَالْتَمِسْهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ التَّمَسَهُ خَلِيلُ اللَّهِ إِبْرَاهِيمُ، فَإِذَا أَنَا مِتُّ فَالْتَمِسِ الْعِلْمَ عِنْدَ أَرْبَعَةِ نَفَرٍ: عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ سَلَامٍ، وَعَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، وَسَلْمَانَ، وَعُوَيْمِرٍ أَبِي الدَّرْدَاءِ، فَإِنْ أعْيَوْكَ فَالنَّاسُ أَعْيَى، قَالَ: ثُمَّ مَاتَ

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, who said: A plague broke out in Syria during ʿUmar's caliphate; a man might not even return to reclaim his she-camel. ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, who then governed Syria, said: “Scatter away from this affliction into the mountains and valleys.” Shuraḥbīl ibn Ḥasana replied: “Rather, it is the mercy of your Lord, the supplication of your Prophet ﷺ, and the death through which righteous people before you passed.” He added: “I accepted Islam with the Messenger of God ﷺ, and this fellow is more misguided than his family's donkey.” When Muʿādh ibn Jabal heard this he said: “God, grant the household of Muʿādh their share of this affliction.” Two of his wives contracted the plague and died. His son was then afflicted. Muʿādh entered and said: “The truth comes from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters” (2:147). The son replied: “You will find me, God willing, among the patient” (37:102), and then died. Muʿādh buried him and was himself struck by the plague. He would faint and, on recovering, say: “My Lord, overwhelm me with Your affliction; by Your might, You know that I love You.” He repeated this as he lost and regained consciousness. Once he awoke to find a man weeping beside him. He asked: “Why do you weep?” The man said: “By God, I do not weep for any worldly gain I hoped to receive from you, but for the knowledge I used to obtain from you.” Muʿādh said: “Do not weep. Knowledge does not disappear: seek it where God's intimate friend Abraham sought it. When I die, seek knowledge from four men: ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām, ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, Salmān, and ʿUwaymir Abū al-Dardāʾ. If they cannot help you, everyone else will be even less able.” Then he died.

records.matn_ar: وَقَعَ طَاعُونٌ بِالشَّامِ فِي عَهْدِ عُمَرَ، فَكَانَ الرَّجُلُ لَا يَرْجِعُ إِلَيْهِ بِنَاقَتِهِ، فَقَالَ عَمْرُو بْنُ الْعَاصِ - وَهُوَ أَمِيرُ الشَّامِ يَوْمَئِذٍ: تَفَرَّقُوا مِنْ هَذَا الرِّجْزِ فِي هَذِهِ الْجِبَالِ وَهَذِهِ الْأَوْدِيَةِ، وَقَالَ شُرَحْبِيلُ ابْنُ حَسَنَةَ:   «§بَلْ رَحْمَةُ رَبِّكُمْ، وَدَعْوَةُ نَبِيِّكُمْ، وَمَوْتُ الصَّالِحِينَ قَبْلَكُمْ»   ، لَقَدْ أَسْلَمْتُ مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، وَإِنَّ هَذَا لَأَضَلُّ مِنْ حِمَارِ أَهْلِهِ، فَقَالَ مُعَاذُ بْنُ جَبَلٍ وَسَمِعَهُ يَقُولُ ذَلِكَ: اللَّهُمَّ أَدْخِلْ عَلَى آلِ مُعَاذٍ نَصِيبَهُمْ مِنْ هَذَا الْبَلَاءِ، قَالَ: فَطُعِنَتْ لَهُ امْرَأَتَانِ فَمَاتَتَا، ثُمَّ طُعِنَ ابْنٌ لَهُ فَدَخَلَ عَلَيْهِ، فَقَالَ:  {الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكَ فَلَا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْمُمْتَرِينَ}   [البقرة: ١٤٧]  ، فَقَالَ:  {سَتَجِدُنِي إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ مِنَ الصَّابِرِينَ}   [الصافات: ١٠٢]  ، قَالَ: ثُمَّ مَاتَ ابْنُهُ ذَلِكَ، فَدَفَنَهُ ثُمَّ طُعِنَ مُعَاذٌ فَجَعَلَ يُغْشَى عَلَيْهِ فَإِذَا أَفَاقَ قَالَ: رَبِّ غُمَّنِي غَمَّكَ، فَوَعِزَّتِكَ إِنَّكَ لَتَعْلَمُ أَنِّي أُحِبُّكَ، قَالَ: ثُمَّ يُغْشَى عَلَيْهِ، فَإِذَا أَفَاقَ قَالَ مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ، قَالَ: فَأَفَاقَ فَإِذَا هُوَ بِرَجُلٍ يَبْكِي عِنْدَهُ، قَالَ: مَا يُبْكِيكَ؟ فَقَالَ: أَمَا وَاللَّهِ مَا أَبْكِي عَلَى دُنْيَا أطْمَعُ أَنْ أُصِيبَهَا مِنْكَ، وَلَكِنِّي أَبْكِي عَلَى الْعِلْمِ الَّذِي أُصِيبُ مِنْكَ، قَالَ: فَلَا تَبْكِ، فَإِنَّ الْعِلْمَ لَا يَذْهَبُ وَالْتَمِسْهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ التَّمَسَهُ خَلِيلُ اللَّهِ إِبْرَاهِيمُ، فَإِذَا أَنَا مِتُّ فَالْتَمِسِ الْعِلْمَ عِنْدَ أَرْبَعَةِ نَفَرٍ: عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ سَلَامٍ، وَعَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، وَسَلْمَانَ، وَعُوَيْمِرٍ أَبِي الدَّرْدَاءِ، فَإِنْ أعْيَوْكَ فَالنَّاسُ أَعْيَى، قَالَ: ثُمَّ مَاتَ
records.isnad_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, who said:
records.matn_en: A plague broke out in Syria during ʿUmar's caliphate; a man might not even return to reclaim his she-camel. ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, who then governed Syria, said: “Scatter away from this affliction into the mountains and valleys.” Shuraḥbīl ibn Ḥasana replied: “Rather, it is the mercy of your Lord, the supplication of your Prophet ﷺ, and the death through which righteous people before you passed.” He added: “I accepted Islam with the Messenger of God ﷺ, and this fellow is more misguided than his family's donkey.” When Muʿādh ibn Jabal heard this he said: “God, grant the household of Muʿādh their share of this affliction.” Two of his wives contracted the plague and died. His son was then afflicted. Muʿādh entered and said: “The truth comes from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters” (2:147). The son replied: “You will find me, God willing, among the patient” (37:102), and then died. Muʿādh buried him and was himself struck by the plague. He would faint and, on recovering, say: “My Lord, overwhelm me with Your affliction; by Your might, You know that I love You.” He repeated this as he lost and regained consciousness. Once he awoke to find a man weeping beside him. He asked: “Why do you weep?” The man said: “By God, I do not weep for any worldly gain I hoped to receive from you, but for the knowledge I used to obtain from you.” Muʿādh said: “Do not weep. Knowledge does not disappear: seek it where God's intimate friend Abraham sought it. When I die, seek knowledge from four men: ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām, ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, Salmān, and ʿUwaymir Abū al-Dardāʾ. If they cannot help you, everyone else will be even less able.” Then he died.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, who said: Shurayḥ passed people who had left their village and pitched tents. He asked: “What is their situation?” They said: “They fled the plague.” He replied: “They and we are on the same carpet [of fate], and they and we are equally near to what we need.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: “A single house in Rukba amounts to fifty houses in Syria.” [The comparison and the location Rukba are preserved as given in the source.]

records.text_en: Maʿmar said: It reached me that Muʿādh ibn Jabal said when the plague struck Syria and nearly annihilated its people, so that people called it “the Flood”: Muʿādh called the people to gather for prayer. When they assembled, he said: “Do not regard your Lord's mercy and your Prophet's supplication as a punishment with which a people were afflicted. I shall tell you a report that I would not relate if I thought I would remain among you: five things—whoever lives to see them and is able to die, let him die: that a person rejects faith after believing; that blood is shed without right; that someone is given God's wealth on condition that he lie and commit wickedness; that the one who invokes curses against others becomes prominent; and that a man says, ‘I do not know what will become of me, whether I die or live.’” The narrator explained that “the one who invokes curses” means a man cursing his brother.
records.text_ar: ٢٠١٦٧ - قَالَ مَعْمَرٌ: وَبَلَغَنِي أَنَّ مُعَاذَ بْنَ جَبَلٍ، قَالَ حِينَ وَقَعَ الطَّاعُونُ بِالشَّامِ مَرَّةً، فَأَلَمَّ أَنْ يُفْنِيَهُمْ، حَتَّى قَالَ النَّاسُ: هَذَا الطُّوفَانُ، فَأَذَّنَ مُعَاذٌ بِالنَّاسِ: أَنَّ الصَّلَاةَ جَامِعَةٌ، فَاجْتَمَعُوا إِلَيْهِ، فَقَالَ:   «§لَا تَجْعَلُوا رَحْمَةَ رَبِّكُمْ، وَدَعْوَةَ نَبِيِّكُمْ كعَذَابٍ عُذِّبَ بِهِ قَوْمٌ، أَمَا إِنِّي سَأُخْبِرُكُمْ بِحَدِيثٍ لَوْ ظَنَنْتُ أَنِّي أَبْقَى فِيكُمْ مَا حَدَّثْتُكُمْ بِهِ وَلَكِنْ خَمْسٌ مَنْ أَدْرَكَهُنَّ مِنْكُمْ وَاسْتَطَاعَ أَنْ يَمُوتَ فَلْيَمُتْ: أَنْ يَكْفُرَ امْرُؤٌ بَعْدَ إِيمَانِهِ، أَوْ يَسْفِكَ دَمًا بِغَيْرِ حَقِّهِ، أَوْ يُعْطَى الْمَرْءُ مَالَ اللَّهِ عَلَى أَنْ يَكْذِبَ وَيَفْجُرَ، وَأَنْ يَظْهَرَ الْمُلَاعِنُ، وَأَنْ يَقُولَ الرَّجُلُ: لَا أَدْرِي مَا أَنَا إِنْ مِتُّ وَإِنْ أَنَا حَيِيتُ»   ، يَعْنِي: الْمُلَاعِنَ أَنْ يُلَاعِنَ الرَّجُلُ أَخَاهُ

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported: Maʿmar reported from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUtba, from Umm Qays bint Miḥṣan al-Asadiyya, the sister of ʿUkkāsha ibn Miḥṣan. She brought a son of hers to the Messenger of God ﷺ after treating him for a throat ailment. The Prophet ﷺ asked: “Why do you press your children's throats with this treatment? Use this Indian wood”—meaning *qust*—“for it contains seven cures, among them a cure for pleurisy.” He then took her boy and placed him in his lap. The boy urinated on him, so he called for water and sprinkled it upon the spot. The boy had not yet begun to eat solid food. Al-Zuhrī said: “This became the established practice.” He added: “For the throat ailment it is administered through the nose; for pleurisy it is poured into the side of the mouth.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Ashʿath ibn ʿAbdullāh, from Shahr ibn Ḥawshab, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “ʿAjwa dates are from Paradise and contain healing from poison. Truffles are from the manna, and their water is a remedy for the eye. The truffle is the fat of the earth.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, who said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ because his brother was suffering from stomach trouble. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Give your brother honey to drink.” The man returned and said: “It has only made him worse.” The Prophet ﷺ repeated: “Give your brother honey to drink.” This happened three times. The Prophet ﷺ then said: “The Quran has spoken the truth, and your brother's stomach has lied.” The man gave him honey, and he recovered as though released from bonds.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, who said: “The Prophet ﷺ instructed people to use dyes, and the darkest of them are most pleasing to us”—meaning the blackest.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported: Maʿmar related from Thābit and Qatāda, from Anas, that Abū Bakr dyed his beard with henna and *katam*, while ʿUmar dyed his beard with henna.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported: Maʿmar related from Layth, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Jābir, who said: Abū Quḥāfa was brought to the Messenger of God ﷺ on the day of the conquest, and his head looked like the white blossoms of the *thughāma* plant. He said: “Change its color, but avoid black.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠١٧٩ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ لَيْثٍ، عَنْ أَبِي الزُّبَيْرِ، عَنْ جَابِرٍ، قَالَ: أُتِيَ بِأَبِي قُحَافَةَ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَوْمَ الْفَتْحِ، كَأَنَّ رَأْسَهُ ثَغَامَةٌ بَيْضَاءُ، فَقَالَ:   «§غَيِّروُهُ وَجَنِّبُوهُ السَّوَادَ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported: Maʿmar related from Ayyūb, who said: I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr say: “One of you sets about extinguishing a light that God placed upon his face.” Ayyūb explained: “That was because I had asked him about *wasma* [a substance used for dark dye].”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar: A barber was trimming the Messenger of God's ﷺ moustache and found a white hair. records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar that a man asked Farqad al-Sabakhī about dyeing hair black. He replied: “We have heard that fire will blaze in his head and beard”—meaning on the Day of Resurrection.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, from al-Ḥasan, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The hypocrite has three traits, even if he prays, fasts, and claims to be a Muslim: when he speaks, he lies; when entrusted, he betrays; and when he promises, he breaks his promise.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, from al-Ḥasan, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Do not be deceived by a person's prayer or fasting. Whoever wishes can fast, and whoever wishes can pray, but one who has no trustworthiness has no religion.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn, from Shurayḥ, who said: I heard him say to a man: “Servant of God, leave what makes you doubtful for what does not make you doubtful. By God, no servant gives up any such thing for God's sake and then suffers its loss.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Aʿmash, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from Ḥudhayfa, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ told us two reports. I have seen one come to pass and await the other. He told us: “Trustworthiness descended into the roots of men's hearts, and the Quran descended, so people read the Quran and learned from the customary practice.” Then he told us how trustworthiness would be lifted: “A man sleeps and awakens after trustworthiness has been removed from his heart, leaving a trace like a speck—or he said, a blister—or like a coal rolled upon your foot: it appears to have something inside, though nothing is there. Trustworthiness will continue to be taken away until people say: ‘There is a trustworthy man among such-and-such a clan; there is a trustworthy man among another clan.’” Ḥudhayfa added: “There was once a time when I did not care with which of you I traded. If he was a Muslim, his Islam would make him return what I was due; if he was under covenant, his official would return it to me. But now I would trade with only so-and-so and so-and-so among you.” [The source has a difficult or corrupted phrase introducing Ḥudhayfa's last statement; the change to trading practice is clear.]
records.text_ar: ٢٠١٩٤ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الْأَعْمَشِ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ وَهْبٍ، عَنْ حُذَيْفَةَ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ حَدِيثَيْنِ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَهُمَا وَأَنَا أَنْتَظِرُ الْآخَرَ، حَدَّثَنَا:   «أَنَّ §الْأَمَانَةَ نَزَلَتْ فِي جَذْرِ قُلُوبِ الرِّجَالِ، وَنَزَلَ الْقُرْآنُ، فَقَرَءُوا الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلِمُوا مِنَ السُّنَّةِ»   ، ثُمَّ حَدَّثَنَا عَنْ رَفْعِهِمَا، فَقَالَ:   «تُرْفَعُ الْأَمَانَةُ فَيَنَامُ الرَّجُلُ، ثُمَّ يَسْتَيْقِظُ وَقَدْ رُفِعَتِ الْأَمَانَةُ مِنْ قَلْبِهِ، وَيَبْقَى أَثَرُهَا كَالْوَكْتِ - أَوْ قَالَ: كَالْمَجْلِ - أَوْ كَجَمْرٍ دَحْرَجْتَهُ عَلَى رِجْلِكَ فَهُوَ يَرَى أَنَّ فِيهِ شَيْئًا وَلَيْسَ فِيهِ شَيْءٌ، وَتُرْفَعُ - [١٥٨] - الْأَمَانَةُ حَتَّى يُقَالَ: إِنَّ فِي بَنِي فُلَانٍ رَجُلًا أَمِينًا، وَإِنَّ فِي بَنِي فُلَانٍ رَجُلًا أَمِينًا، وَلَقَدْ رَاسَى حَدِيثًا وَمَا أُبَالِي أَيَّكُمْ أُبَايِعُ، لَئِنْ كَانَ مُسْلِمًا لَيَرُدَّنَّهُ عَلَيَّ إِسْلَامُهُ، وَإِنْ كَانَ مُعَاهَدًا لَيَرُدَّنَّهُ عَلَيَّ سَاعِيهِ، وَأَمَّا الْيَوْمَ فَإِنِّي لَمْ أَكُنْ لِأُبَايِعَ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا فُلَانًا وَفُلَانًا»

records.display_matn_ar: حَدَّثَنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ حَدِيثَيْنِ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَهُمَا وَأَنَا أَنْتَظِرُ الْآخَرَ، حَدَّثَنَا:   «أَنَّ §الْأَمَانَةَ نَزَلَتْ فِي جَذْرِ قُلُوبِ الرِّجَالِ، وَنَزَلَ الْقُرْآنُ، فَقَرَءُوا الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلِمُوا مِنَ السُّنَّةِ»   ، ثُمَّ حَدَّثَنَا عَنْ رَفْعِهِمَا، فَقَالَ:   «تُرْفَعُ الْأَمَانَةُ فَيَنَامُ الرَّجُلُ، ثُمَّ يَسْتَيْقِظُ وَقَدْ رُفِعَتِ الْأَمَانَةُ مِنْ قَلْبِهِ، وَيَبْقَى أَثَرُهَا كَالْوَكْتِ - أَوْ قَالَ: كَالْمَجْلِ - أَوْ كَجَمْرٍ دَحْرَجْتَهُ عَلَى رِجْلِكَ فَهُوَ يَرَى أَنَّ فِيهِ شَيْئًا وَلَيْسَ فِيهِ شَيْءٌ، وَتُرْفَعُ الْأَمَانَةُ حَتَّى يُقَالَ: إِنَّ فِي بَنِي فُلَانٍ رَجُلًا أَمِينًا، وَإِنَّ فِي بَنِي فُلَانٍ رَجُلًا أَمِينًا، وَلَقَدْ رَاسَى حَدِيثًا وَمَا أُبَالِي أَيَّكُمْ أُبَايِعُ، لَئِنْ كَانَ مُسْلِمًا لَيَرُدَّنَّهُ عَلَيَّ إِسْلَامُهُ، وَإِنْ كَانَ مُعَاهَدًا لَيَرُدَّنَّهُ عَلَيَّ سَاعِيهِ، وَأَمَّا الْيَوْمَ فَإِنِّي لَمْ أَكُنْ لِأُبَايِعَ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا فُلَانًا وَفُلَانًا»
records.display_isnad_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Aʿmash, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from Ḥudhayfa, who said:
records.display_matn_en: The Messenger of God ﷺ told us two reports. I have seen one come to pass and await the other. He told us: “Trustworthiness descended into the roots of men's hearts, and the Quran descended, so people read the Quran and learned from the customary practice.” Then he told us how trustworthiness would be lifted: “A man sleeps and awakens after trustworthiness has been removed from his heart, leaving a trace like a speck—or he said, a blister—or like a coal rolled upon your foot: it appears to have something inside, though nothing is there. Trustworthiness will continue to be taken away until people say: ‘There is a trustworthy man among such-and-such a clan; there is a trustworthy man among another clan.’” Ḥudhayfa added: “There was once a time when I did not care with which of you I traded. If he was a Muslim, his Islam would make him return what I was due; if he was under covenant, his official would return it to me. But now I would trade with only so-and-so and so-and-so among you.” [The source has a difficult or corrupted phrase introducing Ḥudhayfa's last statement; the change to trading practice is clear.]

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported: Maʿmar related from Ayyūb, from Ibn Abī Mulayka—or someone else—from ʿĀʾisha, who said: “No trait was more hateful to the companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ than lying. unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: قَالَ مَعْمَرٌ: قَالَ غَيْرُ جَعْفَرٍ: عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ:   «§وَخَيْرُ مَا أُلْقِيَ فِي الْقَلْبِ الْيَقِينُ، وَخَيْرُ الْغِنَى غِنَى النَّفْسِ، وَخَيْرُ الْعِلْمِ مَا نَفَعَ، وَخَيْرُ الْهُدَى مَا اتُّبِعَ، وَمَا قَلَّ وَكَفَى خَيْرٌ مِمَّا كَثُرَ وَأَلْهَى، وَإِنَّمَا يَصِيرُ أَحَدُكُمْ إِلَى مَوْضِعِ أَرْبَعِ أَذْرُعٍ فَلَا تُمِلُّوا النَّاسَ وَلَا تُسْئِمُوهُمْ، فَإِنَّ لِكُلِّ نَفْسٍ نَشَاطًا وَإِقْبَالًا، وَإِنَّ لَهَا سَآمَةً وَإِدْبَارًا، أَلَا وَشَرُّ الرَّوَايَا رَوَايَا الْكَذِبِ، أَلَا وَإِنَّ الْكَذِبَ يَعُودُ إِلَى الْفُجُورِ، وَالْفُجُورَ يَعُودُ إِلَى النَّارِ، أَلَا وَعَلَيْكُمْ بِالصِّدْقِ، فَإِنَّ الصِّدْقَ يَعُودُ إِلَى الْبِرِّ، وَإِنَّ الْبِرَّ - [١٦٠] - يَعُودُ إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ، وَاعْتَبِرُوا فِي ذَلِكَ أَنَّهُمَا إِلْفَانِ، يُقَالُ لِلصَّادِقِ: يَصْدُقُ حَتَّى يُكْتَبَ صِدِّيقًا، وَلَا يَزَالُ يَكْذِبُ حَتَّى يُكْتَبَ كَاذِبًا، أَلَا وَإِنَّ الْكَذِبَ لَا يَحِلُّ فِي جِدٍّ وَلَا هَزْلٍ، وَلَا أَنْ يَعِدَ الرَّجُلُ مِنْكُمْ صَبِيَّهُ ثُمَّ لَا يُنْجِزَ لَهُ، أَلَا وَلَا تَسْأَلُوا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ عَنْ شَيْءٍ فَإِنَّهُمْ قَدْ طَالَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْأَمَدُ فَقَسَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ، وَابْتَدَعُوا فِي دِينِهِمْ، فَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ لَا مَحَالَةَ بِسَائِلِيهِمْ فَمَا وَافَقَ كِتَابَكُمْ فَخُذُوهُ، وَمَا خَالَفَهُ فَاهْدُوا عَنْهُ وَاسْكُتوا، أَلَا وَإِنَّ أَصْغَرَ الْبُيُوتِ الْبَيْتُ الَّذِي لَيْسَ فِيهِ مِنْ كِتَابِ اللَّهِ شَيْءٌ، خَرِبٌ كَخِرَبِ الْبَيْتِ الَّذِي لَا عَامِرَ لَهُ، أَلَا وَإِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ يَخْرُجُ مِنَ الْبَيْتِ الَّذِي يَسْمَعُ فِيهِ سُورَةَ الْبَقَرَةِ تُقْرَأُ فِيهِ»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: Maʿmar said: Someone other than Jaʿfar reported from Ibn Masʿūd: “The finest thing placed in the heart is certainty; the best wealth is richness of the soul; the finest knowledge is that which benefits; the finest guidance is that which is followed. A little that suffices is better than much that distracts. Every one of you will end in a space four cubits long. Do not weary or bore people, for each soul has times of vigor and readiness and times of fatigue and withdrawal. The worst reports are false ones. Lying leads to wickedness and wickedness to the Fire. Hold fast to truthfulness, for truthfulness leads to righteousness and righteousness to Paradise. Know that these two follow each other: the truthful person continues speaking truth until he is recorded as most truthful; the liar continues lying until he is recorded as a liar. Lying is not permissible either in earnest or in jest, nor should one of you promise his child something and fail to deliver it. Do not question the People of the Book, for a long period has passed over them, their hearts have hardened, and they have innovated in their religion. But if you must question them, accept what agrees with your Book; turn away from and remain silent about what contradicts it. The poorest house is one that contains nothing of God's Book: it is ruined, like a deserted house with no inhabitant. Satan leaves a house in which he hears Sūrat al-Baqara being recited.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Zubayr, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever guarantees me six things, I guarantee him Paradise.” They asked: “What are they, Messenger of God?” He replied: “When he speaks, he speaks truthfully; when he makes a promise, he fulfills it; when entrusted, he returns what was entrusted; he lowers his gaze, guards his private parts, and restrains his hand”—or he said, “his tongue.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, who said: “No concession is made for anything people call lying except in three cases: what a husband says to his wife and a wife to her husband to foster affection; reconciliation between people; and warfare, for war involves deception.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٠٥ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، قَالَ:   «§لَا يُرَخَّصُ فِي شَيْءٍ مِمَّا يَقُولُ النَّاسُ أَنَّهُ كَذِبٌ إِلَّا فِي ثَلَاثٍ: الزَّوْجُ لِامْرَأَتِهِ، وَالْمَرْأَةُ لِزَوْجِهَا فِي الْمَوَدَّةِ، وَالْإِصْلَاحِ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ، وَفِي الْحَرْبِ فَإِنَّ الْحَرْبَ خَدْعَةٌ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: “When one of you wishes to deliver the sermon for a matter of concern, let him begin by saying: ‘Praise belongs to God. We praise Him, seek His help and forgiveness, and seek refuge with God from the evils of ourselves. Whoever God guides, none can mislead; whoever He misleads, none can guide. I testify that there is no deity except God alone, without partner, and I testify that Muḥammad is His servant and messenger ﷺ.’ Then he should recite these verses: ‘O you who believe, be mindful of God as He ought to be minded, and do not die except as those who submit’ [3:102]; ‘Be mindful of God, by whom you ask one another, and the ties of kinship. God is ever watching over you’ [4:1]; and ‘O you who believe, be mindful of God and speak words that are sound’ [33:70].”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٠٦ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنْ أَبِي الْأَحْوَصِ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، قَالَ:   «§إِذَا أَرَادَ أَحَدُكُمْ أَنْ يَخْطُبَ خُطْبَةَ الْحَاجَةِ فَلْيَبْدَأْ وَلْيَقُلْ: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ نَحْمَدُهُ وَنَسْتَعِينُهُ وَنَسْتَغْفِرُهُ، وَنَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ شُرُورِ أَنْفُسِنَا، مَنْ يَهْدِي اللَّهُ فَلَا مُضِلَّ لَهُ، وَمَنْ يُضْلِلْ فَلَا هَادِيَ لَهُ، وَأَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ»   ، ثُمَّ يَقْرَأُ هَذِهِ الْآيَاتِ:  {يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقَاتِهِ وَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ}   [آل عمران: ١٠٢]  ،  {اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي تَسَاءَلُونَ - [١٦٣] - بِهِ وَالْأَرْحَامَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَيْكُمْ رَقِيبًا}   [النساء: ١]  ،  {يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَقُولُوا قَوْلًا سَدِيدًا}   [الأحزاب: ٧٠]  ،

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us: a man of the Anṣār informed me, raising the report [to the Prophet ﷺ], that he said: “Every important discourse that does not begin with remembrance of God is cut off [from blessing].”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Budayl al-ʿUqaylī, from Mujāhid, who said: The Prophet ﷺ delivered a sermon on a certain matter. Abū Bakr then stood and gave a shorter sermon than the Prophet's ﷺ, and ʿUmar then stood and gave a shorter one than Abū Bakr's. A young man stood and requested permission from the Prophet ﷺ to speak; permission was granted, but he went on at length until the Prophet ﷺ told him: “Enough, stop now”—or words to that effect. Then he said: “God never sent a prophet except as a conveyor [of the message]. Excessive elaboration in speech is from Satan, and some eloquence is sorcery”—or “In eloquence there is sorcery.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٠٩ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ بُدَيْلٍ الْعَقِيلِيِّ، عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ، قَالَ: خَطَبَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ خُطْبَةً فِي بَعْضِ الْأَمْرِ، ثُمَّ قَامَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ فَخَطَبَ خُطْبَةً دُونَ خُطْبَةِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، ثُمَّ قَامَ عُمَرُ فَخَطَبَ خُطْبَةً دُونَ خُطْبَةِ أَبِي بَكْرٍ، ثُمَّ قَامَ شَابٌّ فَتِيٌ، فَاسْتَأْذَنَ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فِي الْخُطْبَةِ، فَأَذِنَ لَهُ، فَطَوَّلَ الْخُطْبَةَ، فَلَمْ يَزَلْ يَخْطُبُ حَتَّى قَالَ لَهُ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «هِيهِ قَطِ الْآنَ»   أَوْ كَمَا قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ  ثُمَّ قَالَ:   «إِنَّ §اللَّهَ لَمْ يَبْعَثْ نَبِيًّا إِلَّا مُبَلِّغًا، وَإِنَّ تَشْقِيقَ الْكَلَامِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ، وَإِنَّ مِنَ الْبَيَانِ سِحْرًا - أَوْ مِنَ الْبَيَانِ سِحْرٌ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, that Ibn Masʿūd used to say in a prayer seeking guidance: “O God, I seek Your choice through Your knowledge, and seek ability through Your power, and ask You for Your great bounty. You know and I do not know; You are able and I am not; You know all hidden things. If this matter is good for me in my worldly life, my livelihood, and the outcome of my affairs, make it easy for me and bless it for me. If something else is better for me, decree what is good wherever it may be and make me content with it, O Merciful One.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, who said: “[They] rejoiced at the boy when he was born to them and grieved over him when he died. Had he lived, his life would have meant their destruction. Let a person therefore be content with God's decree, for what God chooses for a believer in what the believer dislikes is more often better than what He chooses in what the believer loves.” [The opening subject is missing or damaged in the source.]

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Abān, from Anas, that a man asked the Prophet ﷺ, “Advise me, Messenger of God.” The Prophet ﷺ said: “Approach the matter with careful planning. If you see good in its outcome, proceed; if you fear error, hold back.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, who said: ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ wrote to Muʿāwiya about deliberation. Muʿāwiya replied: “To reflect carefully on a good matter increases insight and right guidance. The rightly guided person keeps away from haste; the disappointed person misses out through failure to deliberate. The one who checks carefully is right, or nearly so; the hasty person is wrong, or nearly so. A person who cannot benefit from gentleness will be harmed by rashness. One who does not benefit from experience will never attain high standing. A person does not attain mature judgment until his forbearance overcomes his ignorance and his desire.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢١٤ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، قَالَ: كَتَبَ عَمْرُو بْنُ الْعَاصِ إِلَى مُعَاوِيَةَ فِي الْأَنَاةِ، فَكَتَبَ إِلَيْهِ مُعَاوِيَةُ:   «أَمَّا بَعْدُ، §فَإِنَّ التَّفَهُّمَ فِي الْخَيْرِ زِيَادَةٌ وَرُشْدٌ، وَإِنَّ الرَّشِيدَ مَنْ رَشَدَ عَنِ الْعَجَلَةِ، وَإِنَّ الْخَائِبَ مَنْ خَابَ عَنِ الْأَنَاةِ، وَإِنَّ الْمُتَثَبِّتَ مُصِيبٌ، أَوْ كَادَ أَنْ يَكُونَ مُصِيبًا، وَإِنَّ الْمُعَجِّلَ مُخْطِئٌ، أَوْ كَادَ أَنْ يَكُونَ مُخْطِئًا، وَإِنَّهُ مَنْ لَا يَنْفَعُهُ الرِّفْقُ يَضُرُّهُ الْخَرَقُ وَمَنْ لَا تَنْفَعُهُ التَّجَارِبُ لَا يُدْرِكُ الْمَعَالِيَ، وَلَنْ يَبْلُغَ الرَّجُلُ مَبْلَغَ الرَّأْيِ حَتَّى يَغْلِبَ حِلْمُهُ جَهْلَهُ وَشَهْوَتَهُ»

The rightly guided person keeps away from haste; the disappointed person misses out through failure to deliberate. The one who checks carefully is right, or nearly so; the hasty person is wrong, or nearly so. A person who cannot benefit from gentleness will be harmed by rashness. One who does not benefit from experience will never attain high standing. A person does not attain mature judgment until his forbearance overcomes his ignorance and his desire.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Muḥammad ibn Ziyād, who said: I heard Abū Hurayra say that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “When one of you puts on sandals, let him start with the right; when he takes them off, let him start with the left. Let him wear both or remove both.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, who said: Someone who had seen ʿAlī informed me that he “walked in one sandal along the middle of the row [or pathway].”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, who said: “Putting on sandals while standing is disliked only because of the difficulty it presents.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAbbād ibn Tamīm, from his uncle, who said: “I saw the Messenger of God ﷺ lying on his back in the mosque, one leg placed over the other.” Al-Zuhrī said: Ibn al-Musayyib also told me: “ʿUmar and ʿUthmān did this so often that their instances cannot be counted.” Al-Zuhrī said: “People have made a great issue of this.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٢١ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ عَبَّادِ بْنِ تَمِيمٍ، عَنْ عَمِّهِ، قَالَ:   «رَأَيْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ §مُسْتَلْقِيًا فِي الْمَسْجِدِ رَافِعًا إِحْدَى رِجْلَيْهِ عَلَى الْأُخْرَى»   ، قَالَ الزُّهْرِيُّ: وَأَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ الْمُسَيِّبِ، قَالَ:   «كَانَ ذَلِكَ مِنْ عُمَرَ، وَعُثْمَانَ رَحْمَةُ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمَا مَا لَا يُحْصَى مِنْهُمَا»   ، قَالَ الزُّهْرِيُّ:   «وَجَاءَ النَّاسُ بِأَمْرٍ عَظِيمٍ»

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yazīd al-Laythī, from Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī, who said: I know it only as a report he raised to the Messenger of God ﷺ: “It is not lawful for a Muslim to abandon his brother for more than three days. They meet, and this one turns away and that one turns away; the better of the two is the one who begins with the greeting of peace.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Suhayl ibn Abī Ṣāliḥ, from his father, from Abū Hurayra, who said the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The gates of Paradise are opened every Monday and Thursday.” Someone other than Suhayl reported: “Deeds are presented every Monday and Thursday. God forgives every servant who associates nothing with Him, except for two people who are estranged. God says to the angels: ‘Leave them until they are reconciled.’”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٢٦ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ سُهَيْلِ بْنِ أَبِي صَالِحٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§تُفْتَحُ أَبْوَابُ الْجَنَّةِ فِي كُلِّ اثْنَيْنِ وَخَمِيسٍ»   ، وَقَالَ غَيْرُ سُهَيْلٍ:   «تُعْرَضُ الْأَعْمَالُ كُلَّ اثْنَيْنِ وَخَمِيسٍ، فَيَغْفِرُ اللَّهُ لِكُلِّ عَبْدٍ لَا يُشْرِكُ بِهِ شَيْئًا، إِلَّا الْمُتَشَاحِنَيْنِ يَقُولُ اللَّهُ لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ: دَعُوهُمَا حَتَّى يَصْطَلِحَا»

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatāda, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Help your brother, whether he is the oppressor or the oppressed.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Hammām, from Abū Hurayra, who said the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the falsest of speech.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٢٨ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ هَمَّامٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§إِيَّاكُمْ وَالظَّنَّ فَإنَّ الظَّنَّ أَكْذَبُ الْحَدِيثِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, who said the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Kinship is a branch of the Merciful One. It will come on the Day of Resurrection with wings beneath the Throne, speaking with a clear, fluent tongue: ‘O God, maintain ties with whoever maintains ties with me, and cut off whoever cuts ties with me.’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, who said: I know this only as a raised report [from the Prophet ﷺ]: “Three things bring their ill consequences upon a person before death: cutting the ties of kinship that God commanded to be maintained; swearing a false oath to take another Muslim's property; and making a claim in order to gain status or increase one's following, for it only diminishes him. No act of obedience brings a swifter reward than maintaining kinship ties, and no disobedience brings swifter punishment than severing them. A people may maintain ties though they are wicked, and their wealth and numbers increase; and they may sever ties, and their wealth and numbers diminish. A false oath leaves a dwelling desolate.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٣١ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ أَبِي كَثِيرٍ، قَالَ: لَا أَعْلَمُهُ إِلَّا رَفَعَهُ قَالَ:   «§ثَلَاثٌ مَنْ كُنَّ فِيهِ رَأَى وَبَالَهُنَّ قَبْلَ مَوْتِهِ: مَنْ قَطَعَ رَحِمًا أَمَرَ اللَّهُ بِهَا أَنْ تُوصَلَ، وَمَنَ حَلَفَ عَلَى يَمِينٍ فَاجِرَةٍ لِيَقْطَعَ بِهَا مَالَ امْرِئٍ مُسْلِمٍ، وَمَنْ دَعَا دَعْوَةً يَتَكَثَّرُ بِهَا فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَزْدَادُ إِلَّا قِلَّةً، وَمَا مِنْ طَاعَةِ اللَّهِ شَيْءٌ أَعْجَلُ ثَوَابًا مِنْ صِلَةِ الرَّحِمِ، وَمِنْ مَعْصِيَةِ اللَّهِ شَيْءٌ أَعْجَلُ عُقُوبَةً مِنْ قَطِيعَةِ الرَّحِمِ، وَإِنَّ الْقَوْمَ لَيَتَوَاصَلُونَ وَهُمْ فَجَرَةٌ، فَتَكْثُرُ أَمْوَالُهُمْ وَيَكْثُرُ عَدَدُهُمْ، وَإِنَّهُمْ - [١٧١] - لَيَتَقَاطَعُونَ فَتَقِلُّ أَمْوَالُهُمْ وَيَقِلُّ عَدَدُهُمْ، وَالْيَمِينُ الْفَاجِرَةُ تَدَعُ الدَّارَ بَلَاقِعَ»

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, who said: I know this only as a raised report [from the Prophet ﷺ]: “Three things bring their ill consequences upon a person before death: cutting the ties of kinship that God commanded to be maintained; swearing a false oath to take another Muslim's property; and making a claim in order to gain status or increase one's following, for it only diminishes him. No act of obedience brings a swifter reward than maintaining kinship ties, and no disobedience brings swifter punishment than severing them. A people may maintain ties though they are wicked, and their wealth and numbers increase; and they may sever ties, and their wealth and numbers diminish. A false oath leaves a dwelling desolate.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from ʿIkrima, who said ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: “Maintaining ties does not mean maintaining ties with someone who maintains ties with you—that is merely reciprocation. Maintaining ties means reaching out to someone who has cut you off.”

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: “Kinship ties may be severed, and favors may go unacknowledged, but when God brings hearts close together, nothing can ever dislodge that bond.” He then recited, “Even if you had spent everything on earth ...” [Quran 8:63], the verse.
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٣٣ - أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ عَنِ ابْنِ طَاوُسٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ، قَالَ:   «إِنَّ §الرَّحِمَ تُقْطَعُ، وَإِنَّ النِّعْمَةَ تُكْفَرُ، وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ إِذَا قَارَبَ بَيْنَ الْقُلُوبِ لَمْ يُزَحْزِحْهَا شَيْءٌ أَبَدًا»   قَالَ: ثُمَّ قَرَأَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ:  {لَوْ أَنْفَقْتَ مَا فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا}   [الأنفال: ٦٣]  الْآيَةَ

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, who said: Abū Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān told me that Raddād al-Laythī informed him, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, that he heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “God, blessed and exalted, said: ‘I am God, and I am al-Raḥmān, the Merciful. I created kinship (al-raḥim) and derived its name from My name. Whoever maintains it, I maintain ties with him; whoever cuts it off, I cut him off.’”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٣٤ - أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنِي أَبُو سَلَمَةَ بْنُ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، أَنَّ رَدَّادًا اللَّيْثِيَّ أَخْبَرَهُ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ عَوْفٍ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَقُولُ:   «قَالَ اللَّهُ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى  §أَنَا اللَّهُ، وَأَنَا الرَّحْمَنُ، خَلَقْتُ الرَّحِمَ وَشَقَقْتُ لَهَا مِنِ اسْمِي، فَمَنْ وَصَلَهَا وَصَلْتُهُ، وَمَنْ قَطَعَهَا بَتَتُّهُ»

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from Abū Isḥāq al-Hamdānī, who said the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Whoever wishes for a postponement of his appointed time and an increase in provision should be mindful of God and maintain the ties of kinship.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٣٥ - أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ الْهَمْدَانِيِّ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§مَنْ سَرَّهُ النَّسْأُ فِي الْأَجَلِ، وَالزِّيَادَةُ فِي الرِّزْقِ فَلْيَتَّقِ اللَّهَ، وَلْيَصِلْ رَحِمَهُ»

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatāda [the source marks an omission], who said: “Kinship will come on the Day of Resurrection with a hook beneath the Throne, speaking with a clear, fluent tongue: ‘O God, maintain ties with those who maintained ties with me, and cut off those who cut me off.’”

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from an unnamed man, from Shahr ibn Ḥawshab, who said the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “One who severs kinship ties will not enter Paradise, nor will one who habitually drinks wine.”

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Aʿmash, who said: Ibn Masʿūd was sitting in a gathering after the dawn prayer. He said: “I adjure anyone here who has severed family ties by God to get up and leave us, for we wish to supplicate our Lord, and the gates of heaven are closed to the one who severs kinship ties.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٤٢ - أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنِ الْأَعْمَشِ، قَالَ: كَانَ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ جَالِسًا بَعْدَ الصُّبْحِ فِي حَلْقَةٍ، فَقَالَ:   «§أَنْشُدُ اللَّهَ قَاطِعَ رَحِمٍ إِلَّا مَا قَامَ عَنَّا، فَإِنَّا نُرِيدُ أَنْ نَدْعُوَ رَبَّنَا، وَإِنَّ أَبْوَابَ السَّمَاءِ مُرْتَجَةٌ دُونَ قَاطِعِ الرَّحِمِ»

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from Ibn al-Musayyib, from Abū Hurayra, who said the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Five things belong to the natural disposition: shaving the pubic hair, circumcision, trimming the moustache, plucking the armpit hair, and clipping the nails.”

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn al-Musayyib, who said: “Abraham was the first to be circumcised, the first to entertain a guest, and the first to see gray hair. When he saw it, he said: ‘My Lord, what is this?’ He replied: ‘This is dignity and forbearance.’ He said: ‘My Lord, increase me in dignity.’ Abraham was circumcised when he was 120 years old and died when he was 200.” ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: “He was circumcised with *al-Qadūm*—a place-name. Maʿmar told me this without doubt.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٤٥ - أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ سَعِيدٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ الْمُسَيِّبِ، قَالَ:   «§إِبْرَاهِيمُ أَوَّلُ مَنِ اخْتَتَنَ، وَأَوَّلُ مَنْ قَرَى الضَّيْفَ، وَأَوَّلُ مَنْ رَأَى الشَّيْبَ»   ، قَالَ:   «فَلَمَّا رَأَى الشَّيْبَ قَالَ: أَيْ رَبِّ مَا هَذَا؟ قَالَ: هَذَا وَقَارٌ وَحِلْمٌ قَالَ: أَيْ رَبِّ، زِدْنِي وَقَارًا»   قَالَ:   «وَاخْتَتَنَ وَهُوَ ابْنُ عِشْرِينَ وَمِائَةٍ، وَمَاتَ وَهُوَ ابْنُ مِائَتَيْ سَنَةٍ»   . قَالَ عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ:   «وَاخْتَتَنَ بِالْقَدُومِ اسْمٌ، هَكَذَا أَخْبَرَنِي مَعْمَرٌ لَا شَكَّ»

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatāda, from an unnamed man, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he disapproved of an animal slaughtered by an uncircumcised man, saying: “His prayer is not accepted, and his testimony is not admissible.”

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Ḥasan, who said: “When a man enters Islam and fears harm to himself if he is circumcised, he need not be circumcised. His slaughtered animals may be eaten, his prayers are accepted, and his testimony is admissible.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar reported from al-Aʿmash, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, who said the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “No one is more patient with injury than God, mighty and exalted. They attribute a child to Him and He overlooks them; they attribute a consort and partner to Him, yet He provides for them and wards harm away from them.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar reported from Abān and others that, after the afternoon prayer, the Prophet ﷺ raised his voice until the young women in their private quarters could hear him. He said: “O people who have professed Islam with their tongues though faith has not entered their hearts: do not hurt the believers or seek out their private faults. Whoever seeks out believers' faults, God will seek out his faults; and whoever has his faults exposed by God will be disgraced in his own home.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٥١ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ أَبَانَ، وَغَيْرِهِ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ بَعْدَ صَلَاةِ الْعَصْرِ، فَرَفَعَ صَوْتَهُ حَتَّى أَسْمَعَ الْعَوَاتِقَ فِي خُدُورِهِنَّ قَالَ:   «يَا مَعْشَرَ مَنْ أَعْطَى الْإِسْلَامَ بِلِسَانِهِ، وَلَمْ يَدْخُلِ الْإِيمَانُ قَلْبَهُ، §لَا تُؤْذُوا الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا عَوْرَاتِهِمْ، فَإِنَّهُ مَنْ تَتَبَّعَ عَوْرَاتِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ تَتَبَّعَ اللَّهُ عَوْرَتَهُ، وَمَنْ تَتَبَّعَ اللَّهُ عَوْرَتَهُ يَفْضَحْهُ فِي بَيْتِهِ»

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar reported from Abān and others that, after the afternoon prayer, the Prophet ﷺ raised his voice until the young women in their private quarters could hear him. records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar reported from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, who attributed this saying to the Messenger of God ﷺ: “The most grievous form of usury is abusing people's reputations; the worst verbal abuse is satirical vilification, and one who retransmits it shares in the abuse.”

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from Ibn al-Musayyib, who said: “The worst usury is a person's excessive attack on the honor of his Muslim brother.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٥٣ - أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنِ ابْنِ الْمُسَيِّبِ، قَالَ:   «§أَرْبَى الرِّبَا اسْتِطَالَةُ الْمَرْءِ فِي عِرْضِ أَخِيهِ الْمُسْلِمِ»

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from someone who heard al-Ḥasan say: “The believer does not act ignorantly; when someone behaves ignorantly toward him, he responds with forbearance; when wronged, he forgives; and when deprived, he endures.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٥٤ - أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَمَّنْ، سَمِعَ الْحَسَنَ يَقُولُ:   «إِنَّ §الْمُؤْمِنَ لَا يَجْهَلُ، وَإِنْ جُهِلَ عَلَيْهِ حَلُمَ، وَإِنْ ظُلِمَ غَفَرَ، وَإِنْ حُرِمَ صَبَرَ»

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: قَالَ: وَقَالَ الْحَسَنُ:   «§الْغِيبَةُ أَنْ تَذْكُرَهُ بِمَا فِيهِ، فَإِذَا ذَكَرْتَهُ بِمَا لَيْسَ فِيهِ فَقَدْ بَهَتَّهُ»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: He said: Al-Ḥasan also said: “Backbiting is mentioning a person for something that truly is in him; if you mention something that is not in him, you have made a false accusation against him.”

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Zayd ibn Uthayʿ, that a man was insulting Abū Bakr while the Messenger of God ﷺ sat nearby. When Abū Bakr moved to defend himself, the Prophet ﷺ stood up. Abū Bakr said: “He was insulting me, but when I began to answer, you stood.” He replied: “An angel was with you, but when you moved to reply to him, it stood up, so I stood up.”

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatāda, that ʿIyāḍ ibn Ḥimār asked: “Messenger of God, if a man of lower standing than me insults me, would I be at fault for defending myself?” The Messenger of God ﷺ replied: “Two people who trade insults are two devils exchanging abuse and accusing one another of lies.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٥٦ - أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، أَنَّ عِيَاضَ بْنَ حِمَارٍ، قَالَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، أَرَأَيْتَ إِنْ شَتَمَنِي رَجُلٌ هُوَ أَوْضَعُ مِنِّي هَلْ عَلَيَّ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ أَنْتَصِرَ مِنْهُ؟ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§الْمُتَشَاتِمَانِ شَيْطَانَانِ يَتَهَاتَرَانِ وَيَتَكَاذَبَانِ»

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: قَالَ: وَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§الْمُتَشَاتِمَانِ مَا قَالَا عَلَى الْأَوَّلِ حَتَّى يَعْتَدِيَ الْمَظْلُومُ»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: He also said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Whatever two people who exchange insults say is charged against the one who started it, unless the wronged person goes beyond bounds.”

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatāda, that a man satirized a group in the time of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. One of the group came to ask ʿUmar to redress the wrong. ʿUmar said: “You may have his tongue.” Then he called the man and said: “Do not act on what I said. I only said it in front of the people so that he would not repeat it.” [The wording “You may have his tongue” is a threat, which ʿUmar then explicitly withdraws.]

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from Abān, from Anas, who said the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “When a person's Muslim brother is backbitten in his presence and he defends him, God will defend him in this world and the next. If he does not defend him, God will overtake him in this world and the next.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٥٨ - أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ أَبَانَ، عَنْ أَنَسٍ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§مَنِ اغْتِيبَ عِنْدَهُ أَخُوهُ الْمُسْلِمُ فَنَصَرهُ، نَصَرَهُ اللَّهُ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ، وَإِنْ لَمْ يَنْصُرْهُ أَدْرَكَهُ اللَّهُ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ»

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from some Meccans, that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said [addressing the Kaʿba]: “I testify that you are God's House and that God has magnified your inviolability; but the inviolability of a Muslim is greater than yours.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٦٠ - أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ بَعْضِ الْمَكِّيِّينَ، أَنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عَمْرِو بْنِ الْعَاصِ، قَالَ:   «§أَشْهَدُ أَنَّكَ بَيْتُ اللَّهِ، وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ عَظَّمَ حُرْمَتَكَ، وَأَنَّ حُرْمَةَ الْمُسْلِمِ أَعْظَمُ مِنْ حُرْمَتِكَ»

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Aʿmash, that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: “What is wrong with you that, when you hear a man tear apart the honor of his brother, you do not stop him?” They said: “We fear his tongue.” He replied: “That is the least reason for you not to be witnesses.” [The final expression is difficult; the source reads *dhālika adnā allā takūnū shuhadāʾ*.]

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilāba, who said the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Righteousness does not wear away; sin is not forgotten; and the One who calls to account never dies. Act as you wish, for as you deal with others, so will you be dealt with.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٦٢ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ أَبِي قِلَابَةَ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§الْبِرُّ لَا يَبْلَى، وَالْإِثْمُ لَا يُنْسَى، وَالدَّيَّانُ لَا يَمُوتُ، فَكُنْ كَمَا شِئْتَ كَمَا تَدِينُ تُدَانُ»

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from Abān: “Jesus son of Mary never found fault with anything. He once passed a dead dog with his disciples, and one of them said: ‘How foul its smell!’ Jesus son of Mary replied: ‘How white its teeth are!’”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٦٣ - أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ أَبَانَ:   «إِنَّ §عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ مَا عَابَ شَيْئًا قَطُّ، فَمَرَّ هُوَ وَأَصْحَابُهُ عَلَى كَلْبٍ مَيِّتٍ، فَقَالَ لَهُ بَعْضُهُمْ: مَا أَنْتَنَ رِيحَهُ ‍‍ فَقَالَ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ: مَا أَبْيَضَ أَسْنَانَهُ»

records.text_en: Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Abī Sabra both informed us: “Two men insulted each other before Abū Bakr, and he said nothing to either of them.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٦٥ - أَخْبَرَنَا ابْنُ جُرَيْجٍ، وَابْنُ أَبِي سَبْرَةَ، قَالَا:   «§تَشَاتَمَ رَجُلَانِ عِنْدَ أَبِي بَكْرٍ فَلَمْ يَقُلْ لَهُمَا شَيْئًا»

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: «§وَتَشَاتَمَ رَجُلَانِ عِنْدَ عُمَرَ فَأَدَّبَهُمَا»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: “Two men also exchanged insults in the presence of ʿUmar, and he disciplined them both.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbayda, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: “If you see your brother commit a sin, do not become Satan's helpers against him by saying, ‘O God, disgrace him! O God, curse him!’ Rather, ask God for well-being. We companions of Muḥammad ﷺ used not to pass judgment on anyone until we knew how he would die. If his life ended well, we knew he had attained good; and if it ended badly, we feared for him because of his deeds.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٦٦ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنْ أَبِي عُبَيْدَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، قَالَ:   «§إِذَا رَأَيْتُمْ أَخَاكُمْ قَارَفَ ذَنْبًا فَلَا تَكُونُوا أَعْوَانًا للشَيْطَانِ عَلَيْهِ، تَقُولُوا: اللَّهُمَّ أَخْزِهِ، اللَّهُمَّ الْعَنْهُ، وَلَكِنْ سَلُوا اللَّهَ الْعَافِيَةَ، فَإِنَّا أَصْحَابَ مُحَمَّدٍ كُنَّا لَا نَقُولُ فِي أَحَدٍ شَيْئًا حَتَّى نَعْلَمَ عَلَى مَا يَمُوتُ، فَإِنْ خُتِمَ لَهُ بِخَيْرٍ عَلِمْنَا أَنَّهُ قَدْ أَصَابَ خَيْرًا، وَإِنْ خُتِمَ لَهُ بِشَرٍّ خِفْنَا عَلَيْهِ عَمَلَهُ»

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilāba, that Abū al-Dardāʾ passed a man who had committed a sin, and people were insulting him. He said: “If you found him in a well, would you not pull him out?” They said: “Certainly.” He said: “Then do not insult your brother; praise God who has spared you.” They asked: “Do you not hate him?” He said: “I hate only his deed. When he gives it up, he is my brother.” Abū al-Dardāʾ also said: “Pray to God in your days of ease, so that He may answer you in your days of hardship.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٦٧ - أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ أَبِي قِلَابَةَ، أَنَّ أَبَا الدَّرْدَاءِ مَرَّ عَلَى رَجُلٍ قَدْ أَصَابَ ذَنْبًا، فَكَانُوا يَسُبُّونَهُ، فَقَالَ:   «أَرَأَيْتُمْ لَوْ وَجَدْتُمُوهُ فِي قَلِيبٍ أَلَمْ تَكُونُوا مُسْتخْرِجِيهِ؟»   ، قَالُوا: بَلَى، قَالَ:   «§فَلَا تَسُبُّوا أَخَاكُمْ وَاحْمَدُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي عَافَاكُمْ»   ، قَالُوا: أَفَلَا تَبْغَضُهُ؟ قَالَ:   «إِنَّمَا أَبْغَضُ عَمَلَهُ، فَإِذَا تَرَكَهُ فَهُوَ أَخِي»   ، قَالَ: وَقَالَ أَبُو الدَّرْدَاءِ:   «ادْعُ اللَّهَ فِي يَوْمِ سَرَّائِكَ لَعَلَّهُ أَنْ يَسْتَجِيبَ فِي يَوْمِ ضَرَّائِكَ»

records.display_matn_ar: أَنَّ أَبَا الدَّرْدَاءِ مَرَّ عَلَى رَجُلٍ قَدْ أَصَابَ ذَنْبًا، فَكَانُوا يَسُبُّونَهُ، فَقَالَ:   «أَرَأَيْتُمْ لَوْ وَجَدْتُمُوهُ فِي قَلِيبٍ أَلَمْ تَكُونُوا مُسْتخْرِجِيهِ؟»   ، قَالُوا: بَلَى، قَالَ:   «§فَلَا تَسُبُّوا أَخَاكُمْ وَاحْمَدُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي عَافَاكُمْ»   ، قَالُوا: أَفَلَا تَبْغَضُهُ؟ قَالَ:   «إِنَّمَا أَبْغَضُ عَمَلَهُ، فَإِذَا تَرَكَهُ فَهُوَ أَخِي»   ، قَالَ: وَقَالَ أَبُو الدَّرْدَاءِ:   «ادْعُ اللَّهَ فِي يَوْمِ سَرَّائِكَ لَعَلَّهُ أَنْ يَسْتَجِيبَ فِي يَوْمِ ضَرَّائِكَ»

records.display_matn_en: that Abū al-Dardāʾ passed a man who had committed a sin, and people were insulting him. He said: “If you found him in a well, would you not pull him out?” They said: “Certainly.” He said: “Then do not insult your brother; praise God who has spared you.” They asked: “Do you not hate him?” He said: “I hate only his deed. When he gives it up, he is my brother.” Abū al-Dardāʾ also said: “Pray to God in your days of ease, so that He may answer you in your days of hardship.”
