records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb told me: “Aslam, let your love not become an obsession, nor your hatred a cause of destruction.” I asked: “How so?” He replied: “When you love, do not become attached as a child becomes attached to something it loves. When you hate, do not hate so intensely that you wish the person ruined or dead.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٦٩ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، قَالَ: قَالَ لِي عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ:   «يَا أَسْلَمُ لَا يَكُنْ حُبُّكَ كَلَفًا، وَلَا يَكُنْ بُغْضُكَ تَلَفًا»   ، قُلْتُ: وَكَيْفَ ذَلِكَ؟ قَالَ:   «§إِذَا أَحْبَبْتَ فَلَا تَكْلَفْ كَمَا يَكْلَفُ الصَّبِيُّ بِالشَّيْءِ يُحِبُّهُ، وَإِذَا أَبْغَضْتَ فَلَا تَبْغَضْ بُغْضًا تُحِبُّ أَنْ يَتْلَفَ صَاحِبُكَ وَيَهْلِكَ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from someone who heard al-Ḥasan say: “Love in moderation and hate in moderation. Some people have gone to extremes in loving others and perished, and some have gone to extremes in hating others and perished. Do not go to extremes in either love or hatred. If something shields your brother's private affairs, do not uncover it. Do not spy on your brother—you have been forbidden to spy on him. Do not belittle him or recoil from him.”

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from someone who heard al-Ḥasan say: “Love in moderation and hate in moderation. Some people have gone to extremes in loving others and perished, and some have gone to extremes in hating others and perished. Do not go to extremes in either love or hatred. If something shields your brother's private affairs, do not uncover it. Do not spy on your brother—you have been forbidden to spy on him. Do not belittle him or recoil from him.”

records.text_en: It was read to ʿAbd al-Razzāq, from Maʿmar, from Jaʿfar ibn Burqān, from Yazīd ibn al-Aṣamm, from Abū Hurayra, who said the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “By the One in whose hand is my soul, if you did not sin, God would remove you and bring a people who sinned and then sought forgiveness, and He would forgive them.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٧١ - قَرَأْنَا عَلَى عَبْدِ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بُرْقَانَ، عَنْ يَزِيدَ بْنِ الْأَصَمِّ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «وَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ §لَوْ لَمْ تُذْنِبُوا لَذَهَبَ اللَّهُ بِكُمْ، وَلَجَاءَ بِقَوْمٍ يُذْنِبُونَ فَيَسْتَغْفِرُونَ، فَيَغْفِرُ لَهُمْ»

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilāba, from Abū Dharr, who said: God said: “My servants, I have forbidden injustice to Myself and forbidden it among you, so do not wrong other servants. My servants, you commit errors by night and day: seek My forgiveness and I shall forgive you every sin without concern. My servants, even if your first and last, your jinn and humankind, young and old, all possessed the heart of the most wicked of you, My sovereignty would not diminish in any way. Even if all of them asked Me and I gave each person what he asked, nothing I possess would be diminished, any more than a needle-tip dipped into the sea reduces the sea.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٧٢ - أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ أَبِي قِلَابَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي ذَرٍّ، قَالَ:   «قَالَ اللَّهُ: §يَا عِبَادِي إِنِّي حَرَّمْتُ الظُّلْمَ عَلَى نَفْسِي، وَجَعَلْتُهُ عَلَيْكُمْ مُحَرَّمًا، فَلَا تَظْلِمُوا الْعِبَادَ، يَا عِبَادِي إِنَّكُمْ تُخْطِئُونَ بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ فَاسْتَغْفِرُونِي فَإِنِّي أَغْفِرُ لَكُمُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا وَلَا أُبَالِي، يَا عِبَادِي لَوْ أَنَّ أَوَّلَكُمْ وَآخِرَكُمْ، وَجِنَّكُمْ وَإِنْسَكُمْ، وَصَغِيرَكُمْ وَكَبِيرَكُمْ، كَانُوا عَلَى قَلْبِ أفْجرِكُمْ لَمْ يُنْقِصْ مِنْ مُلْكِي شَيْئًا، وَلَوْ أَنَّ أَوَّلَكُمْ وَآخِرَكُمْ، وَجِنَّكُمْ وَإِنْسَكُمْ، وَصَغِيرَكُمْ وَكَبِيرَكُمْ، سَأَلُونِي فَأَعْطَيْتُ لِكُلِّ رَجُلٍ مِنْهُمْ مَسْأَلَتَهُ لَمْ يُنْقِصْ ذَلِكَ مِمَّا عِنْدِي شَيْئًا، كَرَأْسِ الْمِخْيَطِ يُغْمَسُ فِي الْبَحْرِ»

records.raw_text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilāba, from Abū Dharr, who said: God said: “My servants, I have forbidden injustice to Myself and forbidden it among you, so do not wrong other servants. My servants, you commit errors by night and day: seek My forgiveness and I shall forgive you every sin without concern. My servants, even if your first and last, your jinn and humankind, young and old, all possessed the heart of the most wicked of you, My sovereignty would not diminish in any way. Even if all of them asked Me and I gave each person what he asked, nothing I possess would be diminished, any more than a needle-tip dipped into the sea reduces the sea.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar reported from al-Aʿmash, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: “None is more patient with offense than God. They attribute a child to Him and He overlooks them; they attribute a companion and partner to Him, yet He provides for them and protects them.” I asked: “Who told you this?” He said: “Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, from the Prophet ﷺ.”

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn, that Ibn Masʿūd said: “When a man among the Children of Israel committed a sin, he would wake to find written on his door: ‘You committed such-and-such a sin; its atonement is such-and-such a deed.’ He might find the required deed too great to carry out.” Ibn Masʿūd said: “I would not wish God had given us that instead of this verse: ‘Whoever does wrong or harms himself, then seeks God's forgiveness, will find God forgiving and merciful’ [Quran 4:110].”

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbayda, from Ibn Masʿūd: “A man passed someone who was prostrating and stepped on his neck. The prostrating man said: ‘You step on my neck while I am prostrating? By God, God will never forgive you for this!’ God then said: ‘Do you presume to swear concerning Me? I have already forgiven him.’”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٧٥ - أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنْ أَبِي عُبَيْدَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ:   «أَنَّ رَجُلًا مَرَّ بِرَجُلٍ وَهُوَ سَاجِدٌ فَوَطِئَ عَلَى رَقَبَتِهِ، فَقَالَ: أَتَطَؤُ عَلَى رَقَبَتِي وَأَنَا سَاجِدٌ، لَا وَاللَّهِ، لَا يَغْفِرُ اللَّهُ لَكَ هَذَا أَبَدًا، قَالَ: فَقَالَ اللَّهُ: §اتَتَأَلَّى عَلَيَّ فَإِنِّي قَدْ غَفَرْتُ لَهُ»

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatāda or al-Ḥasan or both, who said: “Injustice is of three kinds: injustice that is not forgiven, injustice that is not overlooked, and injustice that is forgiven. As for that which is not forgiven, it is associating partners with God; that which is not overlooked is people's wronging one another; and that which is forgiven is a servant's wrongdoing against himself in what lies between him and his Lord.”

records.text_en: Maʿmar said: In the scroll of Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh it says: “Two deeds make the outcome certain, two are multiplied, and one is repaid equally. As for the two that make the outcome certain: whoever meets God without associating anything with Him enters Paradise, and whoever meets God associating partners with Him enters the Fire. As for the multiplied deeds: whoever performs a good deed has it recorded as ten times its like, up to seven hundredfold. As for what is repaid equally: whoever commits an evil deed has only its like recorded against him.” [The wording specifies one of the two multiplied categories here, without spelling out another.]

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar reported from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: “Sins considered insignificant are like travelers who stop in barren country with food that cannot be cooked without a fire. They spread out: one brings a piece of dung, another a bone, another a stick, until they collect enough to cook their food. Likewise the person who commits supposedly insignificant sins tells a lie here, commits a sin there, and accumulates enough that God may cast him face-down into the Fire of Hell.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٧٨ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ يَزِيدَ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، قَالَ:   «§مَثَلُ مُحَقَّرَاتِ الذُّنُوبِ كَمَثَلِ قَوْمٍ سَفْرٍ نَزَلُوا بِأَرْضٍ قَفْرٍ مَعَهُمْ طَعَامٌ لَا يُصْلِحُهُمْ إِلَّا النَّارُ، فَتَفَرَّقُوا فَجَعَلَ هَذَا يَجِيءُ بِالرَّوْثَةِ، وَيَجِيءُ هَذَا بِالْعَظْمِ، وَيَجِيءُ هَذَا بِالْعُودِ حَتَّى جَمَعُوا مِنْ ذَلِكَ مَا أَصْلَحُوا بِهِ طَعَامَهُمْ، فَكَذَلِكَ صَاحِبُ الْمُحَقَّرَاتِ، يَكْذِبُ الْكَذْبَةَ، وَيُذْنِبُ الذَّنْبَ، وَيَجْمَعُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ مَا لَعَلَّهُ أَنْ يَكُبَّهُ اللَّهُ بِهِ عَلَى وَجْهِهِ فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ»

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar reported from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: “Sins considered insignificant are like travelers who stop in barren country with food that cannot be cooked without a fire. They spread out: one brings a piece of dung, another a bone, another a stick, until they collect enough to cook their food. Likewise the person who commits supposedly insignificant sins tells a lie here, commits a sin there, and accumulates enough that God may cast him face-down into the Fire of Hell.”

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from someone who heard al-Ḥasan say: “No one meets God without having sinned except Yaḥyā son of Zakariyyā—peace be upon them—for he did not sin, nor did he desire a woman.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٧٩ - أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَمَّنْ سَمِعَ الْحَسَنَ، يَقُولُ:   «§لَيْسَ مِنْ أَحَدٍ يَلْقَى اللَّهَ إِلَّا أَذْنَبَ إِلَّا يَحْيَى بْنَ زَكَرِيَّا عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَامُ، فَإِنَّهُ لَمْ يُذْنِبْ وَلَمْ يَهِمَّ بِامْرَأَةٍ»

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from Hammām ibn Munabbih, who heard Abū Hurayra say that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “God laughs at two men, one of whom kills the other, yet both enter Paradise.” They asked: “How is that, Messenger of God?” He replied: “This one is killed and enters Paradise, then God accepts the repentance of the other, guides him to Islam, and he fights in God's cause and is martyred.”

records.matn_ar: يَضْحَكُ اللَّهُ لِرَجُلَيْنِ يَقْتُلُ أَحَدُهُمَا الْآخَرَ، كِلَاهُمَا يَدْخُلُ الْجَنَّةَ»   ، قَالُوا: وَكَيْفَ ذَلِكَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ؟ قَالَ:   «يَقْتُلُ هَذَا فَيَلِجُ الْجَنَّةَ، ثُمَّ يَتُوبُ اللَّهُ عَلَى الْآخَرِ فَيَهْدِيهِ إِلَى الْإِسْلَامِ، ثُمَّ يُجَاهِدُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَيُسْتَشْهَدُ»

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbayda, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: “Two men are such that God laughs toward them. One is a man mounted on one of the finest horses among his companions. They encounter the enemy, and his companions flee; he stands firm until killed as a martyr. God laughs at him and says, ‘Look at My servant: no one sees him except Me.’” [The source introduces two men but describes only the first in this report.]
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٨١ - أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنْ أَبِي عُبَيْدَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، قَالَ:   «§رَجُلَانِ يَضْحَكُ اللَّهُ إِلَيْهِمَا: رَجُلٌ تَحْتَهُ فَرَسٌ مِنْ أَمْثَلِ خَيْلِ أَصْحَابِهِ فَلَقُوا الْعَدُوَّ فَانْهَزَمُوا، وَثَبَتْ إِلَى أَنْ قُتِلَ شَهِيدًا، فَذَلِكَ يَضْحَكُ اللَّهُ مِنْهُ، فَيَقُولُ: انْظُرُوا إِلَى عَبْدِي لَا يَرَاهُ أَحَدٌ غَيْرِي»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar reported from Saʿīd al-Jurayrī, from Abū al-ʿAlāʾ ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr, from Abū Dharr, who said: “There are three toward whom God shines [or looks favorably]. First is a man who rises at night, leaves his bed and warmth, performs his ablution well, and stands for prayer. God says to the angels, ‘What moved My servant to do this?’ They say, ‘You know best.’ He says, ‘I know, but tell Me.’ They say, ‘You made him fear something, and he feared it; You made him hope for something, and he hoped for it.’ He says, ‘I call you to witness that I have given him security from what he feared and granted him what he hoped for.’ Second is a man in a detachment who encounters the enemy. His companions flee, but he holds his ground until he is killed or God grants victory. God asks the angels what moved him to do this. They say, ‘You know best.’ He says, ‘I know, but tell Me.’ They say, ‘You made him fear something and hope for something.’ He says, ‘I call you to witness that I have given him security from what he feared and granted him what he hoped for.’ Third is a man who travels all night until late in the night, then stops [the source has a gap]. His companions sleep, but he stands to pray. God asks the angels what moved him to do so. They say, ‘Our Lord, You know best.’ He says, ‘I know, but tell Me.’ They reply, ‘You made him fear something, and he feared it; You made him hope for something, and he hoped for it.’ He says, ‘I call you to witness that I have secured him from what he feared and granted him what he hoped for.’”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٨٢ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ سَعِيدٍ الْجُرَيْرِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِي الْعَلَاءِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ الشِّخِّيرِ، عَنْ أَبِي ذَرٍّ، قَالَ:   «ثَلَاثَةٌ يَسْتَنِيرُ اللَّهُ إِلَيْهِمْ: رَجُلٌ قَامَ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ وَتَرَكَ فِرَاشَهُ وَدِفَاءَهُ، ثُمَّ قَامَ يَتَوَضَّأُ فَأَحْسَنَ الْوُضُوءَ، ثُمَّ قَامَ إِلَى الصَّلَاةِ، فَيَقُولُ اللَّهُ لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ: §مَا حَمَلَ عَبْدِي عَلَى هَذَا أَوْ عَلَى مَا صَنَعَ؟ فَيَقُولُونَ: أَنْتَ أَعْلَمُ، فَيَقُولُ: أَنَا أَعْلَمُ وَلَكِنْ أَخْبِرُونِي، فَيَقُولُونَ: خَوَّفْتَهُ شَيْئًا فَخَافَهُ، - [١٨٦] - وَرَجَّيْتَهُ شَيْئًا فَرَجَاهُ، قَالَ: فَيَقُولُ: فَإِنِّي أُشْهِدُكُمْ أَنِّي قَدْ أَمَّنْتُهُ مِمَّا خَافَ، وَأَعْطَيْتُهُ مَا رَجَا، وَرَجُلٌ كَانَ فِي سَرِيَّةٍ، فَلَقِيَ الْعَدُوَّ فَانْهَزَمَ أَصْحَابُهُ، وَثَبَتَ حَتَّى قُتِلَ أَوْ فَتَحَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ، فَيَقُولُ اللَّهُ لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ: مَا حَمَلَ عَبْدِي عَلَى هَذَا، أَوْ عَلَى مَا صَنَعَ؟ فَيَقُولُونَ: أَنْتَ أَعْلَمُ بِهِ، فَيَقُولُ: أَنَا أَعْلَمُ بِهِ، وَلَكِنْ أَخْبِرُونِي، فَيَقُولُونَ: خَوَّفْتَهُ شَيْئًا فَخَافَهُ، وَرَجَّيْتَهُ شَيْئًا فَرَجَاهُ، قَالَ: فَيَقُولُ: أُشْهِدُكُمْ أَنِّي قَدْ أَمَّنْتُهُ مِمَّا خَافَ، وَأَعْطَيْتُهُ مَا رَجَا، وَرَجُلٌ أَسْرَى لَيْلَةً حَتَّى إِذَا كَانَ فِي آخِرِ اللَّيْلِ نَزَلَ.. . فَنَامَ أَصْحَابُهُ، فَقَامَ هُوَ يُصَلِّي، قَالَ: فَيَقُولُ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ: مَا حَمَلَ عَبْدِي عَلَى هَذَا، أَوْ عَلَى مَا صَنَعَ؟ فَيَقُولُونَ: رَبِّ أَنْتَ أَعْلَمُ، فَيَقُولُ: أَنَا أَعْلَمُ وَلَكِنْ أَخْبِرُونِي، قَالَ: فَيَقُولُونَ: خَوَّفْتَهُ شَيْئًا فَخَافَهُ، وَرَجَّيْتَهُ شَيْئًا فَرَجَاهُ، قَالَ: فَيَقُولُ: فَإِنِّي أُشْهِدُكُمْ أَنِّي أَمَّنْتُهُ مِمَّا خَافَ وَأَعْطَيْتُهُ مَا رَجَا»

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar reported from Saʿīd al-Jurayrī, from Abū al-ʿAlāʾ ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr, from Abū Dharr, who said: “There are three toward whom God shines [or looks favorably]. First is a man who rises at night, leaves his bed and warmth, performs his ablution well, and stands for prayer. God says to the angels, ‘What moved My servant to do this?’ They say, ‘You know best.’ He says, ‘I know, but tell Me.’ They say, ‘You made him fear something, and he feared it; You made him hope for something, and he hoped for it.’ He says, ‘I call you to witness that I have given him security from what he feared and granted him what he hoped for.’ Second is a man in a detachment who encounters the enemy. His companions flee, but he holds his ground until he is killed or God grants victory. God asks the angels what moved him to do this. They say, ‘You know best.’ He says, ‘I know, but tell Me.’ They say, ‘You made him fear something and hope for something.’ He says, ‘I call you to witness that I have given him security from what he feared and granted him what he hoped for.’ Third is a man who travels all night until late in the night, then stops [the source has a gap]. His companions sleep, but he stands to pray. God asks the angels what moved him to do so. They say, ‘Our Lord, You know best.’ He says, ‘I know, but tell Me.’ They reply, ‘You made him fear something, and he feared it; You made him hope for something, and he hoped for it.’ He says, ‘I call you to witness that I have secured him from what he feared and granted him what he hoped for.’”

records.isnad_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar reported from Saʿīd al-Jurayrī, from Abū al-ʿAlāʾ ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr, from Abū Dharr, who said: “
records.matn_en: There are three toward whom God shines [or looks favorably]. First is a man who rises at night, leaves his bed and warmth, performs his ablution well, and stands for prayer. God says to the angels, ‘What moved My servant to do this?’ They say, ‘You know best.’ He says, ‘I know, but tell Me.’ They say, ‘You made him fear something, and he feared it; You made him hope for something, and he hoped for it.’ He says, ‘I call you to witness that I have given him security from what he feared and granted him what he hoped for.’ Second is a man in a detachment who encounters the enemy. His companions flee, but he holds his ground until he is killed or God grants victory. God asks the angels what moved him to do this. They say, ‘You know best.’ He says, ‘I know, but tell Me.’ They say, ‘You made him fear something and hope for something.’ He says, ‘I call you to witness that I have given him security from what he feared and granted him what he hoped for.’ Third is a man who travels all night until late in the night, then stops [the source has a gap]. His companions sleep, but he stands to pray. God asks the angels what moved him to do so. They say, ‘Our Lord, You know best.’ He says, ‘I know, but tell Me.’ They reply, ‘You made him fear something, and he feared it; You made him hope for something, and he hoped for it.’ He says, ‘I call you to witness that I have secured him from what he feared and granted him what he hoped for.’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar reported from Ismāʿīl ibn Umayya, who said the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “God, mighty and exalted, laughs at you”—or a saying followed by garbled words in the source [*māyis laʿūb alʿab*]. A man of Bāhila asked: “Does God laugh?” The Prophet ﷺ said: “Yes.” The man replied: “By God, we shall never lack good from a Lord who laughs.” [The middle portion of the transmitted wording is corrupt and has not been reconstructed.]

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Abū Isḥāq, who said: “Three people are not loved by God: an elderly adulterer, a wealthy oppressor, and an arrogant poor man.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Saʿīd al-Jurayrī, from Abū al-ʿAlāʾ, from Abū Dharr, who said: “God is displeased with three: an elderly adulterer, an arrogant poor man, and a ruler who lies—or a wealthy oppressor.” Maʿmar was uncertain about the final category.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from a companion of the Messenger of God ﷺ, who said: A man asked: “Advise me, Messenger of God.” He said: “Do not become angry.” The man said: “I reflected on the Messenger of God's ﷺ words, and found that anger gathers together every kind of evil.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٨٦ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ حُمَيْدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، عَنْ رَجُلٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَجُلٌ: أَوْصِنِي يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، قَالَ:   «§لَا تَغْضَبْ»   ، قَالَ الرَّجُلُ:   «فَفَكَّرْتُ حِينَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ مَا قَالَ، فَإِذَا الْغَضَبُ يَجْمَعُ الشَّرَّ كُلَّهُ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū Hurayra, who said the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The strong man is not the one who can throw others down.” They asked: “Who, then, is strong, Messenger of God?” He replied: “The one who controls himself when angry.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٨٧ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ حُمَيْدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§لَيْسَ الشَّدِيدُ بِالصُّرَعَةِ»   ، قَالُوا: مَنِ الشَّدِيدُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ؟ قَالَ:   «الَّذِي يَمْلِكُ نَفْسَهُ عِنْدَ الْغَضَبِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Ḥasan, who said the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Anger is a burning ember kindled in the heart of the son of Adam. Do you not see his neck veins swell and his eyes redden? When any of you experiences this, if he is standing let him sit; and if he is sitting let him recline.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٨٩ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «إِنَّ §الْغَضَبَ جَمْرَةٌ تُوقَدُ فِي قَلْبِ ابْنِ آدَمَ، أَلَمْ تَرَوْا إِلَى انْتِفَاخِ أَوْدَاجِهِ وَإِلَى احْمِرَارِ عَيْنَيْهِ، فَإِذَا وَجَدَ أَحَدُكُمْ ذَلِكَ، فَإِنْ كَانَ قَائِمًا فَلْيَقْعُدْ، وَإِنْ كَانَ قَاعِدًا فَلْيَتَّكِ»
records.section_title_en: Anger, Rage and Reports Concerning Them

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: قَالَ: وَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§مَا جُرْعَةٌ أَحَبُّ إِلَى اللَّهِ مِنْ جُرْعَةِ غَيْظٍ كَتَمَهَا رَجُلٌ، أَوْ جُرْعَةِ صَبْرٍ عِنْدَ مُصِيبَةٍ، وَمَا قَطْرَةٌ أَحَبُّ إِلَى اللَّهِ مِنْ قَطْرَةِ دَمْعٍ مِنْ خَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ، وَقَطْرَةِ دَمٍ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: He also said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Whatever two people who exchange insults say is charged against the one who started it, unless the wronged person goes beyond bounds.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: A shaykh from Basra informed us, from another shaykh of theirs, from ʿUmar ibn Saʿīd, from Muslim ibn Yasār, who said the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “No eye fills with tears without God prohibiting the Fire from touching that body; nor do tears run down the cheek so that the face is overtaken by darkness or humiliation. If a single person wept among a people, they would be shown mercy. Everything has a measure and a balance except a tear, by which seas of fire are extinguished.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٩٢ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا شَيْخٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْبَصْرَةِ، عَنْ شَيْخٍ لَهُمْ، عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ، عَنْ مُسْلِمِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§مَا اغْرَوْرَقَتْ عَيْنٌ بِمَائِهَا إِلَّا حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ ذَلِكَ الْجَسَدَ عَلَى النَّارِ، وَلَا سَالَتْ عَلَى خَدِّهَا فَيُرْهِقُ ذَلِكَ الْوَجْهَ قَتَرٌ وَلَا ذِلَّةٌ، وَلَوْ أَنَّ بَاكِيًا بَكَى فِي أُمَّةٍ مِنَ الْأُمَمِ لَرُحِمُوا، وَمَا مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِلَّا لَهُ مِقْدَارٌ وَمِيزَانٌ إِلَّا الدَّمْعَةَ فَإِنَّهُ يُطْفَأُ بِهَا بِحَارٌ مِنْ نَارٍ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from a man whom he named, from Abū Hurayra, who said the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “O God, I have made a covenant with You that You will never break. Whichever of Your Muslim servants I have struck or insulted”—Maʿmar said: “I think he also said ‘or cursed’”—“make it a means of his drawing nearer to You on the day he meets You.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٩٣ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ رَجُلٍ سَمَّاهُ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي اتَّخَذْتُ عِنْدَكَ عَهْدًا لَنْ تُخْلِفَهُ وَلَا تُخْلِفُهُ، أَيُّمَا عَبْدٍ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ ضَرَبْتُهُ أَوْ شَتَمْتُهُ - قَالَ مَعْمَرٌ: حَسِبْتُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: - أَوْ لَعَنْتُهُ، فَاجْعَلْهُ قُرْبَةً لَهُ إِلَيْكَ يَوْمَ يَلْقَاكَ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Hammām ibn Munabbih, who heard Abū Hurayra say that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “O God, I have made a covenant with You that You will not break. I am only a human being. Whichever believer I have harmed, insulted, struck, or cursed, make it for him a blessing, an expiation, and a means of closeness to You on the Day of Resurrection.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbayda, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: I asked the Messenger of God ﷺ: “Which deeds are best?” He replied: “The five prayers at their proper times, kindness to parents, and striving in the cause of God.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from an unnamed man, from al-Ḥasan, that a man asked the Messenger of God ﷺ: “Which Muslims are most truly Muslim?” He replied: “Those from whose tongue and hand other Muslims are safe.” He asked: “Which believers have the most complete faith?” He replied: “Those of the best character.” He asked: “What is the best aspect of faith?” He replied: “Patience and generosity.” He asked: “What prayer is best?” He replied: “Prolonged devout standing.” He asked: “What charity is best?” He replied: “The utmost effort of one who has little.” He asked: “What striving is best?” He replied: “That in which one's blood is shed and one's horse is hamstrung.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar reported from al-Zuhrī, from Ḥabīb, the freedman of ʿUrwa, from ʿUrwa, and also from Abū Murāwiḥ al-Ghifārī, from Abū Dharr, who said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked: “Messenger of God, which deeds are best?” He replied: “Faith in God and striving in God's cause.” He asked: “Which emancipation is best?” He said: “The freeing of the most valuable slave.” He asked: “What if he cannot afford it?” He said: “Then help the skilled craftsman and work on behalf of someone who lacks skill.” He asked: “What if I cannot do that?” He said: “Then spare people your harm, for that is a charity you give on your own behalf.” [The narrator glosses *al-akhraq*, the unskilled person, as *al-aḥmaq*, one lacking judgment.]
records.text_ar: ٢٠٢٩٨ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ حَبِيبٍ، مَوْلَى عُرْوَةَ، عَنْ عُرْوَةَ، وَعَنْ أَبِي مُرَاوِحٍ الْغِفَارِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِي ذَرٍّ، قَالَ: جَاءَ رَجُلٌ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَسَأَلَهُ فَقَالَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، §أَيُّ الْأَعْمَالِ أَفْضَلُ؟ قَالَ:   «إِيمَانٌ بِاللَّهِ وَجِهَادٌ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ»   ، قَالَ: فَأَيُّ الْعَتَاقِ أَفْضَلُ؟ قَالَ:   «أَنْفَسُهَا»   ، قَالَ: أَفَرَأَيْتَ إِنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ؟ قَالَ:   «فَيُعِينُ الصَّانِعَ، وَيَصْنَعُ لِلْأَخْرَقِ»   ، قَالَ: أَفَرَأَيْتَ إِنْ لَمْ أَسْتَطِعْ؟ قَالَ:   «فَدَعِ النَّاسَ مِنْ شَرِّكَ، فَإِنَّهَا صَدَقَةٌ تَصَّدَّقُ بِهَا عَلَى نَفْسِكَ»   يَعْنِي أَخْرَقَ: أَحْمَقَ،

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Abū Qilāba, from more than one person: Saʿd al-Ḍaḥḥāk was passed by companions of the Prophet ﷺ and asked them: “Advise me.” They gave him advice. Muʿādh ibn Jabal was the last to pass, so he said: “Advise me, may God have mercy on you.” Muʿādh replied: “They have advised you thoroughly and have not withheld counsel. I will sum up your affair in a few words: Know that you cannot dispense with your share of worldly life, so arrange it carefully for yourself; it will then accompany you wherever you go.” [The final phrase follows the Arabic source closely, though its meaning is somewhat obscure.]

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Abū Qilāba, from more than one person: Saʿd al-Ḍaḥḥāk was passed by companions of the Prophet ﷺ and asked them: “Advise me.” They gave him advice. Muʿādh ibn Jabal was the last to pass, so he said: “Advise me, may God have mercy on you.” Muʿādh replied: “They have advised you thoroughly and have not withheld counsel. I will sum up your affair in a few words: Know that you cannot dispense with your share of worldly life, so arrange it carefully for yourself; it will then accompany you wherever you go.” [The final phrase follows the Arabic source closely, though its meaning is somewhat obscure.]

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Ḥasan, who said: God says: “My servant draws near to Me through nothing like what I have made obligatory upon him. My servant continues drawing near to Me with voluntary deeds until I love him. Then I become his eyes with which he sees, his ears with which he hears, his hands with which he grasps, and his feet with which he walks. When he calls upon Me, I answer; when he asks Me, I give; and when he seeks My forgiveness, I forgive him.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, who said: A man passed by a group, and one of them said: “I hate that man for God's sake.” The others said: “By God, you should not leave that unsubstantiated. Go, so-and-so, and tell him.” The messenger told the man what had been said. The man went to the Prophet ﷺ and said: “So-and-so claims to hate me for God's sake.” The Messenger of God ﷺ sent for the other man and asked: “Why do you hate him?” He replied: “He is my neighbor; I know him better than anyone. By God, I have never seen him perform any prayer except these obligatory prayers that the righteous and the wicked both perform.” The other man said: “Ask him, Messenger of God: Has he ever seen me delay them past their appointed times or perform their ablutions, bowing, or prostrations badly?” He replied: “No.” The accuser continued: “I have never seen him fast a day except during this month, which both the righteous and the wicked fast.” The man said: “Ask him: Has he seen me break any day of it, or treat its rights lightly?” He said: “No.” The accuser continued: “I have never seen him give charity except the obligatory alms that both the righteous and the wicked pay.” The man said: “Ask him: Have I concealed them, delayed them—or,” he said, “withheld them?” He replied: “No.” The Messenger of God ﷺ then said: “Leave him alone; perhaps he is better than you.”

records.display_matn_ar: مَرَّ رَجُلٌ بِقَوْمٍ، فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ مِنْهُمْ: إِنِّي لَأَبْغَضُ هَذَا لِلَّهِ، فَقَالَ الْقَوْمُ: وَاللَّهِ لَا بِرَّ لَهَا، اذْهَبْ يَا فُلَانُ فَبَلِّغْهُ، قَالَ: فَقَالَ لَهُ الَّذِي قَالَ، فَذَهَبَ الرَّجُلُ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَقَالَ: إِنَّ فُلَانًا يَزْعُمُ أَنَّهُ يَبْغَضُنِي فِي اللَّهِ، فَأَرْسَلَ إِلَيْهِ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَقَالَ:   «§عَلَامَ تَبْغَضُ هَذَا؟»   ، قَالَ: هُوَ لِي جَارٌ وَأَنَا أَعْلَمُ شَيْءٍ بِهِ، وَأَخْبَرُ شَيْءٍ بِهِ، وَاللَّهِ مَا رَأَيْتُهُ صَلَّى صَلَاةً قَطُّ إِلَّا هَذِهِ الصَّلَاةَ الْمَكْتُوبَةَ الَّتِي يُصَلِّيهَا الْبَرُّ وَالْفَاجِرُ، قَالَ: سَلْهُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، هَلْ رَآنِي أَخَّرْتُهَا عَنْ وَقْتِهَا، أَوْ أَسَأْتُ فِي وُضُوئِهَا، أَوْ رُكُوعِهَا أَوْ سُجودِهَا؟ قَالَ: لَا، قَالَ: وَلَا رَأَيْتُهُ صَامَ يَوْمًا قَطُّ إِلَّا هَذَا الشَّهْرَ الَّذِي يَصُومُهُ الْبَرُّ وَالْفَاجِرُ، قَالَ: سَلْهُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، هَلْ رَآنِي أَفْطَرْتُ مِنْهُ يَوْمًا، أَوِ استَخْفَفْتُ بِحَقِّهِ؟ قَالَ: لَا، قَالَ: وَلَا رَأَيْتُهُ تَصَدَّقَ بِشَيْءٍ قَطُّ إِلَّا هَذِهِ الزَّكَاةَ الَّتِي يُؤَدِّيهَا الْبَرُّ وَالْفَاجِرُ، قَالَ: سَلْهُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، هَلْ كَتَمْتُهَا، أَوْ أَخَّرْتُهَا - أَوْ قَالَ: مَنَعْتُهَا -؟ قَالَ: لَا، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «دَعْهُ فَلَعَلَّهُ أَنْ يَكُونَ خَيْرًا مِنْكَ»

records.display_matn_en: A man passed by a group, and one of them said: “I hate that man for God's sake.” The others said: “By God, you should not leave that unsubstantiated. Go, so-and-so, and tell him.” The messenger told the man what had been said. The man went to the Prophet ﷺ and said: “So-and-so claims to hate me for God's sake.” The Messenger of God ﷺ sent for the other man and asked: “Why do you hate him?” He replied: “He is my neighbor; I know him better than anyone. By God, I have never seen him perform any prayer except these obligatory prayers that the righteous and the wicked both perform.” The other man said: “Ask him, Messenger of God: Has he ever seen me delay them past their appointed times or perform their ablutions, bowing, or prostrations badly?” He replied: “No.” The accuser continued: “I have never seen him fast a day except during this month, which both the righteous and the wicked fast.” The man said: “Ask him: Has he seen me break any day of it, or treat its rights lightly?” He said: “No.” The accuser continued: “I have never seen him give charity except the obligatory alms that both the righteous and the wicked pay.” The man said: “Ask him: Have I concealed them, delayed them—or,” he said, “withheld them?” He replied: “No.” The Messenger of God ﷺ then said: “Leave him alone; perhaps he is better than you.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar reported from ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd, from Abū Wāʾil, from Muʿādh ibn Jabal, who said: I was traveling with the Messenger of God ﷺ and came close to him as we rode one morning. I asked: “Messenger of God, tell me a deed that will admit me to Paradise and keep me far from the Fire.” He said: “You have asked about something great, yet it is easy for one to whom God makes it easy: worship God without associating anything with Him, establish prayer, give alms, fast Ramadan, and make pilgrimage to the House.” Then he said: “Shall I point you to the gates of goodness? Fasting is a shield, charity extinguishes sin, and a person's prayer in the depth of the night.” He recited the passage from “Their sides forsake their beds” [32:16] through “as reward for what they used to do” [32:17]. Then he asked: “Shall I tell you the head of the matter, its pillar, and the peak of its summit?” I said: “Yes, Messenger of God.” He replied: “The head of the matter is Islam, its pillar is prayer, and the peak of its summit is striving [in God's cause].” Then he asked: “Shall I tell you what controls all of that?” I replied: “Yes, Prophet of God.” He took hold of his tongue and said: “Restrain this.” I asked: “Messenger of God, are we held accountable for what we say?” He answered: “May your mother be bereaved of you, Muʿādh! What else throws people face-down—or he said, on their noses—into the Fire except what their tongues reap?”

records.isnad_ar: أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ عَاصِمِ بْنِ أَبِي النَّجُودِ، عَنْ أَبِي وَائِلٍ، عَنْ مُعَاذِ بْنِ جَبَلٍ، قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: كُنْتُ مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فِي سَفَرٍ، فَأَصْبَحْتُ قَرِيبًا مِنْهُ وَنَحْنُ نَسِيرُ، فَقُلْتُ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، أَلَا تُخْبِرُنِي بِعَمَلٍ يُدْخِلُنِي الْجَنَّةَ، وَيُبَاعِدُنِي مِنَ النَّارِ، قَالَ:   «لَقَدْ سَأَلْتَ عَنْ عَظِيمٍ، وَإِنَّهُ لَيَسِيرٌ عَلَى مَنْ يَسَّرَهُ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ، §تَعْبُدُ اللَّهَ لَا تُشْرِكُ بِهِ شَيْئًا، وَتُقِيمُ الصَّلَاةَ، وَتُؤْتِي الزَّكَاةَ، وَتَصُومُ شَهْرَ رَمَضَانَ، وَتَحُجُّ الْبَيْتَ»   ثُمَّ قَالَ:   «أَدُلُّكَ عَلَى أَبْوَابِ الْخَيْرِ: الصَّوْمُ جُنَّةٌ، وَالصَّدَقَةُ تُطْفِئُ الْخَطِيئَةَ، وَصَلَاةُ الرَّجُلِ مِنْ جَوْفِ اللَّيْلِ، ثُمَّ قَرَأَ:  {تَتَجَافَى جُنُوبُهُمْ عَنِ الْمَضَاجِعِ}   [السجدة: ١٦] - حَتَّى -  {جَزَاءً بِمَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ}   [السجدة: ١٧]  ثُمَّ قَالَ: أَلَا أُخْبِرُكَ بِرَأْسِ الْأَمْرِ وَعَمُودِهِ وَذِرْوَةِ سَنَامِهِ؟»   ، فَقُلْتُ: بَلَى يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، قَالَ: رَأْسُ الْأَمْرِ الْإِسْلَامُ، وَعَمُودُهُ الصَّلَاةُ، وَذِرْوَةُ سَنَامِهِ الْجِهَادُ   «ثُمَّ قَالَ:»   أَلَا أُخْبِرُكَ بِمِلَاكِ ذَلِكَ كُلِّهِ؟   «، قَالَ: قُلْتُ: بَلَى يَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ، فَأَخَذَ بِلِسَانِهِ قَالَ:»   اكْفُفْ عَلَيْكَ هَذَا   «، فَقُلْتُ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، أَوَإِنَّا لَمَأْخُوذُونَ بِمَا نَتَكَلَّمُ؟ قَالَ:»   ثَكِلَتْكَ أُمُّكَ يَا مُعَاذُ، وَهَلْ يُكِبُّ النَّاسَ فِي النَّارِ عَلَى وُجُوهِهِمْ - أَوْ قَالَ: عَلَى مَنَاخِرِهِمْ - إِلَّا حَصَائِدُ أَلْسِنَتِهِمْ "

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar reported from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, from his father, that the Messenger of God ﷺ was asked: “Which deeds are best?” He replied: “The tolerant, upright monotheistic way.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar reported from Layth, who raised the report [to the Prophet ﷺ], saying: God said: “Son of Adam, devote yourself to worshiping Me and I shall fill your heart with sufficiency and close off your poverty. If you do not, I shall fill your heart with preoccupation and not close off your poverty. Son of Adam, for as long as you call upon Me and hope in Me, I shall forgive you whatever has happened. It is incumbent upon Me not to mislead My servant while he asks Me for guidance. I am the Judge.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, who said: Fāṭima al-Khuzāʿiyya—who had met most of the companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ—told me that the Messenger of God ﷺ visited an Anṣārī woman who was ill. He asked: “How do you feel?” She replied: “Well, Messenger of God, except that Umm Mildam”—meaning fever—“has severely afflicted me.” He said: “Be patient, for it removes the impurities of a human being just as a furnace removes the impurities of iron.”

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from Ibn al-Musayyib, from Abū Hurayra, who said the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The believer resembles growing crops, constantly bent by the wind, and the believer continues to be afflicted with trials. The hypocrite resembles a cedar tree, standing erect until it is harvested [cut down].”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar reported from ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd, from Khaythama, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, who said the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “When a servant follows a good practice of worship and then becomes ill, the angel assigned to him is told: ‘Write for him the same deeds as when he was free to act, until I release him [from illness] or take him to Myself.’”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٣٠٨ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ عَاصِمِ بْنِ أَبِي النَّجُودِ، عَنْ خَيْثَمَةَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «إِنَّ §الْعَبْدَ إِذَا كَانَ عَلَى طَرِيقَةٍ حَسَنَةٍ مِنَ الْعِبَادَةِ، ثُمَّ مَرِضَ قِيلَ لِلْمَلَكِ الْمُوَكَّلِ بِهِ: اكْتُبْ لَهُ مِثْلَ عَمَلِهِ إِذْ كَانَ طَلِيقًا حَتَّى أُطْلِقَهُ أَوْ أَكْفِتَهُ إِلَيَّ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: The Prophet ﷺ visited a sick man and said: “Be patient, for it”—meaning fever—“is a purification.” The man replied: “No; it is a raging fever upon an old man that sends him to the graves.” The Prophet ﷺ said: “Yes, then it is so.” The man died.
records.text_ar: ٢٠٣٠٩ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، قَالَ: دَخَلَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عَلَى رَجُلٍ يَعُودُهُ، فَقَالَ:   «§اصْبِرْ فَإِنَّهَا طَهُورٌ»   - يَعْنِي الْحُمَّى -، قَالَ: كَلَّا، بَلْ حُمَّى تَفُورُ، عَلَى شَيْخٍ كَبِيرٍ، تُزِيرُهُ الْقُبُورَ، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «نَعَمْ، فَهُوَ كَذَلِكَ»   فَمَاتَ الرَّجُلُ

records.display_isnad_ar: أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، قَالَ:
records.display_matn_ar: دَخَلَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عَلَى رَجُلٍ يَعُودُهُ، فَقَالَ:   «§اصْبِرْ فَإِنَّهَا طَهُورٌ»   - يَعْنِي الْحُمَّى -، قَالَ: كَلَّا، بَلْ حُمَّى تَفُورُ، عَلَى شَيْخٍ كَبِيرٍ، تُزِيرُهُ الْقُبُورَ، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «نَعَمْ، فَهُوَ كَذَلِكَ»   فَمَاتَ الرَّجُلُ

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar reported from Abū Isḥāq, from al-ʿAyzār ibn Ḥurayth, from ʿUmar ibn Saʿd, from his father, who said the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “How remarkable is the believer! When good befalls him he praises and thanks God; when a calamity befalls him he praises God and bears it patiently. The believer is rewarded in every part of his life, even for the morsel he raises to his wife's mouth.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٣١٠ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنِ الْعَيْزَارِ بْنِ حُرَيْثٍ، عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ سَعْدٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§عَجِبْتُ لِلْمُؤْمِنِ إِنْ أَصَابَهُ خَيْرٌ حَمِدَ اللَّهَ وَشَكَرَ، وَإِنْ أَصَابَتْهُ مُصِيبَةٌ حَمِدَ اللَّهَ وَصَبَرَ، فَالْمُؤْمِنُ يُؤْجَرُ فِي أَمْرِهِ كُلِّهِ حَتَّى يُؤْجَرَ فِي اللُّقْمَةِ يَرْفَعُهَا إِلَى فِي امْرَأَتِهِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwa, from ʿĀʾisha, who said the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “No illness or pain afflicts a believer without being an expiation for his sins, even a thorn that pricks him or a mishap that befalls him.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar reported from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn, from al-Rabāb al-Qushayrī, who said: We entered to visit Abū al-Dardāʾ during an illness. A Bedouin entered and asked: “What is wrong with your governor?”—for Abū al-Dardāʾ was governor at the time. records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, that a healthy-looking Bedouin entered the mosque while the Prophet ﷺ was there. The Messenger of God ﷺ asked: “Have you ever been ill?” He answered: “No.” He asked, pointing to his temples: “Have these two ever throbbed with pain?” He replied: “No.” When he turned to leave, the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever wishes to look at a man among the people of the Fire should look at this one.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٣١٤ - أخبرنا عبد الرزاق قال أخبرنا معمر عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ بَيْنَا هُوَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ إِذْ دَخَلَ عَلَيْهِ أَعْرَابِيٌّ مُصَحَّحٌ - أَوْ قَالَ: ظَاهِرُ الصِّحَّةِ - قَالَ: فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «هَلْ شَكَيْتَ قَطُّ؟»   ، قَالَ: لَا، قَالَ:   «هَلْ ضَرَبَ عَلَيْكَ هَذَانِ قَطُّ؟»   - وَأَشَارَ إِلَى صُدْغَيْهِ - قَالَ: لَا، فَلَمَّا وَلَّى قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§مَنْ سَرَّهُ أَنْ يَنْظُرَ إِلَى رَجُلٍ مِنْ أَهْلِ النَّارِ فَلْيَنْظُرْ إِلَى هَذَا»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Ḥasan, who said: “Fever is from the furnace of Hell, so extinguish it with cold water.” Maʿmar said: It also reached me that on the day of Khaybar the Prophet ﷺ instructed his companions to pour water upon the fever at the end of the night; they had suffered from it, but it no longer harmed them.
records.text_ar: ٢٠٣١٥ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ، قَالَ:   «إِنَّ §الْحُمَّى مِنْ كِيرِ جَهَنَّمَ، فَأَمِيتُوهَا بِالْمَاءِ الْبَارِدِ»   ، قَالَ مَعْمَرٌ: وَبَلَغَنِي أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ أَمَرَ أَصْحَابَهُ يَوْمَ خَيْبَرَ أَنْ يَصُبُّوا عَلَيْهَا الْمَاءَ بِالسَّحَرِ فَلَمْ يَضُرَّهُمْ، وَقَدْ كَانُوا وَجَدُوا مِنْهَا شَيْئًا "

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us: It reached me that Ibn Masʿūd fell ill and appeared distressed by it. He was asked about this and replied: “The matter has come upon me; it is more apt to awaken me and bring me closer [to awareness] than heedlessness.” [The final expression is difficult in the source.]

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar reported from al-Zuhrī, who said: Anas ibn Mālik told me that a Bedouin approached the Messenger of God ﷺ and asked: “Messenger of God, when will the Hour come?” He replied: “What have you prepared for it?” The Bedouin said: “I have prepared no great deed in which to take pride, except that I love God and His messenger ﷺ.” The Prophet ﷺ replied: “You will be with those you love.”

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbayda, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: “There are three things upon which I swear, and a fourth on which, if I swore, I would be truthful: God will not put a person who has a share in Islam on the same footing as one who has none; no servant takes God as his protector in this world but that God will take care of him in the next; and no man loves a people but that he will come with them on the Day of Resurrection. The fourth, on which I could swear, is that God does not conceal a servant's faults in this world without concealing them for him in the next.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٣١٨ - أخبرنا معمر عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنْ أَبِي عُبَيْدَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، قَالَ:   «§ثَلَاثٌ أَحْلِفُ عَلَيْهِنَّ، وَالرَّابِعَةُ لَوْ حَلَفْتُ لَبَرَرْتُ: لَا يَجْعَلُ اللَّهُ مَنْ لَهُ سَهْمٌ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ كَمَنْ لَا سَهْمَ لَهُ، وَلَا يَتَوَلَّى اللَّهَ عَبْدٌ فِي الدُّنْيَا فَوَلَّاهُ غَيْرَهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ، وَلَا يُحِبُّ رَجُلٌ قَوْمًا إِلَّا جَاءَ مَعَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ، وَالرَّابِعَةُ الَّتِي لَوْ حَلَفْتُ عَلَيْهَا لَبَرَرْتُ: لَا يَسْتُرُ اللَّهُ عَلَى عَبْدٍ فِي الدُّنْيَا إِلَّا سَتَرَ عَلَيْهِ فِي الْآخِرَةِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar reported from al-Ashʿath ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: A man passed by the Prophet ﷺ while people were with him, and someone there said: “I love that man for God's sake.” The Prophet ﷺ asked: “Have you told him?” He said: “No.” He replied: “Go and tell him.” He went and told him, and the man replied: “May the One for whose sake you love me love you.” He returned and told the Prophet ﷺ, who replied: “You will be with those you love, and you will receive what you intended [or hoped to obtain].”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٣١٩ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنِ الْأَشْعَثِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، قَالَ: مَرَّ رَجُلٌ بِالنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَعِنْدَهُ نَاسٌ، فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ مِمَّنْ عِنْدَهُ: إِنِّي لَأُحِبُّ هَذَا لِلَّهِ، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «أَعْلَمْتَهُ؟»   ، قَالَ: لَا، قَالَ:   «فَقُمْ إِلَيْهِ فَأَعْلِمْهُ»   ، فَقَامَ إِلَيْهِ فَأَعْلَمَهُ، فَقَالَ: أَحَبَّكَ الَّذِي أَحْبَبْتَنِي لَهُ، قَالَ: ثُمَّ رَجَعَ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَأَخْبَرَهُ بِمَا قَالَ، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§أَنْتَ مَعَ مَنْ أَحْبَبْتَ، وَلَكَ مَا احْتَسَبْتَ»

records.display_matn_ar: مَرَّ رَجُلٌ بِالنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَعِنْدَهُ نَاسٌ، فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ مِمَّنْ عِنْدَهُ: إِنِّي لَأُحِبُّ هَذَا لِلَّهِ، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «أَعْلَمْتَهُ؟»   ، قَالَ: لَا، قَالَ:   «فَقُمْ إِلَيْهِ فَأَعْلِمْهُ»   ، فَقَامَ إِلَيْهِ فَأَعْلَمَهُ، فَقَالَ: أَحَبَّكَ الَّذِي أَحْبَبْتَنِي لَهُ، قَالَ: ثُمَّ رَجَعَ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَأَخْبَرَهُ بِمَا قَالَ، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§أَنْتَ مَعَ مَنْ أَحْبَبْتَ، وَلَكَ مَا احْتَسَبْتَ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Abān, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Three qualities enable a person to taste the sweetness of faith: that God and His messenger ﷺ be dearer to him than anything else, that he love someone solely for God's sake, and that he hate returning to unbelief as he would hate being thrown into the Fire.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٣٢٠ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَبَانَ، عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§ثَلَاثٌ مَنْ كُنَّ فِيهِ وَجَدَ بِهِنَّ حَلَاوَةَ الْإِيمَانِ: مَنْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَحَبَّ إِلَيْهِ مِمَّا سِوَاهُمَا، وَمَنْ يُحِبُّ الْمَرْءَ لَا يُحِبُّهُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ، وَمَنْ يَكْرَهُ أَنْ يَعُودَ إِلَى الْكُفْرِ كَمَا يَكْرَهُ أَنْ يُقْذَفَ بِهِ فِي النَّارِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from someone who heard al-Ḥasan say that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “None of you believes until I am dearer to him than his children, his parents, and all people.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar reported from Qatāda that Salmān said: “An honest merchant will be with the seven under the shade of God's Throne on the Day of Resurrection. The seven are: a just ruler; a man invited to herself by a woman of lineage and beauty who says, ‘I fear God, Lord of the worlds’; one whose eyes overflow when God is mentioned; one whose heart is attached to the mosques out of love for them; one who gives charity so secretly that his right hand nearly hides it from his left; two men who meet and say to one another, ‘I love you for God's sake,’ and ‘I too love you for God's sake,’ and commit themselves to this; and one who has grown up in goodness since boyhood.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٣٢٢ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، أَنَّ سَلْمَانَ، قَالَ:   «§التَّاجِرُ الصَّادِقُ مَعَ السَّبْعَةِ فِي ظِلِّ عَرْشِ اللَّهِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ، وَالسَّبْعَةُ: إِمَامٌ مُقْسِطٌ، وَرَجُلٌ دَعَتْهُ امْرَأَةٌ ذَاتُ حَسَبٍ وَمِيسَمٍ إِلَى نَفْسِهَا فَقَالَ: إِنِّي أَخَافُ اللَّهَ رَبَّ الْعَالَمِينَ، وَرَجُلٌ ذُكِرَ اللَّهُ عِنْدَهُ فَفَاضَتْ عَيْنَاهُ، وَرَجُلٌ قَلْبُهُ مُعَلَّقٌ بِالْمَسَاجِدِ مِنْ حُبِّهِ إِيَّاهَا، وَرَجُلٌ تَصَدَّقَ بَصَدَقَةٍ كَادَتْ يَمِينُهُ تُخْفِي مِنْ شِمَالِهِ، وَرَجُلٌ لَقِيَ أَخَاهُ فَقَالَ: إِنِّي أُحِبُّكَ لِلَّهِ وَقَالَ الْآخَرُ: وَأَنَا أُحِبُّكَ لِلَّهِ حَتَّى تَصَادَرَا عَلَى ذَلِكَ، وَرَجُلٌ نَشَأَ فِي الْخَيْرِ مُنْذُ هُوَ غُلَامٌ»
records.section_title_en: Those Who Love One Another for God

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar reported from Qatāda that Salmān said: “An honest merchant will be with the seven under the shade of God's Throne on the Day of Resurrection. The seven are: a just ruler; a man invited to herself by a woman of lineage and beauty who says, ‘I fear God, Lord of the worlds’; one whose eyes overflow when God is mentioned; one whose heart is attached to the mosques out of love for them; one who gives charity so secretly that his right hand nearly hides it from his left; two men who meet and say to one another, ‘I love you for God's sake,’ and ‘I too love you for God's sake,’ and commit themselves to this; and one who has grown up in goodness since boyhood.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar reported from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: “Part of faith is that a man love his brother only for God and for His sake.”

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from Ibn Abī Ḥusayn, from Shahr ibn Ḥawshab, from Abū Mālik al-Ashʿarī, who said: I was with the Messenger of God ﷺ when the verse was revealed, “O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if made known to you, would distress you” [Quran 5:101]. They said: “Then we shall ask him.” He said: “God has servants who are neither prophets nor martyrs, but whom prophets and martyrs will envy for their nearness and station before God on the Day of Resurrection.” A Bedouin at the edge of the group stood up, brushed [dust] from his face, waved his hands, and said: “Tell us about them, Messenger of God. Who are they?” I saw the Messenger of God's ﷺ face brighten. He said: “They are servants of God from different countries and different clans and tribal groupings. They are not related by kinship ties, nor do they exchange worldly property. They love one another through God's spirit. God makes their faces light and gives them pulpits of pearl before the Merciful One. People will be alarmed, but they will not; people will be afraid, but they will not.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٣٢٤ - أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي حُسَيْنٍ، عَنْ شَهْرِ بْنِ حَوْشَبٍ، عَنْ أَبِي مَالِكٍ الْأَشْعَرِيِّ، قَالَ: كُنْتُ عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَنَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ - [٢٠٢] - الْآيَةُ:  {يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَسْأَلُوا عَنْ أَشْيَاءَ إِنْ تُبْدَ لَكُمْ تَسُؤْكُمْ}   [المائدة: ١٠١]  ، قَالُوا: فَنَحْنُ نَسْأَلُهُ إِذًا، قَالَ:   «إِنَّ §لِلَّهِ عِبَادًا لَيْسُوا بِأَنْبِيَاءَ، وَلَا شُهَدَاءَ يَغْبِطُهُمُ النَّبِيُّونَ وَالشُّهَدَاءُ بِقُرْبِهِمْ وَمَقْعدِهِمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ»   ، قَالَ: وَفِي نَاحِيَةِ الْقَوْمِ أَعْرَابِيُّ، فَقَامَ فَحَثَى عَلَى وَجْهِهِ وَرَمَى بِيَدَيْهِ، ثُمَّ قَالَ: حَدِّثْنَا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عَنْهُمْ مَنْ هُمْ؟ قَالَ: فَرَأَيْتُ وَجْهَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَبْشَرَ، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «هُمْ عِبَادٌ مِنْ عِبَادِ اللَّهِ، مِنْ بُلْدَانٍ شَتَّى، وَقَبَائِلَ شَتَّى مِنْ شُعُوبِ الْقَبَائِلِ، لَمْ يَكُنْ بَيْنَهُمْ أَرْحَامٌ يَتَوَاصَلُونَ بِهَا، وَلَا دُنْيَا يَتَبَاذَلُونَ بِهَا، يَتَحَابُّونَ بِرُوحِ اللَّهِ، يَجْعَلُ اللَّهُ وُجُوهَهُمْ نُورًا، وَيَجْعَلُ لَهُمْ مَنَابِرَ مِنْ لُؤْلُؤٍ قُدَّامَ الرَّحْمَنِ، يَفْزَعُ النَّاسُ وَلَا يَفْزَعُونَ، وَيَخَافُ النَّاسُ وَلَا يَخَافُونَ»

records.raw_text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from Ibn Abī Ḥusayn, from Shahr ibn Ḥawshab, from Abū Mālik al-Ashʿarī, who said: I was with the Messenger of God ﷺ when the verse was revealed, “O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if made known to you, would distress you” [Quran 5:101]. They said: “Then we shall ask him.” He said: “God has servants who are neither prophets nor martyrs, but whom prophets and martyrs will envy for their nearness and station before God on the Day of Resurrection.” A Bedouin at the edge of the group stood up, brushed [dust] from his face, waved his hands, and said: “Tell us about them, Messenger of God. Who are they?” I saw the Messenger of God's ﷺ face brighten. He said: “They are servants of God from different countries and different clans and tribal groupings. They are not related by kinship ties, nor do they exchange worldly property. They love one another through God's spirit. God makes their faces light and gives them pulpits of pearl before the Merciful One. People will be alarmed, but they will not; people will be afraid, but they will not.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar reported from a man of Quraysh, who said: It was asked: “Who are Your people who truly belong to You, Lord?” He replied: “Those who love one another for My sake; when I am mentioned, they are remembered through Me, and when they are mentioned, I am remembered through them. They return to My obedience as a cat returns to its resting place, and when My prohibitions are violated they become angry as a leopard becomes enraged when attacked.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, who said the Messenger of God ﷺ said—though ʿUmar did not raise it [to the Prophet ﷺ] and often used to say—“Whenever two people love one another for God's sake, the one with the greater reward is the one who loves his companion more intensely.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٣٢٦ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ  - وَكَانَ عُمَرُ لَا يَرْفَعُهُ - يَقُولُ: كَثِيرًا يُقَالُ:   «§مَا تَحَابَّ اثْنَانِ فِي اللَّهِ إِلَّا كَانَ أَعْظَمُهُمَا أَجْرًا أشَدَّهُمَا حُبًّا لِصَاحِبِهِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Abān, from Abū Qilāba, who said the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Whoever visits his brother out of affection for him and in order to renew his acquaintance with him, God sends an angel who calls out, ‘You are good, and Paradise has been made good for you.’ God then says: ‘My servant visited him for My spirit [or for My sake], and it is upon Me to entertain him.’”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٣٢٧ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَبَانَ، عَنْ أَبِي قِلَابَةَ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «مَنْ زَارَ أَخَاهُ صُبَابَةً إِلَيْهِ، وَحَدَاثَةِ عَهْدٍ بِهِ، بَعَثَ اللَّهُ مَلَكًا فَنَادَى: طِبْتَ وَطَابَتْ لَكَ الْجَنَّةُ، قَالَ: ثُمَّ يَقُولُ اللَّهُ: §بِرُوحِي زَارَ عَبْدِي، وَعَلَيَّ قِرَاهُ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from someone who heard al-Ḥasan say: “A man set out to visit a brother who lived far away. An angel came to him and asked: ‘Where are you going?’ He replied: ‘I have a brother whom I want to visit.’ The angel asked: ‘Do you have worldly business with one another?’ He said: ‘No.’ ‘Are there kinship ties you are maintaining?’ ‘No.’ ‘A favor you need to tend to?’ ‘No.’ ‘Then why?’ He said: ‘He is a brother whom I love for God's sake.’ The angel said: ‘I am God's messenger to you: God loves you because you love him.’ Then the angel ascended toward heaven while the man watched.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٣٢٨ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَمَّنْ سَمِعَ الْحَسَنَ يَقُولُ:   «§خَرَجَ رَجُلٌ يَزُورُ أَخًا لَهُ، وَكَانَ نَائِيًا عَنْهُ، فَأَتَاهُ مَلَكٌ فَقَالَ: أَيْنَ تُرِيدُ؟ فَقَالَ: أَخٌ لِي أَرَدْتُ أَنْ أَزُورَهُ، فَقَالَ: أَبَيْنَكُمَا دُنْيَا تَعَاطَيَانِهَا؟ قَالَ: لَا، قَالَ: فَرَحِمٌ تَصِلُهَا؟ قَالَ: لَا، قَالَ: فَنِعْمَةٌ تَرُبُّهَا؟ قَالَ: لَا، قَالَ: فَمَاذَا؟ قَالَ: أَخٌ لِي أَحْبَبْتُهُ لِلَّهِ، قَالَ: فَإِنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ إِلَيْكَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّكَ حِينَ أَحْبَبْتَهُ، قَالَ: ثُمَّ عَرَجَ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ وَالرَّجُلُ يَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from a man of Quraysh—returning to the earlier account—who said: God, blessed and exalted, says: “My most beloved servants are those who love one another for My sake, those who maintain My mosques, and those who seek forgiveness before dawn. When I intend punishment for My creation, I remember these people and turn away My punishment from My creation.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٣٢٩ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ رَجُلٍ، مِنْ قُرَيْشٍ - رَجَعَ الْحَدِيثُ - قَالَ:   «يَقُولُ اللَّهُ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى  إِنَّ §أَحَبَّ عِبَادِي إِلَيَّ الَّذِينَ يَتَحَابُّونَ فِيَّ، وَالَّذِينَ يَعْمُرُونَ مَسَاجِدِي، وَالَّذِينَ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ بِالْأَسْحَارِ، فَأُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ إِذَا أَرَدْتُ بِخَلْقِي عَذَابًا ذَكَرْتُهُمْ، فَصَرفْتُ عَذَابِي عَنْ خَلْقِي»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Abū al-Zinād, that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said to Muʿayqīb al-Dawsī: “Come nearer. Were it anyone other than you, he would not sit any closer to me than the length of a spear.” Muʿayqīb was suffering from leprosy.
records.text_ar: ٢٠٣٣٣ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَبِي الزِّنَادِ، أَنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ، قَالَ لمُعَيْقِيبٍ الدَّوْسِيِّ:   «§ادْنُهْ، فَلَوْ كَانَ غَيْرُكَ مَا قَعَدَ مِنِّي إِلَّا كَقِيدِ الرُّمْحِ»   وَكَانَ أَجْذَمَ

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, who said al-Laythī reported: A man with leprosy came to the Prophet ﷺ, apparently asking for something. The Prophet ﷺ neither hurried him away nor distanced him, and said: “There is no contagion [independent of God's decree].” [The bracketed qualification is interpretive; the literal wording is “There is no contagion.”]
records.text_ar: ٢٠٣٣٤ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، قَالَ اللَّيْثِيُّ: إِنَّ رَجُلًا أَجْذَمَ جَاءَ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، وَكَأَنَّهُ جَاءَ سَائِلًا فَلَمْ يُعْجِلْهُ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَلَا بَعَّدَهُ، وَقَالَ:   «§لَا عَدْوَى»

records.text_en: Maʿmar said: It reached me that a man approached Ibn ʿUmar asking for something. Ibn ʿUmar stood, gave him a dirham, and placed it in his hand. Another man had offered to hand the coin over for him, but Ibn ʿUmar refused to allow him to do it.
records.text_ar: ٢٠٣٣٥ - قَالَ مَعْمَرٌ: وَبَلَغَنِي أَنَّ رَجُلًا جَاءَ إِلَى ابْنِ عُمَرَ فَسَأَلَهُ،   «§فَقَامَ ابْنُ عُمَرَ فَأَعْطَاهُ دِرْهَمًا، فَوَضَعَهُ فِي يَدِهِ، وَكَانَ رَجُلٌ قَدْ قَالَ لِابْنِ عُمَرَ حِينَ قَامَ يُعْطِيهِ: أَنَا أُنَاوِلُهُ، فَأَبَى ابْنُ عُمَرَ أَنْ يُنَاوِلَهُ الرَّجُلُ الدِّرْهَمَ»

records.text_en: Abū Yaʿqūb Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbbād told us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar reported from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Mughīra, from his father, who said: I came to a man addressing a group and sat with him. He said: The Messenger of God ﷺ was described to me while I was at Minā on the way to ʿArafāt. I hurried my mount from group to group until I saw a party of riders. I passed ahead of them and recognized him by the description. As I approached the riders, someone said: “Move out of the riders' way!” The Messenger of God ﷺ replied: “Leave him; he has a need.” I seized the reins—or the halter—and said: “Messenger of God, tell me an action that will bring me nearer to Paradise and farther from the Fire.” He asked: “Are those the two things you seek?” I said: “Yes.” He said: “Establish prayer, give the prescribed alms, make pilgrimage to the House, fast Ramadan, love for others what you would love to be given yourself, and dislike for them what you would dislike being done to you. Now move out of the riders' way.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٣٣٦ - حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو يَعْقُوبَ إِسْحَاقُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ عَبَّادٍ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدِ الرَّزَّاقِ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنِ الْمُغِيِرَةِ، - [٢٠٦] - عَنْ أَبِيهِ، قَالَ: انْتَهَيْتُ إِلَى رَجُلٍ يُحَدِّثُ قَوْمًا فَجَلَسْتُ إِلَيْهِ، فَقَالَ: وُصِفَ لِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَأَنَا بِمِنًى غَادِيًا إِلَى عَرَفَاتٍ، فَجَعَلْتُ أُسْرِفُ بِالرِّكَابِ، كُلَّمَا دُفِعْتُ إِلَى جَمَاعَةٍ انْدَفَعْتُ إِلَيْهِمْ، حَتَّى رَأَيْتُ جَمَاعَةً مِنْ رَكْبٍ فَانْطَلَقْتُ فَقَدَمْتُهُمْ، ثُمَّ تَذَكَّرْتُ فَعَرَفْتُهُ بِالصِّفَةِ، ثُمَّ تَقَدَّمْتُ بَيْنَ يَدَيِ الرِّكَابِ، فَلَمَّا دَنَوْتُ، قَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ: خَلِّ عَنْ وُجُوهِ الرِّكَابِ يَا عَبْدَ اللَّهِ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «دَعُوهُ فَأَرَبٌ مَا لَهُ»   ، فَأَخَذْتُ بِالزِّمَامِ - أَوْ قَالَ: بِالْخِطَامِ - فَقُلْتُ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، حَدِّثْنِي بِعَمَلٍ يُقَرِّبُنِي إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ وَيُبَاعِدُنِي مِنَ النَّارِ، قَالَ:   «أَوَهُمَا عَمَلُكَ؟»   ، قَالَ: قُلْتُ: نَعَمْ، قَالَ:   «§تُقِيمُ الصَّلَاةَ، وَتُؤْتِي الزَّكَاةَ، وَتَحُجُّ الْبَيْتَ، وَتَصُومُ رَمَضَانَ، وَتُحِبُّ لِلنَّاسِ مَا تُحِبُّ أَنْ يُؤْتَى إِلَيْكَ، وَتَكْرَهُ لَهُمْ مَا تَكْرَهُ أَنْ يُؤْتَى إِلَيْكَ، خَلِّ عَنْ وُجُوهِ الرِّكَابِ»

records.matn_ar: انْتَهَيْتُ إِلَى رَجُلٍ يُحَدِّثُ قَوْمًا فَجَلَسْتُ إِلَيْهِ، فَقَالَ: وُصِفَ لِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَأَنَا بِمِنًى غَادِيًا إِلَى عَرَفَاتٍ، فَجَعَلْتُ أُسْرِفُ بِالرِّكَابِ، كُلَّمَا دُفِعْتُ إِلَى جَمَاعَةٍ انْدَفَعْتُ إِلَيْهِمْ، حَتَّى رَأَيْتُ جَمَاعَةً مِنْ رَكْبٍ فَانْطَلَقْتُ فَقَدَمْتُهُمْ، ثُمَّ تَذَكَّرْتُ فَعَرَفْتُهُ بِالصِّفَةِ، ثُمَّ تَقَدَّمْتُ بَيْنَ يَدَيِ الرِّكَابِ، فَلَمَّا دَنَوْتُ، قَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ: خَلِّ عَنْ وُجُوهِ الرِّكَابِ يَا عَبْدَ اللَّهِ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «دَعُوهُ فَأَرَبٌ مَا لَهُ»   ، فَأَخَذْتُ بِالزِّمَامِ - أَوْ قَالَ: بِالْخِطَامِ - فَقُلْتُ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، حَدِّثْنِي بِعَمَلٍ يُقَرِّبُنِي إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ وَيُبَاعِدُنِي مِنَ النَّارِ، قَالَ:   «أَوَهُمَا عَمَلُكَ؟»   ، قَالَ: قُلْتُ: نَعَمْ، قَالَ:   «§تُقِيمُ الصَّلَاةَ، وَتُؤْتِي الزَّكَاةَ، وَتَحُجُّ الْبَيْتَ، وَتَصُومُ رَمَضَانَ، وَتُحِبُّ لِلنَّاسِ مَا تُحِبُّ أَنْ يُؤْتَى إِلَيْكَ، وَتَكْرَهُ لَهُمْ مَا تَكْرَهُ أَنْ يُؤْتَى إِلَيْكَ، خَلِّ عَنْ وُجُوهِ الرِّكَابِ»
records.isnad_en: Abū Yaʿqūb Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbbād told us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar reported from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Mughīra, from his father, who said:
records.matn_en: I came to a man addressing a group and sat with him. He said: The Messenger of God ﷺ was described to me while I was at Minā on the way to ʿArafāt. I hurried my mount from group to group until I saw a party of riders. I passed ahead of them and recognized him by the description. As I approached the riders, someone said: “Move out of the riders' way!” The Messenger of God ﷺ replied: “Leave him; he has a need.” I seized the reins—or the halter—and said: “Messenger of God, tell me an action that will bring me nearer to Paradise and farther from the Fire.” He asked: “Are those the two things you seek?” I said: “Yes.” He said: “Establish prayer, give the prescribed alms, make pilgrimage to the House, fast Ramadan, love for others what you would love to be given yourself, and dislike for them what you would dislike being done to you. Now move out of the riders' way.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from someone who heard al-Ḥasan say: “Moses asked his Lord for a principle that gathered together what is good. He replied: ‘Treat people as you would love Me to treat you.’”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٣٣٧ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَمَّنْ، سَمِعَ الْحَسَنَ، يَقُولُ:   «إِنَّ مُوسَى سَأَلَ رَبَّهُ جِمَاعًا مِنَ الْخَيْرِ، فَقَالَ لَهُ: §اصْحَبِ النَّاسَ بِمَا تُحِبُّ أَنْ أَصْحَبَكَ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: Maʿmar reported from Qatāda, who said: Whenever the Prophet ﷺ saw the new crescent, he magnified God three times, pronounced His oneness, then said three times: “A crescent of goodness and sound guidance.” He then said three times: “I believe in the One who created you.” Then he said: “Praise belongs to God, who has taken away the month of such-and-such and brought in the month of such-and-such.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, who said: I was informed from Ibn al-Musayyib that when the Prophet ﷺ saw the new crescent, he said: “I believe in the One who created you, fashioned you, and made you proportionate.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, who said: A man told me that a man related his own experience: “While I was traveling I saw the new crescent, and heard a speaker I could not see saying: ‘O God, cause it to rise over us with safety and submission, security and faith, righteousness and piety, in a manner You love and approve.’ He kept repeating it until I had memorized it.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٣٤٠ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنِي رَجُلٌ، أَنَّ رَجُلًا، أَخْبَرَهُ هُوَ نَفْسُهُ، قَالَ: بَيْنَمَا أَنَا أَسِيرُ رَأَيْتُ الْهِلَالَ فَسَمِعْتُ قَائِلًا يَقُولُ وَلَا أَرَاهُ:   «§اللَّهُمَّ أَطْلِعْهُ عَلَيْنَا بِالسَّلَامَةِ وَالْإِسْلَامِ، وَالْأَمْنِ وَالْإِيمَانِ، وَالْبِرِّ وَالتَّقْوَى كَمَا تُحِبُّ وَتَرْضَى»   ، فَمَا زَالَ يُرَدِّدُهَا حَتَّى حَفِظْتُهَا

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: Maʿmar reported from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn, who said: Ibn ʿUmar was asked about *al-ukhdha* [a form of magical binding or affliction]. He said: “I consider it nothing but magic.” Someone said: “It can cause a person to be unable to pass stool or urine.” He replied: “It is a binding.” [The term *lifāf* in the response is obscure in this context.]
records.text_ar: ٢٠٣٤١ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ قال: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنِ ابْنِ سِيرِينَ، قَالَ: سُئِلَ ابْنُ عُمَرَ عَنِ §الْأُخْذَةِ، فَقَالَ:   «مَا أُرَاهُ إِلَّا سِحْرًا»   قَالَ: فَقِيلَ: فَإِنَّهَا تَأْخُذُ الْغَائِطَ وَالْبَوْلَ، قَالَ:   «لِفَافٌ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilāba, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ cut an amulet from the necklace of a boy”—meaning al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās. The narrator explained that it was something fastened around a child's neck to ward off the evil eye.
records.text_ar: ٢٠٣٤٢ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ أَبِي قِلَابَةَ، قَالَ:   «§قَطَعَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ التَّمِيمَةَ مِنْ قِلَادَةِ الصَّبِيِّ»   يَعْنِي الْفَضْلَ بْنَ عَبَّاسٍ، قَالَ: وَهِيَ الَّتِي تُخْرَزُ فِي عُنُقِ الصَّبِيِّ مِنَ الْعَيْنِ

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Jazarī, from Ziyād ibn Abī Maryam—or Abū ʿUbayda, Maʿmar was uncertain—who said: Ibn Masʿūd saw beads on his wife's neck which she had hung there to ward off an affliction of redness. He cut them off and said: “The family of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd has no need of associating partners with God.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Ḥasan, that ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn saw a man with a brass ring on his hand. He asked: “What is that on your hand?” The man said: “I made it to remedy weakness.” ʿImrān replied: “It only increases your weakness.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٣٤٤ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ، أَنَّ عِمْرَانَ بْنَ الْحُصَيْنِ، نَظَرَ إِلَى رَجُلٍ فِي يَدِهِ فَتَخٌ مِنْ صُفْرٍ، فَقَالَ:   «مَا هَذَا فِي يَدِكَ؟»   ، قَالَ: صَنَعْتُهُ مِنَ الْوَاهِنَةِ، فَقَالَ عِمْرَانُ:   «§فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَزِيدُكَ إِلَّا وَهْنًا»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn, that the companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ, including Abū Bakr, stayed among the people of a watering place. Al-Nuʿaymān began drawing lines [for divination]—or practicing soothsaying—telling the people that such-and-such would happen. They brought him food and milk, which he sent to his companions. Someone told Abū Bakr: “Do you know where this food comes from? Al-Nuʿaymān obtains it by drawing lines—or by soothsaying.” Abū Bakr said: “So I have been eating from al-Nuʿaymān's soothsaying all day!” He put his hand down his throat and vomited it up.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: Maʿmar reported from al-Zuhrī, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, who said: The Prophet ﷺ was asked about soothsayers and said: “They are nothing.” It was said: “But they sometimes tell us things that turn out to be true.” He replied: “That is a truthful word snatched by a jinn, who throws it into the ear of his ally, and then adds a hundred lies.”

records.display_matn_ar: سُئِلَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عَنِ §الْكُهَّانِ، فَقَالَ:   «لَيْسُوا بِشَيْءٍ»   ، فَقِيلَ لَهُ: إِنَّهُمْ يُخْبرُونَا بِأَشْيَاءَ تَكُونُ حَقًّا؟ قَالَ:   «تِلْكَ كَلِمَةُ حَقٍّ يَخْطَفُهَا الْجِنِّيُّ فَيَقْذِفُهَا فِي أُذُنِ وَلِيِّهِ، فَيَزِيدُ فِيهَا مِائَةَ كَذْبَةٍ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, that Ibn Masʿūd said: “Whoever goes to a soothsayer, questions him, and believes what he says has disbelieved in what was revealed to Muḥammad ﷺ.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, that Kaʿb said: “God said: ‘One who practices magic, or has magic performed for him, or practices soothsaying, or has it practiced for him, or interprets omens, or has omens interpreted for him, is not among My servants. My servants are those who believe in Me and place their trust in Me.’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from unnamed transmitters, that a woman came to ʿĀʾisha and asked: “May I bind my camel?” ʿĀʾisha answered: “Bind your camel.” The woman said: “I am afraid about my husband.” ʿĀʾisha said: “Remove this sorceress from my presence,” and they put her out. [The term “bind” appears to be a euphemism for magical binding, as indicated by the woman's second statement.]

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: Maʿmar reported from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn, from Abū Hurayra, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “Near the end of time, a believer's dream will hardly be false. Those who are most truthful in speech will have the truest dreams. Dreams are of three kinds: a good dream, which is glad tidings from God; a dream concerning things a person has been thinking about; and a dream that brings sorrow from Satan. If any of you sees a dream he dislikes, let him not tell it to anyone, but rise and pray.” Abū Hurayra said: “I like the shackle [seen in a dream], but dislike the iron collar. The shackle signifies firmness in religion.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٣٥٢ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنِ ابْنِ سِيرِينَ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ:   «§فِي آخِرِ الزَّمَانِ لَا تَكَادُ رُؤْيَا الْمُؤْمِنِ تَكْذِبُ، وَأَصْدَقُهُمْ رُؤْيَا أَصْدَقُهُمْ حَدِيثًا، وَالرُّؤْيَا ثَلَاثٌ: الرُّؤْيَا الْحَسَنَةُ بُشْرَى مِنَ اللَّهِ، وَالرُّؤْيَا يُحَدِّثُ بِهَا الرَّجُلُ نَفْسَهُ، وَالرُّؤْيَا تَحْزِينٌ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ، فَإِذَا رَأَى أَحَدُكُمْ رُؤْيَا يَكْرَهُهَا فَلَا يُحَدِّثْ بِهَا أَحَدًا وَلْيَقُمْ فَلْيُصَلِّ»   ، قَالَ أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ:   «يُعْجِبُنِي الْقَيْدُ وَأَكْرَهُ الْغُلَّ، الْقَيْدُ ثَبَاتٌ فِي الدِّينِ»

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: وَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§رُؤْيَا الْمُؤْمِنِ جُزْءٌ مِنْ سِتَّةٍ وَأَرْبَعِينَ جُزْءًا مِنَ النُّبُوَّةِ»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: The Prophet ﷺ also said: “A believer’s dream is one of forty-six parts of prophecy.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Abū Salama, who said: I used to suffer greatly from dreams, though not to the point of being wrapped up [with illness], until Abū Qatāda told me that he heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “A vision comes from God, and a distressing dream comes from Satan. When one of you dreams something he dislikes, let him spit lightly to his left three times and seek refuge from Satan; then it will not harm him.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilāba, who said the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “A dream comes to pass according to its interpretation. It resembles a person who has raised his foot and waits to put it down. When any of you sees a dream, let him tell it only to a sincere adviser or someone knowledgeable.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Ibn al-Musayyib, from Abū Hurayra, who said the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “A believer's dream is one of forty-six parts of prophecy.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, who said: ʿUmar wrote to Abū Mūsā: “As for what follows, I have been commanding you according to what the Quran commands and forbidding you according to what Muḥammad ﷺ forbade, instructing you to follow understanding and customary practice and to study the Arabic language. When one of you sees a dream and tells it to his brother, let him say: ‘Good for us and evil for our enemies.’”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٣٥٦ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، قَالَ: كَتَبَ عُمَرُ إِلَى أَبِي مُوسَى:   «أَمَّا بَعْدُ، فَإِنِّي §كُنْتُ آمُرُكُمْ بِمَا أمَرَكَمْ بِهِ الْقُرْآنُ، وَأَنْهَاكُمْ عَمَّا نَهَاكُمْ عَنْهُ مُحَمَّدٌ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، وَآمُرُكُمْ بِاتِّبَاعِ الْفِقْهِ وَالسُّنَّةِ، وَالتَّفَهُّمِ فِي الْعَرَبِيَّةِ، فَإِذَا رَأَى أَحَدُكُمْ رُؤْيَا فَقَصَّهَا عَلَى أَخِيهِ، فَلْيَقُلْ: خَيْرٌ لَنَا وَشَرٌّ لِأَعْدَائِنَا»

records.text_en: Maʿmar informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAmr ibn ʿĀṣim, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: “The dream of a believer is one of seventy parts of prophecy. This fire of yours is one of seventy parts of the fire of Hell; and the scorching wind from which God created the jinn is one of seventy parts of the heat of Hell.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar reported from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Budayl had a dream and told it to Abū Bakr. He replied: “If your dream is true, you will be killed in a matter shrouded in confusion.” He was killed on the day of Ṣiffīn.
records.text_ar: ٢٠٣٥٨ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنِ ابْنِ سِيرِينَ، قَالَ: رَأَى عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ بُدَيْلٍ رُؤْيَا فَقَصَّهَا عَلَى أَبِي بَكْرٍ فَقَالَ:   «§إِنْ صَدَقَتْ رُؤْيَاكَ، فَإِنَّكَ سَتُقْتَلُ فِي أَمْرٍ ذِي لَبْسٍ»   ، فَقُتِلَ يَوْمَ صِفِّينَ

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from a man who heard Ibrāhīm say: “When one of you sees a dream he dislikes, let him say: ‘I seek refuge in what God's angels and messengers have sought refuge in, from the evil of my dream tonight, lest it harm me in my religion or my worldly life, O Merciful One.’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd God ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Abū Hurayra: A man came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and said: “Last night I dreamed of a canopy from which butter and honey were dripping. I saw people catching it in their hands, some taking much and others little. I saw a rope extending from heaven to earth. I saw you take hold of it and rise; then another man took hold and rose, and a third man took hold and rose, then a fourth took hold but it broke with him, and then it was joined for him and he rose.” Abū Bakr said: “Messenger of God, may my father and mother be your ransom! Please let me interpret it.” He said: “Interpret it.” Abū Bakr said: “The canopy represents Islam. The dripping butter and honey are the Quran, its softness and sweetness; those who gathered much or little are those who take much or little of the Quran. The rope extending from heaven to earth is the truth upon which you stand: you take hold of it and God raises you. After you, another man takes hold and rises, then another man rises, then another whose rope breaks but is joined for him and he rises.” Abū Bakr asked: “Messenger of God, tell me: was I right or wrong?” He replied: “You were right about some things and wrong about others.” Abū Bakr said: “I adjure you, Messenger of God, tell me where I was wrong.” He replied: “Do not swear an oath.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٣٦٠ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، أَنَّ رَجُلًا أَتَى رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَقَالَ: إِنِّي أَرَى اللَّيْلَةَ الظُّلَّةَ يُنْطَفُ مِنْهَا السَّمْنُ وَالْعَسَلُ، فَأَرَى النَّاسَ يَتَكَفَّفُونَ مِنْهَا بِأَيْدِيهِمْ، فَالْمُسْتَكْثِرُ وَالْمُسْتَقِلُّ، وَأَرَى سَبَبًا وَاصِلًا مِنَ السَّمَاءِ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ، فَأَرَاكَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَخَذْتَ بِهِ فَعَلَوْتَ، ثُمَّ أَخَذَ بِهِ رَجُلٌ آخَرُ فَعَلَا، ثُمَّ أَخَذَ بِهِ رَجُلٌ آخَرُ فَعَلَا، ثُمَّ أَخَذَ بِهِ رَجُلٌ آخَرُ فَانْقَطَعَ بِهِ، ثُمَّ وُصِلَ لَهُ فَعَلَا بِهِ، فَقَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، بِأَبِي أَنْتَ وَأُمِّي، وَاللَّهِ لَتَدَعَنِّي فَلَأَعْبُرَنَّهَا، فَقَالَ:   «§اعْبُرْهَا»   فَقَالَ: أَمَّا الظُّلَّةُ فَظُلَّةُ الْإِسْلَامُ، وَأَمَّا مَا يُنْطَفُ مِنَ السَّمْنِ وَالْعَسَلِ فَهُوَ الْقُرْآنُ لِينُهُ وَحَلَاوَتُهُ، وَأَمَّا الْمُسْتَكْثِرُ وَالْمُسْتَقِلُّ فَهُوَ الْمُسْتَكْثِرُ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ، وَالْمُسْتَقِلُّ مِنْهُ، وَأَمَّا السَّبَبُ الْوَاصِلُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ فَهُوَ الْحَقُّ الَّذِي أَنْتَ عَلَيْهِ، تَأْخُذُ بِهِ - [٢١٥] - فَيُعْلِيكَ اللَّهُ، ثُمَّ يَأْخُذُ بِهِ رَجُلٌ آخَرُ بَعْدَكَ فَيَعْلُو بِهِ، ثُمَّ يَأْخُذُ بِهِ رَجُلٌ آخَرُ بَعْدَهُ فَيَعْلُو بِهِ، ثُمَّ يَأْخُذُ بِهِ رَجُلٌ آخَرُ فَيَنْقَطِعُ بِهِ، ثُمَّ يُوصَلُ لَهُ فَيَعْلُو بِهِ، أَيْ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، لَتُحَدِّثْنِي أَصَبْتُ أَمْ أَخْطَأْتُ؟ قَالَ:   «أَصَبْتَ بَعْضًا، وَأَخْطَأْتَ بَعْضًا»   قَالَ: أَقْسَمْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، لَتُخْبِرَنِّي بِالَّذِي أَخْطَأْتُ قَالَ:   «لَا تُقْسِمْ»

records.matn_en: A man came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and said: “Last night I dreamed of a canopy from which butter and honey were dripping. I saw people catching it in their hands, some taking much and others little. I saw a rope extending from heaven to earth. I saw you take hold of it and rise; then another man took hold and rose, and a third man took hold and rose, then a fourth took hold but it broke with him, and then it was joined for him and he rose.” Abū Bakr said: “Messenger of God, may my father and mother be your ransom! Please let me interpret it.” He said: “Interpret it.” Abū Bakr said: “The canopy represents Islam. The dripping butter and honey are the Quran, its softness and sweetness; those who gathered much or little are those who take much or little of the Quran. The rope extending from heaven to earth is the truth upon which you stand: you take hold of it and God raises you. After you, another man takes hold and rises, then another man rises, then another whose rope breaks but is joined for him and he rises.” Abū Bakr asked: “Messenger of God, tell me: was I right or wrong?” He replied: “You were right about some things and wrong about others.” Abū Bakr said: “I adjure you, Messenger of God, tell me where I was wrong.” He replied: “Do not swear an oath.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, who said: A man came to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and said: “I dreamed that the earth grew green, then became barren, then green, then barren.” ʿUmar said: “You are a man who will believe, then disbelieve, then believe, then disbelieve, and die an unbeliever.” The man said: “I saw nothing [of the sort]!” ʿUmar replied, quoting Quran 12:41: “The matter about which you asked has been decided. What was decreed for Joseph's fellow prisoner has been decreed for you.”
