records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn: “ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥa, Kaʿb ibn Mālik and Ḥassān ibn Thābit came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, ‘Messenger of God, why not command ʿAlī to answer those who lampoon you?’ They meant Abū Sufyān ibn al-Ḥārith, Ibn al-Zibaʿrā and al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil. The Prophet ﷺ replied: ‘ʿAlī is not suited to that, but when people defend their Prophet with their swords, they are still more entitled to defend him with their tongues.’ Ḥassān said: ‘I needed nothing further than this in defending you. By God, I would not exchange it for power of speech across all the land from Buṣrā to Ṣanʿāʾ.’ Then he recited: ‘My tongue is a sharp sword without a flaw, and my sea cannot be muddied by buckets.’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, who said that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “It would be better for a man's belly to be filled with pus than to be filled with poetry. If you hear someone reciting it, throw dust in his face.” Maʿmar added: “Yet I heard both al-Zuhrī and Qatāda reciting poetry, whereas al-Ḥasan did not do that.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father: “The Messenger of God ﷺ was traveling when one of the Emigrants dismounted and chanted rajaz verse at the others: ‘Neither a mudd nor half a mudd has nourished her; neither a few dates nor a loaf. Rather, the milk of autumn has nourished her: buttermilk, sour milk and fresh milk. Rather, the cracked colocynth nourished her, and a thin drink like the edge of a rough garment; she spends the night between a pen and a latrine.’” The Prophet ﷺ feared that trouble might arise between the men, so he instructed both to mount their animals. Maʿmar added: “Abū Ḥamza al-Thumālī related a similar account, adding that the Prophet ﷺ turned his she-camel around and ordered both men to mount.” [Some expressions in the transmitted poem are uncertain.]
records.text_ar: ٢٠٥٠٥ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، قَالَ: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فِي سَفَرٍ، فَنَزَلَ رَجُلٌ مِنَ الْمُهَاجِرِينَ فَرَجَزَ بِهِمْ، فَقَالَ: [البحر الرجز] لَمْ يَغْذُهَا مُدٌّ وَلَا نَصِيفُ ... وَلَا تُمَيْرَاتٌ وَلَا رَغِيفُ لَكِنْ غَذَاهَا اللَّبَنُ الْخَرِيفُ ... الْمَخْضُ والْقَارِصُ وَالصَّرِيفُ لَكِنْ غَذَاهَا الْحَنْظَلُ النَّقِيفُ ... وَمِذْقَةٌ كَطُرَّةِ الْخَنِيفِ تَبِيتُ بَيْنَ الزَّرْبِ وَالْكَنِيفِ قَالَ:   «§فَخَافَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَنْ يَكُونَ بَيْنَهُمَا شَرٌّ، فَأَمَرَهُمَا فَرَكِبَا»   ، وَحَدَّثَنِي أَبُو حَمْزَةَ الثُّمَالِيُّ بِنَحْوِ حَدِيثِ هِشَامٍ وَزَادَ فِيهِ: أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عَطَفَ نَاقَتَهُ وَأَمَرَهُمَا فَرَكِبَا

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī: “We heard that ʿĀʾisha used to challenge anyone who claimed that Abū Bakr composed poetry: ‘By God, he never composed a line of poetry, whether before Islam or after it. records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Jaḥshī, from Abū Bakr ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr, from one of his teachers: “ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was told, ‘A young man of such-and-such a clan is a poet.’ ʿUmar asked him, ‘What do you say?’ He recited: ‘I bid Salmā farewell when I prepare to go on campaign; gray hair and Islam suffice to restrain a man.’ ʿUmar replied, ‘You have spoken truthfully.’”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٥٠٨ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ الْجَحْشِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو، عَنْ بَعْضِ أَشْيَاخِهِ، أَنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ، قِيلَ لَهُ: هَذَا §غُلَامُ بَنِي فُلَانٍ شَاعِرٌ، قَالَ: فَقَالَ لَهُ:   «كَيْفَ تَقُولُ؟»   قَالَ: [البحر الطويل] أُوَدِّعُ سَلْمَى إِنْ تَجَهَّزْتُ غَازِيًا ... كَفَى الشَّيْبُ وَالْإِسْلَامُ لِلْمَرْءِ نَاهِيَا، قَالَ عُمَرُ:   «صَدَقْتَ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Ibn al-Musayyib: “Ḥassān recited poetry in the mosque. ʿUmar passed him and gave him a disapproving look, saying, ‘In the mosque? In the mosque?’ Ḥassān replied, ‘By God, I recited it here in the company of one better than you.’ Fearing that Ḥassān would invoke the Messenger of God ﷺ against him, ʿUmar let him continue and left.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Qatāda: “When Iblīs was cast down, he asked, ‘My Lord, You have cursed him; what is his occupation?’ He said, ‘Sorcery.’ He asked, ‘What is his recitation?’ He said, ‘Poetry.’ ‘What is his scripture?’ ‘Tattooing.’ ‘What is his food?’ ‘Every carcass and whatever is slaughtered without God's name being mentioned.’ ‘What is his drink?’ ‘Every intoxicant.’ ‘Where is his residence?’ ‘The bathhouse.’ ‘Where is his place of assembly?’ ‘The markets.’ ‘What is his voice?’ ‘The flute.’ ‘What are his traps?’ ‘Women.’” [The dialogue's pronouns are presented as in the source.]

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Qatāda: “A man said to the Prophet ﷺ: ‘I love beautiful things, even in the straps of my sandals and the loop of my whip. Do you fear I have arrogance?’ The Prophet ﷺ asked, ‘How do you find your heart?’ He replied, ‘Recognizing the truth and at peace with it.’ The Prophet ﷺ said, ‘That is not arrogance. Arrogance is looking down on people and rejecting the truth.’”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٥١٢ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَر، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، أَنَّ رَجُلًا قَالَ لِلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ  إِنِّي لَأُحِبُّ الْجَمَالَ حَتَّى إِنِّي لَأُحِبُّهُ فِي شِرَاكِ نَعْلِي وَعَلَاقَةِ سَوْطِي، فَهَلْ تَخْشَى عَلَيَّ الْكِبْرَ؟ فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «فَكَيْفَ تَجِدُ قَلْبَكَ؟»   ، قَالَ: عَارِفًا لِلْحَقِّ مُطْمَئِنًّا إِلَيْهِ، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «لَيْسَ الْكِبْرُ هُنَالِكَ، وَلَكِنَّ §الْكِبْرَ أَنْ تَغْمِطَ النَّاسَ، وَتَبْطَرَ الْحَقَّ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ al-Jushamī, from his father: “The Messenger of God ﷺ saw me in shabby clothing and asked, ‘Do you have wealth?’ I said, ‘Yes.’ He asked, ‘Of what sort?’ I replied, ‘God has given me every kind, including sheep and camels.’ He said, ‘Then let God's favor and generosity toward you be seen.’ He asked, ‘Are your camels born with their ears intact?’ I replied, ‘Are they born any other way?’—I had not yet embraced Islam at the time. He said, ‘But perhaps you take your knife and cut the ear of one, saying: This one is set free [baḥīra]; and slit the ear of another, saying: This one is dedicated [ṣurum].’ I said, ‘Yes.’ He replied, ‘Do not do that. Whatever property God has given you is lawful to you. God's knife is sharper and God's arm stronger.’ I said, ‘Muḥammad, suppose I pass a man and he neither entertains me nor grants me hospitality, then he later passes by me: should I entertain him or treat him as he treated me?’ The Prophet ﷺ answered, ‘Rather, entertain him.’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn: “The people were alarmed during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ, but Abū Qatāda was slow to respond. The Prophet ﷺ asked him, ‘What held you back?’ He replied, ‘My hair—I was combing it.’ The Prophet ﷺ ordered his head to be shaved. Abū Qatāda said, ‘Messenger of God, leave it to me—or grant me this—for by God I will make amends to your satisfaction.’ He let him keep it. When they encountered the enemy, Abū Qatāda was the first to charge and killed Masʿada. I know of no polytheist who was harder upon the Muslims than he was.”

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn: “The people were alarmed during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ, but Abū Qatāda was slow to respond. The Prophet ﷺ asked him, ‘What held you back?’ He replied, ‘My hair—I was combing it.’ The Prophet ﷺ ordered his head to be shaved. Abū Qatāda said, ‘Messenger of God, leave it to me—or grant me this—for by God I will make amends to your satisfaction.’ He let him keep it. When they encountered the enemy, Abū Qatāda was the first to charge and killed Masʿada. I know of no polytheist who was harder upon the Muslims than he was.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd God ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtba: “When the Prophet ﷺ reached Medina, he found the People of the Book letting their hair hang down without a part, whereas the polytheists parted theirs. When he was uncertain about a matter on which no command had been given, he followed the People of the Book. Accordingly he let his hair hang down, but afterward was commanded to part it. He parted it; parting was the later of the two practices.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Zayd ibn Aslam, that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ asked the Messenger of God ﷺ: “Is it arrogant of me to bring my companions home and feed them?” He replied, “No.” “Is it arrogant for one of us to have a riding animal?” “No.” “Is it arrogant for one of us to have a suit of fine clothing?” “No. Rather, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, arrogance is treating the truth as foolish and despising people.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٥٢٠ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، أَنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عَمْرِو بْنِ الْعَاصِ، قَالَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، أَمِنَ الْكِبْرِ أَنْ أسْتَتْبِعَ أَصْحَابِي إِلَى بَيْتِي فَأُطْعِمَهُمْ؟ قَالَ:   «لَا»   ، قَالَ: أَفَمِنَ الْكِبْرِ أَنْ يَكُونَ لِأَحَدِنَا رَاحِلَةٌ يَرْكَبُهَا؟ قَالَ:   «لَا»   ، قَالَ: أَفَمِنَ الْكِبْرِ أَنْ يَكُونَ لِأَحَدِنَا حُلَّةٌ يَلْبَسُهَا؟ قَالَ:   «لَا، وَلَكِنَّ §الْكِبْرَ يَا عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عَمْرٍو أَنْ تُسَفِّهَ الْحَقَّ، وَتَغْمِطَ النَّاسَ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, who said that Ayyūb related to him from al-Ḥasan: “A man praised another man excessively in the Prophet's ﷺ presence. The Prophet ﷺ said, ‘You have broken his neck! If he heard you say this, he would never prosper.’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Nāfiʿ or another person: “A man said to Ibn ʿUmar, ‘O best of people, son of the best of people!’ He said, ‘I am not the best of people. I am merely one of God's servants who hopes in Him and fears Him. By God, you will continue praising a man until you destroy him.’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd God ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Do not exaggerate in praising me as Christians exaggerated in praising Jesus son of Mary. records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Layth, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās: “I declare no one to be pure except the Prophet ﷺ.”

records.text_en: Maʿmar said: Yaḥyā ibn Abī Rabīʿa al-Ṣanʿānī told us that he heard ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ recite: “There were in the city nine men who spread corruption in the land and did not reform” (Quran 27:48). He explained: “They used to clip coins [fraudulently shave silver dirhams].”

records.text_en: Maʿmar reported from al-Zuhrī that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The guest's right to hospitality lasts three days. Whatever is given beyond that is charity.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٥٢٧ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ:   «§حَقُّ الضِّيَافَةِ ثَلَاثَةُ أَيَّامٍ، فَمَا زَادَ عَلَى ذَلِكَ فَهُوَ صَدَقَةٌ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-ʿAyzār: “Some Bedouins came to Ibn ʿAbbās and said, ‘We perform prayer, give the alms, make pilgrimage to the House, and fast during Ramadan, but certain Emigrants say that we count for nothing.’ Ibn ʿAbbās replied, ‘Whoever performs prayer, gives alms, makes pilgrimage to the House, fasts during Ramadan and entertains guests will enter Paradise.’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, from Abū Hurayra, from the Prophet ﷺ: “The Angel of Death was sent to Moses. When he came to him, Moses struck him and knocked out his eye. The angel returned to his Lord and said, ‘You sent me to a servant who does not wish to die.’ God restored his eye and said, ‘Return and tell him to place his hand upon the back of an ox. For every hair his hand covers he shall have a year.’ Moses asked, ‘Lord, and after that?’ He replied, ‘Then death.’ Moses said, ‘Then now.’ He asked God to bring him within a stone's throw of the Holy Land. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘If I were there, I could show you his grave beside the road, beneath the red sandhill.’”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٥٣٠ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ طَاوُسٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ:   «أُرْسِلَ مَلَكُ الْمَوْتِ إِلَى مُوسَى، فَلَمَّا جَاءَهُ صَكَّهُ فَفَقَأَ عَيْنَهُ، فَرَجَعَ إِلَى رَبِّهِ، فَقَالَ: أَرْسَلْتَنِي إِلَى عَبْدٍ لَا يُرِيدُ الْمَوْتَ، قَالَ: فَرَدَّ اللَّهُ عَيْنَهُ، فَقَالَ: §ارْجِعْ إِلَيْهِ فَقُلْ لَهُ: يَضَعُ يَدَهُ عَلَى مَتْنِ ثَوْرٍ فَلَهُ مَا غَطَّتْ يَدُهُ بِكُلِّ شَعْرَةٍ سَنَةٌ، فَقَالَ: أَيْ رَبِّ، ثُمَّ مَهْ؟ قَالَ: ثُمَّ الْمَوْتُ، قَالَ: فَالْآنَ، فَسَأَلَ اللَّهَ أَنْ يُدْنِيَهُ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ الْمُقَدَّسَةِ رَمْيَةً بِحَجَرٍ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ  لَوْ كُنْتُ ثَمَّ لَأَرْيتُكُمْ قَبْرَهُ إِلَى جَنْبِ الطَّرِيقِ تَحْتَ الْكَثِيبِ الْأَحْمَرِ»   .

records.display_matn_ar: أُرْسِلَ مَلَكُ الْمَوْتِ إِلَى مُوسَى، فَلَمَّا جَاءَهُ صَكَّهُ فَفَقَأَ عَيْنَهُ، فَرَجَعَ إِلَى رَبِّهِ، فَقَالَ: أَرْسَلْتَنِي إِلَى عَبْدٍ لَا يُرِيدُ الْمَوْتَ، قَالَ: فَرَدَّ اللَّهُ عَيْنَهُ، فَقَالَ: §ارْجِعْ إِلَيْهِ فَقُلْ لَهُ: يَضَعُ يَدَهُ عَلَى مَتْنِ ثَوْرٍ فَلَهُ مَا غَطَّتْ يَدُهُ بِكُلِّ شَعْرَةٍ سَنَةٌ، فَقَالَ: أَيْ رَبِّ، ثُمَّ مَهْ؟ قَالَ: ثُمَّ الْمَوْتُ، قَالَ: فَالْآنَ، فَسَأَلَ اللَّهَ أَنْ يُدْنِيَهُ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ الْمُقَدَّسَةِ رَمْيَةً بِحَجَرٍ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ  لَوْ كُنْتُ ثَمَّ لَأَرْيتُكُمْ قَبْرَهُ إِلَى جَنْبِ الطَّرِيقِ تَحْتَ الْكَثِيبِ الْأَحْمَرِ»   .
records.display_isnad_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, from Abū Hurayra, from the Prophet ﷺ: “
records.display_matn_en: The Angel of Death was sent to Moses. When he came to him, Moses struck him and knocked out his eye. The angel returned to his Lord and said, ‘You sent me to a servant who does not wish to die.’ God restored his eye and said, ‘Return and tell him to place his hand upon the back of an ox. For every hair his hand covers he shall have a year.’ Moses asked, ‘Lord, and after that?’ He replied, ‘Then death.’ Moses said, ‘Then now.’ He asked God to bring him within a stone's throw of the Holy Land. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘If I were there, I could show you his grave beside the road, beneath the red sandhill.’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilāba: “When God cursed Iblīs, Iblīs asked to be granted respite and was granted it. records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, who said that Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh and Abū Bakr ibn Sulaymān informed him that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ led us one night in the night prayer near the end of his life. After concluding he rose and said, ‘Consider this night of yours: after one hundred years from it, not a single person now living on the face of the earth will remain.’” Ibn ʿUmar said: “The people misunderstood this saying in their discussion of reports about one hundred years. The Prophet ﷺ meant that none of those living on the earth today would remain—meaning that generation would come to an end.”

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, who said that Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh and Abū Bakr ibn Sulaymān informed him that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ led us one night in the night prayer near the end of his life. After concluding he rose and said, ‘Consider this night of yours: after one hundred years from it, not a single person now living on the face of the earth will remain.’” Ibn ʿUmar said: “The people misunderstood this saying in their discussion of reports about one hundred years. The Prophet ﷺ meant that none of those living on the earth today would remain—meaning that generation would come to an end.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Thābit and Qatāda, from Anas: “Some Companions of the Prophet ﷺ looked for water for ablution and could find none. The Prophet ﷺ asked, ‘Is there any water here?’ I saw him place his hand in a vessel that held water and say, ‘Perform ablution in God's name.’ Water gushed from between his fingers while the people performed ablution, until the last of them had finished.” Thābit asked Anas, “How many were there, in your estimation?” He replied, “About seventy men.”

records.text_en: Maʿmar reported from ʿAwf, from Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī, from ʿImrān ibn al-Ḥuṣayn: “The Messenger of God ﷺ and his Companions were on a journey and suffered severe thirst. He sent two men of his Companions—ʿAlī and al-Zubayr, or someone else—saying, ‘You will find a woman in a certain place with a camel carrying two water skins. Bring her here.’ They found her riding between the two skins and told her to come to the Messenger of God ﷺ. She asked, ‘Who is the Messenger of God? That man who has left his religion?’ They replied, ‘That is the man you mean, and he truly is God's Messenger.’ They brought her to him. He ordered some water taken from her two skins into a vessel, said what God willed him to say, and returned the water to the two skins. He had their mouths opened and ordered the people to fill their vessels and water skins. Not a single vessel or water skin was left unfilled. ʿImrān said: ‘It seemed to me that her two skins only became fuller.’ The Prophet ﷺ ordered her cloth spread out and asked his Companions to bring some of their travel provisions, filling it for her. He told her, ‘Go. We have taken nothing from your water; rather, God has given us drink.’ She returned to her people and told them, ‘I have come from the greatest sorcerer of people—or else he really is God's Messenger.’ Her whole clan came and embraced Islam.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٥٣٧ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ عَوْفٍ، عَنْ أَبِي رَجَاءٍ الْعُطَارِدِيِّ، عَنْ عِمْرَانَ بْنِ الْحُصَيْنِ، قَالَ: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فِي سَفَرٍ هُوَ وَأَصْحَابُهُ فَأَصَابَهُمْ عَطَشٌ شَدِيدٌ، فَأَرْسَلَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ رَجُلَيْنِ مِنْ أَصْحَابِهِ - عَلِيٌّ وَالزُّبَيْرُ أَوْ غَيْرُهُمَا - فَقَالَ:   «§إِنَّكُمَا سَتَجِدَانِ امْرَأَةً فِي مَكَانِ كَذَا وَكَذَا مَعَهَا بَعِيرٌ عَلَيْهِ مَزَادَتَانِ، فَأْتِيَا بِهَا»   ، فَأَتَيَا الْمَرْأَةَ، فَوجَدَاهَا قَدْ رَكِبَتْ بين مزادتيها عَلَى الْبَعِيرِ، فَقَالَا لَهَا: أَجِيبِي رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، فَقَالَتْ: مَنْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ؟ أَهَذَا الصَّابِئُ؟ قَالَا: هَذَا الَّذِي تَعْنِينَ وَهُوَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ حَقًّا، فَجَاءَا بِهَا، فَأَمَرَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَجَعَلَ فِي إِنَاءٍ مِنْ مُزَادَتَيْهَا شَيْئًا، ثُمَّ قَالَ مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ أَنْ يَقُولَ، ثُمَّ أَعَادَ الْمَاءَ فِي الْمَزَادَتَيْنِ، ثُمَّ أَمَرَ بِعُرَى الْمَزَادَتَيْنِ فَفُتِحَتْ، ثُمَّ أَمَرَ النَّاسَ فَمَلَئُوا آنِيَتَهُمْ وَأسْقِيتَهُمْ، فَلَمْ يَدَعُوا إِنَاءً وَلَا سِقَاءً إِلَّا مَلَئُوهُ، فَقَالَ عِمْرَانُ: فَكَانَ يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيَّ أَنَّهُمَا لَمْ يَزْدَادَا إِلَّا امْتِلَاءً، قَالَ: فَأَمَرَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ بِثَوْبِهَا فَبُسِطَ، ثُمَّ أَصْحَابَهُ، فَجَاءُوا مِنْ أَزْوَادِهِمْ حَتَّى مَلَأَ لَهَا ثَوْبَهَا، ثُمَّ قَالَ:   «اذْهَبِي فَإِنَّا لَمْ نَأْخُذْ مِنْ مَائِكَ شَيْئًا، - [٢٧٨] - وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ سَقَانَا»   ، فَجَاءَتْ أَهْلَهَا، فَأَخْبَرَتْهُمْ، فَقَالَتْ: جِئْتُكُمْ مِنْ عِنْدِ أَسْحَرَ النَّاسِ، أَوْ إِنَّهُ لِرَسُولُ اللَّهِ حَقًّا، قَالَ: فَجَاءَ أَهْلُ ذَلِكَ الْحَيِّ فَأَسْلَمُوا كُلُّهُمْ

records.raw_text_en: Maʿmar reported from ʿAwf, from Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī, from ʿImrān ibn al-Ḥuṣayn: “The Messenger of God ﷺ and his Companions were on a journey and suffered severe thirst. He sent two men of his Companions—ʿAlī and al-Zubayr, or someone else—saying, ‘You will find a woman in a certain place with a camel carrying two water skins. Bring her here.’ They found her riding between the two skins and told her to come to the Messenger of God ﷺ. She asked, ‘Who is the Messenger of God? That man who has left his religion?’ They replied, ‘That is the man you mean, and he truly is God's Messenger.’ They brought her to him. He ordered some water taken from her two skins into a vessel, said what God willed him to say, and returned the water to the two skins. He had their mouths opened and ordered the people to fill their vessels and water skins. Not a single vessel or water skin was left unfilled. ʿImrān said: ‘It seemed to me that her two skins only became fuller.’ The Prophet ﷺ ordered her cloth spread out and asked his Companions to bring some of their travel provisions, filling it for her. He told her, ‘Go. We have taken nothing from your water; rather, God has given us drink.’ She returned to her people and told them, ‘I have come from the greatest sorcerer of people—or else he really is God's Messenger.’ Her whole clan came and embraced Islam.”

records.display_matn_en: The Messenger of God ﷺ and his Companions were on a journey and suffered severe thirst. He sent two men of his Companions—ʿAlī and al-Zubayr, or someone else—saying, ‘You will find a woman in a certain place with a camel carrying two water skins. Bring her here.’ They found her riding between the two skins and told her to come to the Messenger of God ﷺ. She asked, ‘Who is the Messenger of God? That man who has left his religion?’ They replied, ‘That is the man you mean, and he truly is God's Messenger.’ They brought her to him. He ordered some water taken from her two skins into a vessel, said what God willed him to say, and returned the water to the two skins. He had their mouths opened and ordered the people to fill their vessels and water skins. Not a single vessel or water skin was left unfilled. ʿImrān said: ‘It seemed to me that her two skins only became fuller.’ The Prophet ﷺ ordered her cloth spread out and asked his Companions to bring some of their travel provisions, filling it for her. He told her, ‘Go. We have taken nothing from your water; rather, God has given us drink.’ She returned to her people and told them, ‘I have come from the greatest sorcerer of people—or else he really is God's Messenger.’ Her whole clan came and embraced Islam.”

records.text_en: Maʿmar reported from Qatāda, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rabāḥ, from Abū Qatāda: “We were traveling with the Prophet ﷺ when he began to tilt—or sway—on his mount. I supported him with my hand until he awoke, and when he swayed again I supported him again. He said, ‘O God, protect Abū Qatāda as he protected me tonight. I believe we have put you to hardship. Move off the road.’ We moved aside and made our mounts kneel. The Messenger of God ﷺ lay down, and each of us used his camel's foreleg as a pillow. We did not wake until the sun had risen; it was the cry of a shrike that awakened us. We said, ‘Messenger of God, we are ruined.’ He replied, ‘You are not ruined. Prayer is not missed by someone asleep; it is missed by someone awake.’ He asked whether anyone had water. I brought him an ablution vessel, a leather water container. He relieved himself, then came and performed ablution, returned it to me and said, ‘Keep this; there may be something remarkable in what remains.’ He ordered Bilāl to call the prayer, prayed two cycles, moved from that place, then instructed him to give the commencement call, and led us in the dawn prayer. The army went on. The Prophet ﷺ said, ‘Had they obeyed Abū Bakr and ʿUmar they would have spared themselves hardship; by disobeying them they brought hardship on themselves.’ Abū Bakr and ʿUmar had advised the soldiers not to stop before reaching water, while the others insisted on stopping until the Messenger of God ﷺ caught up. We reached them at the height of noon and they were nearly overcome with thirst. He asked me for the water container, and I brought it. He tucked it beneath his arm and poured water for them, saying, ‘Drink and perform ablution.’ They did so and filled every vessel they had, until he kept asking, ‘Is anyone still thirsty?’ Then he handed it back to me, and it appeared to contain as much as when he took it. They were seventy-two men.”

أَوْ قَالَ: مَادَ - عَنِ الرَّاحِلَةِ، قَالَ: فَدَعَمْتُهُ بِيَدِي حَتَّى اسْتَيْقَظَ، ثُمَّ مَالَ فَدَعَمْتُهُ بِيَدِي حَتَّى اسْتَيْقَظَ، فَقَالَ:   «اللَّهُمَّ احْفَظْ أَبَا قَتَادَةَ كَمَا حَفِظَنِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةَ، مَا أَرَانَا إِلَّا قَدْ شَقَقْنَا عَلَيْكَ، تَنَحَّ عَنِ الطَّرِيقِ»   قَالَ: فَتَنَحَّى عَنِ الطَّرِيقِ، فَأَنَاخَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، وَأَنَخْنَا مَعَهُ، فَتَوَسَّدَ كُلٌّ مِنَّا ذِرَاعَ رَاحِلَتِهِ، فَمَا اسْتيقَظَنَا حَتَّى أَشْرَقَتِ الشَّمْسُ وَمَا اسْتيقَظَنَا إِلَّا بِصَوْتِ الصُّرَدِ فَقُلْنَا: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، هَلَكْنَا، فَقَالَ:   «لَمْ تَهْلِكُوا، إِنَّ الصَّلَاةَ لَا تَفُوتُ النَّائِمَ، إِنَّمَا تَفُوتُ الْيَقْظَانَ»   ثُمَّ قَالَ:   «هَلْ مِنْ مَاءٍ فَأَتَيْتُهُ بِمِيضَأَةٍ - وَهِيَ الْإِدَوَاةُ - قَالَ أَبُو قَتَادَةَ: فَقَضَى حَاجَتَهُ، ثُمَّ جَاءَنِي فَتَوَضَّأَ، ثُمَّ دَفَعَهَا إِلَيَّ، - [٢٧٩] - ثُمَّ قَالَ لِي:»   احْفَظْهَا لَعَلَّهُ أَنْ يَكُونَ لِبَقِيَّتِهَا نَبَأٌ   «قَالَ: فَأَمَرَ بِلَالًا، فَنَادَى وَصَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ، ثُمَّ تَحَوَّلَ مِنْ مَكَانِهِ ذَلِكَ، فَأَمَرَهُ فَأَقَامَ فَصَلَّى بِنَا الصُّبْحَ، قَالَ: ثُمَّ سَارَ الْجَيْشُ، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ»   إِنْ يُطِيعُوا أَبَا بَكْرٍ، وَعُمَرَ يَرْفُقُوا بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ، وَإِنْ يَعْصُوهُمَا يَشُقُّوا عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ   «، قَالَ: وَكَانَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ، وَعُمَرُ أشَارَا عَلَيْهِمْ أَلَّا يَنْزِلُوا حَتَّى يَبْلُغُوا الْمَاءَ، وَقَالَ بَقِيَّةُ النَّاسِ: بَلْ نَنْزِلُ حَتَّى يَأْتِيَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، فَنَزَلُوا فَجِئْنَاهُمْ فِي نَحْرِ الظَّهِيرَةِ وَقَدْ هَلَكُوا مِنَ الْعَطَشِ، قَالَ: فَدَعَانِي بِالْمِيضَأَةِ، فَأَتَيْتُهُ بِهَا فَاسْتَأْبَطَهَا، ثُمَّ جَعَلَ يَصُبُّ لَهُمْ، ثُمَّ قَالَ:»   §اشْرَبُوا وَتَوَضَّئُوا   «فَفَعَلُوا وَمَلَئُوا كُلَّ إِنَاءٍ كَانَ مَعَهُمْ، حَتَّى جَعَلَ يَقُولُ:»   هَلْ مِنْ عَالٍّ " ثُمَّ رَدَّهَا إِلَيَّ، فَيُخَيَّلُ إِلَيَّ أَنَّهَا كَمَا أَخَذَهَا مِنِّي، وَكَانُوا اثْنَيْنِ وَسَبْعِينَ رَجُلًا

أَوْ قَالَ: مَادَ - عَنِ الرَّاحِلَةِ، قَالَ: فَدَعَمْتُهُ بِيَدِي حَتَّى اسْتَيْقَظَ، ثُمَّ مَالَ فَدَعَمْتُهُ بِيَدِي حَتَّى اسْتَيْقَظَ، فَقَالَ:   «اللَّهُمَّ احْفَظْ أَبَا قَتَادَةَ كَمَا حَفِظَنِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةَ، مَا أَرَانَا إِلَّا قَدْ شَقَقْنَا عَلَيْكَ، تَنَحَّ عَنِ الطَّرِيقِ»   قَالَ: فَتَنَحَّى عَنِ الطَّرِيقِ، فَأَنَاخَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، وَأَنَخْنَا مَعَهُ، فَتَوَسَّدَ كُلٌّ مِنَّا ذِرَاعَ رَاحِلَتِهِ، فَمَا اسْتيقَظَنَا حَتَّى أَشْرَقَتِ الشَّمْسُ وَمَا اسْتيقَظَنَا إِلَّا بِصَوْتِ الصُّرَدِ فَقُلْنَا: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، هَلَكْنَا، فَقَالَ:   «لَمْ تَهْلِكُوا، إِنَّ الصَّلَاةَ لَا تَفُوتُ النَّائِمَ، إِنَّمَا تَفُوتُ الْيَقْظَانَ»   ثُمَّ قَالَ:   «هَلْ مِنْ مَاءٍ فَأَتَيْتُهُ بِمِيضَأَةٍ - records.raw_text_en: Maʿmar reported from Qatāda, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rabāḥ, from Abū Qatāda: “We were traveling with the Prophet ﷺ when he began to tilt—or sway—on his mount. I supported him with my hand until he awoke, and when he swayed again I supported him again. He said, ‘O God, protect Abū Qatāda as he protected me tonight. I believe we have put you to hardship. Move off the road.’ We moved aside and made our mounts kneel. The Messenger of God ﷺ lay down, and each of us used his camel's foreleg as a pillow. We did not wake until the sun had risen; it was the cry of a shrike that awakened us. We said, ‘Messenger of God, we are ruined.’ He replied, ‘You are not ruined. Prayer is not missed by someone asleep; it is missed by someone awake.’ He asked whether anyone had water. I brought him an ablution vessel, a leather water container. He relieved himself, then came and performed ablution, returned it to me and said, ‘Keep this; there may be something remarkable in what remains.’ He ordered Bilāl to call the prayer, prayed two cycles, moved from that place, then instructed him to give the commencement call, and led us in the dawn prayer. The army went on. The Prophet ﷺ said, ‘Had they obeyed Abū Bakr and ʿUmar they would have spared themselves hardship; by disobeying them they brought hardship on themselves.’ Abū Bakr and ʿUmar had advised the soldiers not to stop before reaching water, while the others insisted on stopping until the Messenger of God ﷺ caught up. We reached them at the height of noon and they were nearly overcome with thirst. He asked me for the water container, and I brought it. He tucked it beneath his arm and poured water for them, saying, ‘Drink and perform ablution.’ They did so and filled every vessel they had, until he kept asking, ‘Is anyone still thirsty?’ Then he handed it back to me, and it appeared to contain as much as when he took it. They were seventy-two men.”

records.display_matn_ar: كُنَّا مَعَ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فِي بَعْضِ أَسْفَارِهِ إِذْ مَالَ - أَوْ قَالَ: مَادَ - عَنِ الرَّاحِلَةِ، قَالَ: فَدَعَمْتُهُ بِيَدِي حَتَّى اسْتَيْقَظَ، ثُمَّ مَالَ فَدَعَمْتُهُ بِيَدِي حَتَّى اسْتَيْقَظَ، فَقَالَ:   «اللَّهُمَّ احْفَظْ أَبَا قَتَادَةَ كَمَا حَفِظَنِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةَ، مَا أَرَانَا إِلَّا قَدْ شَقَقْنَا عَلَيْكَ، تَنَحَّ عَنِ الطَّرِيقِ»   قَالَ: فَتَنَحَّى عَنِ الطَّرِيقِ، فَأَنَاخَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، وَأَنَخْنَا مَعَهُ، فَتَوَسَّدَ كُلٌّ مِنَّا ذِرَاعَ رَاحِلَتِهِ، فَمَا اسْتيقَظَنَا حَتَّى أَشْرَقَتِ الشَّمْسُ وَمَا اسْتيقَظَنَا إِلَّا بِصَوْتِ الصُّرَدِ فَقُلْنَا: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، هَلَكْنَا، فَقَالَ:   «لَمْ تَهْلِكُوا، إِنَّ الصَّلَاةَ لَا تَفُوتُ النَّائِمَ، إِنَّمَا تَفُوتُ الْيَقْظَانَ»   ثُمَّ قَالَ:   «هَلْ مِنْ مَاءٍ فَأَتَيْتُهُ بِمِيضَأَةٍ - وَهِيَ الْإِدَوَاةُ - قَالَ أَبُو قَتَادَةَ: فَقَضَى حَاجَتَهُ، ثُمَّ جَاءَنِي فَتَوَضَّأَ، ثُمَّ دَفَعَهَا إِلَيَّ، ثُمَّ قَالَ لِي:»   احْفَظْهَا لَعَلَّهُ أَنْ يَكُونَ لِبَقِيَّتِهَا نَبَأٌ   «قَالَ: فَأَمَرَ بِلَالًا، فَنَادَى وَصَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ، ثُمَّ تَحَوَّلَ مِنْ مَكَانِهِ ذَلِكَ، فَأَمَرَهُ فَأَقَامَ فَصَلَّى بِنَا الصُّبْحَ، قَالَ: ثُمَّ سَارَ الْجَيْشُ، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ»   إِنْ يُطِيعُوا أَبَا بَكْرٍ، وَعُمَرَ يَرْفُقُوا بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ، وَإِنْ يَعْصُوهُمَا يَشُقُّوا عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ   «، قَالَ: وَكَانَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ، وَعُمَرُ أشَارَا عَلَيْهِمْ أَلَّا يَنْزِلُوا حَتَّى يَبْلُغُوا الْمَاءَ، وَقَالَ بَقِيَّةُ النَّاسِ: بَلْ نَنْزِلُ حَتَّى يَأْتِيَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، فَنَزَلُوا فَجِئْنَاهُمْ فِي نَحْرِ الظَّهِيرَةِ وَقَدْ هَلَكُوا مِنَ الْعَطَشِ، قَالَ: فَدَعَانِي بِالْمِيضَأَةِ، فَأَتَيْتُهُ بِهَا فَاسْتَأْبَطَهَا، ثُمَّ جَعَلَ يَصُبُّ لَهُمْ، ثُمَّ قَالَ:»   §اشْرَبُوا وَتَوَضَّئُوا   «فَفَعَلُوا وَمَلَئُوا كُلَّ إِنَاءٍ كَانَ مَعَهُمْ، حَتَّى جَعَلَ يَقُولُ:»   هَلْ مِنْ عَالٍّ " ثُمَّ رَدَّهَا إِلَيَّ، فَيُخَيَّلُ إِلَيَّ أَنَّهَا كَمَا أَخَذَهَا مِنِّي، وَكَانُوا اثْنَيْنِ وَسَبْعِينَ رَجُلًا
records.display_isnad_en: Maʿmar reported from Qatāda, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rabāḥ, from Abū Qatāda: “
records.display_matn_en: We were traveling with the Prophet ﷺ when he began to tilt—or sway—on his mount. I supported him with my hand until he awoke, and when he swayed again I supported him again. He said, ‘O God, protect Abū Qatāda as he protected me tonight. I believe we have put you to hardship. Move off the road.’ We moved aside and made our mounts kneel. The Messenger of God ﷺ lay down, and each of us used his camel's foreleg as a pillow. We did not wake until the sun had risen; it was the cry of a shrike that awakened us. We said, ‘Messenger of God, we are ruined.’ He replied, ‘You are not ruined. Prayer is not missed by someone asleep; it is missed by someone awake.’ He asked whether anyone had water. I brought him an ablution vessel, a leather water container. He relieved himself, then came and performed ablution, returned it to me and said, ‘Keep this; there may be something remarkable in what remains.’ He ordered Bilāl to call the prayer, prayed two cycles, moved from that place, then instructed him to give the commencement call, and led us in the dawn prayer. The army went on. The Prophet ﷺ said, ‘Had they obeyed Abū Bakr and ʿUmar they would have spared themselves hardship; by disobeying them they brought hardship on themselves.’ Abū Bakr and ʿUmar had advised the soldiers not to stop before reaching water, while the others insisted on stopping until the Messenger of God ﷺ caught up. We reached them at the height of noon and they were nearly overcome with thirst. He asked me for the water container, and I brought it. He tucked it beneath his arm and poured water for them, saying, ‘Drink and perform ablution.’ They did so and filled every vessel they had, until he kept asking, ‘Is anyone still thirsty?’ Then he handed it back to me, and it appeared to contain as much as when he took it. They were seventy-two men.”

records.text_en: Maʿmar reported from Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Jaḥshī, who said that their elders told them: “ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh came to the Prophet ﷺ at Uḥud after losing his sword. The Prophet ﷺ gave him a date-palm stalk, which became a sword in his hand.”

records.text_en: Maʿmar reported from Thābit, from Anas: “Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr and another man of the Helpers spoke with the Messenger of God ﷺ about some need of theirs until part of a very dark night had passed. They left him to return home, each carrying a small staff. One man's staff shone and lit their way as they walked. When their roads divided, the other man's staff also shone; each traveled by the light of his own staff until he reached his family.”

But when he returned home and threw the remainder to his family, they counted it and found it equal to the full sum he had received.”

records.text_en: Maʿmar reported from Qatāda: “Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr and a companion traveled by night in darkness, when the tip of one man's whip suddenly gave light. His companion said, ‘If we told people of this, they would call us liars.’ Muṭarrif answered, ‘The denier is more false,’ meaning that someone who denies God's favor is the greater liar.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Jaḥshī, from Ibn al-Munkadir: “Safīna, the freedman of the Messenger of God ﷺ, became separated from the army in Roman territory—or was taken captive—and escaped in search of the army. He came upon a lion and said to it, ‘Abū al-Ḥārith, I am the freedman of the Messenger of God ﷺ, and this is my predicament.’ The lion approached him, moving its tail, and stood beside him. Whenever it heard a sound, it went toward it and then returned to walk beside him. It continued accompanying him until he reached the army, whereupon it returned.”

records.display_matn_en: Safīna, the freedman of the Messenger of God ﷺ, became separated from the army in Roman territory—or was taken captive—and escaped in search of the army. He came upon a lion and said to it, ‘Abū al-Ḥārith, I am the freedman of the Messenger of God ﷺ, and this is my predicament.’ The lion approached him, moving its tail, and stood beside him. Whenever it heard a sound, it went toward it and then returned to walk beside him. It continued accompanying him until he reached the army, whereupon it returned.”

records.display_matn_ar: كُنْتُ أَمْشِي مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فِي حَقٍّ لِبَعْضِ أَهْلِ الْمَدِينَةِ، فَقَالَ:   «يَا أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ، هَلَكَ الْمُكْثِرُونَ إِلَّا مَنْ قَالَ: كَذَا وَكَذَا، وَهَكَذَا وَهَكَذَا، وَقَلِيلٌ مَا هُمْ»   ، ثُمَّ مَشَى سَاعَةً، ثُمَّ قَالَ:   «يَا أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ، §أَلَا أَدُلُّكَ عَلَى كَنْزٍ مِنْ كُنُوزِ الْجَنَّةِ؟»   ، فَقُلْتُ: بَلَى يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، قَالَ:   «تَقُولُ: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ الْعَلِيِّ الْعَظِيمِ، وَلَا مَلْجَأَ مِنَ اللَّهِ إِلَّا إِلَيْهِ»   ، قَالَ: ثُمَّ مَشَى سَاعَةً فَقَالَ:   «يَا أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ، هَلْ تَدْرِي مَا حَقُّ اللَّهِ عَلَى النَّاسِ، وَمَا حَقُّ النَّاسِ عَلَى اللَّهِ؟»   ، قَالَ: قُلْتُ: اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَعْلَمُ قَالَ:   «حَقُّ اللَّهِ عَلَى النَّاسِ أَنْ يَعْبُدُوهُ وَلَا يُشْرِكُوا بِهِ شَيْئًا، فَإِذَا فَعَلُوا ذَلِكَ فَحَقٌّ عَلَى اللَّهِ أَنْ لَا يُعَذِّبَهُمْ»
records.display_isnad_en: Maʿmar reported from Abū Isḥāq, from Kuhayl ibn Ziyād, from Abū Hurayra: “
records.display_matn_en: I walked with the Messenger of God ﷺ in a walled garden belonging to some of the people of Medina. He said, ‘Abū Hurayra, those with abundant wealth are ruined—except those who give it away in this direction and that direction, and how few they are.’ After a while he asked, ‘Shall I direct you to a treasure from the treasures of Paradise?’ I said, ‘Yes, Messenger of God.’ He said, ‘Say: There is no power or strength except through God, the Most High, the Magnificent, and there is no refuge from God except with Him.’ After walking a while he asked, ‘Do you know God's right over people and people's right upon God?’ I said, ‘God and His Messenger know best.’ He replied, ‘God's right over people is that they worship Him without associating anything with Him. Once they do that, their right upon God is that He not punish them.’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Hammām, who heard Abū Hurayra say that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “A woman entered the Fire because of a female cat—or a male cat—she had tied up. She neither fed it nor released it to gnaw at the small creatures of the earth, until it died of starvation.”

records.text_en: Maʿmar reported from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn, from Abū al-Daylam, from Muʿādh ibn Jabal: “When death came upon him, we said, ‘It appears that your time has come. Give us your counsel.’ He replied, ‘I too believe my time has come, and this is a terrible moment for lies. Know that whoever dies certain of three things—that God is his Lord, that the Hour is coming without doubt, and that God will raise those in the graves—’ Ibn Sīrīn was uncertain whether he said, ‘will enter Paradise’ or ‘will escape the Fire.’”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٥٥٢ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنِ ابْنِ سِيرِينَ، عَنْ أَبِي الدَّيْلَمِ، عَنْ مُعَاذِ بْنِ جَبَلٍ، قَالَ: حَضَرَهُ الْمَوْتُ، فَقُلْنَا لَهُ: لَا نَرَاكَ إِلَّا قَدْ حُضِرْتَ، فَأَوْصِنَا، قَالَ:   «فَأَنَا لَا أُرَانِي إِلَّا قَدْ حُضِرْتُ وَسَاءَ حِينُ الْكَذِبِ هَذَا، اعْلَمُوا أَنَّهُ §مَنْ مَاتَ وَهُوَ يُوقِنُ بِثَلَاثٍ: بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ رَبُّهُ، وَأَنَّ السَّاعَةَ آتِيَةٌ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهَا، وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ يَبْعَثُ مَنْ فِي الْقُبُورِ - قَالَ ابْنُ سِيرِينَ: فَإِمَّا قَالَ: - يَدْخُلُ الْجَنَّةَ، وَإِمَّا قَالَ: يَنْجُو مِنَ النَّارِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Qatāda: “Ibn ʿUmar was asked about the words ‘There is no god but God’: Does a person's conduct do no harm alongside this declaration, just as no conduct avails one without it? He said, ‘Provide your evening meal, but do not be deceived.’” [A terse metaphor in the transmitted answer.]

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī: “When the Messenger ﷺ died, some of his Companions were nearly overwhelmed with troubled thoughts; ʿUthmān was among them. ʿUmar passed by him, greeted him and received no reply, so he complained to Abū Bakr. Abū Bakr said, ‘Come with me to him.’ They approached and greeted ʿUthmān, and he answered. Abū Bakr asked, ‘What happened? Your brother greeted you earlier and you did not answer.’ ʿUthmān said, ‘I did not do that.’ ʿUmar retorted, ‘You did! But that is the pride of you Umayyads.’ Abū Bakr said, ‘You did, but something must have occupied you.’ ʿUthmān explained, ‘I was remembering the Messenger of God ﷺ and that God took him before we could ask about the means of salvation in this matter.’ Abū Bakr said, ‘I did ask him about that.’ ʿUthmān replied, ‘May my father and mother be sacrificed for you! You were the one most entitled to do so.’ Abū Bakr said: ‘I asked, “Messenger of God, what is the salvation for this matter in which we find ourselves?” He replied, “Whoever accepts the word that I offered my uncle, which he rejected, will find salvation in it.”’”

records.text_en: Maʿmar reported from Qatāda, from Abū al-Naḍr, from Anas, who said that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “God Almighty promised me that four hundred thousand of my community would enter Paradise.” Abū Bakr asked, “Grant us more, Messenger of God!” The Prophet ﷺ cupped his hands together and said, “And this much.” Abū Bakr again asked for more; the Prophet ﷺ repeated the gesture. ʿUmar said, “Enough, Abū Bakr.” Abū Bakr replied, “Leave me alone, ʿUmar! What would it cost you if God admitted all of us to Paradise?” ʿUmar said, “If God wills, He can admit all His creation to Paradise in one handful.” The Prophet ﷺ said, “ʿUmar has spoken the truth.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Hammām ibn Munabbih, from Abū Hurayra, who said that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “God says: If My servant intends a good deed, record one good deed for him; if he does it, record ten like it. If he intends a bad deed and does it, record one bad deed; if he abandons it, record one good deed.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Aʿmash, that Ibn Masʿūd passed a man admonishing a group and said, “O preacher, do not make people despair.”

records.text_en: Maʿmar reported from al-Zuhrī, who said that Anas ibn Mālik told him: “One day, while we were seated with the Messenger of God ﷺ, he said, ‘A man of Paradise is about to come to you along this path.’ A man of the Helpers arrived with water dripping from his beard after ablution and his sandals held in his left hand. The next day the Prophet ﷺ made the same announcement and the same man appeared as before. On the third day it happened again. When the Prophet ﷺ departed, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ followed the man and told him, ‘I have quarreled with my father and sworn not to enter his home for three nights. Could you host me until they pass?’ The man agreed. ʿAbd Allāh later related that he stayed with him three nights but did not see him rise to pray during the night. Whenever he awoke and turned in bed, he mentioned God and magnified Him until the dawn prayer. He spoke only good. After the three nights ʿAbd Allāh said, ‘I did not actually quarrel with my father. But I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say three times that a man of Paradise was approaching, and each time you appeared. I wanted to stay with you and observe your deeds so I might imitate you, but I have not seen you perform extraordinary deeds. What brought you to the station the Messenger of God ﷺ described?’ The man said, ‘Only what you saw.’ As ʿAbd Allāh was leaving, he called him back and said, ‘It is only what you saw, except that I harbor no deceit or ill will toward any Muslim and do not envy anyone for what God has given him.’ ʿAbd Allāh replied, ‘That is what brought you there, and it is what we cannot manage.’”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٥٥٩ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنِي أَنَسُ بْنُ مَالِكٍ، قَالَ: كُنَّا يَوْمًا جُلُوسًا عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَقَالَ:   «§يَطْلُعُ عَلَيْكُمُ الْآنَ مِنْ هَذَا الْفَجِّ رَجُلٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ»   ، قَالَ: فَطَلَعَ رَجُلٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْأَنْصَارِ تَنْطِفُ لِحْيَتُهُ مِنْ وُضُوئِهِ، قَدْ عَلَّقَ نَعْلَيْهِ فِي يَدِهِ الشِّمَالِ فَسَلَّمَ، فَلَمَّا كَانَ الْغَدُ، قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ، فَطَلَعَ ذَلِكَ الرَّجُلُ عَلَى مِثْلِ الْمَرَّةِ الْأُولَى، فَلَمَّا كَانَ الْيَوْمُ الثَّالِثُ، قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ مِثْلَ مَقَالَتِهِ أَيْضًا، فَطَلَعَ ذَلِكَ الرَّجُلُ عَلَى مِثْلِ حَالِهِ الْأَوَّلِ، فَلَمَّا قَامَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ تَبِعَهُ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عَمْرِو بْنِ الْعَاصِ فَقَالَ: إِنِّي لَاحَيْتُ أَبِي، فَأَقْسَمْتُ أَلَّا أَدْخُلَ عَلَيْهِ ثَلَاثًا، فَإِنْ رَأَيْتَ أَنْ تُؤْوِيَنِي إِلَيْكَ حَتَّى تَمْضِيَ الثَّلَاثُ فَعَلْتَ، قَالَ: نَعَمْ، قَالَ أَنَسٌ: كَانَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ يُحَدِّثُ أَنَّهُ بَاتَ مَعَهُ ثَلَاثَ لَيَالٍ، فَلَمْ يَرَهُ يَقُومُ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ شَيْئًا، غَيْرَ أَنَّهُ إِذَا تَعَارَّ انْقَلَبَ عَلَى فِرَاشِهِ، وَذَكَرَ اللَّهَ وَكَبَّرَ حَتَّى يَقُومَ لِصَلَاةِ الْفَجْرِ، قَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: غير أَنِّي لَمْ أَسْمَعْهُ يَقُولُ إِلَّا خَيْرًا، فَلَمَّا - [٢٨٨] - مَضَتِ الثَّلَاثُ، وَكِدْتُ أَحْتَقِرُ عَمَلَهُ، قُلْتُ: يَا عَبْدَ اللَّهِ، لَمْ يَكُنْ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ وَالِدِي هِجْرَةٌ وَلَا غَضَبٌ، وَلَكِنِّي سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَقُولُ ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ:   «يَطْلُعُ الْآنَ عَلَيْكُمْ رَجُلٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ»   ، فَطَلَعْتَ ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ، فَأَرَدْتُ أَنْ آوِيَ إِلَيْكَ لَأَنْظُرَ مَا عَمَلُكَ، فَأَقْتَدِيَ بِكَ، فَلَمْ أَرَكَ تَعْمَلُ كَبِيرَ عَمَلٍ، فَمَا الَّذِي بَلَغَ بِكَ مَا قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ؟ قَالَ: مَا هُوَ إِلَّا مَا رَأَيْتَ قَالَ: فَانْصَرَفْتُ عَنْهُ، فَلَمَّا وَلَّيْتُ دَعَانِي فَقَالَ: مَا هُوَ إِلَّا مَا رَأَيْتَ، غَيْرَ أَنِّي لَا أَجِدُ فِي نَفْسِي عَلَى أَحَدٍ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ غِشًّا، وَلَا أَحْسُدُهُ عَلَى مَا أَعْطَاهُ اللَّهُ إِيَّاهُ إِلَيْهِ، فَقَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: هَذِهِ الَّتِي بَلَغَتْ بِكَ هِيَ الَّتِي لَا نُطِيقُ
records.raw_text_ar: ٢٠٥٥٩ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنِي أَنَسُ بْنُ مَالِكٍ، قَالَ: كُنَّا يَوْمًا جُلُوسًا عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَقَالَ:   «§يَطْلُعُ عَلَيْكُمُ الْآنَ مِنْ هَذَا الْفَجِّ رَجُلٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ»   ، قَالَ: فَطَلَعَ رَجُلٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْأَنْصَارِ تَنْطِفُ لِحْيَتُهُ مِنْ وُضُوئِهِ، قَدْ عَلَّقَ نَعْلَيْهِ فِي يَدِهِ الشِّمَالِ فَسَلَّمَ، فَلَمَّا كَانَ الْغَدُ، قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ، فَطَلَعَ ذَلِكَ الرَّجُلُ عَلَى مِثْلِ الْمَرَّةِ الْأُولَى، فَلَمَّا كَانَ الْيَوْمُ الثَّالِثُ، قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ مِثْلَ مَقَالَتِهِ أَيْضًا، فَطَلَعَ ذَلِكَ الرَّجُلُ عَلَى مِثْلِ حَالِهِ الْأَوَّلِ، فَلَمَّا قَامَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ تَبِعَهُ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عَمْرِو بْنِ الْعَاصِ فَقَالَ: إِنِّي لَاحَيْتُ أَبِي، فَأَقْسَمْتُ أَلَّا أَدْخُلَ عَلَيْهِ ثَلَاثًا، فَإِنْ رَأَيْتَ أَنْ تُؤْوِيَنِي إِلَيْكَ حَتَّى تَمْضِيَ الثَّلَاثُ فَعَلْتَ، قَالَ: نَعَمْ، قَالَ أَنَسٌ: كَانَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ يُحَدِّثُ أَنَّهُ بَاتَ مَعَهُ ثَلَاثَ لَيَالٍ، فَلَمْ يَرَهُ يَقُومُ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ شَيْئًا، غَيْرَ أَنَّهُ إِذَا تَعَارَّ انْقَلَبَ عَلَى فِرَاشِهِ، وَذَكَرَ اللَّهَ وَكَبَّرَ حَتَّى يَقُومَ لِصَلَاةِ الْفَجْرِ، قَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: غير أَنِّي لَمْ أَسْمَعْهُ يَقُولُ إِلَّا خَيْرًا، فَلَمَّا - [٢٨٨] - مَضَتِ الثَّلَاثُ، وَكِدْتُ أَحْتَقِرُ عَمَلَهُ، قُلْتُ: يَا عَبْدَ اللَّهِ، لَمْ يَكُنْ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ وَالِدِي هِجْرَةٌ وَلَا غَضَبٌ، وَلَكِنِّي سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَقُولُ ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ:   «يَطْلُعُ الْآنَ عَلَيْكُمْ رَجُلٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ»   ، فَطَلَعْتَ ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ، فَأَرَدْتُ أَنْ آوِيَ إِلَيْكَ لَأَنْظُرَ مَا عَمَلُكَ، فَأَقْتَدِيَ بِكَ، فَلَمْ أَرَكَ تَعْمَلُ كَبِيرَ عَمَلٍ، فَمَا الَّذِي بَلَغَ بِكَ مَا قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ؟ قَالَ: مَا هُوَ إِلَّا مَا رَأَيْتَ قَالَ: فَانْصَرَفْتُ عَنْهُ، فَلَمَّا وَلَّيْتُ دَعَانِي فَقَالَ: مَا هُوَ إِلَّا مَا رَأَيْتَ، غَيْرَ أَنِّي لَا أَجِدُ فِي نَفْسِي عَلَى أَحَدٍ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ غِشًّا، وَلَا أَحْسُدُهُ عَلَى مَا أَعْطَاهُ اللَّهُ إِيَّاهُ إِلَيْهِ، فَقَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: هَذِهِ الَّتِي بَلَغَتْ بِكَ هِيَ الَّتِي لَا نُطِيقُ
records.display_text_ar: ٢٠٥٥٩ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنِي أَنَسُ بْنُ مَالِكٍ، قَالَ: كُنَّا يَوْمًا جُلُوسًا عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَقَالَ:   «§يَطْلُعُ عَلَيْكُمُ الْآنَ مِنْ هَذَا الْفَجِّ رَجُلٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ»   ، قَالَ: فَطَلَعَ رَجُلٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْأَنْصَارِ تَنْطِفُ لِحْيَتُهُ مِنْ وُضُوئِهِ، قَدْ عَلَّقَ نَعْلَيْهِ فِي يَدِهِ الشِّمَالِ فَسَلَّمَ، فَلَمَّا كَانَ الْغَدُ، قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ، فَطَلَعَ ذَلِكَ الرَّجُلُ عَلَى مِثْلِ الْمَرَّةِ الْأُولَى، فَلَمَّا كَانَ الْيَوْمُ الثَّالِثُ، قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ مِثْلَ مَقَالَتِهِ أَيْضًا، فَطَلَعَ ذَلِكَ الرَّجُلُ عَلَى مِثْلِ حَالِهِ الْأَوَّلِ، فَلَمَّا قَامَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ تَبِعَهُ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عَمْرِو بْنِ الْعَاصِ فَقَالَ: إِنِّي لَاحَيْتُ أَبِي، فَأَقْسَمْتُ أَلَّا أَدْخُلَ عَلَيْهِ ثَلَاثًا، فَإِنْ رَأَيْتَ أَنْ تُؤْوِيَنِي إِلَيْكَ حَتَّى تَمْضِيَ الثَّلَاثُ فَعَلْتَ، قَالَ: نَعَمْ، قَالَ أَنَسٌ: كَانَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ يُحَدِّثُ أَنَّهُ بَاتَ مَعَهُ ثَلَاثَ لَيَالٍ، فَلَمْ يَرَهُ يَقُومُ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ شَيْئًا، غَيْرَ أَنَّهُ إِذَا تَعَارَّ انْقَلَبَ عَلَى فِرَاشِهِ، وَذَكَرَ اللَّهَ وَكَبَّرَ حَتَّى يَقُومَ لِصَلَاةِ الْفَجْرِ، قَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: غير أَنِّي لَمْ أَسْمَعْهُ يَقُولُ إِلَّا خَيْرًا، فَلَمَّا مَضَتِ الثَّلَاثُ، وَكِدْتُ أَحْتَقِرُ عَمَلَهُ، قُلْتُ: يَا عَبْدَ اللَّهِ، لَمْ يَكُنْ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ وَالِدِي هِجْرَةٌ وَلَا غَضَبٌ، وَلَكِنِّي سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَقُولُ ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ:   «يَطْلُعُ الْآنَ عَلَيْكُمْ رَجُلٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ»   ، فَطَلَعْتَ ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ، فَأَرَدْتُ أَنْ آوِيَ إِلَيْكَ لَأَنْظُرَ مَا عَمَلُكَ، فَأَقْتَدِيَ بِكَ، فَلَمْ أَرَكَ تَعْمَلُ كَبِيرَ عَمَلٍ، فَمَا الَّذِي بَلَغَ بِكَ مَا قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ؟ قَالَ: مَا هُوَ إِلَّا مَا رَأَيْتَ قَالَ: فَانْصَرَفْتُ عَنْهُ، فَلَمَّا وَلَّيْتُ دَعَانِي فَقَالَ: مَا هُوَ إِلَّا مَا رَأَيْتَ، غَيْرَ أَنِّي لَا أَجِدُ فِي نَفْسِي عَلَى أَحَدٍ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ غِشًّا، وَلَا أَحْسُدُهُ عَلَى مَا أَعْطَاهُ اللَّهُ إِيَّاهُ إِلَيْهِ، فَقَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: هَذِهِ الَّتِي بَلَغَتْ بِكَ هِيَ الَّتِي لَا نُطِيقُ
records.raw_text_en: Maʿmar reported from al-Zuhrī, who said that Anas ibn Mālik told him: “One day, while we were seated with the Messenger of God ﷺ, he said, ‘A man of Paradise is about to come to you along this path.’ A man of the Helpers arrived with water dripping from his beard after ablution and his sandals held in his left hand. The next day the Prophet ﷺ made the same announcement and the same man appeared as before. On the third day it happened again. When the Prophet ﷺ departed, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ followed the man and told him, ‘I have quarreled with my father and sworn not to enter his home for three nights. Could you host me until they pass?’ The man agreed. ʿAbd Allāh later related that he stayed with him three nights but did not see him rise to pray during the night. Whenever he awoke and turned in bed, he mentioned God and magnified Him until the dawn prayer. He spoke only good. After the three nights ʿAbd Allāh said, ‘I did not actually quarrel with my father. But I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say three times that a man of Paradise was approaching, and each time you appeared. I wanted to stay with you and observe your deeds so I might imitate you, but I have not seen you perform extraordinary deeds. What brought you to the station the Messenger of God ﷺ described?’ The man said, ‘Only what you saw.’ As ʿAbd Allāh was leaving, he called him back and said, ‘It is only what you saw, except that I harbor no deceit or ill will toward any Muslim and do not envy anyone for what God has given him.’ ʿAbd Allāh replied, ‘That is what brought you there, and it is what we cannot manage.’”

records.isnad_en: Maʿmar reported from al-Zuhrī, who said that Anas ibn Mālik told him: “
records.matn_en: One day, while we were seated with the Messenger of God ﷺ, he said, ‘A man of Paradise is about to come to you along this path.’ A man of the Helpers arrived with water dripping from his beard after ablution and his sandals held in his left hand. The next day the Prophet ﷺ made the same announcement and the same man appeared as before. On the third day it happened again. When the Prophet ﷺ departed, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ followed the man and told him, ‘I have quarreled with my father and sworn not to enter his home for three nights. Could you host me until they pass?’ The man agreed. ʿAbd Allāh later related that he stayed with him three nights but did not see him rise to pray during the night. Whenever he awoke and turned in bed, he mentioned God and magnified Him until the dawn prayer. He spoke only good. After the three nights ʿAbd Allāh said, ‘I did not actually quarrel with my father. But I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say three times that a man of Paradise was approaching, and each time you appeared. I wanted to stay with you and observe your deeds so I might imitate you, but I have not seen you perform extraordinary deeds. What brought you to the station the Messenger of God ﷺ described?’ The man said, ‘Only what you saw.’ As ʿAbd Allāh was leaving, he called him back and said, ‘It is only what you saw, except that I harbor no deceit or ill will toward any Muslim and do not envy anyone for what God has given him.’ ʿAbd Allāh replied, ‘That is what brought you there, and it is what we cannot manage.’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Zayd ibn Aslam: “A man in a former community exerted himself in worship and was severe with himself, but he also caused people to despair of God's mercy. When he died, he asked, ‘My Lord, what awaits me with You?’ He was told, ‘The Fire.’ He asked, ‘Lord, then what of my worship and diligence?’ He was told, ‘You caused people to despair of My mercy in the world, so today I make you despair of My mercy.’”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٥٦١ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ أَنَّ رَجُلًا كَانَ فِي الْأُمَمِ الْمَاضِيَةِ يَجْتَهِدُ فِي الْعِبَادَةِ، وَيُشَدِّدُ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ، وَيُقَنِّطُ النَّاسَ مِنْ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ، ثُمَّ مَاتَ فَقَالَ: أَيْ رَبِّ مَا لِي عِنْدَكَ؟ قَالَ: النَّارُ، قَالَ: يَا رَبِّ، فَأَيْنَ عِبَادَتِي وَاجْتِهَادِي؟ فَقِيلَ لَهُ: §كُنْتَ تُقَنِّطُ النَّاسَ مِنْ رَحْمَتِي فِي الدُّنْيَا، وَأَنَا أُقَنِّطُكَ الْيَوْمَ مِنْ رَحْمَتِي "

records.text_en: It was recited to ʿAbd al-Razzāq through Maʿmar, from Hammām ibn Munabbih, who heard Abū Hurayra say that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “None of you will be saved by his own deeds, but strive to act correctly and come as close as you can.” They asked, “Not even you, Messenger of God?” He answered, “Not even I, unless God envelops me in His mercy and grace.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٥٦٢ - قَالَ: قَرَأْنَا عَلَى عَبْدِ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ هَمَّامِ بْنِ مُنَبِّهٍ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ يَقُولُ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§لَيْسَ وَاحِدٌ مِنْكُمْ بِمُنْجِيهِ عَمَلُهُ، وَلَكِنْ سَدِّدُوا وَقَارِبُوا»   ، قَالُوا: وَلَا أَنْتَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ؟ قَالَ:   «وَلَا أَنَا إِلَّا أَنْ يَتَغَمَّدَنِي اللَّهُ بِرَحْمَةٍ مِنْهُ وَفَضْلٍ»   .،

records.text_en: Maʿmar reported from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn: “Khālid ibn al-Wāshima visited ʿĀʾisha after the Battle of the Camel. She asked, ‘What happened to so-and-so?’—meaning Ṭalḥa. He said, ‘He was killed, Mother of the Believers.’ She said, ‘We belong to God, and to Him we return. ؒ.’ She asked after another man, and when told he had been killed she again pronounced the return formula and prayed for mercy. Khālid said, ‘Then we belong to God, and so do Zayd and Zayd's companions’—meaning Zayd ibn Ṣūḥān. She asked, ‘Was Zayd killed?’ He answered, ‘Yes.’ She said, ‘We belong to God, and to Him we return. ؒ.’ I said, ‘Mother of the Believers, this one belonged to one army and that one to another, yet you pray for mercy upon them all! By God, they will never be united.’ She replied, ‘Do you not know that God's mercy is vast and that He has power over all things?’”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٥٦٤ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنِ ابْنِ سِيرِينَ، قَالَ: دَخَلَ خَالِدُ بْنُ الْوَاشِمَةِ عَلَى عَائِشَةَ بَعْدَ الْجَمَلِ، فَقَالَتْ:   «مَا فَعَلَ فُلَانٌ؟»   - تَعْنِي طَلْحَةَ - قَالَ: قُتِلَ يَا أُمَّ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ، قَالَتْ:   «إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ، يَرْحَمُهُ اللَّهُ، مَا فَعَلَ فُلَانٌ؟»   ، قَالَ: قُتِلَ، قَالَ: - [٢٩٠] - فَرَجَّعَتْ أَيْضًا، وَقَالَتْ:   «يَرْحَمُهُ اللَّهُ»   ، قَالَ: قُلْتُ: بَلْ نَحْنُ لِلَّهِ، وَإِنَّا لِلَّهِ عَلَى زَيْدٍ وَأَصْحَابِ زَيْدٍ - يَعْنِي زَيْدَ بْنَ صُوحَانَ - قَالَتْ:   «وَقُتِلَ زَيْدٌ؟»   ، قَالَ: قُلْتُ: نَعَمْ، قَالَتْ:   «إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ، يَرْحَمُهُ اللَّهُ»   ، قَالَ: قُلْتُ: يَا أُمَّ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ، هَذَا مِنْ جُنْدٍ، وَهَذَا مِنْ جُنْدٍ تَرَحَّمِينَ عَلَيْهِمْ جَمِيعًا، وَاللَّهِ لَا يَجْتَمِعُونَ أَبَدًا، قَالَتْ:   «أَوَلَا تَدْرِي، §رَحْمَةُ اللَّهُ وَاسِعَةٌ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ»

She asked, ‘Was Zayd killed?’ He answered, ‘Yes.’ She said, ‘We belong to God, and to Him we return. ؒ.’ I said, ‘Mother of the Believers, this one belonged to one army and that one to another, yet you pray for mercy upon them all! By God, they will never be united.’ She replied, ‘Do you not know that God's mercy is vast and that He has power over all things?’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha: “The Messenger of God ﷺ entered while a well-dressed woman was with me. He asked, ‘Who is she?’ I said, ‘So-and-so, daughter of so-and-so; she does not sleep at night.’ He said, ‘Enough! Undertake only the deeds you can manage. God does not tire until you tire. The deeds dearest to God are those a person does regularly, even if few.’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Khālid, from Abū Qilāba: “A man came to the Prophet ﷺ asking him to perform the funeral prayer for his mother, who had fasted continuously until she died. The Prophet ﷺ said, ‘She neither fasted nor broke her fast,’ and refused to pray over her.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, from Ibn Masʿūd: “Someone who forbids what is lawful is like someone who permits what is forbidden.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz: “The Prophet ﷺ was asked, ‘Which religion is best?’ He replied, ‘The tolerant, upright religion.’”

records.text_en: Maʿmar reported from Qatāda, from Anas, who said that the Messenger of God ﷺ said that God Almighty says: “Child of Adam, remember Me within yourself and I shall remember you within Myself. If you remember Me in an assembly, I shall remember you in an assembly of angels—or,” the transmitter said, “in a better assembly. If you come a handspan nearer to Me, I shall come a forearm's length nearer to you; if you come a forearm's length nearer, I shall come an armspan nearer. If you come to Me walking, I shall come to you running.” Maʿmar said that Qatāda remarked, “And God is quicker to forgive.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٥٧٥ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، عَنْ أَنَسٍ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «قَالَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: §يَا ابْنَ آدَمَ اذْكُرْنِي فِي نَفْسِكَ أَذْكُرْكَ فِي نَفْسِي، وَإِنْ ذَكَرْتَنِي فِي مَلَإٍ ذَكَرْتُكَ فِي مَلَإٍ مِنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ - أَوْ قَالَ: فِي مَلَإٍ خَيْرٍ مِنْهُمْ - وَإِنْ دَنَوْتَ مِنِّي شِبْرًا دَنَوْتُ مِنْكَ ذِرَاعًا، وَإِنْ دَنَوْتَ ذِرَاعًا دَنَوْتُ بَاعًا، وَلَوْ أَتَيْتَنِي تَمْشِي أَتَيْتُكَ أُهَرْوِلُ»   قَالَ مَعْمَرٌ: قَالَ قَتَادَةُ:   «وَاللَّهُ أَسْرَعُ بِالْمَغْفِرَةِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Umm ʿIkrima bint Khālid: “She sent her brother to Abū Hurayra to ask about saying: ‘There is no god but God alone, without partner. His is the kingdom, His is praise, and He has power over all things.’ Abū Hurayra answered, ‘Whoever says it ten times has the equivalent of freeing a slave.’ He added, ‘So increase the number of slaves you free.’”

records.text_en: Maʿmar reported from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Agharr Abū Muslim, from Abū Hurayra and Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Whenever a group gathers to remember God, the angels surround them, mercy covers them, serenity descends upon them, and God mentions them among those in His presence.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٥٧٧ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنِ الْأَغَرِّ أَبِي مُسْلِمٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، وَأَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيِّ، عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ:   «§مَا اجْتَمَعَ قَوْمٌ يَذْكُرُونَ اللَّهَ إِلَّا حَفَّتْهُمُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ وَتَغَشَّتْهُمُ الرَّحْمَةُ، وَنَزَلَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّكِينَةُ، وَذَكَرَهُمُ اللَّهُ فِيمَنْ عِنْدَهُ»

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: وَقَالَ:   «إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُمْهِلُ حَتَّى إِذَا ذَهَبَ ثُلُثُ اللَّيْلِ الْأَوَّلُ، نَزَلَ إِلَى هَذِهِ السَّمَاءِ الدُّنْيَا، فَنَادَى: §هَلْ مِنْ مُذْنِبٍ يَتُوبُ، هَلْ مِنْ مُسْتَغْفِرٍ، هَلْ مِنْ دَاعٍ، هَلْ مِنْ سَائِلٍ، إِلَى الْفَجْرِ»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: He also said: “God grants respite. When the first third of the night has passed, He descends to the lowest heaven and calls until dawn: Is there a sinner who will repent? Is there anyone seeking forgiveness? Anyone calling upon Me? Anyone asking?”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from more than one person, from al-Ḥasan: “On the Day of Resurrection a herald will call, ‘The gathering will learn who deserves honor! Where are those whose sides left their beds,’ continuing through ‘and spend from what We have provided them’? [The text cites Quran 2:3, although the first phrase is from 32:16.] They will rise and step over the people. The herald will call again, ‘The gathering will learn who deserves honor! Where are those whom neither trade nor commerce distracts from the remembrance of God?’ [24:37.] They will rise and pass over the people. Then he will call, ‘The gathering will learn who deserves honor! Where are those who praised God in every condition?’ They will rise, and they will be numerous. Accountability and reckoning will then concern those who remain.”

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from more than one person, from al-Ḥasan: “On the Day of Resurrection a herald will call, ‘The gathering will learn who deserves honor! Where are those whose sides left their beds,’ continuing through ‘and spend from what We have provided them’? [The text cites Quran 2:3, although the first phrase is from 32:16.] They will rise and step over the people. The herald will call again, ‘The gathering will learn who deserves honor! Where are those whom neither trade nor commerce distracts from the remembrance of God?’ [24:37.] They will rise and pass over the people. Then he will call, ‘The gathering will learn who deserves honor! Where are those who praised God in every condition?’ They will rise, and they will be numerous. Accountability and reckoning will then concern those who remain.”

He told her, ‘Say “Glory be to God” one hundred times, for that is better than freeing one hundred slaves. Praise God one hundred times; that is better than providing one hundred horses for God's cause. Say “God is greatest” one hundred times; that is better than offering one hundred sacrificial camels to God's House. Say one hundred times, “There is no god but God alone without partner; His is the kingdom and His is praise, and He has power over all things.” That is better than everything between heaven and earth. No one's deed will be raised as better than this, unless that person says the same as you or more.’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from ʿĀṣim ibn Sulaymān, from Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī: “Salmān used to teach us the magnification of God, saying: ‘Magnify God: God is greatest, God is greatest,’ repeatedly. ‘O God, You are too high and exalted to have a consort, a child, a partner in sovereignty, or a protecting ally against humiliation. records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Abū Isḥāq, from Jurayy al-Nahdī, from a man of Banū Sulaym, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Saying ‘Glory be to God’ fills half the scale, and praise fills it completely. Magnifying God fills what lies between heaven and earth. Fasting is half of patience, and purification is half of faith.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn al-Awdī, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ informed us that mosques are God's houses upon earth and that God has undertaken to honor whoever visits Him within them.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī, who attributed the saying to the Prophet ﷺ: “Mosques have steadfast attendants whose companions are angels. The angels look for them. If they have a need, they assist them; if they fall ill, they visit them; if they are absent, they ask about them. And when they attend, the angels say, ‘Remember God, and God will remember you.’”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٥٨٥ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ عَطَاءٍ الْخُرَاسَانِيِّ، رَفَعَ الْحَدِيثَ قَالَ:   «إِنَّ §لِلْمَسَاجِدِ أَوْتَادًا جُلَسَاؤُهُمُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ يَتَفَقَّدُونَهُمْ، فَإِنْ كَانُوا فِي حَاجَةٍ أَعَانُوهُمْ، وَإِنْ مَرِضُوا عَادُوهُمْ، وَإِنْ خُلِّفُوا افْتَقَدُوهُمْ، وَإِنْ حَضَرُوا قَالُوا: اذْكُرُوا ذَكَرَكُمُ اللَّهُ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Zayd ibn Aslam: “The Prophet ﷺ was traveling when a man took a fledgling bird. Its mother came and threw herself into the man's lap beside the fledgling, and he caught her. The Prophet ﷺ said, ‘How remarkable this bird is! Out of mercy for her young she came and threw herself into your hands. By God, God is more merciful toward His believing servant than this bird is toward her fledgling.’”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٥٨٦ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، قَالَ: كَانَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فِي بَعْضِ أَسْفَارِهِ، فَأَخَذَ رَجُلٌ فَرْخَ طَائِرٍ، فَجَاءَ الطَّائِرُ فَأَلْقَى نَفْسَهُ فِي حِجْرِ الرَّجُلِ مَعَ فَرْخِهِ، فَأَخَذَهُ الرَّجُلُ، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «عَجَبًا لِهَذَا الطَّائِرِ جَاءَ وَأَلْقَى نَفْسَهُ فِي أَيْدِيكُمْ رَحْمَةً لِوَلَدِهِ، فَوَاللَّهِ §لَلَّهُ أَرْحَمُ بِعَبْدِهِ الْمُؤْمِنِ مِنْ هَذَا الطَّائِرِ بفَرْخِهِ»

records.display_matn_en: The Prophet ﷺ was traveling when a man took a fledgling bird. Its mother came and threw herself into the man's lap beside the fledgling, and he caught her. The Prophet ﷺ said, ‘How remarkable this bird is! Out of mercy for her young she came and threw herself into your hands. By God, God is more merciful toward His believing servant than this bird is toward her fledgling.’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from ʿĀṣim, from Abū ʿUthmān: “ʿUyayna ibn Ḥiṣn saw ʿUmar kissing one of his children and asked, ‘Do you kiss them while you are Commander of the Believers? If I were Commander of the Believers, I would never kiss a child of mine!’ ʿUmar repeatedly asked him to swear he meant it. Then he said, ‘What can I do if God has removed mercy from your heart? God shows mercy only to the merciful among His servants.’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, who said the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “I and the woman with the darkened cheeks will be in Paradise like these two,” indicating his middle and index fingers. They asked, “Messenger of God, who is the woman with the darkened cheeks?” He replied: “A woman whose husband died and who remained to care for her dependents.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Ismāʿīl ibn Umayya, from an unnamed man, from Abū Hurayra, who said that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Someone who looks after a widow and a poor person is like one who fights in God's cause, or someone who stands in prayer throughout the night and fasts by day. I and the person who responsibly cares for an orphan will be like these two in Paradise on the Day of Resurrection,” indicating his middle and index fingers.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā: “The prophet David said: ‘Be to the orphan like a compassionate father. Know that you reap what you sow. Know that a good wife is to her husband in beauty like a crowned king wearing a gold-inlaid crown, and that a bad wife is to her husband like a heavy burden on an elderly man's back. A fool's speech before a gathering is like someone singing beside the head of a dead person. Do not promise your brother something and fail to fulfill it, for that creates enmity between you. How excellent is knowledge after ignorance, how ugly is poverty after wealth, and how ugly is misguidance after guidance!’”

records.display_matn_en: Be to the orphan like a compassionate father. Know that you reap what you sow. Know that a good wife is to her husband in beauty like a crowned king wearing a gold-inlaid crown, and that a bad wife is to her husband like a heavy burden on an elderly man's back. A fool's speech before a gathering is like someone singing beside the head of a dead person. Do not promise your brother something and fail to fulfill it, for that creates enmity between you. How excellent is knowledge after ignorance, how ugly is poverty after wealth, and how ugly is misguidance after guidance!’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Ḥasan: “A daughter of the Messenger of God ﷺ came to complain of her husband. The Prophet ﷺ said: ‘Return, daughter. A woman is not a proper wife until she does what pleases her husband while he exercises restraint. If I were to command one thing to prostrate to another, I would order a woman to prostrate to her husband because of the greatness of his right over her. The best women are those who give thanks when given something and are patient when it is withheld.’” Al-Ḥasan remarked: “If I swore such a woman cannot be found in Basra, I would be speaking the truth. records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Ibn al-Munkadir, that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: “Three things are crushing afflictions: a bad neighbor in a permanent home; a bad wife—if you visit her ... and if you leave you cannot trust her; and a ruler who does not accept the good you do and does not forgive your wrongdoing.” [The text has an ellipsis concerning the wife.]

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from ʿAwf ibn al-Qāsim or al-Qāsim ibn ʿAwf: “When Muʿādh ibn Jabal visited Syria, he saw Christians prostrating to their patriarchs and bishops. On returning to the Prophet ﷺ, he said, ‘I saw Christians prostrate to their patriarchs and bishops, and you have a greater right that we should prostrate to you.’ The Prophet ﷺ replied: ‘If I were going to command anything to prostrate before anything other than God, I would command a wife to prostrate before her husband. A woman will never discharge the full right of her husband—even if he asks her for intimacy while she is upon a camel saddle and she does not refuse him.’”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٥٩٦ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ عَوْفِ بْنِ الْقَاسِمِ أَوِ الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ عَوْفٍ - أَنَّ مُعَاذَ بْنَ جَبَلٍ، لَمَّا قَدِمَ الشَّامَ رَأَى النَّصَارَى تَسْجُدُ لِبَطَارِقَتِهَا، وَأَسَاقِفَتِهَا، فَلَمَّا قَدِمَ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ: إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ النَّصَارَى تَسْجُدُ لِبَطَارِقَتِهَا، وَأَسَاقِفَتِهَا، وَأَنْتَ كُنْتَ أَحَقَّ أَنْ نَسْجُدَ لَكَ، فَقَالَ:   «§لَوْ كُنْتُ آمِرًا شَيْئًا أَنْ يَسْجُدَ لِشَيْءٍ دُونَ اللَّهِ، لَأَمَرْتُ الْمَرْأَةَ أَنْ تَسْجُدَ لِزَوْجِهَا، وَلَنْ تُؤَدِّيَ امْرَأَةٌ حَقَّ زَوْجِهَا، حَتَّى لَوْ سَأَلَهَا نَفْسَهَا وَهِيَ عَلَى قَتَبٍ لَمْ تَمْنَعْهُ نَفْسَهَا»

records.text_en: Maʿmar reported from Yaḥyā ibn Shihāb, from a woman who heard ʿĀʾisha say: “When a woman was in labor, she would be placed on a camel saddle to make childbirth easier.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Qatāda: “It was said: A woman with a bad character is like a leaking water skin when one is thirsty; and a beautiful woman who behaves immorally is like a pig wearing a golden collar.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٦٠٠ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، قَالَ: كَانَ يُقَالُ:   «§مَثَلُ الْمَرْأَةِ السَّيِّئَةِ الْخُلُقِ كَالسِّقَاءِ الْوَاهِي فِي الْمَعْطَشَةِ، وَمَثَلُ الْمَرْأَةِ الْجَمِيلَةِ الْفَاجِرَةِ كمَثَلُ خِنْزِيرٍ فِي عُنُقِهِ طَوْقٌ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ»

records.display_isnad_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Ibn al-Musayyib, from Abū Hurayra, and through Ibn Ṭāwūs from his father: “The Prophet ﷺ proposed marriage to Umm Hāniʾ daughter of Abū Ṭālib. She said, ‘Messenger of God, I have grown old and have dependents.’ The Messenger of God ﷺ said, ‘
records.display_matn_en: The best women who have ridden camels are the women of Quraysh: the tenderest toward a small child and the most careful of their husband's wealth.’” Al-Zuhrī added in the version through Ibn al-Musayyib: “Mary daughter of ʿImrān never rode a camel.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Jazarī, from Mujāhid, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “No benefit God grants a Muslim is better for him than a righteous wife: she delights him when he looks at her, guards herself in his absence, and obeys him when he asks. A woman is married for four reasons: her religion, beauty, wealth and lineage. Seek the religious one; may your hands be covered in dust [an idiomatic exclamation].”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٦٠٥ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الْكَرِيمِ الْجَزَرِيِّ، عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§مَا فَائِدَةٌ أَفَادَهَا اللَّهُ عَلَى امْرِئٍ مُسْلِمٍ خَيْرٌ لَهُ مِنْ زَوْجَةٍ صَالِحَةٍ، إِذَا نَظَرَ إِلَيْهَا سَرَّتْهُ، وَإِذَا غَابَ عَنْهَا حَفِظَتْهُ فِي نَفْسِهَا، وَإِنْ أَمَرَهَا أَطَاعَتْهُ، تُنْكَحُ الْمَرْأَةُ لِأَرْبَعٍ: لِدِينِهَا، وَجَمَالِهَا، وَمَالِهَا، وَحَسَبِهَا، فَعَلَيْكَ بِذَاتِ الدِّينِ تَرِبَتْ يَدَاكَ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, that the prophet David ﷺ said: “Three qualities in a person please me: moderation in poverty and wealth, justice in anger and contentment, and reverence in private and public. Three qualities destroy a person: avarice that is obeyed, desire that is followed, and self-admiration. And whoever receives four things has received the good of this world and the next: a tongue that remembers, a thankful heart, a patient body and an accommodating—or,’ the transmitter said, ‘agreeable—wife.’”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٦٠٦ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ،   «أَنَّ دَاوُدَ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ: §ثَلَاثٌ مَنْ كُنَّ فِيهِ أعَجَبْنَنِي: الْقَصْدُ فِي الْفَقْرِ وَالْغِنَاءِ، وَالْعَدْلُ فِي الْغَضَبِ وَالرِّضَا، وَالْخَشْيَةُ فِي السِّرِّ وَالْعَلَانِيَةِ، وَثَلَاثٌ مَنْ كُنَّ فِيهِ أهْلَكَتْهُ: شُحٌّ مُطَاعٌ، وَهَوًى مُتَّبَعٌ، وَإِعْجَابُ الْمَرْءِ بِنَفْسِهِ، وَأَرْبَعٌ مَنْ أُعْطِيَهُنَّ فَقَدْ أُعْطِيَ خَيْرَ الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ: لِسَانٌ ذَاكِرٌ، وَقَلَبٌ شَاكِرٌ، وَبَدَنٌ صَابِرٌ، وَزَوْجَةٌ مُوَافِقَةٌ - أَوْ قَالَ: مُوَاتِيَةٌ»

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, that the prophet David ﷺ said: “Three qualities in a person please me: moderation in poverty and wealth, justice in anger and contentment, and reverence in private and public. Three qualities destroy a person: avarice that is obeyed, desire that is followed, and self-admiration. And whoever receives four things has received the good of this world and the next: a tongue that remembers, a thankful heart, a patient body and an accommodating—or,’ the transmitter said, ‘agreeable—wife.’”

records.text_en: Maʿmar reported from ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Jazarī, from Ibn ʿAbbās: “The women of the Children of Israel were ruined because of their feet, and the women of this community will be ruined because of their heads.”

records.text_en: Maʿmar reported from Sulaymān al-Taymī, from Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī, from Usāma ibn Zayd, who said that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “I stood at Paradise's gate and saw that most who entered it were the poor; I stood at the Fire's gate and saw that most of its inhabitants were women. The wealthy had been held back, except those destined for the Fire who had already been ordered there.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Shall I tell you who the people of Paradise are?” They said, “Yes, Messenger of God.” He replied: “Every weak person who is regarded as weak, clad in two worn garments and paid no attention to, who, if he swore an oath by God, God would honor his oath.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٦١٢ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§أَلَا أُخْبِرُكُمْ بِأَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ؟»   ، فَقَالُوا: بَلَى يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، قَالَ:   «كُلُّ ضَعِيفٍ مُتَضَعِّفٍ ذِي طِمْرَيْنِ لَا يُؤْبَهُ لَهُ، لَوْ أَقْسَمَ عَلَى اللَّهِ لَأَبَرَّهُ»   ،

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from Zayd ibn Aslam, a report resembling the preceding one, adding that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Shall I tell you who the people of the Fire are? Every coarse, arrogant, overbearing hoarder who withholds what he has.”

records.text_en: Maʿmar reported from Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī, who could not remember whether he attributed the saying to the Prophet ﷺ: “Whoever puts to sea after it becomes turbulent has forfeited the protection [guaranteed to him], and whoever sleeps upon an unprotected roof without a parapet has forfeited that protection.”

records.isnad_en: Maʿmar reported from Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī, who could not remember whether he attributed the saying to the Prophet ﷺ: “
records.matn_en: Whoever puts to sea after it becomes turbulent has forfeited the protection [guaranteed to him], and whoever sleeps upon an unprotected roof without a parapet has forfeited that protection.”

records.text_en: Maʿmar reported from Qatāda that Abū ʿUbayda ibn al-Jarrāḥ said: “I wish I were a ram, so that my family might slaughter me, eat my flesh and sip my broth.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٦١٥ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، قَالَ: قَالَ: أَبُو عُبَيْدَةَ بْنُ الْجَرَّاحِ:   «§وَدِدْتُ أَنِّي كُنْتُ كَبْشًا فَيَذْبَحُنِي أَهْلِي يَأْكُلُونَ لَحْمِي وَيَحْسُونَ مَرَقَتِي»
records.section_title_en: The Majority of the Inhabitants of Paradise and the Fire

unnumbered_continuations.text_en: ʿImrān ibn al-Ḥuṣayn also said: “I wish I were ashes upon a hill, scattered by winds on a stormy day.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Part of the excellence of a person's Islam is leaving what does not concern him.”
