records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿUmāra ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ḥudhayfa, who said: “Beware of civil strife. Let no one step forward into it. By God, no one enters it without being swept away like refuse in a flood. As it approaches, it resembles one thing; when it passes, its real nature becomes plain. An ignorant man will mistake its appearance. When you see it, remain in your houses, break your swords, and cut up your bowstrings [the Arabic says ‘tent-pegs’].”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٧٤٠ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنْ عُمَارَةَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، عَنْ حُذَيْفَةَ، قَالَ:   «§إِيَّاكُمْ وَالْفِتَنَ لَا يَشْخَصْ لَهَا أَحَدٌ، وَاللَّهِ مَا شَخَصَ فِيهَا أَحَدٌ إِلَّا نَسَفَتْهُ كَمَا يَنْسِفُ السَّيْلُ الدِّمَنَ، إِنَّهَا مُشْبِهَةٌ مُقْبِلَةٌ، حَتَّى يَقُولَ الْجَاهِلُ هَذِهِ تُشَبِّهُ مُقْبِلَةً وَتُبَيِّنُ مُدْبِرَةً، فَإِذَا رَأَيْتُمُوهَا فَاجْثَمُوا فِي بُيُوتِكُمْ، وَكَسِّرُوا سُيُوفَكُمْ، وَقَطِّعُوا أوتَادَكُمْ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from several persons including al-Ḥasan, that the Prophet ﷺ said to ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr: “What will you do when you are left among the dregs of humanity, whose agreements and trusts are confused and who clash like this?” He intertwined his fingers. ʿAbd Allāh asked what he should do. He replied: “Hold to what you recognize as right, leave what you reject, concern yourself with those close to you, and beware of their masses.” Al-Ḥasan added a remark about how difficult it would be to restrain oneself in such a time; the final words are somewhat obscure in the source.
records.text_ar: ٢٠٧٤١ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ غَيْرِ وَاحِدٍ، مِنْهُمُ الْحَسَنُ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ لِعَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو:   «§كَيْفَ أَنْتَ إِذَا بَقِيتَ فِي حُثَالَةِ النَّاسِ، مَرِجَتْ عُهُودُهُمْ وَأَمَانَاتُهُمْ، وَاخْتَلَفُوا فَكَانُوا هَكَذَا»   ، - وَشَبَّكَ بَيْنَ أَصَابِعِهِ - قَالَ: فَبِمَ تَأْمُرُنِي يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ؟ قَالَ:   «عَلَيْكَ بِمَا تَعْرِفُ، وَدَعْ مَا تُنْكِرُ، وَعَلَيْكَ بِخَاصَّتِكَ، وَإِيَّاكَ وَعَوَامَّهُمْ»   قَالَ: يَقُولُ الْحَسَنُ: فَوَاللَّهِ مَا تَمَالَكَ إِنْ كَانَ فِيَّ عَلَى أَسْوَاءِ ذَلِكَ

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, that Ibn Masʿūd said: “What will you do when a trial envelops you in which the young grow up and the old grow old, and it comes to be regarded as established practice, so that when it is changed people say: ‘This is reprehensible’?” Asked when, he said: “When trustworthy people are few and rulers many; jurists few and reciters many; religious knowledge is sought for purposes other than religion, and worldly advantage is pursued through deeds intended for the hereafter.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٧٤٢ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، أَنَّ ابْنَ مَسْعُودٍ، قَالَ:   «§كَيْفَ بِكُمْ إِذَا لَبِسَتْكُمْ فِتْنَةٌ يَرْبُو فِيهَا الصَّغِيرُ، وَيَهْرَمُ فِيهَا الْكَبِيرُ، وَيُتَّخَذُ سُنَّةٌ، فَإِنْ غُيِّرَتْ يَوْمًا، قِيلَ: هَذَا مُنْكَرٌ»   ، قَالُوا: وَمَتَى ذَلِكَ يَا أَبَا عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ؟ قَالَ:   «إِذَا قَلَّتْ أُمَنَاؤُكُمْ، وَكَثُرَتْ أُمَرَاؤُكُمْ، وَقَلَّتْ فُقَهَاؤُكُمْ، وَكَثُرَتْ قُرَّاؤُكُمْ، وَتُفِقِّهَ لِغَيْرِ الدِّينِ، وَالْتُمِسَتِ الدُّنْيَا بِعَمَلِ الْآخِرَةِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from Abān, from Sulaym ibn Qays al-Ḥanẓalī: ʿUmar preached: “What I most fear for you after me is that an innocent man will be seized, cut apart as a sacrificial camel is cut, and have his flesh stripped as its flesh is stripped, while people call him a rebel although he is not.” ʿAlī, standing below the pulpit, asked—or spoke of—the time when calamity would intensify, partisanship arise, descendants be taken captive, and trials grind people as millstones grind grain and fire consumes wood. ʿUmar asked when that would happen. ʿAlī said: “When people study religious law for something other than religion, learn for something other than practice, and seek the world through deeds of the hereafter.”

records.display_matn_ar: خَطَبَ عُمَرُ فَقَالَ:   «إِنَّ §أَخْوَفَ مَا أَتَخَوَّفُ عَلَيْكُمْ بَعْدِي أَنْ يُؤْخَذَ الرَّجُلُ مِنْكُمُ الْبَرِيءُ، فَيُؤْشَرُ كَمَا يُؤْشَرُ الْجَزُورُ، وَيُشَاطُ لَحْمُهُ كَمَا يُشَاطُ لَحْمُهَا، وَيُقَالُ: عَاصٍ وَلَيْسَ بِعَاصٍ»   قَالَ: فَقَالَ عَلِيُّ وَهُوَ تَحْتَ الْمِنْبَرِ:   «وَمَتَى ذَلِكَ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ؟ أَوْ: بِمَا تَشْتَدُّ الْبَلِيَّةُ، وَتَظْهَرُ الْحَمِيَّةُ، وَتُسْبَى الذُّرِّيَّةُ، وَتَدُقَّهُمُ الْفِتَنُ كَمَا تَدُقُّ الرَّحَا ثُفْلَهَا، وَكَمَا تَدُقُّ النَّارُ الْحَطَبَ؟»   قَالَ:   «وَمَتَى ذَلِكَ يَا عَلِيُّ؟»   ، قَالَ:   «إِذَا تُفُقِّهَ لِغَيْرِ الدِّينِ، وَتُعُلِّمَ لِغَيْرِ الْعَمَلِ، وَالْتُمِسَتِ الدُّنْيَا بِعَمَلِ الْآخِرَةِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from Abān, from al-Ḥasan, from Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “I fear harj for you.” Asked what that meant, he replied: “Killing.” They pointed out that they already killed many polytheists every day. He said: “Not killing polytheists, but killing one another.” They asked whether that would happen even though God's Book remained among them and they had their reason. He said: “Yes, despite God's Book being among you. The minds of most people of that time will be taken away and replaced by worthless people who think they have something [of understanding] when they have nothing.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٧٤٤ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَبَانَ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ، عَنْ أَبِي مُوسَى الْأَشْعَرِيِّ، قَالَ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمُ الْهَرْجَ»   ، قَالُوا: وَمَا الْهَرْجُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ؟ قَالَ:   «الْقَتْلُ»   ، قَالُوا: وَأَكْثَرُ مِمَّا نَقْتُلُ الْيَوْمَ، إِنَّا لَنَقْتُلُ فِي الْيَوْمِ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ كَذَا وَكَذَا؟ فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «لَيْسَ قَتْلَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ، وَلَكِنْ قَتْلَ بَعْضِكُمْ بَعْضًا»   ، قَالُوا: وَفِينَا كِتَابُ اللَّهِ؟ قَالَ:   «وَفِيكُمْ كِتَابُ اللَّهِ»   ، قَالُوا: وَمَعَنَا عُقُولُنَا؟ قَالَ:   «إِنَّهُ تُنْتَزَعُ عُقُولُ عَامَّةِ ذَاكُمُ الزَّمَانِ، وَيُخْلَفُ لَهَا هَبَاءٌ مِنَ النَّاسِ يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ عَلَى شَيْءٍ وَلَيْسُوا عَلَى شَيْءٍ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilāba: Abū Qilāba and Muslim ibn Yasār met. Muslim had joined Ibn al-Ashʿath's rebellion. He said: “I went out with him, but by God I did not draw a sword, shoot an arrow, or thrust a spear.” Abū Qilāba replied: “Yet a man may have seen you standing there and thought, ‘There stands Muslim ibn Yasār ready to fight,’ and consequently shot an arrow, thrust a spear, and struck with his sword.” Muslim wept so bitterly that Abū Qilāba wished he had said nothing.

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilāba: Abū Qilāba and Muslim ibn Yasār met. Muslim had joined Ibn al-Ashʿath's rebellion. He said: “I went out with him, but by God I did not draw a sword, shoot an arrow, or thrust a spear.” Abū Qilāba replied: “Yet a man may have seen you standing there and thought, ‘There stands Muslim ibn Yasār ready to fight,’ and consequently shot an arrow, thrust a spear, and struck with his sword.” Muslim wept so bitterly that Abū Qilāba wished he had said nothing.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from an unnamed man, from Ibn al-Musayyab, who said: “There will be a civil war in Syria beginning like children's play. It flares up in one place and subsides in another, not ending until a caller announces: ‘So-and-so is the ruler!’” Ibn al-Musayyab would then clasp or strike his hands until they trembled and say: “That is the true ruler! That is the true ruler!”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٧٤٦ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ رَجُلٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ الْمُسَيِّبِ، قَالَ:   «§تَكُونُ فِتْنَةٌ بِالشَّامِ كَانَ أَوَّلُهَا لَعِبَ الصِّبْيَانِ تَطْفُو مِنْ جَانِبٍ، وَتَسْكُنُ مِنْ جَانِبٍ، فَلَا تَتَنَاهَى حَتَّى يُنَادِيَ مُنَادٍ إِنَّ الْأَمِيرَ فُلَانٌ»   قَالَ: فَيُقَبِّلُ ابْنُ الْمُسَيِّبِ يَدَيْهِ حَتَّى إِنَّهُمَا لَيَنْتَفِضَانِ، ثُمَّ يَقُولُ:   «ذَاكُمُ الْأَمِيرُ حَقًّا، ذَاكُمُ الْأَمِيرُ حَقًّا»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr, from Kurz ibn ʿAlqama al-Khuzāʿī: A Bedouin asked the Messenger of God ﷺ whether Islam had an endpoint. He replied: “Yes. Whenever God intends good for a household, Arab or non-Arab, He causes Islam to enter among them.” Asked what followed, he said: “Then trials will come like overhanging clouds.” The Bedouin objected. The Prophet ﷺ said: “By Him in whose hand is my soul, during them you will turn into striking black serpents [figurative wording], striking one another's necks.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Hind daughter of al-Ḥārith—al-Zuhrī noted that she kept a wrap inside her sleeve—from Umm Salama, who said: “One night the Messenger of God ﷺ woke saying: ‘There is no god but God! What treasures have been opened tonight! There is no god but God! What tribulations have descended tonight! Who will awaken the women of these chambers? Many a woman clothed in this world will be naked in the hereafter.’”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwa, from Zaynab daughter of Abū Salama, from Zaynab daughter of Jaḥsh: “The Messenger of God ﷺ entered and said: ‘Woe to the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near! Today an opening of this size has appeared in the barrier of Gog and Magog.’ He made a circle with his thumb and the finger next to it. I asked whether we would perish while righteous people were among us. He said: ‘Yes, when corruption becomes widespread.’”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٧٤٩ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ عُرْوَةَ، عَنْ زَيْنَبَ بِنْتِ أَبِي سَلَمَةَ، عَنْ زَيْنَبَ بِنْتِ جَحْشٍ قَالَتْ: دَخَلَ عَلَيْنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَهُوَ يَقُولُ:   «§وَيْلٌ لِلْعَرَبِ مِنْ شَرٍّ قَدِ اقْتَرَبَ، فُتِحَ الْيَوْمَ مِنْ رَدْمِ يَأْجُوجَ وَمَأْجُوجَ مِثْلُ هَذَا»   ، وَحَلَّقَ إِبْهَامَهُ بِالَّتِي تَلِيهَا، قَالَتْ: فَقُلْتُ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، أَنَهْلِكُ وَفِينَا الصَّالِحُونَ؟ قَالَ:   «نَعَمْ، إِذَا كَثُرَ الْخَبَثُ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Abū Idrīs al-Khawlānī: “I met Abū al-Dardāʾ, Shaddād ibn Aws, and ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit and retained reports from them, but I missed Muʿādh ibn Jabal. Yazīd ibn ʿUmayra told me that Muʿādh used to say at every gathering: ‘God is a just Judge; blessed is His name. The doubters are ruined. Ahead lie trials in which wealth will be abundant and the Quran made accessible to men and women, freemen and slaves, young and old. A man will soon read the Quran and say, “I have read it, yet why do people not follow me?” Then he will say, “They will not follow me until I introduce something else for them.” Beware of innovations, for what is invented is misguidance. Beware a wise man's error: Satan may place misguidance on a wise man's tongue, while a hypocrite may utter a true word.’ We asked how to recognize these. He said: ‘Avoid those obscure and questionable words from the wise man that make you say, “What is this?” Yet do not let that turn you entirely away from him, for he may return to the truth and accept it when he hears it. Truth has its own light.’”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٧٥٠ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِي إِدْرِيسَ الْخَوْلَانِيِّ، قَالَ: أَدْرَكْتُ أَبَا الدَّرْدَاءِ وَوَعَيْتُ عَنْهُ، وَأَدْرَكْتُ شَدَّادَ بْنَ أَوْسٍ وَوَعَيْتُ عَنْهُ، وَأَدْرَكْتُ عُبَادَةَ بْنَ الصَّامِتِ وَوَعَيْتُ عَنْهُ، وَفَاتَنِي مُعَاذُ بْنُ جَبَلٍ، فَأَخْبَرَنِي يَزِيدُ بْنُ عُمَيْرَةَ أَنَّهُ كَانَ يَقُولُ فِي كُلِّ مَجْلِسٍ يَجْلِسُهُ:   «§اللَّهُ حَكَمٌ قِسْطٌ، تَبَارَكَ اسْمُهُ، - [٣٦٤] - هَلَكَ الْمُرْتَابُونَ، مِنْ وَرَائِكُمْ فِتَنٌ يَكْثُرُ فِيهَا الْمَالُ، وَيُفْتَحُ فِيهَا الْقُرْآنُ حَتَّى يَأْخُذَهُ الرَّجُلُ وَالْمَرْأَةُ، وَالْحُرُّ وَالْعَبْدُ، وَالصَّغِيرُ وَالْكَبِيرُ، فَيُوشِكُ الرَّجُلُ أَنْ يَقْرَأَ الْقُرْآنَ، فَيَقُولَ: قَدْ قَرَأْتُ الْقُرْآنَ، فَمَا لِلنَّاسِ لَا يَتَّبِعُونِي وَقَدْ قَرَأْتُ الْقُرْآنَ؟ ثُمَّ يَقُولُ: مَا هُمْ بِمُتَّبِعِيَّ حَتَّى أَبْتَدِعَ لَهُمْ غَيْرَهُ، فَإِيَّاكُمْ وَمَا ابْتُدِعَ، فَإِنَّ مَا ابْتُدِعَ ضَلَالَةٌ، اتَّقُوا زَيْغَ الْحَكِيمِ، فَإنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ يُلْقِي عَلَى فِي الْحَكِيمِ الضَّلَالَةَ، وَيُلْقِي لِلْمُنَافِقِ كَلِمَةَ الْحَقِّ، قَالَ: قُلْنَا: وَمَا يُدْرِينَا يَرْحَمُكَ اللَّهُ أَنَّ الْمُنَافِقَ يُلْقِي كَلِمَةَ الْحَقِّ، وَأَنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ يُلْقِي عَلَى فِي الْحَكِيمِ الضَّلَالَةَ؟ قَالَ: اجْتَنِبُوا مِنْ كَلَامِ الْحَكِيمِ كُلَّ مُتَشَابِهٍ، الَّذِي إِذَا سَمِعْتَهُ قُلْتَ: مَا هَذَا؟ وَلَا يُثْنِيكَ ذَلِكَ عَنْهُ، فَإِنَّهُ لَعَلَّهُ أَنْ يُرَاجِعَ وَيُلْقِي الْحَقَّ إِذَا سَمِعَهُ، فَإنَّ عَلَى الْحَقِّ نُورًا»

records.raw_text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Abū Idrīs al-Khawlānī: “I met Abū al-Dardāʾ, Shaddād ibn Aws, and ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit and retained reports from them, but I missed Muʿādh ibn Jabal. Yazīd ibn ʿUmayra told me that Muʿādh used to say at every gathering: ‘God is a just Judge; blessed is His name. The doubters are ruined. Ahead lie trials in which wealth will be abundant and the Quran made accessible to men and women, freemen and slaves, young and old. A man will soon read the Quran and say, “I have read it, yet why do people not follow me?” Then he will say, “They will not follow me until I introduce something else for them.” Beware of innovations, for what is invented is misguidance. Beware a wise man's error: Satan may place misguidance on a wise man's tongue, while a hypocrite may utter a true word.’ We asked how to recognize these. He said: ‘Avoid those obscure and questionable words from the wise man that make you say, “What is this?” Yet do not let that turn you entirely away from him, for he may return to the truth and accept it when he hears it. Truth has its own light.’”

records.display_matn_ar: أَدْرَكْتُ أَبَا الدَّرْدَاءِ وَوَعَيْتُ عَنْهُ، وَأَدْرَكْتُ شَدَّادَ بْنَ أَوْسٍ وَوَعَيْتُ عَنْهُ، وَأَدْرَكْتُ عُبَادَةَ بْنَ الصَّامِتِ وَوَعَيْتُ عَنْهُ، وَفَاتَنِي مُعَاذُ بْنُ جَبَلٍ، فَأَخْبَرَنِي يَزِيدُ بْنُ عُمَيْرَةَ أَنَّهُ كَانَ يَقُولُ فِي كُلِّ مَجْلِسٍ يَجْلِسُهُ:   «§اللَّهُ حَكَمٌ قِسْطٌ، تَبَارَكَ اسْمُهُ، هَلَكَ الْمُرْتَابُونَ، مِنْ وَرَائِكُمْ فِتَنٌ يَكْثُرُ فِيهَا الْمَالُ، وَيُفْتَحُ فِيهَا الْقُرْآنُ حَتَّى يَأْخُذَهُ الرَّجُلُ وَالْمَرْأَةُ، وَالْحُرُّ وَالْعَبْدُ، وَالصَّغِيرُ وَالْكَبِيرُ، فَيُوشِكُ الرَّجُلُ أَنْ يَقْرَأَ الْقُرْآنَ، فَيَقُولَ: قَدْ قَرَأْتُ الْقُرْآنَ، فَمَا لِلنَّاسِ لَا يَتَّبِعُونِي وَقَدْ قَرَأْتُ الْقُرْآنَ؟ ثُمَّ يَقُولُ: مَا هُمْ بِمُتَّبِعِيَّ حَتَّى أَبْتَدِعَ لَهُمْ غَيْرَهُ، فَإِيَّاكُمْ وَمَا ابْتُدِعَ، فَإِنَّ مَا ابْتُدِعَ ضَلَالَةٌ، اتَّقُوا زَيْغَ الْحَكِيمِ، فَإنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ يُلْقِي عَلَى فِي الْحَكِيمِ الضَّلَالَةَ، وَيُلْقِي لِلْمُنَافِقِ كَلِمَةَ الْحَقِّ، قَالَ: قُلْنَا: وَمَا يُدْرِينَا يَرْحَمُكَ اللَّهُ أَنَّ الْمُنَافِقَ يُلْقِي كَلِمَةَ الْحَقِّ، وَأَنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ يُلْقِي عَلَى فِي الْحَكِيمِ الضَّلَالَةَ؟ قَالَ: اجْتَنِبُوا مِنْ كَلَامِ الْحَكِيمِ كُلَّ مُتَشَابِهٍ، الَّذِي إِذَا سَمِعْتَهُ قُلْتَ: مَا هَذَا؟ وَلَا يُثْنِيكَ ذَلِكَ عَنْهُ، فَإِنَّهُ لَعَلَّهُ أَنْ يُرَاجِعَ وَيُلْقِي الْحَقَّ إِذَا سَمِعَهُ، فَإنَّ عَلَى الْحَقِّ نُورًا»
records.display_isnad_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Abū Idrīs al-Khawlānī: “
records.display_matn_en: I met Abū al-Dardāʾ, Shaddād ibn Aws, and ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit and retained reports from them, but I missed Muʿādh ibn Jabal. Yazīd ibn ʿUmayra told me that Muʿādh used to say at every gathering: ‘God is a just Judge; blessed is His name. The doubters are ruined. Ahead lie trials in which wealth will be abundant and the Quran made accessible to men and women, freemen and slaves, young and old. A man will soon read the Quran and say, “I have read it, yet why do people not follow me?” Then he will say, “They will not follow me until I introduce something else for them.” Beware of innovations, for what is invented is misguidance. Beware a wise man's error: Satan may place misguidance on a wise man's tongue, while a hypocrite may utter a true word.’ We asked how to recognize these. He said: ‘Avoid those obscure and questionable words from the wise man that make you say, “What is this?” Yet do not let that turn you entirely away from him, for he may return to the truth and accept it when he hears it. Truth has its own light.’”

records.display_matn_en: ʿUmar asked who could tell them about tribulations. Ḥudhayfa offered, and ʿUmar remarked on his boldness. Ḥudhayfa first said: “A man's trial concerning his family and property is expiated by charity, prayer, and fasting.” ʿUmar said that was not what he meant. Ḥudhayfa asked whether he meant trials surging like the sea. ʿUmar said yes. Ḥudhayfa said: “Between you and them is a closed door.” Asked whether it would be opened or broken down, he said: “Broken down.” ʿUmar replied: “Then it will not be closed again.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, that the Prophet ﷺ asked his wives: “Which of you will have the dogs of a certain water source bark at her?”—meaning al-Ḥawʾab. records.display_matn_ar: قَالَ ابْنُ الزُّبَيْرِ: مَا شَيْءٌ كَانَ يُحَدِّثُنَاهُ كَعْبٌ إِلَّا قَدْ أَتَى عَلَى مَا قَالَ إِلَّا قَوْلَهُ:   «إِنَّ §فَتَى ثَقِيفٍ يَقْتُلُنِي وَهَذَا رَأْسُهُ بَيْنَ يَدَيَّ»   - يَعْنِي الْمُخْتَارَ - قَالَ ابْنُ سِيرِينَ: وَلَا يَشْعُرُ أَنَّ أَبَا مُحَمَّدٍ قَدْ خُبِئَ لَهُ. يَعْنِي الْحَجَّاجَ

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from several members of a household or clan, from Hind daughter of al-Muhallab, whom ʿIkrima used to visit. One day ʿIkrima said: “I will tell you something I have told nobody else: ‘This authority will remain with the Umayyads so long as two spears are not raised against one another among them. Once two of their spears clash, it will leave them and never return.’”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٧٥٦ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنِي غَيْرُ وَاحِدٍ مِنَ الْحَيِّ، عَنْ هِنْدَ بِنْتِ الْمُهَلَّبِ، قَالَ: وَكَانَ عِكْرِمَةُ يَدْخُلُ عَلَيْهَا قَالَ: فَقَالَ عِكْرِمَةُ يَوْمًا: لَأُحَدِّثَنَّكِ حَدِيثًا مَا حَدَّثْتُهُ أَحَدًا غَيْرَكِ:   «§لَا يَزَالُ هَذَا الْأَمْرُ فِي بَنِي أُمَيَّةَ مَا لَمْ يَخْتَلِفْ بَيْنَهُمْ رُمْحَانِ، فَإِذَا اخْتَلَفَ بَيْنَهُمْ رُمْحَانِ خَرَجَتْ مِنْهُمْ فَلَمْ تَرْجِعْ فِيهِمْ أَبَدًا»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn: “While I was in Kūfa before Ibn al-Zubayr's conflict, ʿAbīda told me: ‘Finish your business, then return to your home region; something momentous is about to happen in the land.’ I asked what he recommended. He said: ‘Stay in your house.’ When I returned to Basra, Ibn al-Zubayr's civil strife erupted.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٧٥٧ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنِ ابْنِ سِيرِينَ، قَالَ: قَالَ لِي عَبِيدَةُ وَأَنَا بِالْكُوفَةِ، وَذَلِكَ قَبْلَ فِتْنَةِ ابْنِ الزُّبَيْرِ:   «§افْرُغْ مِنْ ضَيْعَتِكَ، ثُمَّ انْحَدِرْ إِلَى مِصْرِكَ، فَإِنَّهُ سَيَحْدُثُ فِي الْأَرْضِ حَدَثٌ»   ، قَالَ: قُلْتُ: فَبِمَ تَأْمُرُنِي؟ قَالَ:   «تَلْزَمُ بَيْتَكَ»   قَالَ: فَلَمَّا قَدِمْتُ الْبَصْرَةَ وَقَعَتْ فِتْنَةُ ابْنِ الزُّبَيْرِ

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from ʿĀṣim, from Abū al-ʿĀliya al-Riyāḥī, who used to say: “Learn Islam and, once you have learned it, do not turn away from it. Hold to the straight path, for the straight path is Islam; do not deviate to right or left. Hold to the practice of your Prophet ﷺ and his Companions before they killed their companion and did what they did. I had read the Quran fifteen years before they killed their companion and did what they did. Beware of matters that sow enmity and hatred among people.” The source has a textual ellipsis before the quotation.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from someone who heard Ibn Sīrīn: The Prophet ﷺ foretold an approaching civil war. A man with his head covered passed by, and he said: “That man will be in the right at that time.” Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra grasped the man's arm, turned his face toward the Prophet ﷺ, and asked whether he meant this man. He said yes. When the man's head covering was removed, he was ʿUthmān.

records.display_matn_ar: ذَكَرَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فِتْنَةً فَقَرَّبَهَا، فَمَرَّ رَجُلٌ مُقَنَّعٌ رَأْسُهُ، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§هَذَا يَوْمَئِذٍ عَلَى الْحَقِّ»   ، قَالَ: فَقَامَ إِلَيْهِ كَعْبُ بْنُ عُجْرَةَ فَأَخَذَ بِعَضُدِهِ، ثُمَّ أَقْبَلَ بِوَجْهِهِ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَقَالَ: هُوَ ذَا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ؟ قَالَ:   «نَعَمْ»   ، قَالَ: وَكَشَفَ عَنْ رَأْسِهِ، فَإِذَا هُوَ عُثْمَانُ
records.display_isnad_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from someone who heard Ibn Sīrīn:
records.display_matn_en: The Prophet ﷺ foretold an approaching civil war. A man with his head covered passed by, and he said: “That man will be in the right at that time.” Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra grasped the man's arm, turned his face toward the Prophet ﷺ, and asked whether he meant this man. He said yes. When the man's head covering was removed, he was ʿUthmān.

records.text_en: Maʿmar transmitted from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd God or ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yazīd—Maʿmar was uncertain which—from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī: A man asked which people were best. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “A believer who struggles with his life and wealth in God's cause.” Asked who came next, he said: “A man living apart in a mountain valley, worshipping his Lord and sparing others his evil.”

records.text_en: Maʿmar transmitted from Ibn Khuthaym, from Nāfiʿ ibn Sarjis, from Abū Hurayra: “People, a trial like fragments of a dark night has overshadowed you. Safest from it is the owner of sheep living on their milk, or a man beyond the mountain passes holding his horse's reins and living by his sword.”

records.raw_text_en: Maʿmar transmitted from Ibn Khuthaym, from Nāfiʿ ibn Sarjis, from Abū Hurayra: “People, a trial like fragments of a dark night has overshadowed you. Safest from it is the owner of sheep living on their milk, or a man beyond the mountain passes holding his horse's reins and living by his sword.”

records.text_en: Maʿmar transmitted from al-Zuhrī, from Sinān ibn Abī Sinān al-Dīlī, from Abū Wāqid al-Laythī: “We went out with the Messenger of God ﷺ before Ḥunayn and passed a lote tree. We said: ‘Messenger of God, give us a Dhāt Anwāṭ like the unbelievers have,’ for they used to hang their weapons on such a tree and gather reverently around it. The Prophet ﷺ said: ‘God is greatest! This is like the Children of Israel saying to Moses, “Make for us a god as they have gods” [Q 7:138]. You will follow the paths of those who came before you.’”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٧٦٣ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ سِنَانِ بْنِ أَبِي سِنَانٍ الدِّيلِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِي وَاقِدٍ اللَّيْثِيِّ، قَالَ: خَرَجْنَا مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَبْلَ حُنَيْنٍ فَمَرَرْنَا بِالسِّدْرَةِ، فَقُلْنَا: أَيْ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، اجْعَلْ لَنَا هَذِهِ ذَاتَ أَنْوَاطٍ كَمَا لِلْكُفَّارِ ذَاتُ أَنْوَاطٍ، وَكَانَ الْكُفَّارُ يَنُوطُونَ سِلَاحَهُمْ بِسِدْرَةٍ، وَيَعْكُفُونَ حَوْلَهَا، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، هَذَا كَمَا قَالَتْ بَنُو إِسْرَائِيلَ لِمُوسَى:  {اجْعَلْ لَنَا إِلَهًا كَمَا لَهُمْ آلِهَةٌ}   [الأعراف: ١٣٨]  إِنَّكُمْ تَرْكَبُونَ سُنَنَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ»

records.text_en: Maʿmar transmitted from Zayd ibn Aslam, from an unnamed man, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “You will follow the ways of the Children of Israel span by span and cubit by cubit. If a man among them entered a lizard's hole, you would follow him.”

records.text_en: Maʿmar transmitted from Qatāda that Ḥudhayfa said: “You will imitate the ways of the Children of Israel like one feather matching another, or one sandal strap another. If a man among them did such-and-such, someone in this community will do the same.” Someone pointed out that there had been apes and pigs among the Children of Israel. He replied: “There will be apes and pigs in this community too.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٧٦٥ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، أَنَّ حُذَيْفَةَ، قَالَ:   «§لَتَرْكَبُنَّ سُنَنَ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ حَذْوَ الْقُذَّةِ بِالْقُذَّةِ، وَحَذْوَ الشِّرَاكِ بِالشِّرَاكِ، حَتَّى لَوْ فَعَلَ رَجُلٌ مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ كَذَا وَكَذَا، فَعَلَهُ رَجُلٌ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْأُمَّةِ»   ، فَقَالَ لَهُ رَجُلٌ: قَدْ كَانَ فِي بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ قِرَدَةٌ وَخَنَازِيرُ، قَالَ:   «وَهَذِهِ الْأُمَّةُ سَيَكُونُ فِيهَا قِرَدَةٌ وَخَنَازِيرَ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn, from ʿUqba ibn Aws, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ: “Two factions will fight over a call of the age of ignorance when a ruler—or tribe—emerges. Even the party that prevails will be humiliated. Its enemy will covet what it has, and it will plunge headlong into the Fire.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Abū Salama, from Abū Hurayra: “I know of a trial soon to come, beside which the one before it will seem no greater than a rabbit's leap. I know the way out of it.” Asked what it was, he replied: “I will restrain my hand until someone comes to kill me.”

records.text_en: Maʿmar said an elder among his people related: A woman went to one of the Prophet's ﷺ wives and asked her to pray that God restore movement to her hand. Asked what had happened, she explained: “My father was wealthy and extremely charitable. My mother gave almost nothing. Once, after we slaughtered a cow, she gave a poor person a piece of fat in his hand and a scrap of cloth. Both parents died. In a dream I saw my father beside a river giving people drink. I went looking for my mother and found her naked except for that cloth, with the fat in her hand, striking it against the other hand and sucking the residue, crying that she was thirsty. I fetched a vessel from my father and gave her water. Someone standing nearby called: ‘May God paralyze the hand of whoever gave her drink!’ I woke to find my hand paralyzed.” [An ellipsis interrupts the source narrative before the curse.]
records.text_ar: ٢٠٧٦٨ - قَالَ مَعْمَرٌ: وَحَدَّثَنِي شَيْخٌ لَنَا أَنَّ امْرَأَةً جَاءَتْ إِلَى بَعْضِ أَزْوَاجِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، فَقَالَتْ لَهَا: ادْعِي اللَّهَ أَنْ يُطْلِقَ لِي يَدِي، قَالَتْ: §وَمَا شَأْنُ يَدِكِ؟ قَالَتْ: كَانَ لِي أَبَوَانِ، فَكَانَ أَبِي كَثِيرَ الْمَالِ كَثِيرَ الْمَعْرُوفِ كَثِيرَ الْفَضْلِ - أَوْ قَالَتْ: كَثِيرَ الصَّدَقَةِ - وَلَمْ يَكُنْ عِنْدَ أُمِّي مِنْ ذَلِكَ شَيْءٌ، لَمْ أَرَهَا تَصَدَّقَتْ بِشَيْءٍ قَطُّ، غَيْرَ أَنَّا نَحَرْنَا بَقَرَةً، فَأَعْطَتْ مِسْكِينًا شَحْمَةً فِي يَدِهِ، وَأَلْبَسَتْهُ خِرْقَةً، فَمَاتَتْ أُمِّي، وَمَاتَ أَبِي، فَرَأَيْتُ أَبِي عَلَى نَهْرٍ يَسْقِي النَّاسَ، فَقُلْتُ: يَا أَبَتَاهُ، هَلْ رَأَيْتَ أُمِّي؟ قَالَ لَا، أَوَمَاتَتْ؟ قَالَتْ: قُلْتُ: نَعَمْ، قَالَتْ: فَذَهَبْتُ أَلْتَمِسُهَا فَوَجَدْتُهَا قَائِمَةً عُرْيَانَةً لَيْسَ عَلَيْهَا إِلَّا تِلْكَ الْخِرْقَةُ، وَتِلْكَ الشَّحْمَةُ فِي - [٣٧١] - يَدِهَا وَهِيَ تَضْرِبُ بِهَا عَلَى يَدِهَا الْأُخْرَى، وَتَمَصُّ أَثَرَهَا، وَتَقُولُ: يَا عَطَشَاهُ، فَقُلْتُ: يَا أُمَّهْ، أَلَا أَسْقِيكِ؟ قَالَتْ: بَلَى، فَذَهَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي، فَأَخَذْتُ إِنَاءً مِنْ عِنْدِهِ، فَسَقَيْتُهَا فِيهِ.. . مَنْ كَانَ عِنْدَهَا قَائِمًا، فَقَالَ: مَنْ سَقَاهَا أَشَلَّ اللَّهُ يَدَهُ، قَالَتْ: فَاسْتَيْقَظْتُ وَقَدْ شَلَّتْ يَدِي "

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, who raised the report to the Prophet ﷺ: “There will be discord when a caliph dies. A man will leave Medina for Mecca. The people will bring him from his house against his wishes and pledge allegiance between the Corner and the Station. An army from Syria will march against him and be swallowed up in al-Baydāʾ. Groups from Iraq and the abdāl of Syria will then come to pledge allegiance to him. He will bring forth treasures and distribute wealth, and Islam will settle firmly upon the earth. He will live in that condition seven years—or, he said, nine years.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٧٦٩ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، يَرْفَعُهُ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ:   «§يَكُونُ اخْتِلَافٌ عِنْدَ مَوْتِ خَلِيفَةٍ، فَيَخْرُجُ رَجُلٌ مِنَ الْمَدِينَةِ، فَيَأْتِي مَكَّةَ، فَيَسْتَخْرِجُهُ النَّاسُ مِنْ بَيْتِهِ وَهُوَ كَارِهٌ، فَيُبَايِعُونَهُ بَيْنَ الرُّكْنِ وَالْمَقَامِ، فَيُبْعَثُ إِلَيْهِ جَيْشٌ مِنَ الشَّامِ، حَتَّى إِذَا كَانُوا بِالْبَيْدَاءِ خُسِفَ بِهِمْ، فَيَأْتِيهِ عَصَائِبُ الْعِرَاقِ، وَأَبْدَالُ الشَّامِ فَيُبَايِعُونَهُ، فَيَسْتَخْرِجُ الْكُنُوزَ، وَيَقْسِمُ الْمَالَ، وَيُلْقِي الْإِسْلَامُ بِجِرَانِهِ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ، يَعِيشُ فِي ذَلِكَ سَبْعَ سِنِينَ، أَوْ قَالَ: تِسْعَ سِنِينَ»

records.text_en: Maʿmar transmitted from Abū Hārūn, from Muʿāwiya ibn Qurra, from Abū al-Ṣiddīq al-Nājī, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī: “The Messenger of God ﷺ mentioned affliction that would befall this community until a man found no shelter from oppression. Then God would raise up a man from my descendants and household who would fill the earth with equity as it had been filled with injustice and oppression. Those in heaven and on earth would be pleased with him. The sky would pour down all its rain, and the earth bring out its abundance, until the living would long for the dead [to enjoy it]. He would live in that condition seven, eight, or nine years.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamra, from ʿAlī: “The earth will be filled with injustice and oppression until no one can even say ‘God, God’ to seek His help. records.text_en: Maʿmar transmitted from Ismāʿīl ibn Umayya, from a man whom he thought was Saʿīd, from Abū Hurayra, raising the report: “Woe to the Arabs because of an evil that has drawn near around the year sixty! Trust will be treated as spoils, charitable dues as debts, testimony based on favoritism, and judgment according to desire.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān: People complained to Ibn Masʿūd that the Euphrates might break through its banks and asked him to send someone to dam it. He said: “We shall not dam it. By God, a time will come when you will seek a basin full of water and find none. Every body of water will return to its source, and whatever water and Muslims remain will be in Syria.”

records.text_en: The transmitters recited to ʿAbd al-Razzāq from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, from al-Ḥasan, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The Hour will not come until mountains move from their places and you witness the tremendous event that you never used to see.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from Hammām ibn Munabbih, who heard Abū Hurayra report the Messenger of God ﷺ saying: “The Hour will not come until you fight Khūz and Kirmān, non-Arab peoples with reddish faces, flattened noses, small eyes, faces like hammered shields, and shoes made of hair.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from someone who heard al-Ḥasan say: “Among the signs of the Hour are that knowledge becomes prominent, merchants increase, and people fight a group wearing shoes of hair with faces like hammered shields.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, who said that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The Hour will not come until a group is swallowed into the earth in the sheep pastures, nor until a man of much wealth and many children is swallowed into the earth.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٧٨٤ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§لَا تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ حَتَّى يُخْسَفَ بِقَوْمٍ فِي مَرَاتِعِ الْغَنَمِ، وَلَا تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ حَتَّى يُخْسَفَ بِرَجُلٍ كَثِيرِ الْمَالِ وَالْوَلَدِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from Abū Isḥāq, from an unnamed man, from Ibn Masʿūd: “In the year thirty-five, something momentous will happen. If you perish, that would be understandable; if you survive, perhaps [there is hope]. In the year seventy you will see things you disapprove of.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٧٨٥ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنْ رَجُلٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، قَالَ:   «§إِذَا كَانَتْ سَنَةُ خَمْسٍ وَثَلَاثِينَ حَدَثَ أَمْرٌ عَظِيمٌ، فَإِنْ تَهْلِكُوا فَبِالْحَرَى، وَإِنْ تَنْجُوا فَعَسَى، وَإِذَا كَانَتْ سَبْعِينَ رَأَيْتُمْ مَا تُنْكِرُونَ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, from Shahr ibn Ḥawshab: “When allegiance to Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiya reached us, I decided to depart for Syria to avoid the trouble of that pledge. I went and heard of a gathering where Nawf spoke. I arrived and saw a man with damaged eyes in a striped cloak: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ. When Nawf saw him he stopped speaking. ʿAbd Allāh asked him to continue, but Nawf said that as a Companion of the Messenger ﷺ he had a greater right to speak. ʿAbd Allāh said: ‘These rulers have prevented us from transmitting reports.’ Nawf insisted that he relate something he heard directly. ʿAbd Allāh said that he heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘There will be another emigration after the first, when the best people migrate to the place Abraham migrated. Only the worst inhabitants of the earth will remain, cast out by their lands and abhorred by God. Fire will gather them along with apes and pigs; it will stay with them overnight where they stay, rest with them where they rest, and devour whoever falls behind.’”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٧٩٠ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، عَنْ شَهْرِ بْنِ حَوْشَبٍ، قَالَ: لَمَّا جَاءَتْنَا بَيْعَةُ يَزِيدَ بْنِ مُعَاوِيَةَ قُلْتُ: لَوْ خَرَجْتُ إِلَى الشَّامِ فَتَنَحَّيْتُ مِنْ شَرِّ هَذِهِ الْبَيْعَةِ، فَخَرَجْتُ حَتَّى قَدِمْتُ الشَّامَ، - [٣٧٧] - فَأُخْبِرْتُ بِمَقَامٍ يَقُومُهُ نَوْفٌ، فَجِئْتُهُ، فَإِذَا رَجُلٌ فَاسِدُ الْعَيْنَيْنِ، عَلَيْهِ خَمِيصَةٌ، فَإِذَا هُوَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عَمْرِو بْنِ الْعَاصِ، فَلَمَّا رَآهُ نَوْفٌ أَمْسَكَ عَنِ الْحَدِيثِ، فَقَالَ لَهُ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: حَدِّثْ مَا كُنْتَ تُحَدِّثُ بِهِ، قَالَ: أَنْتَ أَحَقُّ بِالْحَدِيثِ مِنِّي، أَنْتَ صَاحِبُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، فَقَالَ: إِنَّ هَؤُلَاءِ قَدْ مَنَعُونَا عَنِ الْحَدِيثِ - يَعْنِي الْأُمَرَاءَ -، قَالَ: أَعْزِمُ عَلَيْكَ إِلَّا حَدَّثْتَنَا حَدِيثًا سَمِعْتَهُ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَقُولُ:   «§إِنَّهَا سَتَكُونُ هِجْرَةٌ بَعْدَ هِجْرَةٍ لَخِيَارِ النَّاسِ إِلَى مُهَاجَرِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، لَا يَبْقَى فِي الْأَرْضِ إِلَّا شِرَارُ أَهْلِهَا، تَلْفِظُهُمْ أَرْضُهُمْ، تَقْذَرُهُمْ نَفْسُ اللَّهِ، تَحْشُرُهُمُ النَّارُ مَعَ الْقِرَدَةِ وَالْخَنَازِيرِ، تَبِيتُ مَعَهُمْ إِذَا بَاتُوا، وَتَقِيلُ مَعَهُمْ إِذَا قَالُوا، وَتَأْكُلُ مَنْ تَخَلَّفَ»

unnumbered_continuations.text_ar: قَالَ: وَسَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَقُولُ:   «§سَيَخْرُجُ أُنَاسٌ مِنْ أُمَّتِي مِنْ قِبَلِ الْمَشْرِقِ يَقْرَءُونَ الْقُرْآنَ لَا يُجَاوِزُ تَرَاقِيَهُمْ، كُلَّمَا خَرَجَ مِنْهَا قَرْنٌ قُطِعَ، كُلَّمَا خَرَجَ مِنْهَا قَرْنٌ قُطِعَ، حَتَّى عَدَدَهَا زِيَادَةً عَلَى عَشْرِ مَرَّاتٍ، كُلَّمَا خَرَجَ مِنْهَا قَرْنٌ قُطِعَ، حَتَّى يَخْرُجَ الدَّجَّالُ فِي بَقِيَّتِهِمْ»
unnumbered_continuations.text_en: He also said: “I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: People will emerge from my community from the east, reciting the Quran though it does not pass beyond their throats.” [The source continuation is attached to report 20790.]

records.display_matn_ar: لَمَّا جَاءَتْنَا بَيْعَةُ يَزِيدَ بْنِ مُعَاوِيَةَ قُلْتُ: لَوْ خَرَجْتُ إِلَى الشَّامِ فَتَنَحَّيْتُ مِنْ شَرِّ هَذِهِ الْبَيْعَةِ، فَخَرَجْتُ حَتَّى قَدِمْتُ الشَّامَ، فَأُخْبِرْتُ بِمَقَامٍ يَقُومُهُ نَوْفٌ، فَجِئْتُهُ، فَإِذَا رَجُلٌ فَاسِدُ الْعَيْنَيْنِ، عَلَيْهِ خَمِيصَةٌ، فَإِذَا هُوَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عَمْرِو بْنِ الْعَاصِ، فَلَمَّا رَآهُ نَوْفٌ أَمْسَكَ عَنِ الْحَدِيثِ، فَقَالَ لَهُ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: حَدِّثْ مَا كُنْتَ تُحَدِّثُ بِهِ، قَالَ: أَنْتَ أَحَقُّ بِالْحَدِيثِ مِنِّي، أَنْتَ صَاحِبُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، فَقَالَ: إِنَّ هَؤُلَاءِ قَدْ مَنَعُونَا عَنِ الْحَدِيثِ - يَعْنِي الْأُمَرَاءَ -، قَالَ: أَعْزِمُ عَلَيْكَ إِلَّا حَدَّثْتَنَا حَدِيثًا سَمِعْتَهُ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَقُولُ:   «§إِنَّهَا سَتَكُونُ هِجْرَةٌ بَعْدَ هِجْرَةٍ لَخِيَارِ النَّاسِ إِلَى مُهَاجَرِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، لَا يَبْقَى فِي الْأَرْضِ إِلَّا شِرَارُ أَهْلِهَا، تَلْفِظُهُمْ أَرْضُهُمْ، تَقْذَرُهُمْ نَفْسُ اللَّهِ، تَحْشُرُهُمُ النَّارُ مَعَ الْقِرَدَةِ وَالْخَنَازِيرِ، تَبِيتُ مَعَهُمْ إِذَا بَاتُوا، وَتَقِيلُ مَعَهُمْ إِذَا قَالُوا، وَتَأْكُلُ مَنْ تَخَلَّفَ»
records.display_isnad_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, from Shahr ibn Ḥawshab: “
records.display_matn_en: When allegiance to Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiya reached us, I decided to depart for Syria to avoid the trouble of that pledge. I went and heard of a gathering where Nawf spoke. I arrived and saw a man with damaged eyes in a striped cloak: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ. When Nawf saw him he stopped speaking. ʿAbd Allāh asked him to continue, but Nawf said that as a Companion of the Messenger ﷺ he had a greater right to speak. ʿAbd Allāh said: ‘These rulers have prevented us from transmitting reports.’ Nawf insisted that he relate something he heard directly. ʿAbd Allāh said that he heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘There will be another emigration after the first, when the best people migrate to the place Abraham migrated. Only the worst inhabitants of the earth will remain, cast out by their lands and abhorred by God. Fire will gather them along with apes and pigs; it will stay with them overnight where they stay, rest with them where they rest, and devour whoever falls behind.’”

records.display_matn_ar: عَشْرُ آيَاتٍ بَيْنَ يَدَيِ السَّاعَةِ: خَسْفٌ بِالْمَشْرِقِ، وَخَسْفٌ بِالْمَغْرِبِ، وَخَسْفٌ بِحِجَازِ الْعَرَبِ، وَالرَّابِعَةُ الدَّجَّالُ، وَالْخَامِسَةُ عِيسَى، وَالسَّادِسَةُ دَابَّةُ الْأَرْضِ، وَالسَّابِعَةُ الدُّخَانُ، وَالثَّامِنَةُ خُرُوجُ يَأْجُوجَ وَمَأْجُوجَ، وَالتَّاسِعَةُ رِيحٌ بَارِدَةٌ طَيِّبَةٌ يُرْسِلُهَا اللَّهُ فَيَقْبِضُ بِتِلْكَ الرِّيحِ نَفْسَ كُلِّ مُؤْمِنٍ، وَالْعَاشِرَةُ طُلُوعُ الشَّمْسِ مِنْ مَغْرِبِهَا»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from Qatāda: “It reached us that suffering will grow so severe that a man passing his brother's grave will say, ‘Would that I were in your place,’ not because he longs to meet God but because of the severity of the troubles he sees.”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٧٩٤ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، قَالَ: بَلَغَنَا أَنَّهُ   «§يَشْتَدُّ الْبَلَاءُ حَتَّى يَمُرَّ الرَّجُلُ بِقَبْرِ أَخِيهِ فَيَقُولَ: يَا لَيْتَنِي مَكَانَكَ، لَيْسَ بِهِ شَوقٌ إِلَى لِقَاءِ اللَّهِ، وَلَكِنْ لِمَا يَرَى مِنْ شِدَّةِ الْبَلَاءِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Abū Hurayra, who said that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The Hour will not come until the women of Daws sway their buttocks around Dhū al-Khalaṣa,” an idol which Daws worshipped in the age of ignorance at Tabāla. Maʿmar added that he heard someone other than al-Zuhrī say that a building had since been built upon that stone.
records.text_ar: ٢٠٧٩٥ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنِ ابْنِ الْمُسَيِّبِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§لَا تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ حَتَّى تَضْطَرِبَ أَلْيَاتُ نِسَاءِ دَوْسٍ حَوْلَ ذِي الْخَلَصَةِ، وَكَانَتْ صَنَمًا تَعْبُدُهَا دَوْسٌ فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ بِتَبَالَةَ»   قَالَ مَعْمَرٌ:   «وَسَمِعْتُ غَيْرَ الزُّهْرِيِّ يَقُولُ: عَلَى ذَلِكَ الْحَجَرِ بَيْتٌ بُنِيَ الْيَوْمَ»

records.display_isnad_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Abū Hurayra, who said that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “
records.display_matn_en: The Hour will not come until the women of Daws sway their buttocks around Dhū al-Khalaṣa,” an idol which Daws worshipped in the age of ignorance at Tabāla. Maʿmar added that he heard someone other than al-Zuhrī say that a building had since been built upon that stone.

records.text_en: Maʿmar transmitted from al-Zuhrī, who said Anas ibn Mālik told him: “The Messenger of God ﷺ came out at midday, prayed the noon prayer, then mounted the pulpit and spoke of the Hour and great events preceding it. He said: ‘Anyone who wishes to ask me something should ask. By God, whatever you ask, I will answer while standing here.’ People wept, and he repeatedly said: ‘Ask me.’ A man stood and asked where he would enter; the Prophet ﷺ said: ‘The Fire.’ ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥudhāfa asked who his father was. The Prophet ﷺ said: ‘Your father is Ḥudhāfa.’ He continued inviting questions, until ʿUmar knelt and said: ‘We are content with God as Lord, Islam as religion, and Muḥammad ﷺ as Messenger.’ The Prophet ﷺ fell silent, then said: ‘By Him in whose hand is my soul, Paradise and the Fire were shown to me just now across this wall while I was praying. I have never seen anything like what I saw today of good and evil.’”
records.text_ar: ٢٠٧٩٦ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنِي أَنَسُ بْنُ مَالِكٍ: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ خَرَجَ حِينَ زَاغَتِ الشَّمْسُ وَصَلَّى الظُّهْرَ، فَلَمَّا سَلَّمَ قَامَ عَلَى الْمِنْبَرِ فَذَكَرَ فِي السَّاعَةِ، وَذَكَرَ أَنَّ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ أُمُورًا عِظَامًا، ثُمَّ قَالَ:   «مَنْ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يَسْأَلَ عَنْ شَيْءٍ فَلْيَسْأَلْ عَنْهُ، فَوَاللَّهِ لَا تَسْأَلُونِي عَنْ شَيْءٍ إِلَّا حَدَّثْتُكُمْ بِهِ مَا دُمْتُ فِي مَقَامِي هَذَا»   قَالَ أَنَسٌ: فَأَكْثَرَ النَّاسُ الْبُكَاءَ حِينَ سَمِعُوا ذَلِكَ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، وَأَكْثَرَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَنْ يَقُولَ:   «سَلُونِي سَلُونِي»   قَالَ: فَقَامَ إِلَيْهِ رَجُلٌ فَقَالَ: أَيْنَ مُدْخَلُهُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ؟ قَالَ:   «النَّارُ»   قَالَ: وَقَامَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ حُذَافَةَ فَقَالَ: مَنْ أَبِي يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ؟ - [٣٨٠] - قَالَ:   «أَبُوكَ حُذَافَةُ»   ، قَالَ: ثُمَّ أَكْثَرَ أَنْ يَقُولَ:   «سَلُونِي»   ، قَالَ فَبَرَكَ عُمَرُ عَلَى رُكْبَتَيْهِ وَقَالَ: رَضِينَا بِاللَّهِ رَبًّا، وَبِالْإِسْلَامِ دِينًا، وَبِمُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ رَسُولًا، قَالَ: فَسَكَتَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ حِينَ قَالَ عُمَرُ ذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «أَلَا وَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ §لَقَدْ عُرِضَتْ عَلَيَّ الْجَنَّةُ وَالنَّارُ آنِفًا فِي عُرْضِ هَذَا الْحَائِطِ، وَأَنَا أُصَلِّي فَلَمْ أَرَ كَالْيَوْمِ فِي الْخَيْرِ وَالشَّرِّ»

records.display_matn_ar: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ خَرَجَ حِينَ زَاغَتِ الشَّمْسُ وَصَلَّى الظُّهْرَ، فَلَمَّا سَلَّمَ قَامَ عَلَى الْمِنْبَرِ فَذَكَرَ فِي السَّاعَةِ، وَذَكَرَ أَنَّ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ أُمُورًا عِظَامًا، ثُمَّ قَالَ:   «مَنْ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يَسْأَلَ عَنْ شَيْءٍ فَلْيَسْأَلْ عَنْهُ، فَوَاللَّهِ لَا تَسْأَلُونِي عَنْ شَيْءٍ إِلَّا حَدَّثْتُكُمْ بِهِ مَا دُمْتُ فِي مَقَامِي هَذَا»   قَالَ أَنَسٌ: فَأَكْثَرَ النَّاسُ الْبُكَاءَ حِينَ سَمِعُوا ذَلِكَ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، وَأَكْثَرَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَنْ يَقُولَ:   «سَلُونِي سَلُونِي»   قَالَ: فَقَامَ إِلَيْهِ رَجُلٌ فَقَالَ: أَيْنَ مُدْخَلُهُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ؟ قَالَ:   «النَّارُ»   قَالَ: وَقَامَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ حُذَافَةَ فَقَالَ: مَنْ أَبِي يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ؟ قَالَ:   «أَبُوكَ حُذَافَةُ»   ، قَالَ: ثُمَّ أَكْثَرَ أَنْ يَقُولَ:   «سَلُونِي»   ، قَالَ فَبَرَكَ عُمَرُ عَلَى رُكْبَتَيْهِ وَقَالَ: رَضِينَا بِاللَّهِ رَبًّا، وَبِالْإِسْلَامِ دِينًا، وَبِمُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ رَسُولًا، قَالَ: فَسَكَتَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ حِينَ قَالَ عُمَرُ ذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «أَلَا وَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ §لَقَدْ عُرِضَتْ عَلَيَّ الْجَنَّةُ وَالنَّارُ آنِفًا فِي عُرْضِ هَذَا الْحَائِطِ، وَأَنَا أُصَلِّي فَلَمْ أَرَ كَالْيَوْمِ فِي الْخَيْرِ وَالشَّرِّ»

records.display_matn_en: The Messenger of God ﷺ came out at midday, prayed the noon prayer, then mounted the pulpit and spoke of the Hour and great events preceding it. He said: ‘Anyone who wishes to ask me something should ask. By God, whatever you ask, I will answer while standing here.’ People wept, and he repeatedly said: ‘Ask me.’ A man stood and asked where he would enter; the Prophet ﷺ said: ‘The Fire.’ ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥudhāfa asked who his father was. The Prophet ﷺ said: ‘Your father is Ḥudhāfa.’ He continued inviting questions, until ʿUmar knelt and said: ‘We are content with God as Lord, Islam as religion, and Muḥammad ﷺ as Messenger.’ The Prophet ﷺ fell silent, then said: ‘By Him in whose hand is my soul, Paradise and the Fire were shown to me just now across this wall while I was praying. I have never seen anything like what I saw today of good and evil.’”

records.text_en: Al-Zuhrī said that ʿUbayd God ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtba reported: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥudhāfa's mother said to him: “I have never seen a more undutiful son! Were you so certain that your mother had not done something people did in the age of ignorance, that you risked exposing her publicly?” ʿAbd Allāh replied: “By God, had he attributed me to a Black slave, I would have acknowledged him as my father.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakra: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said: “The Banū Qanṭūrāʾ will soon drive you out of Iraq.” I asked whether we would return. He said: “That is what you most wish to know! Yes, you will return and enjoy a measure of life there.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Maʿmar, from Jaʿfar ibn Burqān, from Yazīd ibn al-Aṣamm, from Abū Hurayra: “The Arabs will be driven back to their original homelands until their most valuable wealth consists of sheep and camels.” Abū Hurayra also spoke of a resourceful woman taking one or two water skins, or one or two larger leather vessels [the report ends here].

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq told us: Maʿmar told us, from Qatāda: Anas ibn Mālik said to us: "I will narrate to you a ḥadīth that you will find no one narrating to you after me. I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: 'Among the signs of the Hour are that knowledge will depart, ignorance will appear, wine will be drunk, fornication will spread, men will become few and women many, until one man will be the guardian of fifty women.'"
records.text_ar: ٢٠٨٠١ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، قَالَ: قَالَ لَنَا أَنَسُ بْنُ مَالِكٍ: لَأُحَدِّثَنَّكُمْ حَدِيثًا لَا تَجِدُونَ أَحَدًا يُحَدِّثُكُمُوهُ بَعْدِي، سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَقُولُ:   «إِنَّ §مِنْ أَشْرَاطِ السَّاعَةِ أَنْ يَذْهَبَ الْعِلْمُ، وَيَظْهَرَ الْجَهْلُ، وَيُشْرَبَ الْخَمْرُ، وَيَفْشُوَ الزِّنَا، وَيَقِلَّ الرِّجَالُ، وَيَكْثُرَ النِّسَاءُ، حَتَّى يَكُونَ قَيِّمَ خَمْسِينَ امْرَأَةً رَجُلٌ وَاحِدٌ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq, from Maʿmar, from Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Jaḥshī, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Dīnār, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Before the Hour there will be deceptive years in which the trustworthy will be accused of betrayal, the traitor will be trusted, and the *ruwaybiḍa* will speak on the affairs of the public." It was asked: "What is the *ruwaybiḍa*, Messenger of God?" He said: "The lowly among people."

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq told us: Maʿmar told us, from Suhayl ibn Abī Ṣāliḥ, from his father, from Abū Hurayra: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "The Euphrates will uncover a mountain of gold, and people will fight over it. Ninety out of every hundred (or he said ninety-nine) will be killed, and each of them will think that he will be the one to survive."

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilāba: Something was mentioned in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ that I do not remember, except that he said: "That will be at the time of the *naskh* of the Qurʾān." A man like a Bedouin said: "What is the *naskh* of the Qurʾān, Messenger of God?" The Prophet ﷺ was silent for a while, then said: "Like this: his community will pass away, and a people will remain, long of neck like this" (he brought his hands together, then stretched them apart, gesturing) "like cattle." They said: "Shall we not teach it to our sons and wives?" He said: "The Jews and Christians have read it."
records.text_ar: ٢٠٨٠٥ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ أَبِي قِلَابَةَ، قَالَ: ذُكِرَ شَيْءٌ عِنْدَ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ لَا أَحْفَظُهُ إِلَّا أَنَّهُ قَالَ:   «ذَاكَ عِنْدَ نَسْخِ الْقُرْآنِ»   قَالَ: فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ كَالْأَعْرَابِيِّ: مَا نَسْخُ الْقُرْآنِ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ؟ قَالَ: فَسَكَتَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ سَاعَةً، وَقَالَ:   «مِثْلُ هَذَا، §يَذْهَبُ أُمَّتُهُ وَيَبْقَى قَوْمٌ طُوَالُ الْأَعْنَاقِ هَكَذَا - وَجَمَعَ يَدَيْهِ ثُمَّ مَدَّهُمَا وَأَشَارَ - كَالْأَنْعَامِ»   قَالُوا: أَوَلَا نُقْرِئُهُ أَبْنَاءَنَا وَأَزْوَاجَنَا؟ قَالَ:   «قَدْ قَرَأَتِ الْيَهُودُ وَالنَّصَارَى»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Ṭāwus, from his father, who said: "A time will surely come upon people when the best of their dwellings will be that which the Messenger of God ﷺ forbade: the desert."

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq, from Maʿmar, from Ashʿath ibn ʿAbdullāh, from Shahr ibn Ḥawshab, from Abū Hurayra: A wolf came to a shepherd and took a sheep from his flock. The shepherd pursued it until he snatched the sheep back. The wolf climbed a hill, sat on its haunches and settled, and said: "You went after a provision God had provided for me, you took it, and then you snatched it from me?" The man said: "By God, I have never seen the like of today, a wolf speaking!" The wolf said: "More astonishing than this is a man among the palm groves between the two lava fields, who tells you of what has passed and of what will be after you." The man was a Jew. He came to the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ confirmed his story. Then the Prophet ﷺ said: "It is a sign among the signs before the Hour. A man is about to go out and not return until his sandals and his whip tell him what his family did after he left."
records.text_ar: ٢٠٨٠٨ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ أَشْعَثَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، عَنْ شَهْرِ بْنِ حَوْشَبٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ: جَاءَ ذِئْبٌ إِلَى رَاعِي غَنَمٍ فَأَخَذَ مِنْهَا شَاةً، فَطَلَبَهُ الرَّاعِي حَتَّى انْتَزَعَهَا مِنْهُ، قَالَ: صَعِدَ الذِّئْبُ عَلَى تَلٍّ فَأَقْعَى وَاسْتَقَرَّ، وَقَالَ: عَمَدْتَ إِلَى رِزْقٍ رَزَقَنِيهِ اللَّهُ أَخَذْتَهُ، ثُمَّ انْتَزَعْتَهُ مِنِّي؟ قَالَ الرَّجُلُ: تَاللَّهِ لَئِنْ رَأَيْتُ كَالْيَوْمِ ذِئْبًا يَتَكَلَّمُ، قَالَ الذِّئْبُ: أَعْجَبُ مِنْ هَذَا رَجُلٌ فِي النُّخَيْلَاتِ بَيْنَ الْحَرْثَيْنِ، يُخْبِرُكُمْ بِمَا مَضَى وَبِمَا هُوَ كَائِنٌ بَعْدَكُمْ، قَالَ: وَكَانَ الرَّجُلُ يَهُودِيًّا، فَجَاءَ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، فَصَدَّقَهُ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، ثُمَّ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «§إِنَّهَا - [٣٨٤] - أَمَارَةٌ مِنْ أَمَارَاتٍ بَيْنَ يَدَيِ السَّاعَةِ، قَدْ أَوْشَكَ الرَّجُلُ أَنْ يَخْرُجَ فَلَا يَرْجِعَ حَتَّى يُحَدِّثَهُ نَعْلَاهُ وَسَوْطُهُ بِمَا أَحْدَثَ أَهْلُهُ بَعْدَهُ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq, from Maʿmar, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, from Abū al-Kanūd, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: "The likeness of the world is that of a *thaghb*." We said: "What is a *thaghb*?" He said: "A pool whose clear water has gone and whose murk remains, so every believer loves death."

records.text_en:
ʿAbd al-Razzāq told us: Maʿmar told us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Wahb ibn Jābir al-Khaywānī, who said: I was with ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ when a steward came to him from Syria, one night of Ramadan remaining. ʿAbdullāh said to him: "Have you left my family what suffices them?" He said: "I left them some provision." ʿAbdullāh said: "I adjure you to go back and leave them what suffices them, for I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: 'It is sin enough for a man to neglect those whom he sustains.'" Then he began to tell us: "When the sun sets it gives greeting, prostrates and asks permission, and it is given permission. Until one day it sets, gives greeting, prostrates and asks permission, and is not given permission. It says: 'My Lord, the journey is long, and if I am not given permission I will not arrive.' It is held back as long as God wills. Then it is said to it: 'Rise from where you set.' From that day until the Day of Resurrection: '*It will not benefit a soul its faith if it had not believed before*' [6:158]."

He said: And he mentioned Gog and Magog, and said: "A man among them does not die until a thousand are born to him from his loins. Behind them are three nations whose number none knows but God: Mansik, Tāwīl and Tāwīs."

ʿAbd al-Razzāq told us: Maʿmar told us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Wahb ibn Jābir al-Khaywānī, who said: I was with ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ when a steward came to him from Syria, one night of Ramadan remaining. ʿAbdullāh said to him: "Have you left my family what suffices them?" Until one day it sets, gives greeting, prostrates and asks permission, and is not given permission. It says: 'My Lord, the journey is long, and if I am not given permission I will not arrive.' It is held back as long as God wills. Then it is said to it: 'Rise from where you set.' From that day until the Day of Resurrection: '*It will not benefit a soul its faith if it had not believed before*' [6:158]."

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq, from Maʿmar, from Maṭar and others, from al-Ḥasan, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Your hands will be filled from the non-Arabs. Then they will become lions who do not flee, then they will strike your necks and eat your spoils."

records.text_en:
We read to ʿAbd al-Razzāq, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl al-ʿAdawī, from a man he named, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: We were sitting with him in Kufa when a red wind blew, and people began to say: "The Hour has come!" Then a man came who had no other cry, saying: "The Hour has come, Ibn Masʿūd! The Hour has come, Ibn Masʿūd!" He sat upright and became angry, for he had been reclining, and said: "By God, the Hour will not come until no inheritance is divided and no one rejoices over spoils." And he said: "There will be a war/apostasy between you and those people." Ḥumayd said: I said to the man: "You mean the Romans?" He said: "Yes."

[He continued:] "The believers will call on one another for reinforcement and be killed. A detachment will pledge itself to death, not to return except victorious. They will fight until night comes between them, and each side withdraws with neither having prevailed, and the detachment is annihilated. Then the second day is the same, then the third day the same. Then on the fourth day the remainder of the Muslims will rise against them, and a slaughter will take place the like of which has never been seen, so that brothers of one father would count themselves off to reach a hundred, and none of them would remain but one man."

Ibn Masʿūd said: "Would an inheritance be divided here?" (Maʿmar said: Qatāda used to give this ḥadīth a continuous chain.) He said: "They proceed until they enter Constantinople, and find in it so much gold and silver that a man goes hopping along [under the load]. While they are so engaged, the cry comes to them that the Dajjāl has taken their place among your homes, so they abandon what is in their hands." Ibn Masʿūd said: "Would one rejoice over spoils here?" "They send out a vanguard of ten horsemen, or twelve." Ibn Masʿūd said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "I know their names, their tribes and the colors of their horses. They are that day the best horsemen on earth." The Dajjāl fights them and they are martyred.
records.text_ar: ٢٠٨١٢ - قَرَأْنَا عَلَى عَبْدِ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ حُمَيْدِ بْنِ هِلَالٍ الْعَدَوِيِّ، عَنْ رَجُلٍ سَمَّاهُ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ قَالَ: إِنَّا لَجُلُوسٌ عِنْدَهُ بِالْكُوفَةِ إِذْ هَاجَتْ رِيحٌ حَمْرَاءُ، فَجَعَلَ النَّاسُ يَقُولُونَ: قَامَتِ السَّاعَةُ، حَتَّى جَاءَ رَجُلٌ لَيْسَ لَهُ هِجِّيرَى، يَقُولُ: قَدْ قَامَتِ السَّاعَةُ يَا ابْنَ مَسْعُودٍ، قَدْ قَامَتِ السَّاعَةُ يَا ابْنَ مَسْعُودٍ فَاسْتَوَى جَالِسًا وَغَضِبَ، وَكَانَ مُتَّكِئًا، فَقَالَ: وَاللَّهِ §لَا تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ حَتَّى لَا يُقْسَمَ - [٣٨٦] - مِيرَاثٌ، وَلَا يُفْرَحَ بِغَنِيمَةٍ، وَقَالَ: إِنَّهَا سَتَكُونُ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَ هَؤُلَاءِ رِدَّةٌ - قَالَ حُمَيْدٌ: فَقُلْتُ لِلرَّجُلِ: الرُّومَ تَعْنِي؟ قَالَ: نَعَمْ - وَيَسْتَمِدُّ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ بَعْضُهُمْ بَعْضًا، فَيُقْتَلُونَ، فَتَشْتَرِطُ شُرْطَةً لِلْمَوْتِ ألَّا يَرْجِعُوا إِلَّا غَالِبِينَ، فَيَقْتَتِلُونَ حَتَّى يَحُولَ بَيْنَهُمُ اللَّيْلُ، فَيَفِيءُ هَؤُلَاءِ وَيَفِيءُ هَؤُلَاءِ، وَكُلٌّ غَيْرُ غَالِبٍ، وَتَفْنَى الشُّرْطَةُ، ثُمَّ الْيَوْمَ الثَّانِي كَذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ الْيَوْمَ الثَّالِثَ كَذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ الْيَوْمَ الرَّابِعَ يَنهَدُ إِلَيْهِمْ بَقِيَّةُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ فَيُقْتَلُونَ مَقْتَلَةً لَمْ يُرَ مِثْلُهَا، حَتَّى إِنَّ بَنِي الْأَبِ كَانُوا يَتَعَادَوْنَ عَلَى مِائَةٍ لَا يَبْقَى مِنْهُمْ إِلَّا الرَّجُلُ   «، قَالَ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ: أفَيُقْسَمُ هَاهُنَا مِيرَاثٌ؟ - قَالَ مَعْمَرٌ: وَكَانَ قَتَادَةُ يَصِلُ هَذَا الْحَدِيثَ - قَالَ: فَيَنْطَلِقُونَ حَتَّى يَدْخُلُوا قُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةَ، فَيَجِدُونَ فِيهَا مِنَ الصَّفْرَاءِ وَالْبَيْضَاءِ، مَا أَنَّ الرَّجُلَ يَتَحَجَّلُ حَجْلًا، فَبَيْنَا هُمْ كَذَلِكَ إِذْ جَاءَهُمُ الصَّرِيخُ أَنَّ الدَّجَّالَ قَدْ خَلَفَ فِي دِيَارِكُمْ، فَيَرْفُضُونَ مَا فِي أَيْدِيهِمْ، قَالَ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ: أفَيُفْرَحُ هَاهُنَا بِغَنِيمَةٍ؟ فَيَبْعَثُونَ مِنْهُمْ طَلِيعَةً عَشَرَةَ فَوَارِسَ، أَوِ اثْنَيْ عَشَرَ، قَالَ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ»   إِنِّي لَأَعْرِفُ أَسْمَاءَهُمْ وَقَبَائِلَهُمْ، وَأَلْوَانَ خُيُولِهِمْ، هُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَيْرُ فَوَارِسَ - [٣٨٧] - فِي الْأَرْضِ، فَيُقَاتِلُهُمُ الدَّجَّالُ فَيُسْتَشْهَدُونَ "

قَالَ حُمَيْدٌ: فَقُلْتُ لِلرَّجُلِ: الرُّومَ تَعْنِي؟ قَالَ: نَعَمْ - وَيَسْتَمِدُّ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ بَعْضُهُمْ بَعْضًا، فَيُقْتَلُونَ، فَتَشْتَرِطُ شُرْطَةً لِلْمَوْتِ ألَّا يَرْجِعُوا إِلَّا غَالِبِينَ، فَيَقْتَتِلُونَ حَتَّى يَحُولَ بَيْنَهُمُ اللَّيْلُ، فَيَفِيءُ هَؤُلَاءِ وَيَفِيءُ هَؤُلَاءِ، وَكُلٌّ غَيْرُ غَالِبٍ، وَتَفْنَى الشُّرْطَةُ، ثُمَّ الْيَوْمَ الثَّانِي كَذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ الْيَوْمَ الثَّالِثَ كَذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ الْيَوْمَ الرَّابِعَ يَنهَدُ إِلَيْهِمْ بَقِيَّةُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ فَيُقْتَلُونَ مَقْتَلَةً لَمْ يُرَ مِثْلُهَا، حَتَّى إِنَّ بَنِي الْأَبِ كَانُوا يَتَعَادَوْنَ عَلَى مِائَةٍ لَا يَبْقَى مِنْهُمْ إِلَّا الرَّجُلُ   «، قَالَ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ: أفَيُقْسَمُ هَاهُنَا مِيرَاثٌ؟ - قَالَ مَعْمَرٌ: وَكَانَ قَتَادَةُ يَصِلُ هَذَا الْحَدِيثَ - قَالَ: فَيَنْطَلِقُونَ حَتَّى يَدْخُلُوا قُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةَ، فَيَجِدُونَ فِيهَا مِنَ الصَّفْرَاءِ وَالْبَيْضَاءِ، مَا أَنَّ الرَّجُلَ يَتَحَجَّلُ حَجْلًا، فَبَيْنَا هُمْ كَذَلِكَ إِذْ جَاءَهُمُ الصَّرِيخُ أَنَّ الدَّجَّالَ قَدْ خَلَفَ فِي دِيَارِكُمْ، فَيَرْفُضُونَ مَا فِي أَيْدِيهِمْ، قَالَ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ: أفَيُفْرَحُ هَاهُنَا بِغَنِيمَةٍ؟ فَيَبْعَثُونَ مِنْهُمْ طَلِيعَةً عَشَرَةَ فَوَارِسَ، أَوِ اثْنَيْ عَشَرَ، قَالَ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ»   إِنِّي لَأَعْرِفُ أَسْمَاءَهُمْ وَقَبَائِلَهُمْ، وَأَلْوَانَ خُيُولِهِمْ، هُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَيْرُ فَوَارِسَ فِي الْأَرْضِ، فَيُقَاتِلُهُمُ الدَّجَّالُ فَيُسْتَشْهَدُونَ "
records.raw_text_en:
We read to ʿAbd al-Razzāq, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl al-ʿAdawī, from a man he named, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: We were sitting with him in Kufa when a red wind blew, and people began to say: "The Hour has come!" Then a man came who had no other cry, saying: "The Hour has come, Ibn Masʿūd! The Hour has come, Ibn Masʿūd!" He sat upright and became angry, for he had been reclining, and said: "By God, the Hour will not come until no inheritance is divided and no one rejoices over spoils." And he said: "There will be a war/apostasy between you and those people." Ḥumayd said: I said to the man: "You mean the Romans?" He said: "Yes."

[He continued:] "The believers will call on one another for reinforcement and be killed. A detachment will pledge itself to death, not to return except victorious. They will fight until night comes between them, and each side withdraws with neither having prevailed, and the detachment is annihilated. Then the second day is the same, then the third day the same. Then on the fourth day the remainder of the Muslims will rise against them, and a slaughter will take place the like of which has never been seen, so that brothers of one father would count themselves off to reach a hundred, and none of them would remain but one man."

Ibn Masʿūd said: "Would an inheritance be divided here?" (Maʿmar said: Qatāda used to give this ḥadīth a continuous chain.) He said: "They proceed until they enter Constantinople, and find in it so much gold and silver that a man goes hopping along [under the load]. While they are so engaged, the cry comes to them that the Dajjāl has taken their place among your homes, so they abandon what is in their hands." Ibn Masʿūd said: "Would one rejoice over spoils here?" "They send out a vanguard of ten horsemen, or twelve." Ibn Masʿūd said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "I know their names, their tribes and the colors of their horses. They are that day the best horsemen on earth." The Dajjāl fights them and they are martyred.

records.display_matn_ar: إِنَّا لَجُلُوسٌ عِنْدَهُ بِالْكُوفَةِ إِذْ هَاجَتْ رِيحٌ حَمْرَاءُ، فَجَعَلَ النَّاسُ يَقُولُونَ: قَامَتِ السَّاعَةُ، حَتَّى جَاءَ رَجُلٌ لَيْسَ لَهُ هِجِّيرَى، يَقُولُ: قَدْ قَامَتِ السَّاعَةُ يَا ابْنَ مَسْعُودٍ، قَدْ قَامَتِ السَّاعَةُ يَا ابْنَ مَسْعُودٍ فَاسْتَوَى جَالِسًا وَغَضِبَ، وَكَانَ مُتَّكِئًا، فَقَالَ: وَاللَّهِ §لَا تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ حَتَّى لَا يُقْسَمَ مِيرَاثٌ، وَلَا يُفْرَحَ بِغَنِيمَةٍ، وَقَالَ: إِنَّهَا سَتَكُونُ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَ هَؤُلَاءِ رِدَّةٌ - قَالَ حُمَيْدٌ: فَقُلْتُ لِلرَّجُلِ: الرُّومَ تَعْنِي؟ قَالَ: نَعَمْ - وَيَسْتَمِدُّ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ بَعْضُهُمْ بَعْضًا، فَيُقْتَلُونَ، فَتَشْتَرِطُ شُرْطَةً لِلْمَوْتِ ألَّا يَرْجِعُوا إِلَّا غَالِبِينَ، فَيَقْتَتِلُونَ حَتَّى يَحُولَ بَيْنَهُمُ اللَّيْلُ، فَيَفِيءُ هَؤُلَاءِ وَيَفِيءُ هَؤُلَاءِ، وَكُلٌّ غَيْرُ غَالِبٍ، وَتَفْنَى الشُّرْطَةُ، ثُمَّ الْيَوْمَ الثَّانِي كَذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ الْيَوْمَ الثَّالِثَ كَذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ الْيَوْمَ الرَّابِعَ يَنهَدُ إِلَيْهِمْ بَقِيَّةُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ فَيُقْتَلُونَ مَقْتَلَةً لَمْ يُرَ مِثْلُهَا، حَتَّى إِنَّ بَنِي الْأَبِ كَانُوا يَتَعَادَوْنَ عَلَى مِائَةٍ لَا يَبْقَى مِنْهُمْ إِلَّا الرَّجُلُ   «، قَالَ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ: أفَيُقْسَمُ هَاهُنَا مِيرَاثٌ؟ - قَالَ مَعْمَرٌ: وَكَانَ قَتَادَةُ يَصِلُ هَذَا الْحَدِيثَ - قَالَ: فَيَنْطَلِقُونَ حَتَّى يَدْخُلُوا قُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةَ، فَيَجِدُونَ فِيهَا مِنَ الصَّفْرَاءِ وَالْبَيْضَاءِ، مَا أَنَّ الرَّجُلَ يَتَحَجَّلُ حَجْلًا، فَبَيْنَا هُمْ كَذَلِكَ إِذْ جَاءَهُمُ الصَّرِيخُ أَنَّ الدَّجَّالَ قَدْ خَلَفَ فِي دِيَارِكُمْ، فَيَرْفُضُونَ مَا فِي أَيْدِيهِمْ، قَالَ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ: أفَيُفْرَحُ هَاهُنَا بِغَنِيمَةٍ؟ فَيَبْعَثُونَ مِنْهُمْ طَلِيعَةً عَشَرَةَ فَوَارِسَ، أَوِ اثْنَيْ عَشَرَ، قَالَ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ»   إِنِّي لَأَعْرِفُ أَسْمَاءَهُمْ وَقَبَائِلَهُمْ، وَأَلْوَانَ خُيُولِهِمْ، هُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَيْرُ فَوَارِسَ فِي الْأَرْضِ، فَيُقَاتِلُهُمُ الدَّجَّالُ فَيُسْتَشْهَدُونَ "
records.display_isnad_en: We read to ʿAbd al-Razzāq, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl al-ʿAdawī, from a man he named, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said:
records.display_matn_en:
We were sitting with him in Kufa when a red wind blew, and people began to say: "The Hour has come!" Then a man came who had no other cry, saying: "The Hour has come, Ibn Masʿūd! The Hour has come, Ibn Masʿūd!" He sat upright and became angry, for he had been reclining, and said: "By God, the Hour will not come until no inheritance is divided and no one rejoices over spoils." And he said: "There will be a war/apostasy between you and those people." Ḥumayd said: I said to the man: "You mean the Romans?" He said: "Yes."

[He continued:] "The believers will call on one another for reinforcement and be killed. A detachment will pledge itself to death, not to return except victorious. They will fight until night comes between them, and each side withdraws with neither having prevailed, and the detachment is annihilated. Then the second day is the same, then the third day the same. Then on the fourth day the remainder of the Muslims will rise against them, and a slaughter will take place the like of which has never been seen, so that brothers of one father would count themselves off to reach a hundred, and none of them would remain but one man."

Ibn Masʿūd said: "Would an inheritance be divided here?" (Maʿmar said: Qatāda used to give this ḥadīth a continuous chain.) He said: "They proceed until they enter Constantinople, and find in it so much gold and silver that a man goes hopping along [under the load]. While they are so engaged, the cry comes to them that the Dajjāl has taken their place among your homes, so they abandon what is in their hands." Ibn Masʿūd said: "Would one rejoice over spoils here?" "They send out a vanguard of ten horsemen, or twelve." Ibn Masʿūd said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "I know their names, their tribes and the colors of their horses. They are that day the best horsemen on earth." The Dajjāl fights them and they are martyred.

records.text_en:
ʿAbd al-Razzāq told us: Maʿmar told us, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn, from ʿUqba ibn Aws al-Dawsī, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, who said: "The Romans will have a king whom they do not disobey, or hardly disobey. He will come until he camps in such-and-such a land." ʿAbdullāh said: "I have not forgotten it." He said: "The believers will call on one another for reinforcement until the people of Aden Abyan reinforce them on their young camels." ʿAbdullāh said: "It is written in the Book: 'They will fight for ten days with nothing separating them but the night. You will have no food except what is in your water-skins. Their swords do not tire…' [the words 'wa-yubārikuhum wa-lā nisāʾihim' are corrupt] '…and you likewise. Then their king, meaning the king of the Romans, orders the ships and turns away. Then he says: "Whoever wishes, let him flee now." God turns the rout against them, and they are slain in a slaughter the like of which has not been seen, or will not be seen, so that a bird passes by them and falls dead from their stench. The martyr that day has a double share over the martyrs before him, and the believer that day a double share over the believers before him. The remainder of them will never be shaken by anything, and the remainder of them will fight the Dajjāl.'"

Ibn Sīrīn said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām used to say: "If this battle reaches me while I am sick, carry me on my bed until you place me between the two ranks."
records.text_ar: ٢٠٨١٣ - أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنِ ابْنِ سِيرِينَ، عَنْ عُقْبَةَ بْنِ أَوْسٍ الدَّوْسِيِّ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرِو بْنِ الْعَاصِ، قَالَ:   «§يَكُونُ عَلَى الرُّومِ مَلِكٌ لَا يَعْصُونَهُ - أَوْ لَا يَكَادُونَ يَعْصُونَهُ -، فَيَجِيءُ حَتَّى يَنْزِلَ بِأَرْضِ كَذَا وَكَذَا»   ، قَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ:   «أَنَا مَا نَسَيْتُهَا»   ، قَالَ:   «وَيَسْتَمِدُّ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ بَعْضُهُمْ بَعْضًا حَتَّى يَمُدَّهُمْ أَهْلُ عَدَنَ أَبْيَنَ عَلَى قَلَصَاتِهِمْ»   ، قَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ:   «إِنَّهُ لَفِي الْكِتَابِ مَكْتُوبٌ: فَيَقْتَتِلُونَ عَشْرًا لَا يَحْجُزُ بَيْنَهُمْ إِلَّا اللَّيْلُ، لَيْسَ لَكُمْ طَعَامٌ إِلَّا مَا فِي إِدَاوِيكُمْ، لَا تَكِلُّ سُيُوفُهُمْ وَيباركهم وَلَا نِسَائِهِمْ، وَأَنْتُمْ أَيْضًا كَذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ يَأْمُرُ مَلِكُهُمْ بِالسُّفُنِ فَيَنْحَرِفُ - يَعْنِي مَلِكَ الرُّومِ - قَالَ: ثُمَّ يَقُولُ: مَنْ شَاءَ الْآنَ فَلْيَفِرَّ، فيجَعَلُ اللَّهُ الدَّبْرَةَ عَلَيْهِمْ، فَيُقْتَلُونَ مَقْتَلَةً لَمْ يُرَ مِثْلُهَا - أَوْ لَا يُرَى مِثْلُهَا -، حَتَّى إِنَّ الطَّائِرَ لَيَمُرُّ بِهِمْ فَيَقَعُ مَيِّتًا مِنْ نَتْنِهِمْ، لِلشَّهِيدِ يَوْمَئِذٍ كِفْلَانِ عَلَى مَنْ مَضَى قَبْلَهُ مِنَ الشُّهَدَاءِ، وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِ يَوْمَئِذٍ كِفْلَانِ عَلَى مَنْ مَضَى مِنْهُمْ قَبْلَهُ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ، قَالَ: وَبَقِيَّتُهُمْ لَا يُزَلْزِلُهُمْ شَيْءٌ أَبَدًا، وَبَقِيَّتُهُمْ يُقَاتِلُ الدَّجَّالَ»   قَالَ ابْنُ سِيرِينَ: فَكَانَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ - [٣٨٨] - سَلَامٍ يَقُولُ:   «إِنْ أَدْرَكَنِي هَذَا الْقِتَالُ وَأَنَا مَرِيضٌ فَاحْمِلُونِي عَلَى سَرِيرِي حَتَّى تَجْعَلُونِي بَيْنَ الصَّفَّيْنِ»

records.raw_text_en:
ʿAbd al-Razzāq told us: Maʿmar told us, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn, from ʿUqba ibn Aws al-Dawsī, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, who said: "The Romans will have a king whom they do not disobey, or hardly disobey. He will come until he camps in such-and-such a land." ʿAbdullāh said: "I have not forgotten it." He said: "The believers will call on one another for reinforcement until the people of Aden Abyan reinforce them on their young camels." ʿAbdullāh said: "It is written in the Book: 'They will fight for ten days with nothing separating them but the night. You will have no food except what is in your water-skins. Their swords do not tire…' [the words 'wa-yubārikuhum wa-lā nisāʾihim' are corrupt] '…and you likewise. Then their king, meaning the king of the Romans, orders the ships and turns away. Then he says: "Whoever wishes, let him flee now." God turns the rout against them, and they are slain in a slaughter the like of which has not been seen, or will not be seen, so that a bird passes by them and falls dead from their stench. The martyr that day has a double share over the martyrs before him, and the believer that day a double share over the believers before him. The remainder of them will never be shaken by anything, and the remainder of them will fight the Dajjāl.'"

Ibn Sīrīn said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām used to say: "If this battle reaches me while I am sick, carry me on my bed until you place me between the two ranks."

records.display_matn_ar: يَكُونُ عَلَى الرُّومِ مَلِكٌ لَا يَعْصُونَهُ - أَوْ لَا يَكَادُونَ يَعْصُونَهُ -، فَيَجِيءُ حَتَّى يَنْزِلَ بِأَرْضِ كَذَا وَكَذَا»   ، قَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ:   «أَنَا مَا نَسَيْتُهَا»   ، قَالَ:   «وَيَسْتَمِدُّ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ بَعْضُهُمْ بَعْضًا حَتَّى يَمُدَّهُمْ أَهْلُ عَدَنَ أَبْيَنَ عَلَى قَلَصَاتِهِمْ»   ، قَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ:   «إِنَّهُ لَفِي الْكِتَابِ مَكْتُوبٌ: فَيَقْتَتِلُونَ عَشْرًا لَا يَحْجُزُ بَيْنَهُمْ إِلَّا اللَّيْلُ، لَيْسَ لَكُمْ طَعَامٌ إِلَّا مَا فِي إِدَاوِيكُمْ، لَا تَكِلُّ سُيُوفُهُمْ وَيباركهم وَلَا نِسَائِهِمْ، وَأَنْتُمْ أَيْضًا كَذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ يَأْمُرُ مَلِكُهُمْ بِالسُّفُنِ فَيَنْحَرِفُ - يَعْنِي مَلِكَ الرُّومِ - قَالَ: ثُمَّ يَقُولُ: مَنْ شَاءَ الْآنَ فَلْيَفِرَّ، فيجَعَلُ اللَّهُ الدَّبْرَةَ عَلَيْهِمْ، فَيُقْتَلُونَ مَقْتَلَةً لَمْ يُرَ مِثْلُهَا - أَوْ لَا يُرَى مِثْلُهَا -، حَتَّى إِنَّ الطَّائِرَ لَيَمُرُّ بِهِمْ فَيَقَعُ مَيِّتًا مِنْ نَتْنِهِمْ، لِلشَّهِيدِ يَوْمَئِذٍ كِفْلَانِ عَلَى مَنْ مَضَى قَبْلَهُ مِنَ الشُّهَدَاءِ، وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِ يَوْمَئِذٍ كِفْلَانِ عَلَى مَنْ مَضَى مِنْهُمْ قَبْلَهُ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ، قَالَ: وَبَقِيَّتُهُمْ لَا يُزَلْزِلُهُمْ شَيْءٌ أَبَدًا، وَبَقِيَّتُهُمْ يُقَاتِلُ الدَّجَّالَ»   قَالَ ابْنُ سِيرِينَ: فَكَانَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ سَلَامٍ يَقُولُ:   «إِنْ أَدْرَكَنِي هَذَا الْقِتَالُ وَأَنَا مَرِيضٌ فَاحْمِلُونِي عَلَى سَرِيرِي حَتَّى تَجْعَلُونِي بَيْنَ الصَّفَّيْنِ»
records.display_isnad_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq told us: Maʿmar told us, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn, from ʿUqba ibn Aws al-Dawsī, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, who said: "
records.display_matn_en:
The Romans will have a king whom they do not disobey, or hardly disobey. He will come until he camps in such-and-such a land." ʿAbdullāh said: "I have not forgotten it." He said: "The believers will call on one another for reinforcement until the people of Aden Abyan reinforce them on their young camels." ʿAbdullāh said: "It is written in the Book: 'They will fight for ten days with nothing separating them but the night. You will have no food except what is in your water-skins. Their swords do not tire…' [the words 'wa-yubārikuhum wa-lā nisāʾihim' are corrupt] '…and you likewise. Then their king, meaning the king of the Romans, orders the ships and turns away. Then he says: "Whoever wishes, let him flee now." God turns the rout against them, and they are slain in a slaughter the like of which has not been seen, or will not be seen, so that a bird passes by them and falls dead from their stench. The martyr that day has a double share over the martyrs before him, and the believer that day a double share over the believers before him. The remainder of them will never be shaken by anything, and the remainder of them will fight the Dajjāl.'"

Ibn Sīrīn said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām used to say: "If this battle reaches me while I am sick, carry me on my bed until you place me between the two ranks."

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq told us: Maʿmar told us, from Ibn Abī Dhiʾb, from Saʿīd al-Maqburī, who said: Abū Hurayra said: "The nights and days will not pass until the raider attacks Rūmiya [Rome], does [the same] to Constantinople, and thinks he has accomplished it. And the Hour will not come until a man from Qaḥṭān drives the people." [The first sentence is obscure.]

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq told us: Maʿmar told us, from al-Zuhrī, from Sālim, from Ibn ʿUmar: The Messenger of God ﷺ passed by Ibn Ṣayyād with a group of his Companions, among them ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. He was playing with the boys at the fortress of Banū Maghāla, and he was a boy. He did not notice until the Messenger of God ﷺ struck his back with his hand and said: "Do you testify that I am the Messenger of God?" Ibn Ṣayyād looked at him and said: "I testify that you are the messenger of the unlettered." Ibn Ṣayyād said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Do you testify that I am the messenger of God?" The Prophet ﷺ said: "I believe in God and His messenger." Then the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "What comes to you?" Ibn Ṣayyād said: "A truthful one and a liar come to me." The Prophet ﷺ said: "The matter has been confused for you." Then the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "I have concealed something for you," and he concealed for him [the verse] "*the Day when the sky brings a clear smoke*" [44:10]. Ibn Ṣayyād said: "It is the *dukh*." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Begone! You will not exceed your measure." ʿUmar said: "Messenger of God, permit me to strike his neck." The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "If he is the one, you will not be given power over him, and if he is not, there is no good for you in killing him."

records.matn_ar: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ مَرَّ بِابْنِ صَيَّادٍ فِي نَفَرٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِهِ، مِنْهُمْ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ، وَهُوَ يَلْعَبُ مَعَ الْغِلْمَانِ عِنْدَ أُطُمِ بَنِي مَغَالَةَ وَهُوَ غُلَامٌ، فَلَمْ يَشْعُرْ حَتَّى ضَرَبَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ظَهْرَهُ بِيَدِهِ، فَقَالَ:   «§أَتَشْهَدُ أَنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ؟»   ، فَنَظَرَ إِلَيْهِ ابْنُ صَيَّادٍ فَقَالَ: أَشْهَدُ أَنَّكَ رَسُولُ الْأُمِّيِّينَ، قَالَ ابْنُ صَيَّادٍ لِلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ  أَتَشْهَدُ أَنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ؟ فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «آمَنْتُ بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ»   فَقَالَ لَهُ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «مَا يَأْتِيكَ؟»   ، قَالَ ابْنُ صَيَّادٍ: يَأْتِينِي صَادِقٌ وَكَاذِبٌ، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «خُلِّطَ عَلَيْكَ الْأَمْرُ»   ، ثُمَّ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «إِنِّي قَدْ خَبَأْتُ لَكَ خَبِيئًا»   وَخَبَأَ لَهُ  {يَوْمَ تَأْتِي السَّمَاءُ بِدُخَانٍ مُبِينٍ}   [الدخان: ١٠]  ، فَقَالَ ابْنُ صَيَّادٍ: هُوَ الدُّخُّ، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «اخْسَأْ، فَلَنْ تَعْدُوَ قَدْرَكَ»   فَقَالَ عُمَرُ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، ائْذَنْ لِي فِيهِ فَأَضْرِبَ عُنُقَهُ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ    «إِنْ يَكُ هُوَ فَلَنْ تُسَلَّطَ عَلَيْهِ، وَإِنْ لَا يَكُنْ هُوَ فَلَا خَيْرَ لَكَ فِي قَتْلِهِ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Sinān ibn Abī Sinān, that he heard Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī narrate that the Prophet ﷺ concealed [the word] "smoke" for Ibn Ṣayyād and asked him what he had concealed, and he said: "*Dukh*." He said: "Begone! You will not exceed your measure" (or: your term). When he turned away, the Prophet ﷺ said: "What did he say?" Some said: "*Dukh*," and others said: "No, he said *rīḥ* [wind]." The Prophet ﷺ said: "You have differed while I am among you, and after me you will differ even more."

Ibn ʿUmar said: The Messenger of God ﷺ and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb went one day to the palm grove where Ibn Ṣayyād was. When they entered the grove, the Messenger of God ﷺ began to shield himself behind the trunks of the palms, stealthily approaching Ibn Ṣayyād to hear something from him before he saw him. Ibn Ṣayyād was lying on his bed in a velvet cloth in which there was a murmuring. His mother saw the Messenger of God ﷺ shielding himself behind the trunks and said: "Ṣāf" (his name), "this is Muḥammad!" He rose up. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "If she had left him, he would have made things clear."

records.text_en:
ʿAbd al-Razzāq, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Sālim, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ stood among the people, praised God as He deserves, then mentioned the Dajjāl and said: "I warn you of him. There was no prophet who did not warn his people of him; Noah warned his people. But I will tell you something about him that no prophet told his people: you know that he is one-eyed, and that God is not one-eyed."

[This continuation is in the supplied English only; it is not in the Arabic text.] Al-Zuhrī said: ʿUmar ibn Thābit al-Anṣārī told me that some of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ told him that the Messenger of God ﷺ said that day to the people, warning them of the trial of the Dajjāl: "None of you will see his Lord until he dies. And between his [the Dajjāl's] eyes is written 'unbeliever,' which is read by whoever dislikes his deeds."
